"I don't know yet whether I'll invite her or not — we'll see. As for the others, don't mind them — they're not really anything to do with us."

Lu Huaixi's tone was easy, a smile still on her lips.

She was asking for Little Doctor Ceng not for the Old Madam's sake but for her own.

The year ahead held unknown variables. How many twists and turns were hidden inside the Marquis Manor, she — an outsider just arrived — had no way to see clearly.

And then there was her relationship with Xie Yuanjing.

The two of them were bound together for a year, and she couldn't very well go on indefinitely without "consummating the marriage."

But she didn't trust the manor's people — and even less the manor's physicians.

She needed someone she knew and trusted to establish themselves in front of the Xie family's people through legitimate means, and then be openly at her disposal.

That way, when Xie Yuanjing was away, she'd have her own physician — no one could take advantage of the gaps.

"I imagine it must be past the noon meal hour by now? I'm hungry."

Lu Huaixi stepped onto the covered walkway, and when she was sure there was no one nearby, raised a hand to pat her stomach.

The Xie Old Madam seemed to have no trouble going without food — and apparently enjoyed drawing things out, waiting for her to be the first to crack and speak.

"I forgot to give the instruction before I left. I don't know if they prepared the noon meal — they might think I'm eating in another courtyard."

The thought of food made her voice, which had been brisk until now, soften into a trace of aggrieved petulance — faint and high, a little childlike.

Behind her, the ever-composed Jing Shuang gave an involuntary laugh, the gaze she directed at Lu Huaixi instantly warming.

"It's been prepared, Eldest Young Mistress. Just a little more patience — once you're back in the courtyard, you can eat."

"Really?"

Lu Huaixi turned to look at her, dark eyes opening just a fraction wider, pupils black and bright.

"Yes. The Eldest Young Master specifically before he left —"

"How long have you been out here?"

The words were cut short by a sudden voice.

All three of them looked over at once.

Lu Huaixi immediately caught sight of Xie Yuanjing's clear, refined features not far away, and froze for a moment — then, understanding breaking through, gave a small, happy leap and jogged toward him.

"You're back so early — how?"

She tilted her face up, chin lifted just slightly, the line of her jaw a lovely curve.

Sunlight fell on Lu Huaixi's face, illuminating the clarity of her fair skin — like flawless white jade, perfect and unblemished — making one momentarily lose oneself in looking.

Xie Yuanjing's gaze met hers instinctively, then dropped slightly.

Whether it was the wine he'd had, or something else, he suddenly felt a little thirsty, his mind not as clear as usual.

"The wine finished early. Didn't stay for the noon meal."

Xie Yuanjing steadied himself, and his gaze went back to her eyes. "You were in there so long — did the Old Madam make things difficult for you?"

"She didn't make things difficult. I just may not have gotten around to everything."

"Not gotten around to it?"

"Mm, mm."

Lu Huaixi nodded several times, and thinking of what had just happened, pressed a hand over her smile. "I'll tell you when we get back."

Then, as if only just remembering something, she looked in the direction Xie Yuanjing had come from. "Were you heading somewhere? Then I won't hold you up — I can tell you later."

Xie Yuanjing didn't know why, but he laughed a little too, and followed her quieter tone.

"Nowhere to be."

He said: "I came to fetch you."

Lu Huaixi looked up and saw Xie Yuanjing's handsome face — the man's eyes narrowed just slightly, those dark pupils deep and still.

Having drunk a little, the usual air that kept everyone at arm's length had thinned. The whole person carried a languid, unhurried ease, and when the corner of his mouth curved, there was an indescribable, effortless charm.

Lu Huaixi's heart gave a sudden, sharp leap.

She wanted to step back a couple of paces and let it settle — but found, to her own lack of dignity, that she failed completely.

She simply did not want to move.

—

Back in the Old Madam's courtyard.

The frustration the Old Madam had held back now came down in full on Mu Weimi.

The words were not particularly harsh — after all, this was someone she had raised, whom she deeply trusted.

But Mu Weimi heard every one of them. She kept her head low, as if she knew her fault — eyes reddening, a tear threatening to fall. And yet beneath her sleeves, her hands were clenched so tight they were almost tearing the handkerchief apart.

After a long while, the Old Madam seemed to tire of speaking.

Seeing the pathetic, grieved look on the face before her, she finally softened her tone a little.

"Next time, don't act on your own impulse in front of her. She's a Lu family born legitimate daughter — that rank speaks for itself. Of course she would know people of consequence. You rushed in without knowing her measure first, and now you've made a fool of yourself."

"Weimi understands. Grand Aunt, please don't be upset."

"If you want me not to be upset, act with more care going forward. Keep certain feelings that should not be visible — keep them hidden."

"Yes, Weimi understands."

Seeing the person before her ease just slightly, Mu Weimi stepped forward and said quietly:

"It was my fault just now. I was too concerned for Grand Aunt's health, and momentarily forgot that Elder Sister-in-law might truly know such a remarkable physician. When it's a little later, Weimi will go and make her apologies to Elder Sister-in-law — ask her not to be at odds with Grand Aunt."

A veiled insinuation hidden in those words of apology.

Mu Weimi was of course unwilling to accept this. She still wasn't fully convinced.

As she saw it, if Lu Huaixi really could summon that kind of physician at will, she wouldn't have gone on speaking in circles and refused to simply agree outright.

Especially when Xie Yuanjing clearly didn't care about her situation.

If Lu Huaixi hadn't been doing it deliberately — then she had simply lied to the Old Madam. In that case, going to apologize was nothing.

Turning it over in her mind, Mu Weimi finally suppressed the churning from before.

"Grand Aunt, please eat first. Don't let Weimi's matters make you upset on your own behalf."

"Good that you can think of it that way."

The Old Madam closed her eyes briefly, then opened them. "Yuanjing's rear court, in the end, will not always have only one person. Eventually, someone who can soothe him — who understands the moment — must be there."

"Weimi understands. As long as I can care for you and my cousin, I'm willing to do anything. Even if I can never truly be my cousin's person — not a word of complaint will cross my lips."

Outside, the Second Madam Qi Miaoji, just arriving with the herbal medicine, happened to catch those last two lines.

She couldn't help curling her lip, a flicker of contempt in her eyes for this so-called cousin.

"Still daydreaming when the bride has already married in."

The nanny beside her was alarmed and quickly tried to hush her: "We're in the Old Madam's courtyard — Second Madam, that sort of talk really can't be said here."

"What is there to be afraid of? It's so late. No one heard."

Qi shi simply stopped at the doorway and refused to go in.

"I don't know what that Old Madam of ours is thinking. Taking in a distant relative is one thing — but now she wants to drag her own grandson into it? Setting all that aside — isn't the Lu girl perfectly fine?"

Today was the First Branch's joyous occasion, and she had been in excellent spirits all day — looking forward to meeting the new bride tomorrow.

If they got along, they could make a point of spending more time together.

But tonight, just as she had been about to go back to her rooms and rest, she'd been summoned here to wait on the Old Madam.

Ordinarily, duties like this fell to the Third Young Madam. The Old Madam had always favored her youngest daughter-in-law — always finding opportunities to give the Third Branch little advantages.

But tonight the hour had grown too late, and the Old Madam hadn't the heart to drag the Third Young Madam out. Unable to call on the First Branch either, she'd sent for her instead.

Qi shi had a stomach full of grievances and nowhere to direct them. Hearing nonsense like this, she naturally couldn't hold herself back from speaking up for the First Branch.

chapters.title: Some Things Still Need to Be Taught
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi followed Xie Yuanjing back dutifully, brow faintly knit, still turning over that sudden fierce heartbeat.

She couldn't entirely find a reason for it — something half-formed, not quite sudden.

But —

It shouldn't be.

"Next time they call you over there, refuse outright. Tell them I won't allow it."

It had been a long time with no reply. Xie Yuanjing looked back and found the girl lost in thought — wearing an expression of frustrated bewilderment at something she couldn't work out.

He watched her for a moment. That crease between her brows never eased, and she was only half-looking where she was going. He slowed his steps slightly.

The walkway led down to a few stone steps. Xie Yuanjing watched her lift her foot and find nothing but air, then watched those eyes go wide — her body beginning to pitch forward. He paused for one beat, and at the last moment reached out and caught her.

Once she was steady and the fear had set in, he let go and stood beside her.

"Lesson learned?"

They were very close. Xie Yuanjing could still feel the warmth coming from the slender curve of her waist.

Lu Huaixi's attention was not on the hand that had just released her. She only pressed a palm lightly to her chest and glanced over at him, the fading unease still in her eyes.

Below the steps was a gravel path. The stones had been smoothed and rounded, but they were still hard and unforgiving.

If she had really gone down, this face of hers would have taken the brunt of it — and her head would have fared no better.

"You were watching me the whole time?"

Lu Huaixi looked at him, tilting her head.

"Yes. Waiting to see you fall."

"Then you still reached out."

The muttered words carried the faintest thread of complaint — though she was also aware it was he who had caught her, and she wasn't truly aggrieved. "You could have warned me sooner."

Xie Yuanjing found it amusing.

"Almost fell because you weren't watching where you were going — and it becomes someone else's fault?"

Lu Huaixi lightly pressed her lips together. "I didn't say that."

Servants occasionally passed through this stretch of walkway. Catching sight of the Eldest Young Master and Eldest Young Mistress standing together — one tilting her head as she talked, the other looking down with patient attention — they were somewhat startled.

But startled as they were, no one dared to stare.

When Lu Huaixi saw yet another person bow and walk past, she grew a little self-conscious and collected herself.

"Let's go."

"Mm."

Xie Yuanjing replied, but didn't move. "What were you thinking about just now?"

"...Nothing."

"Can't say?"

Of course she couldn't.

Lu Huaixi looked away and spoke evasively. "Come on, let's go — I haven't even eaten noon meal yet, and I'm hungry."

Xie Yuanjing looked at her for a moment, the corner of his mouth curving slightly.

Then he reached out, knocked lightly on her head, and asked nothing more.

"Watch where you walk from now on."

"I know, I know."

—

Back at the Lu manor, it was only the second day after Lu Huaixi had married out, and the First Branch already felt noticeably quieter.

Lu Ningyou, the eldest young miss, was afraid her mother wouldn't adjust well and had come specially from her husband's household to keep her company, speaking in her gentle, careful way.

Whether her younger sister had ever had an engagement, she knew perfectly well. Lady Liu hadn't hidden it from her — but to spare her worry, she had left out the other details.

"Mother, Huaixi marrying is a happy occasion. You mustn't fret like this — besides, you know what that girl is like. She can be cheerful anywhere. Are you really afraid she'll suffer?"

True enough — and yet Lu Huaixi was still so young, and she'd only just recently come to know the man from the Xie family. Lu Ningyou worried all the same.

"And as for the scene Xie Yuanjing made yesterday — you wouldn't believe it, Mother. Even my in-laws, who never pay attention to gossip, were talking about him. They all said he must have truly set his heart on it."

Lady Liu's lips moved faintly, but she said nothing.

How could she tell her eldest daughter that her younger sister had married in name only — and would be separating after a year?

"Mother, please stop worrying. Meeting someone, going through the wedding — this is how it is for most girls. And Huaixi has a young master who is both of good family and handsome — what more could you ask? Besides, I could see for myself yesterday that Huaixi seemed quite at ease with him. They seem happy together."

"They seemed... happy?"

"Yes, Mother."

Lu Ningyou smiled. "Yesterday, that brother-in-law of mine went out of his way to speak to Huaixi — had her laughing several times. Everyone outside says he's difficult to read and hard to get along with, but I didn't find him that way at all — at least not around Huaixi."

"I hadn't seen any of that."

Lady Liu sighed — but those words did ease something in her.

She knew perfectly well that worrying was useless, and the child had already married. What she needed to do was be her daughter's dependable support.

But being a mother — and knowing that her daughter had been rushed into this marriage to escape the palace, only to face a separation afterward — Lady Liu felt a debt of guilt no matter how she thought about it.

"I do hope they get along well. But you know your sister — she only looks well-behaved on the surface, enough to fool people. In truth she's willful. And Xie Yuanjing is so cold with everyone else..."

"Relax, Mother. From what I can see, my brother-in-law treats Huaixi very well. Cold? Between those two, there will be warmth enough for many years yet."

"..."

Lady Liu felt more heartsick than ever.

The separation was always going to come. She had never believed that someone like Xie Yuanjing would change his mind, nor did she imagine the two families would remain kin-by-marriage indefinitely.

But Huaixi was still at that tender, impressionable age. She didn't know — if the girl spent too long with Xie Yuanjing — whether she might start to feel something more.

"Let it be. Their affairs are beyond what an outsider can touch. I only worry because the Marquis Manor isn't entirely calm."

"No family's inner household ever is — even our own Lu family —"

Something crossed Lu Ningyou's mind, and her expression turned cool.

"I never imagined the Second Branch mother and daughter could harbor such vicious intentions. Has Grandfather responded yet?"

At that, Lady Liu's expression also grew subdued.

The Old Master did feel grieved at the thought of Lu Huaixi going to the palace. He had made up his mind to protect her. But the Second Branch was also of the Lu family.

Learning that the First Branch would not yield, the Old Master had turned back to persuade them several times.

In truth, he didn't want to send any of his granddaughters.

Lady Liu understood his difficulty. But she would not concede — nor would she let her daughter have suffered all of this for nothing.

Her Huaixi should have had a few more peaceful years at home — time to choose slowly and carefully, until her heart was ready, and then let things unfold naturally.

Instead, all of it had been ruined by the Second Branch.

Not only had she been forced to marry so young, but she would carry the name of a separation afterward. No matter how Lady Liu thought of it, she couldn't swallow this.

"Regardless of whether your grandfather sends word — the Second Branch should not expect to quietly turn this page. It is impossible."

"I understand. If there's anything I can help with, Mother must tell me."

Lu Ningyou's eyes cooled, thinking of how a nanny had come to her yesterday to say that Lu Tangshu had apparently made an attempt to intercept Xie Yuanjing. She gave a cold smile.

Arrogance and recklessness through and through.

On that alone — regardless of whether Xie Yuanjing was a good match for Huaixi — Lu Tangshu would find no peace.

"All right — I've said all I needed to say. Take care of yourself. I worry about Huaixi, but I also think of you."

"Don't worry, Mother. My in-laws and husband treat me well."

"I can tell — they wouldn't keep agreeing to let you slip out if they weren't easygoing. Stay a little while and then head back — don't always be running around outside."

"No hurry. My husband is coming to fetch me after he finishes his duties."

At this, Lu Ningyou smiled, her expression softening considerably.

"It's only a shame that on Huaixi's return visit day I won't be able to come. Otherwise we could have had a long talk."

"You just stay home and rest properly."

Lady Liu glanced at Lu Ningyou's belly and shook her head with a soft sigh. "She listens to you. As her elder sister, you'd better set her a good example."

"Naturally."

Lu Ningyou blinked, thinking of the small box of books she had slipped privately to her younger sister, and couldn't help smiling again.

Their mother had said privately that Huaixi was still young, and that the Xie from the Xie Manor would not do anything to her.

But certain things — even if they came early — still needed to be taught.

chapters.title: Otherwise She'll Die of Rage
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi hadn't yet seen what her sister had sent over.

The moment she stepped back into the courtyard she caught a wonderfully tempting aroma, and when she walked inside she heard something bubbling away in a pot.

Summer had arrived early, and the days had grown warm.

But Xie Yuanjing liked coolness, and wherever there was a pot going in his rooms, there would always be a basin of ice beside it—so the air was not the least bit stifling.

Lu Huaixi was genuinely hungry.

Seeing the spread before her, she had no more room in her head for the thoughts she'd been turning over on the way back. She glanced at Xie Yuanjing, and at his nod found herself a seat.

"Are you eating too?"

She hadn't said what she wanted. What had been prepared was, most likely, arranged to Xie Yuanjing's taste.

But as it happened, she liked it too.

Still, courtesy required she ask.

"Didn't you say just now that you came back before finishing your midday meal?"

Xie Yuanjing held back a "I'm not hungry" and said nothing, only walked over and sat down beside her.

He was easy about meals at the best of times—he ate when he had a moment, forgot when he was busy. He had no particular understanding of what it was like to love food and eat well; that wasn't him. In his eyes, the ordinary small business of eating really wasn't worth singling out for special attention.

But when Lu Huaixi picked up her chopsticks, he glanced over anyway.

"It smells so good."

The person before him narrowed her eyes slightly, the corners of her mouth lifting high.

She said just that one thing, and then ate quietly, unhurried, as though she were engaged in something as refined as tasting tea or admiring flowers.

But she took bite after bite without stopping, absorbed in the food. When something was especially good, her long lashes would dip low, curving with the arc of her downward gaze.

Watching her, Xie Yuanjing found he'd worked up an appetite himself. He couldn't help eating some, and even had an extra bowl of soup.

—

Outside the courtyard, Mu Weiming—compelled to make another visit—was stopped at the gate.

She didn't know Xie Yuanjing had already returned to the household. She only wanted to see Lu Huaixi, needle her a little, then put on a show of apologising so the Old Madam would see it.

But she hadn't even gotten close before she was blocked.

"I'm here to see First Cousin's wife. By the Old Madam's instruction."

Mu Weiming pressed down her displeasure and raised her head, her tone sharper than usual.

Before, when Xie Yuanjing had told her not to enter, she had endured it and stayed out of sight.

She had been telling herself that he probably liked gentle, sensible women. Given time, once he saw how she felt about him, even the coldest person would warm a little.

But Xie Yuanjing never softened, and when he looked at her it wasn't even with cold indifference—he simply didn't bother looking at all.

Though Mu Weiming was growing impatient, she still didn't dare push too hard. He had no one at his side; she would always have her opportunity.

And then he had suddenly married, taking home a pampered noblewoman—and rather than spare her a glance, he had gone out on his wedding day to meet with colleagues.

Now that Mu Weiming had met Lu Huaixi in person and been put in her place right in front of the Old Madam, there was no more tolerance left in her.

"I know my cousin isn't in the household. I only need to see First Cousin's wife on a matter. If the Old Madam's errand is delayed, when my cousin returns, neither of us will be able to explain ourselves."

"The First Young Mistress is occupied at the moment and cannot receive visitors."

"Even occupied with the Old Madam's instructions?"

Mu Weiming kept her tone mild. Though she was holding down her resentment, reason still held.

Xie Yuanjing didn't care for the new bride, so she was sure he wouldn't have told Lu Huaixi about anything that had passed between them.

And as long as Lu Huaixi didn't know, she could say almost anything and plant discontent in her heart.

Once that seed took root and sprouted, the marriage would only grow more strained.

A man like Xie Yuanjing could never tolerate a spoiled, troublesome noblewoman in his inner household for long.

"You may send word in first. If First Cousin's wife is unwilling to see me, I'll go straight back to the Old Madam's side. I won't cause anyone trouble."

"Honoured Guest, please return."

The guard was unmoved by Mu Weiming's gentler approach—his manner, if anything, grew more resolute.

"The First Young Lord has given instructions: no disturbances while he and the First Young Mistress are taking their meal."

"What?"

Mu Weiming went still. "My cousin and Lu Huaixi—are having a meal together?"

Hearing her refer to the First Young Mistress by name, the guard's brow furrowed.

The First Young Lord had made it plain: the First Young Mistress was also the master of this house.

"Honoured Guest, you should address her as the First Young Mistress, as we do."

Blocked—and treated as though she were no different from a servant. The colour left Mu Weiming's face.

But she still forced a smile. She had no intention of making a scene at Xie Yuanjing's gate and undoing everything she had worked for.

"I spoke carelessly—I've grown so comfortable with First Cousin's wife that I forgot myself."

She paused, as if she couldn't quite believe it, and asked again. "Just now you said my cousin is having a meal with First Cousin's wife. But this morning I heard First Cousin's wife say my cousin had left the household to see a colleague. At this hour, he really shouldn't be here."

The guard could see perfectly well what she was angling for.

He had no intention of divulging the master's whereabouts to an outsider—and even less intention of discussing the master and young mistress's private affairs.

"Honoured Guest, please return."

The guard raised a hand, his expression cool and impatient.

"The First Young Lord once issued a clear instruction, which the Honoured Guest was present to hear. If the Honoured Guest insists on staying, it is her own face she puts at risk."

There was nothing more to be said. Mu Weiming abandoned all pretence.

She lifted her gaze over the guard's head and looked straight toward the courtyard ahead.

The path was clear. A few more steps and she could walk right in—and yet no matter how she applied herself, those few steps might as well have been a wall.

Mu Weiming gripped her handkerchief and turned away. Out of sight, the composure finally fell from her face entirely.

Xie Yuanjing was having a meal with Lu Huaixi?

It couldn't be. If they were truly that close, why had he gone out today at all?

While she was still turning it over, voices drifted from up ahead. Mu Weiming looked—and walked straight into the Fourth Miss, Xie Qinyin, returning from outside.

Xie Qinyin had caught the full brunt of whatever resentment and fury Mu Weiming hadn't managed to smooth away.

She glanced at the path Mu Weiming had come from, and let out a quiet, contemptuous sound.

"Some people still won't give it up—still making eyes at my First Brother."

"What is Fourth Miss saying? Weiming doesn't quite follow."

"I'm not the Old Madam, and I'm not the third branch. You don't have to put on a show in front of me."

Xie Qinyin spoke plainly, with no particular warmth.

The second branch had always been closer to the first branch. She had long resented the Old Madam's favouritism toward the third branch—and she had even less patience for the woman in front of her, who had gone along with the third branch in schemes against her, and had made moves against her First Brother.

"I've never been one to compare by status—but even setting status aside, you can't match my First Sister-in-law. And she's the woman my First Brother went to great lengths to bring home. The two of them are doing very well. I'm advising you—you'd best give up any crooked ideas."

"Fourth Cousin, you've misunderstood me."

Mu Weiming had a belly full of fire with nowhere to put it.

She was already unsettled from what had just happened. Hearing Xie Qinyin take Lu Huaixi's side so openly, she couldn't be bothered keeping up appearances any longer.

The woman he went to great lengths to bring home. As if.

It was plainly a noblewoman he'd had to marry for the greater good—how good could the two of them possibly be?

"Fourth Cousin had best not rush to conclusions. Whether those two are doing well—that remains to be seen."

"Would you dare say that to my First Brother's face?"

Mu Weiming's lips moved. The next moment she heard: "If you dare, I'll take you to him right now. I'd let you stand in front of First Sister-in-law and say it myself."

Xie Qinyin finished with a cold, dismissive look and walked off toward her own courtyard.

Based on Mu Weiming's presumptuous display just now, she was absolutely going straight to her First Brother to report her.

Did Mu Weiming really think living in the marquis' household a few years gave her the standing to compare herself to her new sister-in-law?

"Miss—she is still someone the Old Madam keeps close. Why bother lowering yourself to her level?"

The personal maidservant stepped forward once the figure had gone. "If she says something to the Old Madam, she might punish you in return."

"Am I afraid of her? Besides, she was speaking about First Sister-in-law. If anything comes of it, First Brother is right there to handle it."

"The Miss is naturally not afraid of a courtesy cousin. But she only said a few words—even if the First Young Lord hears of it, it's not really something he can step into. Inner household matters are inner household matters."

"That's not necessarily true."

Xie Qinyin thought of the news she had heard from her mother that morning, and suddenly laughed.

"My First Brother is doing very well by First Sister-in-law right now. I heard from Mother that this very morning he put the entire household in her hands. I almost said it just now—I held back. Otherwise it would have killed Mu Weiming with envy."

chapters.title: I Talk in My Sleep?
chapters.content:
Back in the courtyard, Lu Huaixi knew nothing of what had happened outside. She had eaten until she was full—considerably more than she'd had the night before.

She got up afterward to wash and wipe her hands, and when she turned back around she noticed a food box sitting to one side.

"What else is in here?"

The sweet cakes had only ever been meant as something to nibble on for fun. Since she'd had a proper midday meal, there was no real reason to bring out the small things.

Xie Yuanjing was about to have someone take it away when he looked up and saw that the now-satisfied diner had already lifted the lid.

In a moment, her eyes widened a little—visibly surprised. And then the next instant those rounded eyes curved upward into a smile.

"Oh, there are sweet cakes—and they're exactly the ones I like most."

The words Xie Yuanjing had been about to say died in his mouth.

He watched her freshly washed hand reach in and pull out a piece of cake, then pause in mid-air, the look in her eyes careful and uncertain as she glanced over at him.

Rather than get up, he simply leaned back against the chair and unhurriedly wiped his fingertips with a cloth, meeting her gaze.

"Are these for me to eat?"

The question came out smaller than her usual speaking voice, as though she wasn't quite certain.

But her eyes were saying yes, yes, definitely yes.

Xie Yuanjing had rarely encountered anyone quite so entertaining. He was long accustomed to not sparing people's feelings—there were few enough people who smiled at him to begin with.

"What if they weren't?"

"If they weren't..."

Lu Huaixi looked down at the thing in her hand.

She had already taken it out—her fingerprints were already on it.

"If they weren't, I'd have someone go and buy another box to replace them for you."

Xie Yuanjing laughed. He genuinely hadn't expected that even if they weren't for her, she still had no intention of being polite.

"They're only some cakes—no need to replace anything."

He put down the cloth. "Didn't you just say you were full?"

"I can still manage a little more."

Lu Huaixi looked over at him, then caught herself. "So these are for me to eat, then."

Her tone was certain.

Without waiting for a reply, she ate the piece in her hand.

Lu Huaixi was pleased. Seeing that Xie Yuanjing was done teasing her, she pulled out the contents one by one and settled back down beside him.

"You have such a good eye for these things—they're exactly what I love to eat most."

She paused, finishing what was in her mouth in quiet, before adding: "Are you eating any now, or later? Should I leave you half?"

Lu Huaixi had a habit of not speaking while eating.

First Madam Lu had raised her well—her manners were impeccable in every respect. But in private, without outsiders present, a small thread of easy carelessness still crept in.

Though even that carelessness stayed within bounds.

When she ate these cakes, for example, she didn't bite off small pieces. She would hold a whole piece lightly between her fingertips, bring it carefully to her lips, close her mouth, and chew slowly.

Throughout, her expression stayed calm and composed, all her attention on what was in her mouth. Her eyes didn't wander.

Xie Yuanjing watched her profile, and found himself thinking that no flower and no view could compare to the simple pleasure of sitting here watching Lu Huaixi eat.

When he still hadn't answered, Lu Huaixi finished and asked again.

"Are you eating or not?"

"Not eating. Don't save any."

Xie Yuanjing came back to himself, shaking his head with a slight smile. "But don't eat too many."

"I won't eat too many. I'll save half for later."

"You really like them that much?"

"I do. I just didn't expect you to like them too."

Lu Huaixi had naturally assumed he must like them too, since he'd bought them. Xie Yuanjing didn't explain.

"When you were at home, who used to buy these for you?"

"My brother, mostly."

Lu Huaixi thought back. "Sometimes I'd have my brother get them, sometimes I'd ask the household kitchen. Father found me a pastry chef—someone who specialises in confections and small bites. Quite good, actually. I'll have to bring you by to try some."

Outside, Gong Zhuo happened to have something to report. Catching Lu Huaixi's last words, he couldn't resist glancing into the room.

He caught the faint, barely-there curve at the corner of his master's mouth, and understood enough to keep the deference in his voice while allowing himself a small smile.

"Young Mistress—the master doesn't care for sweet things."

"He doesn't care for sweet things?"

Lu Huaixi looked over, then raised a hand and pointed at the things on the table. "Then what about all of this?"

Seeing that the master had no intention of stopping him, Gong Zhuo continued. "These were bought specially for the Young Mistress."

Lu Huaixi went quiet for a moment.

Xie Yuanjing didn't probe into why she had suddenly stopped talking. He only gestured for Gong Zhuo to continue his report.

Perhaps because something serious was being discussed, the atmosphere in the room had grown considerably more solemn. Lu Huaixi ate one more piece, then rose and wiped her hands again, settling quietly to one side without interrupting.

It was only after Gong Zhuo finished and withdrew that Xie Yuanjing pressed his fingertips to the bridge of his nose, composing himself, and rose to head toward the study.

"I'll be back shortly."

"Oh."

Lu Huaixi nodded, but she wasn't someone who could hold back questions for long. She waited a moment, then asked: "How did you know I liked these things?"

Xie Yuanjing's step paused. Then he turned and walked back toward her.

He was very tall. When he stood and looked down at Lu Huaixi, his shadow fell and covered her completely.

Hearing her ask, he couldn't help recalling the restless sounds she had made in her sleep the night before.

"You told me yourself."

"I told you? When did I say that?"

"Last night. In your sleep."

After he said it he watched her for a moment, and seeing she didn't believe him, repeated back to her exactly what he had heard.

Only when he saw her close her mouth and concede defeat did Xie Yuanjing stop, giving a quiet laugh.

He didn't say anything more. He left the rest for her to turn over on her own—only when he reached the doorway did his step pause again.

"Go and select a few cooks."

Gong Fei outside startled. Cooks?

"Match the standard of the Lu household's pastry chef. Whatever they have there, I want the same here."

Hearing that, Lu Huaixi's lips pressed together even more firmly.

She watched the retreating figure, blinking, her long lashes trembling one beat after another.

The thoughts she had been turning over since returning to the courtyard surfaced again—not unwelcome, not agitating, just like willow branches by the river, swaying back and forth and tickling at something she couldn't quite name.

Unable to make sense of it, she called for Yaoshu.

"Do I really talk in my sleep?"

Yaoshu thought for a moment, then nodded. "Occasionally."

—

Lu Ningyu's things arrived just as Lu Huaixi was listening to Yaoshu recount Mu Weiming's earlier visit.

She accepted the wooden box without any rush to open it.

"I just forgot to ask."

"What did the First Young Mistress want to ask?"

Yaoshu lightly rubbed her mistress's shoulders. "About that courtesy cousin?"

"Not entirely."

Lu Huaixi closed her eyes.

She had forgotten to ask Xie Yuanjing what his feelings were toward Mu Weiming.

She needed to know first—then she could decide whether to place the woman on the side of rival, acquaintance, or irrelevant stranger.

Though if she turned out to be on the friendly side...

Recalling the roundabout way that woman had gone about things, Lu Huaixi felt a flicker of annoyance.

She didn't like dealing with people like that. If Xie Yuanjing happened to care for her, then she would have to weigh whether to keep her distance from him as well.

Nothing mattered more than her own peace of mind.

That thought settled, Lu Huaixi pulled her attention back and absently opened the wooden box.

She glanced down at what was inside—and immediately went still, then lowered the lid again.

chapters.title: Do You Have Someone You Like?
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi had been remarkably well-behaved these past two days—keeping so quiet that if Xie Yuanjing didn't speak to her first, she could go entire stretches without making a sound.

Occasionally she was called to Lady Xie's courtyard to learn about managing the household affairs, or invited by Xie Qinyin to the second branch. The rest of the time she simply worked through her own thoughts.

At night she needed no urging to sleep. While the sky was still light she would have herself tidied up and climb into bed, pull the thin quilt up to cover half her face, and lie straight as a ruler with both hands properly at her sides.

On the third evening, Xie Yuanjing came in from outside.

After changing his clothes he came to find her, and found her lying with her eyes closed as if she were asleep—except for the long lashes, which kept trembling.

He stopped a short distance from the bed, looking down at her in silence.

The shadow he cast fell across Lu Huaixi, as if deliberately making itself known.

After a good while, seeing that she was almost unable to keep up the pretence, Xie Yuanjing spoke without urgency.

"Asleep?"

"...Nearly."

Lu Huaixi opened her eyes and turned her head slightly to one side.

A small face half-hidden—and the eyes above it all the more lively for it, not the slightest trace of sleepiness in them.

"All right. Then sleep."

Xie Yuanjing didn't press her about anything. He gave a nod and turned to leave—and left her behind, curiosity suddenly stirred with nowhere to go.

Lu Huaixi said nothing at first, only blinked, watching the person who had just arrived walk back out.

But how could she stand it?

She was not the well-behaved creature she appeared to be. And she was insatiably curious.

Seeing Xie Yuanjing open things up and then say nothing, she tossed and turned in bed for quite some time before finally throwing back the quilt, folding her legs, and sitting up.

Her inner robe was thick and modest, her dark hair loose down her back, a few strands swaying with the movement and settling against her cheek.

"Xie Yuanjing."

She called to him.

Unwilling to put on shoes and socks, she stayed put.

The man outside had already picked up a ledger and begun flipping through it. Hearing her call, he didn't move—his gaze stayed on the pages.

Lu Huaixi raised her voice slightly.

In the outer room, Jing Shuang and Yaoshu exchanged a glance.

Lu Huaixi's quietness these past two days had been so pronounced that Yaoshu was half-sick with worry, convinced the two of them had quarrelled.

But when she saw them together they seemed entirely at ease—even in silence there was an inexplicable warmth between them.

There was still no response from inside.

Yaoshu looked at Jing Shuang again; the latter shook her head slightly.

Both masters were inside. Without instructions, there was no reason for them to enter.

Lu Huaixi called out three times in total. It was only on the third call that Xie Yuanjing set down what he was holding and rose.

And on the table behind him, the ledger—which had had enough pages to keep him reading for quite a while—had not turned a single page since Lu Huaixi first called out. It had stayed exactly where it was.

"What is it?"

Xie Yuanjing walked in.

He found her sitting in the middle of the bed, dark hair loose and draped carelessly, eyes bright and curious. His own expression stayed calm, the deep dark of his pupils giving nothing away.

"What were you going to say to me just now?"

Seeing him finally come in, Lu Huaixi leaned forward slightly. "Tell me, tell me."

"Not sleeping?"

"I'll sleep in a bit."

Xie Yuanjing looked down at her for a moment, then unexpectedly said: "What have you been doing these past two days?"

"Why are you asking me that?"

The person on the bed looked puzzled. "You've barely left the household yourself these past two days, have you?"

Most of where she'd gone and what she'd done, he would already know.

After hearing that, Xie Yuanjing was silent for another stretch—long enough that even Lu Huaixi began to feel uneasy, racking her memory for whether she'd done anything she shouldn't have.

But there was truly nothing. She had barely even felt like looking at other people. When would she have had the heart to cause him any trouble?

Just as she was starting to drum her fingers inwardly, the silence finally broke.

"Understood."

"...Understood, and now tell me what you came in to say."

She paused and checked his face to make sure there was no displeasure there before continuing: "Also, you still haven't told me properly about the people in the household. Apart from the second branch, who else is on your side?"

"Is that me not telling you, or you not intending to listen?"

"I never didn't..."

Well—perhaps she hadn't been intending to listen.

These past two days Lu Huaixi had barely surfaced from her own head. On one side, those sent-over items had her flustered and anxious beyond words. On the other, Mu Weiming had her thinking through how to handle things with Xie Yuanjing.

"Then tell me now. I'll listen to everything at once."

She said it and pulled the thin quilt up over her legs. "I'm not sleepy anymore."

Xie Yuanjing didn't call out her claim of not being sleepy when she clearly hadn't wanted to sleep in the first place. He lowered his head slightly, his cool eyes catching her reflection.

"Actually, there's not much to explain. There's no one truly on my side."

He said: "Among the people you've met—it's only a matter of not yet enemies and not worth thinking about."

Xie Yuanjing never spoke in absolutes. What he left unsaid wasn't a safety net—it was allowance for human nature.

He had never said these things to anyone before. Talk of who was on whose side had a slightly naive ring to it.

But Lu Huaixi didn't know that. She only felt that when Xie Yuanjing said there was no one on his side, he sounded a little pitiable.

"How can there be no one on your side? Isn't your mother? And now there's me. I'm on your side too."

She furrowed her brow. "If I'm on your side, then my family certainly is too."

The candles had been lit early, burning bright. Occasionally a gust found the gap in the not-quite-closed window and stirred the wicks, one gentle pulse after another.

This room of Xie Yuanjing's rarely saw outsiders. He didn't allow it.

The inner room in particular had never been entered by anyone else. Even his mother, since he was seven years old, had no longer come inside.

Beyond that, there had been his younger brother.

His brother had always been warm toward him—whatever was good, his brother would want to bring it straight to him, obedient and gentle.

But then his brother was gone, and no one else had ever entered this room again.

He didn't welcome it. Others didn't feel at ease.

Lu Huaixi was the only one who had ever been comfortable staying here, and who slept soundly under this roof.

"Is that so. I hadn't noticed."

When he spoke again, Xie Yuanjing's voice had gone slightly rough—enough to make Lu Huaixi blink.

"On my side, and still withholding things instead of speaking?"

"...I didn't."

Lu Huaixi gripped the bedding and lowered her head.

Seeing her once again take on that earnest, pitiful look of someone waiting to be scolded, Xie Yuanjing said nothing more.

He watched her for a long moment, then finally gave a quiet sound.

"If there's nothing, then there's nothing."

He walked over and sat down nearby. "I came in just now to ask whether you'd looked at the return visit gift list for tomorrow."

"The gift list?" Lu Huaixi nodded at once. "I went through it yesterday."

"Not that one—I added a few things to the end. If anything seems off, there's still time to change it."

Xie Yuanjing's attentiveness never failed to catch Lu Huaixi off guard.

She found herself realising that in this entire marriage, beyond the first bewildering stretch, this man had every time he appeared left her with something steadying.

Even here in this strange and complicated marquis' household, he made her feel safe.

"I haven't looked at it yet—but you don't need to let me look."

She smiled, eyes curving warmly. "You decide."

That night, Lu Huaixi and Xie Yuanjing talked for a long time.

Beyond the first few serious exchanges, what followed was mostly Lu Huaixi pulling him along, as if trying to make up for all the quiet she'd kept over the past two days.

Xie Yuanjing was a man of few words, his expression always calm. But he would answer her now and then, and when she got too carried away he would reach in and rein her back.

In the end Lu Huaixi wasn't sure when drowsiness caught up with her.

When she was drowsy, her mind didn't want to think. Things she might otherwise have kept to herself became harder to hold in.

She saw Xie Yuanjing come over and tell her to sleep, and after a moment's quiet reach out and tuck the thin quilt more firmly around her. Lu Huaixi, half in a haze, called out to stop him.

"Xie Yuanjing."

"Mm? What is it?"

The man had just straightened up, backlit, looking down at her from the side of the bed.

Lu Huaixi couldn't make out his expression, but hearing the voice he had deliberately made softer, she felt her guard slip away entirely.

"Do you have a girl you like?"

Her eyes had already drifted shut with drowsiness. "Do you like Mu Weiming?"

chapters.title: His Kindness Was Not For Her
chapters.content:
When Lu Huaixi opened her eyes again, the sky outside was bright, and the daybed beside her was empty.

She sat up, foggy with sleep, lashes still dewy.

Her head felt thick. She couldn't string two thoughts together—only once she had finished getting ready did fragments of the night before finally come back to her.

She had apparently gone ahead and asked Xie Yuanjing outright—not only about his feelings toward that courtesy cousin, but whether he had someone he liked at all.

Lu Huaixi was startled by herself. She hadn't expected that when relaxed she could be this completely unguarded with her words.

"First Young Mistress, the carriage is ready."

Jing Shuang's voice cut through her thoughts, and she pulled herself upright.

Her cheeks felt warm—belated mortification and embarrassment settling in.

What had she been thinking, going off and asking whether he had someone he liked? Asking about Mu Weiming would have been enough. She didn't need to know whether he liked anyone else besides.

Lu Huaixi walked out, brow lightly creased.

Though—how had Xie Yuanjing answered her?

He seemed to have been quiet for a moment, as if genuinely thinking it over. And then, just as she had been about to fall asleep, he had said: no.

He had no girl he liked. He had never given it any thought.

In other words—he had no interest in matters of the heart.

Someone was waiting beside the carriage. It was Xie Yuanjing.

His expression was as composed as always—dark eyes calm as a deep pool.

When Lu Huaixi met his gaze a moment of discomfort passed through her, but Xie Yuanjing seemed not to notice. He watched her walk toward him, then stepped up into the carriage before her and turned, extending a hand.

He helped her up with an easy pull, then immediately let go.

"Haven't had breakfast?"

"Mm, there wasn't time."

Lu Huaixi ducked her head to climb into the carriage.

The curtain lifted, and a faint fragrance floated from inside.

She looked in—saw small cakes and pastries arranged inside—and once again couldn't help turning to look at him.

"Come in first."

Xie Yuanjing's tone was as even as ever. But catching her surprised look, he gave a quiet laugh.

"Children tend to sleep in. I thought it likely you'd have had no time to eat."

"..."

Outside were maidservants and guards. Lu Huaixi's mouth moved slightly, but she decided against arguing over who was a child.

She settled herself and then, unable to resist, glanced at Xie Yuanjing again.

His hand was resting loosely against the carriage curtain on one side—knuckles curved, fingertips beautiful, obviously long-fingered hands with an easy strength about them.

At that moment he was looking sideways, saying something quiet and low to a guard who had just come over, his voice dropping into a tone that carried a faint weight of authority.

Before long he came inside and sat down opposite her.

"Why aren't you eating? Those are the ones you like."

Xie Yuanjing glanced at the untouched cakes. "Still half asleep?"

Lu Huaixi came back to herself and shook her head, picking up a small piece and putting it in her mouth.

Beside the cakes sat a steaming flat-baked bread, still warm from the griddle.

Two days ago she had been talking with Yaoshu about Shun'an Lane and had happened to mention the griddle-bread stall on the next street over—idly, just in passing. She hadn't thought that in less than two days, this would arrive.

"You're so thoughtful and attentive."

She paused, then added: "My brother would never put food in the carriage for me. He'd say he hadn't eaten either and we should both endure it together."

Xie Yuanjing didn't reply at first. Only when she had finished the second piece did he say quietly: "It's as it should be."

As it should be.

Lu Huaixi suddenly felt a little too full.

While eating, she didn't speak—so for the third piece, she didn't take another cake but instead reached for the griddle bread, which was slightly larger.

Not because she was hungry—just for an excuse to be quiet.

When she thought about it, she and Xie Yuanjing hadn't spent that much time together. But looking back, every time this person appeared he had left behind something she found hard to forget.

Sometimes it was something he said—the kind of thing that settled a person's nerves. Sometimes it was something he sent—always exactly right. Sometimes it was a small object. Sometimes it was something he did.

He always found a way to leave his mark in her heart—never abrupt, never rushed.

Many people said Xie Yuanjing was hard to read, difficult to get close to, nearly impossible to befriend deeply.

At first Lu Huaixi hadn't thought so, because Xie Yuanjing had been good to her.

But now she thought she might have been wrong.

Xie Yuanjing wasn't being good to Lu Huaixi. Xie Yuanjing was being good to the person who held the title of his wife.

Whether that wife's surname was Lu or anything else—that was outside the scope of what he cared about.

The griddle bread took a long time to finish. Afterward, Lu Huaixi didn't eat anything more.

She took out her handkerchief and wiped her hands—slowly, carefully, one small section at a time.

After a while, the carriage slowed, turned slightly to one side, and stopped.

When the curtain lifted, she saw the familiar estate before her.

The strange emotion from a moment ago dissolved. Lu Huaixi, having sorted her thoughts, looked out at the sight and smiled, eyes curving.

This was what she should be thinking about. This was the home she had briefly left and would come back to.

Before she rose, she looked back at Xie Yuanjing across from her, those dark eyes smiling into a beautiful arc. "Let me tell you a secret."

"What?"

Xie Yuanjing, catching her high spirits, found his own expression soften without quite meaning to.

"Your household's cooks aren't as good as mine."

Lu Huaixi said it, then laughed to herself for a moment—and when her mother's voice drifted in from outside, she rose before Xie Yuanjing and jumped down from the carriage without thinking twice about propriety.

She didn't see the expression on Xie Yuanjing's face behind her, and didn't bother with rules or decorum.

"Mother!"

Lady Liu came forward to meet her, with Lu Yuanzhao close beside.

Lu Yandao was further back, accompanying the Old Master.

The whole family had come out to welcome her home—a genuine, wholehearted welcome.

"Didn't Brother-in-law come with you?"

Seeing only his sister, Lu Yuanzhao couldn't help frowning, speaking first.

He had always been a little wary of Xie Yuanjing, turning things over carefully before every interaction with him.

But now things were different—wary as he still was, that old fox had married his sister, and on a day this significant there was no sign of the man. He was too anxious to care about anything else.

"How could he just let you—"

"Mother-in-law."

A voice came from inside the carriage, cutting his words off.

Lu Yuanzhao closed his mouth at once, then shot a look at his sister.

Lu Huaixi's expression was the picture of innocence.

It wasn't that she hadn't said anything—her brother's mouth had simply been too fast.

Xie Yuanjing stepped down from the carriage and stopped just behind Lu Huaixi's shoulder, the two of them standing very close, close enough that Lu Huaixi could feel the left side of her back brush against his chest.

"Brother."

Xie Yuanjing looked at Lu Yuanzhao and addressed him naturally, with an ease that made Lu Yuanzhao startle back a step in spite of himself, nearly losing composure.

"We were tidying up the food box in the carriage—it took a moment."

"Tidying the food box?"

Lady Liu was surprised. "You came over without breakfast?"

"Huaixi hadn't eaten. I had someone prepare a few things for her."

Lady Liu looked back at her daughter, lips moving as if there was something she wanted to say—then didn't.

chapters.title: Do You Have What It Takes
chapters.content:
Return visits were always a significant occasion.

Few people in the Lu household knew the real circumstances of this marriage. What they knew was that the pampered, cherished daughter of the family had married the eldest young lord of the marquis' household, and that both the procession to take her away and the procession bringing her back had been impressively grand.

The Lu Old Master himself had come out to receive them. Lu Huaixi walked at Xie Yuanjing's side, appearing perfectly composed, though in truth her mind had already drifted off somewhere else entirely.

Lost in thought, she didn't watch her step crossing the gate's threshold and stumbled.

A steadying pressure came immediately to her waist, warm and firm through the thin fabric of her dress.

"Not watching the road again?"

His voice was very low, the words dropping into her ear in a single breath.

He didn't seem to be waiting for Lu Huaixi to respond. He spoke and then looked straight back toward Old Master Lu, continuing their conversation.

But that hand didn't draw back. Even once he knew she had steadied herself, he kept the light hold there, and guided her along the rest of that stretch of path.

Lu Huaixi instinctively looked up and caught the clean, precise line of Xie Yuanjing's profile.

He had been listening to people talk ever since they arrived, giving the occasional reply, his gaze never coming this way.

Lu Huaixi had assumed he wouldn't notice what was happening on her side—but somehow he seemed keenly aware of her every move.

She was just about to pull her attention back when the corner of her eye caught a glance coming from behind—from the second branch, Lu Tangshu.

She pressed down whatever was in her chest and looked back openly.

It wasn't quite a provocation—just a calm, easy smile in that direction, and because of where she was standing, the look even came with a slight tilt of her head.

Lu Tangshu's expression darkened a shade.

But before she could react, she watched Lu Huaixi look away—and the hand resting at her waist seemed to tighten, just slightly, as if reminding her to watch the road.

A wave of bitter resentment rose, and the harder she tried to suppress it, the more she found herself staring.

Then someone moved to block her view.

Only once they reached the front hall did Xie Yuanjing finally withdraw his hand.

"You go and keep your mother company for now. I'll come find you later."

"Right—my brother doesn't know about our arrangement."

Not sure whether Xie Yuanjing was aware, Lu Huaixi mentioned it.

Her intent was to tell him that if her brother actually scolded him as a real brother-in-law, it would at least be understandable.

But Xie Yuanjing—whether or not he fully understood—only gave a quiet laugh after she finished.

"Mind yourself. Learn to watch the road."

"..."

Just then, the Second Madam Luo Yue-hui arrived with Lu Tangshu, calling Lu Huaixi's name in greeting.

This time the woman's manner was nothing like the lofty-elder posture she had maintained back at the household. Seeing Lu Huaixi now, her tone had softened considerably, and she expressed concern for Lu Huaixi's daily comforts.

"Since you left, Second Aunt has found the house so quiet. I've been thinking of you. A few days ago when I went out with the other ladies I spotted some gowns and a set of jewellery, and thought they'd suit you perfectly. I'll have someone send them over later."

Lu Huaixi had rarely seen the second branch spend money on her—it was a genuinely unusual sight.

But she immediately thought of the Flower and Bird Envoy's list. The smile in her eyes grew a shade thinner—though her eyes were still curved.

Whatever was offered to her lips, she had no reason to refuse.

"How kind of Second Aunt. I don't think I've ever received a gift from you outside of the New Year's, Second Aunt."

Lady Luo's expression grew slightly uncomfortable. Feeling Xie Yuanjing's gaze settle on her too, she gave an awkward little laugh and excused herself to go speak with Lady Liu.

Plainly she was lowering herself for a reason—most likely she had something to ask.

Lu Huaixi noted it and looked away. After all, Lu Tangshu was still standing right beside her.

"Second Sister."

Lu Tangshu called out, then turned to look at Xie Yuanjing. "Second Brother-in-law."

Xie Yuanjing gave a mild sound of acknowledgment, not looking at her. He only stepped forward and reached up to brush a few loose strands of hair back from Lu Huaixi's cheek—the kind of small, practiced gesture that looked entirely natural, as though he'd done it countless times.

"Your mother is still waiting. Go talk with her."

"All right."

"Don't eat too many cakes—you won't have room for the midday meal."

Xie Yuanjing reminded her quietly, casting about mentally for the sorts of things a person might say before parting with a child.

Lu Tangshu watched it all, jealousy pricking at her, until she could hold back no longer.

"Second Brother-in-law really does take such good care of Second Sister."

She looked at Lu Huaixi's smooth, glowing face—the picture of someone who had been well looked after—and thought of the name on the list that still couldn't be erased, hanging over her head like a blade. She forgot every instruction her mother had given her and began to speak without thinking.

"You and Second Sister really were meant for each other. If things had gone a little later—Second Sister might have ended up going to the palace. As things stand, Second Sister has simply left the whole mess behind without a thought for any of the other sisters at home."

She stopped, then lowered her eyes.

"Though—well, never mind. We're all family... Second Brother-in-law may not know, but our Second Sister has always had many admirers. Right after she came of age, the Lu household's threshold was practically worn down—so many people inquiring after our Second Sister."

"Is that so."

Seeing Xie Yuanjing respond, Lu Tangshu couldn't help herself.

If Lu Huaixi was capable of this kind of selfish act, what was wrong with saying a few things to vent?

"Oh yes, Second Brother-in-law—every time Second Sister went out, people would find ways to speak with her, and Second Sister is so warm-natured—no matter whose young lord came to her, she would smile pleasantly and never be unkind."

Back when Xie Yuanjing had given that mild response, Lu Huaixi's brow had furrowed slightly.

Lu Tangshu was very obviously implying she had been inappropriately close to people—a vicious thing to say. If this had truly been her husband, he'd have formed resentment toward her by now.

But Lu Huaixi didn't open her mouth.

She trusted Xie Yuanjing.

She thought: he had picked up the thread, so he would deal with it. There was no need for her to respond.

While she was still thinking this, Xie Yuanjing quietly took hold of her fingertips and gave them a light squeeze—a small comfort.

She looked over instinctively—and looked up straight into those deep dark eyes, carrying something tender and indulgent, the corner of his mouth curving into a faint smile.

"My wife is exceptional—and to have been able to settle things with her so early was the great fortune of one Xie Yuanjing."

She knew he was making it up. But watching the seriousness of his expression, Lu Huaixi's heart stopped for a full beat.

She really was hopeless. She shook her head at herself inwardly.

"...Second Brother-in-law really does value Second Sister."

Lu Tangshu was struggling to believe it. She stared at the man, trying to find some trace of displeasure in him from those words.

But the man everyone called untouchably cold was at this moment standing at Lu Huaixi's side in a posture of unmistakable intimacy—holding her hand, speaking with her, voice low and warm.

Lu Tangshu still wanted to say more.

One more thing—like how this woman had been destined for the palace. Or how selfish she was, learning she was on the list and not caring about anyone else, dragging the rest of the family down with her.

But before she could open her mouth, Xie Yuanjing glanced over at her. The moment his gaze left Lu Huaixi it turned deep and cold—glacial.

Even with the faint smile still at the corner of his mouth, that smile had gone cold too.

Something between mockery and warning, his voice dropping low.

"Knowing I value her, don't think any crooked thoughts. She was your Second Sister before—I had no ground to interfere in the sisters' relationship. But now she is more than just your Second Sister."

Xie Yuanjing rarely said this many words to an outsider.

But what landed in Lu Tangshu's ears left no room for even a flicker of delight.

"Now she is also the First Young Mistress of the Xie household. The Third Miss of the Lu family had best think carefully before she opens her mouth—whether she has what it takes to make her suffer—"

chapters.title: My Wife's Account—I'll Settle It With You Slowly
chapters.content:
The last trace of expression left Xie Yuanjing's face. His bearing was cold and imperious, a flicker of danger glinting in his brow—yet his voice remained perfectly measured, each word delivered without haste, his manner as unruffled as someone discussing the weather.

"And—the matter of the attempt to send her to the palace. I will settle that account with you slowly."

Lu Tangshu went white.

Perhaps she had not expected Xie Yuanjing to name it outright, or had not expected him to stand up for Lu Huaixi this firmly.

For a moment she couldn't produce a single word. Only then did the fear and dread rush in all at once.

There was no one beside her, and even if there had been, no one would have dared come to her aid.

In her panic, Lu Tangshu looked toward Lu Huaixi, pleading—every trace of the resentment she had been harbouring moments ago gone, only naked desperation in her eyes.

"Second Sister, there's been a misunderstanding—please help me. Let me explain..."

Lu Huaixi didn't respond.

She had felt a flash of surprise when Xie Yuanjing openly raised the matter of the palace. But she steadied herself almost immediately.

They were on the same side. If she showed any reaction now, the second branch would read a hundred things into it.

And she had no intention of going soft on Lu Tangshu.

The one who broke the standstill was Old Master Lu, not far away.

After issuing a few instructions, he looked back and saw that Xie Yuanjing was still speaking with his granddaughter. He raised his hand and beckoned.

"Yuanjing, come have tea."

Old Master Lu appeared to have grown genuinely fond of Xie Yuanjing.

What had begun as cautious probing had since shifted into evident regard—warmth visibly more natural than before.

Xie Yuanjing gave a response and then, without any particular effort at concealment, let out a quiet laugh.

It looked like a man sharing a private jest—but the words that followed gave no one face at all.

"Old Master, the quality of education for the young ladies in this household leaves quite a lot to be desired."

Lady Luo was still deep in conversation with Lady Liu and hadn't noticed.

Old Master Lu's gaze rested on Lu Tangshu for a moment, then shifted away without expression—his face changing slightly, though he remained as steady and immovable as ever.

"The girls are young and thoughtless. Put a few of them together and they'll say things they shouldn't. If any offence has been given, I hope Yuanjing will overlook it for Huaixi's sake."

With that, the Old Master looked back toward the side and let his tone carry a note of edge. "Tangshu—go back to your own courtyard!"

Xie Yuanjing said nothing more, but the set of his expression didn't improve.

The Old Master's words had signalled something.

Huaixi was his blood granddaughter. So was the second branch. On a day like this, discretion called for things to be smoothed over.

"Today is a return visit day. In the ordinary way of things, this sort of thing should be set aside and laughed off. But when it concerns my wife, some things can be let go—and some cannot."

Xie Yuanjing had put his displeasure plainly on the table, without dismantling the Old Master's intent—but he had also made his own position clear.

"Whatever grievance my wife has suffered in the past—simply moving past it is not an option."

Lu Yandao, standing to one side, had not opened his mouth until now. But he pressed his brow, then smoothed it, and the look he turned on Xie Yuanjing deepened with meaning.

This wasn't about Lu Tangshu's provocation just now. This was a statement—that the second branch of the Lu family scheming to send Lu Huaixi to the palace would not simply be forgotten.

Xie Yuanjing didn't concern himself with anyone else's reaction.

Having spoken, he looked back at Lu Huaixi, who had been quiet for some time, and let the sharpness ease. The corner of his mouth curved slightly, as though he had entirely forgotten he had just been issuing a warning.

"All right. Go and play."

He squeezed her fingertips once more. "Your mother has been waiting a while."

—

In the back courtyard, Lu Huaixi's room was exactly as it had always been.

Three days really wasn't long enough. Short enough that when Lu Huaixi walked in, she was momentarily confused—as if she wasn't entirely sure whether she'd actually left.

Lady Liu sat down at the front of the room.

She hadn't caught everything that had just happened, but the words Xie Yuanjing had spoken she had heard clearly enough.

Having him take this kind of stand eased the weight that had been sitting in Lady Liu's chest over these three days.

"Just now he came out and said what he said plainly—it means he intends to take the matter in hand and stand up for you. Your father had been worried he might only concern himself with the marriage itself. Now that he's shown his hand, your father and he will likely have considerably more dealings ahead."

Lu Huaixi came back to herself from Xie Yuanjing's defense of her a moment ago, took a beat, then nodded.

It was genuine sincerity—the kind that concerned both families.

She gave a sound of acknowledgment but didn't much feel like saying more.

"Let's not talk about that for now, Mother. Is the second branch asking something of you?"

She steadied her thoughts, set aside what she'd been turning over, and remembered the second Madam's manner toward her today, and the Old Master's reaction. Her brow furrowed slightly.

"Is it about the palace list?"

"Yes, it is."

Lady Liu didn't hide it. She knew her daughter cared about this matter—and she knew that for all the appearance of composure, this girl was not someone who simply bore a grievance in silence.

"The name can't be removed from the list. But Lu Tangshu refuses to go to the palace. Lady Luo doesn't dare make a scene with me directly, so she went to your grandfather first and then through him."

"So Grandfather is also reluctant to send her."

Lady Liu didn't answer immediately, but Lu Huaixi had already guessed the outcome.

It was precisely because the Old Master had relented that Lady Luo had then turned and come to Lady Liu.

As long as the first branch was willing to look the other way rather than press the matter, the second branch still had room to find a solution.

"Yes. Your grandfather was angry—but he wants to protect the Lu family's daughters from entering the palace."

Lady Liu's expression grew cool. "But he wants to protect his granddaughter. I want to protect my daughter. Each of us will make our own move."

"Mother—"

"Though there's also a clever one."

Lady Liu seemed to recall something and added: "Fourth Sister came to find me yesterday."

"Fourth Sister?"

Lu Huaixi was surprised.

"Fourth Sister is lively but timid—she always looks to Lu Tangshu before she does anything. How could she suddenly come to you? Does the second branch know?"

Fourth Miss Lu Sui-dong was the second branch's concubine-born daughter, almost the same age as Lu Tangshu.

Her mother had once been greatly favoured—Lu Huaixi remembered as a child often seeing her second uncle with Lu Sui-dong's mother close at his side.

But then her mother had caused a scene, and Lu Sui-dong had been left out in the cold. To get by, she had been forced to pull in her own nature and endlessly please the principal wife.

Later, when Lu Tangshu couldn't find anyone to play with, she had become something between a companion and a servant—following her around, keeping her company, learning to wait on her.

"Most likely they don't know."

Lady Liu said: "Lady Luo's private methods are severe. Fourth Sister wants to live a peaceful life, so she's had to learn to watch moods. But I only just found out—she has a great deal of nerve."

chapters.title: Just Waiting to Come Home in One Year
chapters.content:
On the day Lu Huaixi had married out, Fourth Miss Lu Sui-dong had been absolutely delighted.

When all the girls gathered together, every one of them had been curious about this unknown second brother-in-law they had yet to see.

Lu Huaixi heard from her eldest sister that on that day, Lu Sui-dong had been so exuberantly happy that she caught the sharp end of Lu Tangshu's tongue—and didn't dare say another word after that.

Now her mother was saying Fourth Sister had nerve—Lu Huaixi found it genuinely difficult to picture the girl sitting quietly and speaking with her mother.

Lady Liu didn't keep her wondering long.

"Once the Flower and Bird Envoy's list became known, almost all the girls in the household had their suspicions. Especially since Lu Tangshu had made such a scene, crying and smashing things—and yesterday Fourth Sister came without any preamble. She went straight to the point: she wants to take her elder sister's place and enter the palace."

"...Was she forced to come by the Second Madam?"

"At first I assumed the same. She and Lu Tangshu may be legitimate and concubine-born, but they're still both of the Lu family. If it came to entering the palace, there are ways to arrange it—but the more I listened, the clearer it became that she wants to go of her own will. And she's hiding it from Lady Luo."

Thinking of those words, Lady Liu let out a soft exhale.

"She had a good childhood once—then she was suppressed and never got back up. It's a hard way to live. I understand what she means. Her marriage will be entirely in Lady Luo's hands—but she doesn't want that. She wants to find her own way out."

"But..."

"She told me plainly—even if this doesn't work out, she'll find another way. She refuses to be handed off to some man's inner household as a concubine, and she refuses to be Lady Luo's good deed. This palace—she is going in."

Lu Huaixi was quiet for a long moment.

This fourth sister of hers had always been in close contact with her. Or rather—in the Lu household, apart from Lu Tangshu whose heart had gone crooked, her other sisters had all been reasonably close to her.

But however warm Fourth Sister was toward her, she was still the second branch's concubine-born daughter. Every move she made required watching Lady Luo's face first.

To come behind the second branch's back and petition Lady Liu directly—she must have decided to burn the boat.

"Doesn't she know that going into the palace—life and death would truly be..."

"How could she not know? But she says she doesn't care. Marrying anyone else is also life and death uncertain. And she's not wrong—for any other girl, Lady Luo might play the good person. But for her... it would be difficult."

Hearing that, Lu Huaixi's lips moved.

Lady Luo would likely not find her a particularly good match. The jealousy and hatred Lady Luo had once harboured for that concubine was something even Lu Huaixi had heard about.

Fourth Sister probably knew it too. Which was why, faced with the choice between becoming a concubine herself or suffering through someone's bitter inner household, she had chosen to take a chance.

"Did you agree, Mother?"

"No."

Lady Liu still kept her voice cool. "But her coming to me in secret, without Lady Luo knowing—that reasoning is not without consideration."

"What does that mean? She wants more than just the standing she'd get from entering the palace?"

"Yes. She doesn't want Lu Tangshu to fare well."

Lady Liu said: "She wants my help in getting her into the palace. In return, she would help me deal with Lady Luo and her daughter. Her meaning is that if Lu Tangshu were to enter the palace and be favoured, she would certainly seek revenge—but Fourth Sister would not."

Managing the inner household was not something Lady Liu had ever had any interest in outsourcing to another. And she certainly had no need to bargain with anyone.

If she wanted to stand up for her daughter, she had methods enough—clean ones, without underhanded schemes.

Lu Tangshu had wanted to destroy her daughter's future and climb over her to rise. So she would return the favour.

Send her to the palace to be her "honoured lady"—give her exactly what she wanted. It was a perfectly fine outcome.

But there was also another path.

"Huaixi—what do you think?"

Lady Liu came back to herself and looked at her daughter.

"I want to hear your thoughts first."

"Is it because you think sending her to the palace has risks?" Lu Huaixi replied.

"You don't need to worry about what comes after. The household will handle those considerations."

Lady Liu had thought it through: if Lu Tangshu went to the palace, the Lu family would inevitably be bound to her to some degree. Even if they kept their distance and didn't interfere, she would have her moment of prominence for a while. Looking at it—that was always going to feel like swallowing something uncomfortable.

And given the direction Lu Tangshu's thinking had gone, if her life were hard she might do something even more reckless. The first branch wasn't afraid—they would just be sending her step by step toward her own end. But none of it was pleasant.

Whatever the outcome, she needed to hear her daughter's thoughts first.

Her daughter might want the scheme returned to the sender in full—and if so, that was exactly what she would do.

"Mother, I'm not letting this go."

Lu Huaixi looked up with unhurried candour—her clear, limpid dark eyes catching the light and looking bright and guileless.

But the words she spoke carried a calm that had nothing of the naivety written on her face.

"Have Third Sister betrothed and married."

Lu Huaixi smiled, eyes curving.

"She doesn't want to go to the palace? Then let her marry. And quickly—pick fast, marry fast. If something well-matched isn't available, then something below her standing. I've already married ahead of her as the elder sister, so her marrying now isn't improper."

Lu Tangshu wanted to raise her own standing, wanted a splendid marriage, wanted everyone to envy her. Then let every one of those wishes be turned on its head.

When Lu Huaixi said these things, she didn't feel the slightest bit cruel.

And she wasn't afraid of anyone objecting—she said it at her own unhurried pace, as casually as if she were describing what good things she'd eaten that day.

Lady Liu looked at her, and her expression softened involuntarily—a thread of guilt surfacing in her eyes.

Not catching the second branch's intentions in time had forced her easygoing, carefree girl into an early marriage.

Now her daughter looked composed enough—but Lady Liu knew her child.

If she truly felt nothing, she wouldn't be this composed about proposing to have Lu Tangshu betrothed and married off.

She still minded. She still felt the injustice.

"Then let her be married off."

Lady Liu took Lu Huaixi's hand. "She wanted to step on you to raise her standing. Let her fall until she has no standing left."

Not long after, a maidservant came from outside to refill the tea—adding some of the cakes that Lu Huaixi had always liked.

Lady Liu saw what had been brought and thought again of what she had overheard when her daughter stepped down from the carriage.

"I didn't get to say this to you earlier—when you go out with someone, Yaoshu is right there with you. How could you put Xie Yuanjing to work tidying the food box for you?"

Having finished the serious talk, Lady Liu's tone gentled, and thinking of something, she shook her head slightly.

"I know you've had to carry a lot. Coming home, perhaps you let your guard down. But however agreeable his temperament, the two of you are not truly husband and wife. These things—don't let yourself get too used to expecting them."

"I didn't suffer any hardship."

Lu Huaixi thought about saying his temperament wasn't actually all that agreeable—then reconsidered, and found that actually, it kind of was.

Xie Yuanjing had never shown her a cold face, let alone lost his temper.

When he was with her he was patient and warm—and always found ways to show, openly, that she had someone backing her in the marquis' household. He made sure everyone could see it.

Whatever he had said about "as it should be," he had handled everything with care and exactness. There was nothing to fault.

At that thought, Lu Huaixi swallowed what she'd been about to say.

"Don't worry, Mother. I remember that he and I aren't truly husband and wife. Today I really did just sleep in—I'll call for Yaoshu next time. I won't trouble him."

"Of course I'm not blaming you—I'm only worried that over time you'll get used to it, and start expecting it outside too. He is the marquis' household's First Young Lord after all. Even if he and our Lu family's first branch are on the same ship right now, he's still someone with his own temperament. And besides, everything he does has a purpose—"

Lady Liu looked at her and paused, then spoke more deliberately.

"That said—don't hear what I'm saying and turn cold toward him either. The way he looks after you is, one could argue, what's due to you. And what's due to you, your father will compensate him in equal—or even greater—measure. So if you suffer any grievance in the marquis' household, you don't need to be afraid."

There were things Lady Liu had hesitated to say.

Her daughter was very clever, and she already understood perfectly well what Xie Yuanjing's warmth was for.

But she still had to be careful. Because this eldest young lord of the Xie family, if he wanted someone to grow attached, was far too capable of it.

"I know, Mother."
