"Now everyone is saying Qingyun Peak mistreated you, saying the junior sister harmed you. Are you happy?"

Happy?

She was, actually.

Waiting three months to be let down — even without destroying her own cultivation, she would have been finished by then anyway.

Ye Wanwan gave a cold laugh. "Heh."

Ji Changhuai: "What are you laughing at?"

Ye Wanwan opened her eyes. "I'm laughing at how stupid you are."

The refined, genteel face before her was the senior brother she knew well — one of the people she had most respected in her last life.

But Ye Wanwan didn't miss the indifference in his eyes. He wasn't concerned about her. He was only resentful that she had caused him trouble.

And brought harm to Ye Qian's reputation.

Ye Wanwan would never forget — when she had "shattered" Ye Qian's golden core and desperately tried to explain to this man that it hadn't been her, Ji Changhuai had never believed her, not even once. He had coldly pushed her away. "I am so disappointed in you."

And the next time she saw him, it was the sword through her heart.

A senior brother like that — better off without.

Ji Changhuai's brow tightened. "What kind of look is that?"

"However Senior Brother looks at me, I look at Senior Brother the same way. So Senior Brother — what kind of look is it?"

Ye Wanwan held his gaze without flinching.

Ji Changhuai felt something jolt in his chest. The rumors outside were saying Ye Wanwan had gone mad. Looking at her cold, flat stare now, he wondered — had she really?

His expression grew colder. Power gathered in his palm. He grabbed Ye Wanwan by the throat, his voice like ice. "Whoever you are, get out of my junior sister."

"Get out!"

Ye Wanwan's expression didn't change.

Ji Changhuai's eyes shifted again and again. Then, without another word, he pressed a palm to the top of her head and snapped, "Soul search."

The soul-search technique was a forceful, domineering method that ignored the other party's will and directly inspected their primordial spirit.

If done improperly, it could easily damage the other person's mind and cause unpredictable consequences.

And the current Ye Wanwan's body was still critically weak — completely unable to withstand this kind of harm.

A violent, invasive, tearing sensation drilled into her mind. Ye Wanwan's entire skull felt like it was about to explode. She wanted to scream but couldn't. Her body and spirit both took a devastating blow.

She opened her mouth. What came out was blood.

A great deal of it.

After a long while, Ji Changhuai stood there, stunned. "The primordial spirit...... it's correct."

It really was his junior sister.

No soul possession.

Ye Wanwan's front and the corners of her mouth were covered in blood, and yet she was still smiling. "It's me. Senior Brother. I'm Ye Wanwan. I've never changed."

Only then did Ji Changhuai realize he was still gripping Ye Wanwan by the throat. He startled and let go.

But Ye Wanwan's neck had already been bruised purple, and the blood from her mouth hadn't stopped. He reached out in a panic. "I'm sorry, junior sister, I'm sorry. I thought you——"

Ye Wanwan had no strength left to deal with him.

The pain — she was in so much pain.

Destroying her own cultivation wasn't a pleasant experience, and Ji Changhuai's palm had nearly shattered what little remained of her breath. But she clenched her teeth, refusing to collapse in front of this man.

Yet she had no idea how fragile she was in this moment.

Looking at the girl who seemed about to fall apart before him, Ji Changhuai was truly frightened. "I'll transfer spiritual energy to you, I'll transfer it now, junior sister — don't be afraid."

Ji Changhuai hurried to channel spiritual energy into Ye Wanwan.

Ye Wanwan tried to speak, but couldn't make a sound.

"What are you saying?" Ji Changhuai asked urgently.

Ye Wanwan said, her voice a rasp: "I'm...... not your junior sister...... your junior sister...... is outside."

Ji Changhuai sensed something, turned to look at the doorway. A girl in blue was standing there, her eyes brimming with tears. Ji Changhuai froze. "Junior sister."

chapters.title: Heaven-Grade Five Spirit Roots
chapters.content:
Ji Changhuai panicked. He had just called out the wrong name in his rush — he quickly got to his feet. "Junior sister, why have you come?"

And just like that, he forgot completely about the critically injured Ye Wanwan.

Ye Wanwan lay on the bed, feeling as though every part of her was about to break apart — her soul, her body, all of it.

The pain made her curl in on herself.

She desperately wanted to throw these two people out, but she couldn't move.

These miserable excuses for people — why wouldn't they just leave?

Get out!

Hearing Ji Changhuai's voice, Ye Qian forced a smile, though it looked more like a grimace. She held a bowl of medicine and said timidly, "Senior Brother Ji, I heard Seventh Senior Sister came down the mountain, so I came to see her."

Ji Changhuai said gently, reproaching her, "Your own body isn't well yet — why did you come all this way? Your senior sister has us."

Ye Qian bit her lower lip, glancing cautiously at Ye Wanwan. "I'm afraid Senior Sister is still angry with me."

"She won't be," Ji Changhuai took the medicine from her hands and said gently. "You're such a well-behaved junior sister — why would she be angry with you?"

Ye Qian peeked carefully at Ye Wanwan. "Then why won't Senior Sister look at me......"

Ji Changhuai also looked toward Ye Wanwan on the bed. She had turned her back, curled up in the blankets — clearly not wanting to see Ye Qian.

Ye Qian's eyes brimmed with tears. She bit her lower lip and cried, "Senior Sister is still blaming me. I...... I know...... it's all my fault."

Ye Qian wept. "But the matter of the golden core — I truly didn't understand it...... I didn't intend to take Senior Sister's core. I only learned of my father coming up the mountain after I woke up. If I had known beforehand, I would never have agreed to it."

"I'm willing to give the core back to Senior Sister. Please don't blame me, wuu wuu."

Ji Changhuai couldn't bear to see Ye Qian crying, and fussed about coaxing the girl. "Senior Brother knows, I know everything. This isn't your fault. Master has already decided on the matter of the core. Don't say anymore."

"Little Seven doesn't blame you. She could never blame you."

The two of them — one crying, one consoling — went at it for a good while without stopping.

Clang.

Until the room suddenly rang with the sound of a blade being drawn. Both of them startled and looked back toward the bed.

Ye Wanwan's face was the color of paper, but she had still managed to pull out a dagger, which she held out to Ye Qian. "Here."

Ye Qian blinked. "What?"

Ye Wanwan said a single word: "Dig."

The cogs in Ji Changhuai's stunned brain finally started turning again. He furiously knocked the dagger away, and along with it struck Ye Wanwan's hand hard against the bed.

Crack.

Clang.

The blade hit the ground.

Ye Wanwan's face went even paler.

Ji Changhuai recognized it — that was the dagger he had given Ye Wanwan.

He was incensed. "You've truly lost all conscience. Right in front of me, you dare to force little eighth to dig out her core. Who knows what you'd do behind our backs."

"I gave you that magic tool, and this is how you use it?"

Ji Changhuai kicked the dagger away and berated Ye Wanwan at full volume. Ye Wanwan didn't lift her head, listening calmly.

"Get out."

Her voice was faint, but she kept repeating the same word: "Get out."

Get out, both of you!

The red in her eyes slowly ignited.

Ye Wanwan's left hand clenched. Her barely-moving fingertips began, slowly and with great difficulty, to draw a killing talisman.

Kill them.

Kill all of them!

Even in death, she would take them with her!

But just then.

Ye Qian suddenly stopped Ji Changhuai and cried, "Senior Sister and Senior Brother, please don't fight because of me. I know it's all my fault. I'll leave the mountain right now, leave the Supreme Sect — just please don't fight."

"Little Eighth!"

Before Ji Changhuai had finished speaking, Ye Qian had already run out the door in tears. From a distance, one could still hear someone asking, "Junior Sister, what's wrong?"

"Third Senior Brother, I'm leaving the Supreme Sect now."

"Wait, why are you crying — did someone bully you? I know, it must have been Ye Wanwan, I'm going to go teach her a lesson right now!"

Both of them heard the voices at the door.

Before long, Dou Ming appeared, dragging Ye Qian back with him. His first look at Ye Wanwan filled his face with malice. He grabbed her off the bed and pulled her down.

The talisman was broken.

Ye Wanwan finally laughed. She laughed loudly and bleakly, startling everyone in the room.

Because the girl being dragged off the bed was coughing up blood.

More and more of it.

As if it would dye the entire floor red.

And yet her laughter never stopped. As if she were mocking her entire life.

How absurd it all was. How could it have taken her this long to see these people clearly.

All three of their faces had gone white.

Ye Qian was also crying. "Is Senior Sister going to die?"

Blood kept coming up. Dou Ming was so frightened he let go.

……

In the tense atmosphere of the room.

Elder Yu Chun of the Yumu Hall finished taking the girl's pulse and roared: "Did I not say before I left that she needed quiet recovery? What in the world have you all been doing now?"

"Do you resent her being alive?"

"They're still fellow disciples. Dou Ming, your hands were that vicious — were you trying to kill her?"

Dou Ming muttered, "How was I supposed to know her meridians were really severed? I thought she was faking."

"All of you." Elder Yu Chun was so angry he laughed. "Fine. I won't involve myself in your personal disputes. But she is my patient right now. If you get her killed, none of you ever come to the Yumu Hall again."

"And I won't set foot on your Qingyun Peak ever again."

Ji Changhuai and Dou Ming scrambled to apologize and make amends when they heard this.

The junior sister was sickly — Elder Yu Chun had always been the one to treat her. If Elder Yu Chun refused to come to Qingyun Peak, what would the junior sister do in the future?

Both of them rushed to apologize, to say what needed to be said, all to keep the elder happy.

"The junior sister's health still needs your care, Elder — please don't abandon us."

Elder Yu Chun heard these words and looked with complicated feelings toward the girl lying on the bed.

In the past, the one these several people called "junior sister" — that would have been her.

But times change.

Elder Yu Chun wrote out several prescriptions for valuable spirit medicines and thoroughly fleeced Ji Changhuai and Dou Ming.

He urged Ye Wanwan again and again to rest quietly. Even he himself was shaken — with injuries this severe, it was a marvel that Ye Wanwan was still alive.

Her will to live was very strong.

Strong enough that it couldn't be ignored.

Ye Wanwan didn't know what he was thinking. If she had, she would certainly have said — of course she wanted to live. She had been given such a rare second chance.

She absolutely could not die just like this.

Could not!

Because of Yu Chun's instructions, Ye Wanwan was spared the punishment of Xuanbing Cliff and instead given a one-year confinement. Aside from Yu Chun, no one was permitted to see her.

This also gave Ye Wanwan the time she needed to heal.

One month later, the girl's condition gradually stabilized. Yu Chun sighed and said, "You are truly the most resilient patient I have ever seen. In just one month you have already recovered to this extent. But child — your meridians are severed, your golden core dug out. In the future, you may......"

The rest went unsaid.

But he knew Ye Wanwan understood.

The path of cultivation was closed to her.

Seeing Ye Wanwan lower her eyes in silence, Yu Chun consoled her. "Let it go, child. Being alive is enough."

Yu Chun left behind several spirit medicine prescriptions and told Ye Wanwan to rest well. After he left, Ye Wanwan slowly got to her feet and walked around the room.

One day. Two days. Three days. Until the girl had recovered her ability to move, only then did she sit cross-legged.

The cultivation she had once held was entirely gone. There was nothing left.

But Ye Wanwan wasn't worried.

Her spirit roots and meridians had always been different from others. She was born with heaven-grade five spirit roots.

The grade of a spirit root was ranked from: low-grade, mid-grade, high-grade, peak-grade, and the rarest — heaven-grade.

The quality of a single spirit root determines how quickly its owner can absorb the spiritual energy of heaven and earth.

Ye Wanwan's spirit roots were the pinnacle of the peak, the extraordinarily rare heaven-grade.

And yet — she had five of them.

Cultivation speed would be unbearably slow.

So before she had entered any sect, the man who was her father in this body had sealed off her other four elemental roots, leaving only fire.

Because of this, after entering the Supreme Sect, she had advanced steadily and broken through to the golden core stage at fifteen.

But after reaching golden core, she stopped advancing entirely.

In her past life, Ye Wanwan had spent a long time puzzling over why she couldn't cultivate anymore after reaching the golden core stage.

Many years later, she finally understood the reason.

Her spirit roots should never have been sealed.

The five elements cannot be broken apart.

Ye Wanwan gathered her spiritual energy and slowly flushed through her meridians. Every movement was like being torn apart — the pain made her tremble.

But she pushed through it, bit by bit, and finished.

One month later, she broke through the teetering seal inside her body and heard the sound of the restriction unlocking.

She opened her palm. Five currents of spiritual light moved across it — her innate five spirit roots.

She slowly closed her hand.

It was done.

On her pale face, both her eyes burned with scorching brightness.

chapters.title: To Be First Under Heaven
chapters.content:
Three days later.

Ye Wanwan had successfully entered the first level of qi refinement.

"A little slow, but cultivation is still possible."

What she didn't know was how shocking it was that a person with five spirit roots, going from unsealing to breaking through the first level of qi refinement in just three days. That speed was truly terrifying.

But Ye Wanwan was not satisfied with this efficiency.

After all, five spirit roots cultivated slowly.

If she wanted to catch up with the others on Qingyun Peak, she had a great deal of work to do.

In addition to daily breathing exercises, she gave herself new tasks: every day she would commune with the five elemental forces of heaven and earth to build a solid foundation for herself.

As for a cultivation method, Ye Wanwan didn't use anything from Qingyun Peak. She used a basic breathing technique she had bought outside, long ago.

Purchasable for a single spirit stone.

She had thought it through — if she was going to cut all ties with this place, then she wouldn't use their cultivation methods either.

That day, after finishing cultivation, Ye Wanwan's gaze fell on the barren and overgrown medicine garden.

She thought of Elder Yu Chun's words.

"This is a volume of spirit plant techniques and some spirit grass seeds. Even though you cannot cultivate now, if you can re-enter the qi refinement stage, you could become a spirit plant master — that's also a path forward."

"Child, don't give up."

The elder had placed the items in her hands with hope and encouragement. Ye Wanwan looked at the spirit plant manual and the seeds.

She got up and walked toward the medicine garden.

After planting the seeds, Ye Wanwan performed the spirit rain technique from the spirit plant manual.

Spirit plant techniques were the gentlest and simplest of all techniques — yet they contained within them the fundamental cloud-summoning and rain-calling arts.

Ye Wanwan tried it several times and slowly found the trick to it.

The seeds in the medicine garden, nourished by the rain, took root, sprouted, and broke through the soil. In just half a day, they were growing vigorously.

Then Ye Wanwan made a scarecrow, attached a puppet talisman to it, and left it to guard the medicine garden and keep the birds from eating the seedlings.

She herself sat cross-legged in the courtyard to cultivate.

Around the perimeter of the courtyard, she had attached talismans.

Spiritual gathering talismans.

They made the spiritual energy inside and outside the bamboo house rich and abundant.

More conducive to Ye Wanwan's cultivation.

Another month passed.

Ye Wanwan's fire spirit root had risen from the first level of qi refinement to the twelfth. Her other four spirit roots: wood root at level six. Water root at level five. Earth root at level five. Metal root at level three.

If not for Ye Wanwan deliberately holding back, her fire spirit root would already have broken through to foundation establishment.

"As expected, the further back you go, the slower it gets, and the greater the gaps become."

Ye Wanwan murmured quietly.

"But......"

Ye Wanwan clenched her fist. "It'll do."

A little slower than before.

But at least there was progress.

She hadn't expected that using spirit plant techniques every day would benefit not just her wood root but also her earth and water roots. That was a pleasant surprise.

Something hidden in the medicine garden heard her and looked over. Reaching the twelfth level at most in one month — that was indeed......

Fine.

It chewed at the grass in its mouth with force.

"Crunch crunch crunch."

Ye Wanwan heard the noise, turned and looked, and saw something with a black, hard shell.

Ye Wanwan was puzzled. "Where did this turtle come from?"

The black tortoise turned its head and took a few more bites.

Ye Wanwan: "...... So that's why the spirit plants in the medicine field keep disappearing. It's been you, eating them all along?"

Crunch crunch crunch.

Seeing that this creature had no idea what was going on and only cared about eating, Ye Wanwan shook her head and didn't bother with it.

Sunlight fell across her. Ye Wanwan tilted her head back to look at the sky, and murmured quietly.

She still had so many things to do.

Ye Wanwan's daily routine: wake up, meditate for one hour, practice the qi refinement technique.

At the hour of mao, begin spirit plant techniques, cultivating wood, earth, and water roots.

At the hour of chen, practice earth force techniques in the back room, then go to Chaotic Sword Forest and commune with the force of metal.

At noon, eat and rest.

At the hour of wei, practice body cultivation techniques and sword forms.

At the hour of you, review talisman drawing and formation study.

Before sleeping at the hour of hai, analyze the day's progress, readjust the cultivation methods, and refine the approach for the next day.

And so it continued, cycling without pause.

Not a single day slackened.

The five elemental forces she divided and cultivated separately — one by one — but most of the time, practicing one root would bring others along with it. The methods she had spent years thinking through after her foundation was shattered in her last life — she was putting all of them to use now.

Three months later.

Fire spirit root: peak of level thirteen.

Wood, water, earth, metal: level twelve.

When the four roots stagnated at the qi refinement bottleneck for three days without moving, Ye Wanwan stopped and didn't push forward.

She picked up her bucket, watered the spirit plants, and didn't even bother with the spirit rain technique.

"Have I gotten my methods wrong somehow?"

"Crunch."

"Five spirit roots — really can't cultivate further?"

"Crunch crunch."

"Do I need to re-seal them?"

"Crunch crunch crunch crunch."

The unavoidable sound made Ye Wanwan fling the ladle. It rang out with a clang, as if it had struck metal.

The black tortoise, struck by it, still didn't forget to bite a few more times. Over the course of three months, the river turtle's shell had become more and more lustrous, as if someone had polished it.

Ye Wanwan frowned. "No. Sealing them is wrong. I must keep all five roots. Otherwise I can't go any further in this life."

"But what exactly do I need to do?"

Ye Wanwan looked at her hands.

In her last life, after years of wandering, she had asked around about cultivation methods for five spirit roots.

But without exception, everyone had failed at the golden core breakthrough to nascent soul.

In thousands of years of the nine continents, not a single person had ever succeeded.

But Ye Wanwan refused to believe it.

She was going to be that first person!

The black tortoise finally lifted its head this time, looked at her, and slowed the pace of its chewing slightly.

A sharp glint flickered in its small eyes.

Unable to find a method, she would make up for it with hard work. Ye Wanwan repeated the same training as these past three months.

Not a single day slacked.

One month later.

Ye Wanwan finally felt the bottleneck of the qi refinement stage start to loosen.

The qi refinement stage had thirteen levels in total.

Only after passing the thirteenth level could one enter foundation establishment. And the five small currents of energy within Ye Wanwan's body were still in a scattered, unsettled state.

Only when they fully condensed would foundation establishment be considered complete.

Now within Ye Wanwan's body were five currents of energy.

Uniform in size.

Stable in state.

Ye Wanwan calmed herself and felt the flow of heaven and earth energy. The black tortoise sat beside her, the sharp light in its small eyes flickering again.

The heavenly energy swirled, gathered and scattered, scattered and turned, spiraling around the girl.

Following her intent, it sank into her dantian.

As the currents stabilized.

All five generated a vortex eye.

Foundation establishment — complete.

And she had smoothly entered the early stage of foundation establishment.

Ye Wanwan opened her eyes. The spiritual energy around her dispersed. Her gaze fell on the medicine field, and with a wave of her hand the spirit plant technique surged forth — the spirit plants in the field immediately flourished and grew strong.

Truly pleasing to see.

Ye Wanwan murmured quietly: "Three times the speed. That will do."

The black tortoise looked at the peak-grade spirit plants before it. The girl hadn't noticed — the spirit grass she grew was different from anyone else's.

The tortoise bit off a mouthful and, feeling the abundant vitality pouring through it, buried its head and refused to look up.

"Give me time, and I will definitely return to the golden core stage."

Ye Wanwan murmured.

"Definitely."

Time passed in a blink to one year after the start of Ye Wanwan's confinement.

That day.

Ji Changhuai came, together with Dou Ming.

chapters.title: Admitting Fault?
chapters.content:
Hearing the noise.

Ye Wanwan gathered all her talismans and burned them clean.

The firelight reflected in the girl's eyes — still and indifferent.

As soon as they entered, Ji Changhuai placed a small brocade box on the table and said, with some care: "Seventh junior sister, this is...... for you."

Ye Wanwan didn't move.

Dou Ming stood at the doorway, his voice dripping with sarcasm. "This was exchanged by senior brother using a magic treasure with the people of Danha Peak — a core-consolidating pill. There's only one. It can help you rebuild your meridians so you can cultivate again. Your cultivation speed won't be what it used to be, but at least you won't be completely finished."

A core-consolidating pill. In her last life, Ji Changhuai had given her this same pill — but within half a day, he had asked for it back.

Ye Wanwan had never gotten to use it.

Ye Qian, rushing ahead of herself before the sect's grand competition one year later, had made a mistake — her meridians had reversed and damaged her foundation.

Her golden core was Ye Wanwan's.

So Ji Changhuai had taken the pill back.

That thing, back in her hands, would never last even an hour.

Ye Wanwan's eyes held a mocking light. "Then I do appreciate Senior Brother's effort. But there is no need — I don't want it."

Ji Changhuai's face went white. Over the past year, everything he had arranged to send to Ye Wanwan had been refused.

He had assumed it was a young girl throwing a tantrum. But looking at her now, this particular tantrum seemed to have gone on quite a long time.

Dou Ming noticed too. He glared and snapped, "Ye Wanwan, what kind of an attitude is this? What are you putting on airs for?"

"Do you know how much we've done this past year to make up for the disaster you caused?"

"Especially senior brother — if not for him looking after junior sister the whole time, do you think the Ye family would have let you off this easily? What right do you have to give us an attitude?"

Ji Changhuai also said nothing, only looking at Ye Wanwan with a trace of sorrow and reproach.

As if to say she had no idea what was good for her.

Ye Wanwan gave a self-mocking smile. "So I'm the ungrateful one here?"

"What else? Are we the ungrateful ones? Master has already said — if you still don't admit your fault, you'll stay confined here until you die!"

Ye Wanwan's fingers curled slightly.

So the one-year confinement had only been the beginning?

Dou Ming said darkly, "Scared now? If you knew to be scared, you shouldn't have done this in the first place. Lucky for you that junior sister is generous — she's already told Master that as long as you get down on your knees and admit your fault, Master will still let you out."

Ye Wanwan didn't respond. She stroked her teacup and looked at Ji Changhuai. "Senior Brother — if you give me that pill, will you take it back later?"

Dou Ming was infuriated that she was ignoring him. "Ye Wanwan! I'm talking to you!"

Ji Changhuai also didn't understand. "Since I found it for you, why would I take it back?"

"All right."

Ye Wanwan took it and put it away.

She stood up and walked toward the door.

Dou Ming and Ji Changhuai stood where they were without moving.

Ye Wanwan looked back. "Weren't we going to apologize?"

Dou Ming was suspicious. "You agreed? You're not pulling something, are you?" He simply didn't believe Ye Wanwan would bow her head.

The greatest genius on Qingyun Peak — how could she admit fault so easily?

They had come today only on a chance.

Ye Wanwan's eyes held mockery. "Third Senior Brother said it himself — I don't want to be confined until I die, so of course I have to admit my fault."

Dou Ming sneered. "So it's for your freedom."

Ye Wanwan looked out at the bamboo grove. "Yes. Freedom is precious."

And dignity — more so.

It was also time to go.

Ye Wanwan went with Ji Changhuai and Dou Ming out of the bamboo grove, the three of them making their way to Ye Qian's residence. Along the way, they attracted quite a few stares.

Pointing fingers everywhere.

"Isn't that Seventh Junior Sister?"

"I heard she's the one who badly injured Junior Sister's golden core and left Junior Sister bedridden this whole year."

"Such a vicious mind — shattering someone's golden core is no different from killing them."

"And she's still walking around fine. Why hasn't Dao Venerable Yanding expelled her from the sect?"

The remarks reached her ears.

Ji Changhuai said in concern, "Wanwan, they're talking nonsense. Don't take it to heart."

"Senior Brother, I think they're not entirely wrong," said Dou Ming dismissively, shooting a sidelong glance at Ye Wanwan. "Was it false that she shattered Junior Sister's golden core?"

No matter what these people said, Ye Wanwan didn't react.

One year of self-cultivation. She had long since made her peace.

This was simply not a place she belonged.

So why bother getting angry at a crowd of fools?

Ye Qian's residence was at Mirror Lake — a place where water spiritual energy was abundant. Previously it had been Ye Wanwan's, but one year ago, when Ye Qian joined the sect with her peak-grade water spirit root and her frail constitution, the residence had been taken from her.

Back then, Ye Wanwan had been fire elemental — so she had thought, fine, let her have it.

But looking back now.

She had been far too accommodating.

"Senior Brother!"

Dressed in a flowing gown, looking like a pure little white flower, Ye Qian came running toward the wind. "I could hear your voice from the middle of the lake!"

Ji Changhuai's perpetually creased brow relaxed the moment he saw Ye Qian. "Junior Sister, are you feeling better?"

Dou Ming, not to be outdone, spoke up. "Junior Sister, did you only hear Senior Brother? What about Third Senior Brother?"

Ye Qian smiled, her eyes curved. "Of course I heard Third Senior Brother too — I heard both of you, clear as anything~"

She took both of their arms and steered them toward the lakeside cottage. "What good things did you bring me this time?"

"Nothing — we came empty-handed."

"Not empty-handed — Third Senior Brother brought a whole heart full of concern, didn't he?"

"Ha ha ha."

The three of them laughed, and their voices floated far on the lake breeze. Only after a long while did they seem to remember they had forgotten someone.

"Seventh Junior Sister!"

Ji Changhuai suddenly turned around.

Ye Wanwan wasn't looking at them. She stood at the edge of the lake, her gaze resting on the cottage in the middle of the water.

A cool breeze moved across the lake's surface, and on the water's center, there was still one more figure.

"Master!"

Everyone cried out and dropped to their knees.

The disciples all around also knelt one by one.

Only Ye Wanwan continued to stand.

She raised her eyes and met Yanding's gaze, holding it for a long time. Then, under the pressure of his aura, she clasped her hands in a bow.

"Ye Wanwan pays her respects to the Dao Venerable."

She said Dao Venerable, not Master.

Several people looked at Ye Wanwan in astonishment.

Yanding's eyes darkened.

Inside the room.

Ye Qian wrung her fingers, glancing awkwardly between the two senior figures present. "Actually, there's no need to apologize. This matter wasn't entirely Seventh Senior Sister's...... fault."

Ye Qian's father Ye Congyue slammed the table. "How is there no need to apologize? Do you know how many years of cultivation it takes to produce a single golden core?"

"And Qian'er's was a peak-grade water spirit root. Even with a replacement golden core, a transference pill was used — can we even predict how much of an impact there will be going forward?"

"If Qian'er's cultivation is affected by this, how is the Supreme Sect going to answer to my daughter?"

The atmosphere in the room was heavy.

Ji Changhuai's expression was anxious.

Even the normally fearless Dou Ming didn't dare make a sound.

The Supreme Sect's sect master consoled, "Friend Ye need not be so upset. Since this incident occurred within our sect, we will naturally take responsibility for Qian'er's path of cultivation going forward."

As he spoke, he raised his eyes toward Yanding, waiting for him to express his stance.

Yanding said: "Kneel."

Yanding hadn't specified who, but as the aura fell, with a thud, the only person in the room who knelt was Ye Wanwan.

Ye Congyue gave a cold laugh.

Yanding: "Admit your fault."

Ye Wanwan's expression was flat. She looked at Ye Qian. "I accepted the invitation to spar with Junior Sister Ye Qian. Everything was done according to proper procedure. I am not aware of where my fault lies."

Seeing everyone looking over, Ye Qian grew anxious. "Master, this matter truly has nothing to do with Seventh Senior Sister. The sparring was arranged between the two of us. If Seventh Senior Sister broke my golden core — it was because...... because I......"

"Because my own skills were insufficient, and this was the result."

Ye Congyue slammed his palm on the table.

Crack!

Before Ye Congyue's hand landed, a teacup came flying from Yanding's direction and struck Ye Wanwan in the forehead.

Blood dripped down.

Blurring her right eye.

"That was the forehead. Next time, you choose where." Yanding gave a cold smile.

Ye Wanwan didn't wipe the blood from her forehead. She lowered her eyes and said evenly, "I was not at fault. Ye Qian challenged me to a match. My response was fully within reason and rules. If her golden core shattered, it was because her core formation was unstable and it broke of its own accord. It has nothing to do with me."

Ye Wanwan's lips curved. "Don't try to put the blame on me."

Ye Qian's face went deathly pale.

How...... did she know?

Everyone in the room drew a sharp breath.

The intense pressure, and the sect master's increasingly stormy expression above, made Ji Changhuai suddenly step forward.

"Junior Sister!"

Ye Wanwan raised her head.

Smack.

That slap landed on Ye Wanwan's face.

She had no time to dodge.

She froze.

Ji Changhuai said, word by word: "Junior Sister, that is not what you said back in the room. You clearly said — you were here to admit your fault."

chapters.title: She Would Rather Die Than Admit It
chapters.content:
"You said that out of a moment of jealousy toward your junior sister, you had a lapse of judgment and devised a plan. But you only intended to put the junior sister in bed for a while as a lesson — you never expected the consequences to be so severe."

"It was only an accident."

"Wasn't it?"

Ji Changhuai said through clenched teeth.

The pain spread up from her cheek. Ye Wanwan's gaze didn't retreat. She gave a cold laugh. "...... No, I am here to admit fault."

"But not this fault."

"My fault was in taking so many years to see through all of your faces and behavior. Ye Qian's core formation failed, and the blame was pushed onto me. You all knew it — and yet you helped carry out the injustice, dug out my golden core, and had me kneel at Xuanbing Cliff to admit fault. All of it simply because——"

"I have no one standing behind me!"

Ye Wanwan swept her gaze across everyone in the Supreme Sect. "Ye Qian has the backing of the great Ye Clan. She shares the surname Ye. I am nothing but an orphan with no parents. You watched the Ye family push the blame onto me and did nothing, simply because I had no one and was easy to bully."

"Ye Qian is the same. You are all the same."

Ye Wanwan looked coldly at Yanding and the sect master. "A pack of hypocrites hiding behind righteous faces!"

Ji Changhuai's face went white. "Shut your mouth!"

"And you." Ye Wanwan's cold eyes turned to Ji Changhuai. "What kind of fair and caring senior brother are you pretending to be? Don't you know how biased your own heart is? The moment Ye Qian cries, I'm the one who's wrong. The moment her eyes go red, I'm the one bullying her."

"Is she mentally disabled? How does she get bullied by me every time something happens?"

"Isn't she the genius you all praise to the heavens — talent that exceeds mine?"

"Then why is it that every time something goes wrong, the fault is mine?!" Ye Wanwan's voice rang out.

Ji Changhuai raised his hand in fury to strike again.

But Ye Wanwan caught his hand — and slapped him back twice.

Smack, smack.

Two crisp, resounding blows.

Ji Changhuai couldn't believe it.

Ye Wanwan pushed him backward. "That's interest on what you owe me."

Ye Wanwan's gaze went directly to those seated above.

"Dao Venerable Yanding. I don't believe you couldn't see the problem with Ye Qian's core formation. You saw it — and you still stood by and watched our match without intervening. I specifically asked for your opinion before the match!"

"You agreed."

"In the course of our match — I, a golden core early stage, shatter someone else's golden core early stage — and this gets spread around. Isn't that laughable?"

"You all know the truth perfectly well. You want to force me to admit fault, to clear a path for the Ye family's young miss."

"Impossible!"

Ye Wanwan's voice rang out.

Forceful as iron.

Even under Dao Venerable Yanding's pressure — as the weight on her shoulders grew heavier and heavier — Ye Wanwan still did not lower her head.

Ye Congyue's face was dark with fury. He sneered, "Sect Master Chengwen. Dao Venerable Yanding. Is this the disciple you cultivated?"

Clang.

A jade token — the mark of a personal disciple — was taken out by the girl.

She held it up.

Released it.

Clang.

The token hit the ground.

Ye Wanwan smiled with sharp contempt. "Not anymore. It's not that I was expelled from the sect. It's that this sect — is too filthy. I have no desire to remain."

The sect master's expression was flat.

"Do you know what happens when you betray the Supreme Sect?"

Ye Wanwan met his eyes. "It isn't betrayal. It is voluntary departure. Voluntary renunciation of the sect, forfeiture of cultivation and meridians, with a permanent prohibition from setting foot in the Supreme Sect."

Ye Wanwan smiled. "But my cultivation — has already been forfeited."

"What I learned from the Supreme Sect, I give back to you entirely."

"I owe you nothing more!"

"Insolence!"

The full force of the aura was unleashed.

Ye Wanwan was blown out through the cottage door by the impact. Ji Changhuai, Dou Ming, and Ye Qian all went rigid with fright. Particularly Ye Qian.

Her whole body was trembling.

Ye Wanwan crashed down on the veranda.

She climbed back up. "Even if you intend to kill me and silence me, I still say——"

"I did not shatter Ye Qian's golden core."

"It was Ye Qian's core formation that failed, and the blame was placed on me!"

"The Ye family's purpose was to take my golden core!"

"The Supreme Sect aided and abetted them!"

"Blind and heartless!"

"Dao Venerable Yanding — you have betrayed your disciple's trust. You are not worthy of being a master!"

Her words rang out, one by one, across the lake.

Every disciple fell silent.

Ye Wanwan raised her gaze. "If I, Ye Wanwan, should one day disappear — then it was Ye Qian and the Ye family who killed me. And the Supreme Sect was their accomplice!"

Yanding's expression was dark and unreadable. "You won't admit fault?"

Ye Wanwan's voice was ice cold. "I would rather die than admit it."

What good would admitting do?

Bearing a false name, barely surviving — and in the end, still being driven from the Supreme Sect. If that was the outcome regardless, she would not admit it. She would rather die than admit it!

"Very well."

"Confine her to the Black Water Prison."

Within the Supreme Sect, there were two places disciples feared most.

One was the Black Water Prison.

One was Xuanbing Cliff.

Both were the heaviest punishments in the Discipline Hall, reserved only for disciples who had committed grave offenses. And the Black Water Prison, compared to Xuanbing Cliff, was even more terrifying.

The absolute darkness and water confinement could drive a person mad.

Ye Wanwan gave a low laugh. "Dao Venerable Yanding. I am no longer your disciple. You have no right to punish me."

"Take her away," Yanding said coldly.

Ye Wanwan was dragged off.

She didn't struggle. She just let the two disciples drag her, looking toward Ye Congyue as she went. She saw the killing intent in his eyes.

Her lips moved slightly. "Trash."

The killing intent in Ye Congyue's eyes surged even more.

"Master!"

Ji Changhuai knelt, weeping. "Let Seventh Junior Sister go."

Dou Ming looked at the blood-covered Ye Wanwan, his expression dazed. She had...... snapped? But then he turned and looked at Ye Qian, trembling all over.

Dou Ming froze.

Could it be......

That Ye Wanwan had really been wronged?

The room fell silent.

No one dared speak.

But in less than half an hour, the two disciples who had taken Ye Wanwan rushed back. "Sect Master — Ye Junior Sister has escaped!"

"Escaped!"

Everyone was stunned.

"How did she escape? Wasn't her cultivation completely destroyed? Two of you together couldn't hold one person?"

"This......"

One disciple hesitantly produced half a burned talisman and said, "It was a talisman."

The room fell silent again.

Ji Changhuai was astonished. "Talisman cultivation? Since when did she learn that? Our Supreme Sect has no talisman cultivators."

No one knew how Ye Wanwan had learned.

But with the confirmation that she had secretly studied an outside discipline, the charge was clear. The entire Supreme Sect sealed the mountain gate and began searching for any trace of her.

Yanding looked at the half-burned talisman in his hand, his expression dark and difficult to read.

It was Elder Yu Chun who, hearing the news, let out a long and quiet sigh. "The Supreme Sect has made a grave mistake this time."

The Supreme Sect had no talisman cultivators.

But the archive pavilion had books on talismans — left behind by the ancestors.

Several years ago, Yu Chun had happened upon Ye Wanwan in the archive pavilion a few times — the girl reading and drawing talismans at the same time.

He still remembered it clearly to this day.

A disciple with this level of extraordinary talent — and the Supreme Sect had pushed her away.

While the entire Supreme Sect was in an uproar searching for her, Ye Wanwan had gone alone to Xuanbing Cliff.

By the time Ji Changhuai and Dou Ming received word and arrived, Ye Wanwan was already standing in the wind. She looked at all the disciples who had come chasing after her, and seemed to be smiling.

Ji Changhuai and Dou Ming's hearts were trembling. "What are you doing? Come back."

Ye Wanwan's lips curved. Her eyes held a cold and distant light as she repeated, once word at a time: "I did not shatter Ye Qian's golden core."

"Ye Qian wronged me and stole my golden core."

"They forced me to admit fault. I would rather die than admit it." Ye Wanwan looked at them, her gaze deep and steady, enunciating each word clearly: "I — would rather die — than admit it."

As she spoke, in the disbelieving eyes of the crowd, she stepped back, one step at a time.

"I would rather die than admit it!"

With Ye Wanwan's leap, her voice echoed back from the cold wind.

Every disciple was struck with shock and horror. Ji Changhuai lunged forward. "Get back here!"

But Ye Wanwan could not come back.

What lay at the bottom of Xuanbing Cliff — everyone knew.

Before Ye Wanwan even hit the ground, the fierce wind of Xuanbing Cliff would tear her apart. Not even her bones would remain.

Ji Changhuai's outstretched hand could never reach the shadow of that figure — he could only see her mocking eyes.

Ji Changhuai's heart — with a crack — felt as though something important had shattered.

Junior...... Sister.

chapters.title: Using Nothing But Brute Strength, She Leveled Half an Inn
chapters.content:
Three months later.

Anding City.

A girl in plain white robes blended into the crowd and entered the city.

Upon arrival, she first went to a medicine hall and sold a portion of her spirit grass. The spirit stones she received were traded for talisman paper, keeping only a handful of broken stones for travel expenses.

Then she sat down at a noodle stall and ordered a bowl.

And began to eat.

The steam rising from the noodles slowly brought the warmth of the ordinary world back to her.

She let out a long, quiet breath — even finding time to feed the river turtle she had brought out with her.

This girl was none other than Ye Wanwan, who had leapt into Xuanbing Cliff three months ago and been presumed dead.

Xuanbing Cliff was a death ground — but at the very bottom, there was a slim thread of survival.

In her last life, she had escaped the same way. So this time, Ye Wanwan had gambled.

Before going with Ji Changhuai to admit fault, she had already packed all her belongings from the bamboo house and gathered the spirit grass from the medicine garden into her qian kun pouch.

That leap from the cliff.

It had been a gamble.

A gamble on whether she could still live.

And fortunately, this time, she had once again seized that thread of survival.

Even more than that — because she had been thrown into a life-or-death situation, in the instant she leapt into Xuanbing Cliff, Ye Wanwan had broken through the bottleneck of foundation establishment.

Core formation — successful.

But unlike anyone else — she had five golden cores.

Her golden core stage restored.

Yet Ye Wanwan was a little puzzled.

Because outside those five golden cores, there were also five small, faint currents of energy.

She had also re-entered the qi refinement stage.

Not into the golden core early stage, but falling back to qi refinement. Yet Ye Wanwan tested it — and she could still draw upon the power of all five golden cores.

Which meant her actual combat strength was still at the golden core level.

But her realm was qi refinement.

"I can't make sense of this."

If she condensed these five new energy currents into cores — would she have ten golden cores?

Ye Wanwan: "......" Truly unheard of.

Author's note: Don't worry, there will be more later.

Unable to figure it out, Ye Wanwan stopped trying.

She finished her noodles and left, pulling her bamboo hat over her face.

Anding City was still within the Supreme Sect's territory. She couldn't stay long.

She hadn't walked far.

When the medicine hall proprietor returned and saw the spirit grass stacked beside the counter, he asked the assistant in astonishment: "Where did you get this?"

"A young Daoist brought it in."

"Where are they?"

"They left."

The proprietor rushed to the door, but Ye Wanwan was already nowhere to be seen. He asked the assistant urgently, "Why didn't you call me?"

"But Proprietor, this is just regular spirit grass, isn't it? You always say these things, we can decide on our own......"

"Regular? Have you ever seen regular spirit grass stay this fresh after being picked? This is peak-grade spirit grass. Only a heaven-grade spirit plant master could cultivate this — no market price exists for it!"

The assistant scratched his head. "But...... that Daoist just now looked like a small qi refinement stage disciple."

The proprietor froze. "Qi refinement stage?"

That was impossible.

A heaven-grade spirit plant master had to be at least nascent soul stage.

......

Out of the city, Ye Wanwan walked toward Chengshan.

Heading steadily further from the Supreme Sect's territory.

As for the strange anomaly in her dantian, after much deliberation Ye Wanwan had decided to go find someone to ask.

After dying in the modern world, she had been reborn into this body. From age five onward she had been on Qingyun Peak, never once coming down the mountain — so she had very little experience in this wider world. But in her last life she had wandered for years and had some impression of the major landmarks across the nine continents. Following the roads she remembered, she walked for a stretch, then flew for a stretch.

Drawing quite a few stares.

"Remarkable — a qi refinement stage junior can fly now?"

"Isn't flight through magical instruments only possible at foundation establishment?"

"Since when can qi refinement stage do this?"

Ignoring the puzzled remarks around her, Ye Wanwan arrived at Chengshan and entered Jinshi Town.

"Excuse me, elder, do you know of anyone in town by the name of Li Wanzhi?"

She asked at seven or eight households. No one knew.

But she wasn't in a hurry. She had patience.

In her last life, she had met Li Wanzhi a hundred years later. She had heard Li Wanzhi mention in passing that he had gone through a difficult period at Chengshan in his younger days, and only after that had he founded the Hundred Knowledge Sect.

And become the most mysterious sect in the world.

Hidden in the shadows, controlling the secrets of every cultivator across the nine continents. Not even the imperial clans and great noble houses had escaped their eyes.

Intelligence networks spanning the entire world.

Right now, however, he was — well — presumably still struggling through his difficult period.

Ye Wanwan asked all afternoon. As the sky grew dark, she entered an inn and found a seat. She ordered one rice dish and one vegetable.

Having fallen back to qi refinement, her body still needed food.

"Dark already — that ghost thing's going to come out again."

"Everyone shut your doors quick!"

Bang.

The moment Ye Wanwan picked up her chopsticks, every inn and shop in the surrounding area slammed their doors and windows shut at once, and the noise went completely silent.

Ye Wanwan: "......"

Proprietor: "You eat, go ahead, it doesn't affect you."

So Ye Wanwan quietly continued eating.

But a strange creaking, crunching sound made everyone in the inn's scalps prickle.

The proprietor held out a long time before asking cautiously: "Would you prefer not to eat, Daoist?"

Ye Wanwan: "...... That's not me."

The three of them turned. The source of the sound was a table near the doors and windows — covered entirely in empty bowls, two or three rows deep. The tallest row had more than ten stacked bowls, quite conspicuous, blocking the face of the woman sitting there. A man beside her had his face buried in his hands, apparently not wanting to be seen either.

"Senior Sister, people are looking at you."

"Oh."

The girl in blue looked back at them, held their gaze for a moment, then slurped up another mouthful of noodles. The sound was pleasant — and very deliberate.

She was not the source of the strange noise.

Ye Wanwan looked more carefully and located the crunching sound: it was coming from something tied to the corner of a nearby table. The creature — with a human-like face and a sheep's body — was straining mightily to pull free.

But the blue-clad girl kicked it back under the table.

Ye Wanwan's pupils sharpened.

A young taotie.

One of the four great ferocious beasts. A descendant of taotie bloodline.

Though its mixed heritage made it weaker than a true taotie, it was not to be underestimated. And the creature loved to consume gold and jade — which meant feeding it required gold and jade.

Extremely expensive.

If its needs weren't met, its temperament could be explosively violent.

The two young people before her were no older than twenty — and yet they had caught a young taotie.

Ye Wanwan studied their clothing. It looked like some sect's uniform, but she couldn't recall which one.

She had never seen them before.

But at their age, to have captured a young taotie meant they were not ordinary figures. They would not have gone unnoticed among the major sects.

While Ye Wanwan was studying them, Bai Jian and Fang He'an were studying her back.

Bai Jian: "Eats so little. Obviously can't fight."

Fang He'an: "The spirit grass in her sleeve looks like pretty good quality. A spirit plant master?"

All three of them made eye contact, then looked away.

The noise inside the inn had quieted.

The noise outside grew louder.

A fierce, howling force came straight for the inn. Boom — it slammed directly into the doors, windows, and the two people sitting in the corner. "Give me back my gold jade!"

A shout that rattled the ears.

With the windows shattering, the white figure came rolling in and charged straight for the long table. Fang He'an didn't hesitate — he jumped up and ran. Leaving the girl to face the enemy head-on.

The proprietor, the assistant, and Ye Wanwan all looked confused.

Fang He'an, with an air of someone who Knows Things, leisurely explained: "This is our sect's tradition."

Men flee. Women fight.

The two behind him had already traded blows, quickly ending with the white figure's surprise attack failing — because the girl threw one punch and sent the attacker flying out the window.

The white figure stood on the windowsill, stamping with rage and shouting curses.

"Tianyi Sect people — I never did anything to you! Why did you capture my little one?!"

Ye Wanwan paused.

Tianyi Sect?

One of the former top three sects.

Word was this sect only accepted geniuses, refusing anyone who didn't qualify. They had never been short of criticism from other sects for this policy. But as their ranking in the grand competitions had continued to fall — from first, to third, to seventh, to tenth, then out of the top twenty — they had eventually disappeared from the records altogether.

There were even rumors that they had completely collapsed.

And in the world afterward, she had never heard another word about them.

Ye Wanwan hadn't remembered this detail.

Had this sect simply vanished entirely?

The white-clad man couldn't win, and was stomping furiously outside the door. The worse his curses got, the sharper they became. Bai Jian leisurely wiped the corner of her mouth and stood.

Fang He'an saw this and sensed imminent disaster. His eyes nearly popped out. "Second Senior Sister! Don't!"

"We can't afford to——"

Before he finished.

Bai Jian had already smashed the long table with one palm, charged at the windows. Her frame was not large, but the way she moved brought a storm-like force with her, making the entire inn shake and tremble. The entire row of windows collapsed at once.

The young man who had been standing at the window went along with them into the rubble.

A fist wind surged toward him. He stared blankly.

"Hold——"

Fang He'an's last word fell. Bai Jian's foot came to a stop. She turned and looked at the half-leveled inn, opened her mouth, and said, "Forgot."

But Ye Wanwan had seen it clearly.

She had used no spiritual energy.

Using nothing but brute strength, she had leveled half an inn.

chapters.title: She Died Badly in Her Last Life
chapters.content:
"Sorry."

All three of them bowed a perfect ninety degrees toward the proprietor and Ye Wanwan.

Ye Wanwan: "......"

The young man in white was being forced down by Bai Jian. He struggled to get up. "You're the ones who smashed the inn — why do I have to apologize too?"

Bai Jian brought her palm down. The young man crashed face-first into the ground and didn't climb back out for a long while.

"......"

The proprietor shuddered, already near tears.

Fang He'an: "...... Don't be afraid, don't be afraid. My Second Senior Sister doesn't hit people."

But glancing back, Bai Jian was crouched beside the young man, digging a hole.

Fang He'an quietly repeated: "...... She really doesn't hit people."

The proprietor collapsed to his knees, hands raised high above his head. "Two great masters, spare us — we're only a small business, just tell us what you want, we'll give anything!"

Fang He'an: "......"

They really weren't here to rob anyone.

Fang He'an surveyed the damage and could only reach into his pockets for spirit stones. But he had only two left on him. He looked back awkwardly and asked, "Senior Sister, do you have any?"

Bai Jian hauled the young man in white over. "No. But he does." Without ceremony she reached into his pockets and pulled out a pouch.

"Those are my spirit stones!" the young man yelled.

"Now they're mine," Bai Jian said.

Ye Wanwan's gaze stopped on the young man. She studied him for a long time, then asked, with some uncertainty: "Li Wanzhi?"

"Hm?"

All three looked at Ye Wanwan.

"You know each other?"

Ye Wanwan glanced at all three of them. So these three people were all...... people she knew?

Fang He'an and Bai Jian emptied their pockets — still not enough to cover the damages. Li Wanzhi flatly refused to contribute his own money.

Fang He'an: "Can't you even lend it?"

"Can you pay me back?"

Fang He'an: "......"

The two of them were about to come to blows again.

Ye Wanwan walked to the broken door and windows and murmured quietly: "It doesn't need to be this complicated."

She took out a piece of talisman paper from her sleeve.

Used cinnabar to quickly draw a talisman.

A restoration talisman glowed to life.

With a whoosh, an invisible force gathered the door and windows back together, each one returning to its original position.

Fang He'an and the proprietor both stared with their mouths wide open.

Even Bai Jian's eyes lit up.

"So impressive."

But.

The words had barely left her mouth.

Two of the windows came crashing back down.

The street outside was silent.

Ye Wanwan considered. "The talisman paper quality was a bit lacking."

Fang He'an: "...... It's fine, it's fine."

The remaining windows were repaired by Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi together, hammering and clanging deep into the night.

Bai Jian made to help, and Fang He'an waved her off with a silent gesture: "Second Senior Sister, we've got the small stuff."

Li Wanzhi was drenched in cold sweat.

If they let Bai Jian help, this whole street wouldn't survive.

Bai Jian could only hold the little taotie and wait by the door.

Ye Wanwan stood watching from the side.

Bai Jian was long-limbed, lean but clearly muscled. Standing next to Ye Wanwan, she looked not only healthier but half a head taller.

So Bai Jian's gaze toward Ye Wanwan carried a faint trace of sympathy. She reached into her chest pocket and held out a steamed bun.

Ye Wanwan blinked.

"Saved it before dinner. Clean."

Ye Wanwan looked at her hand. She knew Bai Jian had noticed that she hadn't touched her food and drink before the inn was destroyed.

She reached out and took it. "Thank you."

Bai Jian grinned. "You're welcome."

The smile flashed into her eyes, and Ye Wanwan's mind lurched — and suddenly a flood of information came:

"Bai Jian. The Tianyi Sect's one hundred and first generation personal disciple. Born with divine strength. Possesses a heaven-grade earth spirit root. Betrayed by her lover. Her spirit root and heart-lungs torn out. Not even a whole body left."

A memory flashing past, and with it, Bai Jian's face — eyes open, unwilling to die.

Ye Wanwan's face went pale.

The steamed bun slipped from her fingers.

Before it hit the ground, someone caught it.

Bai Jian caught it, looked at Ye Wanwan, and placed the bun back in her hand. That warm skin-to-skin contact, and the warmth in her voice, stood in stark contrast to the brutal image in her mind.

Which only made Ye Wanwan tremble more.

"Your face doesn't look good. Did he do something to upset you? I'll beat him up for you."

The pointed-at Li Wanzhi: "......"

He was about to jump up and shout back, but Fang He'an pressed him down. "When did you bully a young girl?"

"Me?" Li Wanzhi pointed at himself in disbelief. "You're talking about me? What have I bullied? I don't even know her."

Fang He'an wore a look of: You really expect me to believe that?

"She came all this way to find you specifically — you must have done something. Otherwise why would she be here?"

Li Wanzhi threw down his tools, so angry he wanted to start yelling. But out of basic decency toward Ye Wanwan being a girl, he muttered and grumbled, "I just refused to join your Tianyi Sect. You can't go around ruining my reputation over that, can you?"

Fang He'an: "Look — she's about to cry."

Li Wanzhi was self-righteous: "That has nothing to do with me."

"Really crying now — a tear, there it goes."

"I really don't...... know her."

Li Wanzhi's voice grew less and less confident. He could see Bai Jian's palm coming and leapt three feet in the air to avoid it.

Seeing Ye Wanwan's eyes genuinely reddening, he darted in front of her, waving his hands. "Hey hey hey — I couldn't possibly have really wronged you, right? This really is our first meeting, as far as I can recall. The most I've ever done in my life is sneak into Tianyi Sect and take a few of their things — nothing from you."

Li Wanzhi was thoroughly flustered.

Even Fang He'an stood at the doorway not knowing what to do.

Ye Wanwan raised her hand and touched her face, and only then realized she had actually shed tears. She found it a little strange and said: "Too much wind. Got in my eyes."

Li Wanzhi was practically ready to kneel.

"If you don't say something soon, my reputation in this life is finished."

After a whole night of commotion, the doors and windows were finally repaired. The four of them wasted no time, leaving Jinshi Town before dawn.

Li Wanzhi kept as far from Ye Wanwan as possible, but Fang He'an deliberately shouldered him over. "Get over there."

"Then give me back little Gold Jade."

"Confiscated."

The two of them bickered back and forth. Li Wanzhi felt Ye Wanwan looking at him the whole time, the hairs on his back standing straight.

But no matter how he thought about it, he couldn't figure out what connection he could possibly have with Ye Wanwan. A girl this pretty — if he had ever met her, there was no way he'd have forgotten.

Ye Wanwan kept a straight face. "We knew each other in a past life."

Bai Jian and Fang He'an exchanged a meaningful look. "Oh~"

Li Wanzhi: "......"

Li Wanzhi spat, "If it was a past life, how would you remember?"

"I remember." Ye Wanwan looked at him. "Everything you've done since you were three years old — you told me yourself. I remember all of it."

Li Wanzhi was thrown off. He opened his mouth. "I don't believe you."

Ye Wanwan said quietly: "You also said — whenever I'm in trouble, I can come to you. You'll always protect me."

Ye Wanwan looked at him.

Her eyes were clear and bright.

"Does that...... still count?"

"......" The denial wouldn't come out. Li Wanzhi scratched his hair, even more puzzled than before. "Sounds like something I'd brag about. But I never said it. Right? This is definitely our first time meeting."

Fang He'an looked between the two of them. "Second Senior Sister, what do we do?"

The sect master had told them to bring back one Li Wanzhi. Did they now need to bring back an extra one?

Bai Jian said without hesitation: "Take them both."

chapters.title: A Junior Sister Picked Up for Free
chapters.content:
The Tianyi Sect.

It was located in the south while the Supreme Sect was in the north.

The two places were extremely far apart.

Bai Jian, flying on her sword alone, carried three people and one beast for three days and three nights before finally passing the Qinling Mountains and arriving in Tianyi Sect territory.

Back on her own ground.

Bai Jian and Fang He'an visibly relaxed.

The group rested in the trees for a night so Bai Jian could recover her spiritual energy. For this purpose, Fang He'an produced a hundred flatbreads.

"Senior Sister, eat."

Bai Jian finished them all in half an hour.

At first light the next day, Bai Jian brought the three of them through the boundary formations of Tianyi Sect's mountain range and flew straight toward the sect's main peak.

A continuous, endless mountain range came into view — an imposing sight even from a distance.

Unlike the graceful peaks of the Supreme Sect.

Tianyi Sect's mountains were grand and sweeping. The summits were capped with white snow. At this time of year, green was nowhere to be seen — mostly grey and white — yet this did nothing to diminish their towering, forbidding grandeur.

However.

Before they reached the main peak, an enraged shout arrived first.

"Who dug up my herbs again?!"

"Who!"

Hearing this, Fang He'an's face fell. "We were in such a rush when we left — I dug up Xun Yin Senior Uncle's herbs to use as travel expenses. I completely forgot to say anything."

Bai Jian looked at him. "You're finished."

Fang He'an sent his sword flying forward. "Senior Uncle—— it was me——"

The commotion from the high peak, chaos and shouting faintly carried by the wind, reached them. Ye Wanwan looked down from her sword at the endless mountain range below — spiritual energy flowing, earth energy thick and present, but the mountain face was red.

Not the vivid red of flames.

The red of utter poverty.

Li Wanzhi was profoundly discouraged. "Getting dragged in here by them — you and I are both done for in this lifetime."

Ye Wanwan looked at him, eyes saying: How so?

Li Wanzhi saw her look and knew this person had no idea what he was talking about.

"You don't know about Tianyi Sect?"

Ye Wanwan: "I do."

"Then you know what they're famous for?"

"Geniuses."

"No. Being poor."

Ye Wanwan: "......"

Li Wanzhi, hand on his chest, stricken: "I've never seen a sect this poor in my life. So poor they can't even afford to eat properly."

"You tell me, how are you supposed to live in a place like this?"

Li Wanzhi lowered his voice and proposed to Ye Wanwan: "When we get a chance, run. Whatever you do, don't stay."

Ye Wanwan said nothing.

She wasn't planning to stay anyway.

But would a Li Wanzhi like this really know how five spirit roots ought to be cultivated?

Ye Wanwan was skeptical.

Had she come too early?

Bai Jian flew ahead, and in moments, her sword cut through the air like a streak of light, bringing all of them down onto the main peak.

She flew too fast. After landing, Li Wanzhi spun around several times and spent a full quarter-hour retching.

While Ye Wanwan's expression remained completely unchanged.

Ye Wanwan: "......" Her skepticism deepened.

"You're both qi refinement stage. Her rank is higher than yours — how are you this weak?" Bai Jian said matter-of-factly, though her words stabbed Li Wanzhi like knives.

Li Wanzhi gritted his teeth and turned aside. "What level are you at?"

Ye Wanwan: "Level one."

Li Wanzhi: "......"

How did a qi refinement level one cultivator manage to use a restoration talisman?

Ye Wanwan's expression remained unreadable, as if she hadn't noticed his disbelief.

What did level one matter?

Level one could still draw talismans.

Bai Jian seemed to receive some kind of transmission, tilted her head to listen for a moment, then told the two of them: "Follow me. The Sect Master wants to see you."

Ye Wanwan paused. "Is it all right if I don't go?"

Bai Jian: "No."

So Ye Wanwan had no choice but to follow Bai Jian. Li Wanzhi was dragged along.

She had expected to be taken to a great hall, but Bai Jian changed direction and headed toward a building on a side peak instead.

And then the smell of food drifted over.

Ye Wanwan guessed: "The kitchen?"

Bai Jian said matter-of-factly: "Yes. This is the disciples' dining area. Those below the core formation stage haven't attained bigu, so Tianyi Sect also has a dining hall."

Ye Wanwan understood.

But meeting the sect master in a dining hall — wasn't that a bit unusual?

"This is right around breakfast time. And today is senior brother's duty shift."

Bai Jian entered.

When a voice came from within.

"Li Yan went out, I'm covering today." A cold, blank face came out from the kitchen, carrying a large pot of white rice.

No side dishes.

Upon seeing him, Bai Jian paid her respects without a hint of surprise: "Senior Uncle Yan Qu."

Li Wanzhi, despite his usual arrogance, straightened up at the sight of this cold-faced man and gave a proper bow.

"Senior...... Senior Uncle......"

Ye Wanwan was not a Tianyi Sect member, but she was young enough that she followed Bai Jian's lead and gave a junior's bow. "Junior Ye Wanwan pays her respects to Senior."

Yan Qu heard the voice and fixed his gaze on Ye Wanwan. His eyes suddenly flickered. "This young one......"

"Newly taken in?"

Bai Jian said: "Yes."

Ye Wanwan: ?

Yan Qu's gaze was sharp and penetrating, seeming to see straight through things. Ye Wanwan frowned and looked back at him.

But Bai Jian stepped in front of Ye Wanwan, blocking Yan Qu's appraisal. "Senior Uncle, you're frightening her."

Yan Qu gave a noncommittal sound, but withdrew some of his attention. "Sit."

The three of them took their seats.

Li Wanzhi, accepting his fate, took a bowl and began scooping rice, handing one bowl to Ye Wanwan too. "Eat. Any later and there won't be any left."

Ye Wanwan looked at the rice, not particularly hungry.

Bai Jian scooped herself a bowl and set it aside. Then, with a clang, she picked up the entire pot.

Seeing Ye Wanwan look over, Bai Jian asked: "Want more?"

She was being generous — she scooped a large ladle and pressed it down into Ye Wanwan's bowl, causing the rice to spill over the sides. Then pressed it down firmly.

After which she placed the entire pot in front of herself, as if guarding her personal property.

Ye Wanwan: "......"

Yan Qu and Li Wanzhi looked thoroughly unsurprised.

No one had started yet. The bowl Bai Jian had scooped out was clearly for Fang He'an.

As for the bowl Yan Qu had set aside — who that was for was unknown.

Laughter came from the kitchen. "Little Bai, you're back."

Bai Jian nodded in greeting: "Shifu."

Tianyi Sect's Sect Master Li Mingde came out carrying two large platters of meat dishes, set them down in front of Bai Jian and the others. Seeing Li Wanzhi, he smiled warmly: "Good work on the task."

Li Wanzhi drooped.

Sect Master Li continued, smiling: "Little one, don't be down. Stay at Tianyi Sect and you won't be at a disadvantage. You won't regret it."

Li Wanzhi muttered: "I doubt that."

In the month since joining the sect, he had been taken advantage of more times than he could count.

The sect master's gaze moved past Li Wanzhi and fell on Ye Wanwan — with a trace of surprise. "And this is......"

Bai Jian: "Junior sister."

The four others at the table fell silent. Only Yan Qu continued looking thoughtfully at Ye Wanwan, not contradicting this.

Bai Jian said: "I brought her back. Junior sister."

Ye Wanwan couldn't help speaking up: "Senior Sister Bai, I......"

She had come to have a look.

Just to figure out what that omen had meant.

But somehow she had ended up a junior sister.

Bai Jian turned her head to look at her. "You don't like me?"

Ye Wanwan: "No, not at all."

Bai Jian: "You don't like Tianyi Sect?"

Ye Wanwan: "...... Can't say I do either."

Bai Jian: "Good. Shifu, she agreed to stay."

The four at the table: "......"

Such a straightforward exchange, completely free of roundabout reasoning, made even Li Mingde laugh. "Good. Then stay."

Ye Wanwan: ? No one actually asked me, did they?

And yet the exchange between master and disciple had settled the matter just like that.

Ye Wanwan had no opening to speak.

Fang He'an rushed back in. "I didn't miss mealtime, did I? Oh, Xun Yin Senior Uncle penalized me, starting tomorrow I have to go help him replant all the herbs. Anyway—"

Stepping through the door, Fang He'an saw the two unfamiliar figures at the table. His voice suddenly became very formal. "Sect Master Senior Uncle, Senior Uncle Yan Qu, I request permission to go help Senior Uncle with the herbs every day."

Sect Master Li Mingde chuckled. "Little An, come meet your junior sister."

"Hm?"

Fang He'an looked at Li Wanzhi, then at Ye Wanwan. "Junior sister?"

Bai Jian and Yan Qu: "Right now."

Fang He'an: "......" What on earth had happened while he was away?

chapters.title: Girls Get Different Treatment
chapters.content:
Ye Wanwan looked around the table and understood that this was settled.

Because no matter what she said, everyone just piled food into her bowl.

"Eat."

"You're too thin."

The long-missed warmth made the words Ye Wanwan wanted to say about leaving slow to a halt.

She watched Sect Master Li Mingde smile warmly at everyone eating around the table — especially when his eyes fell on Bai Jian, full of pride.

The pride of an elder looking at their own child.

It was a feeling she had never once gotten from Yanding.

Pride......

Feeling seen......

Ye Wanwan found herself without words, and simply lowered her head and ate.

Let it be for now.

She was going to leave eventually anyway.

Bai Jian finished an entire pot of white rice — perfectly clean. Even the sauce at the bottom of the vegetable bowl was soaked up with the rice. Not a single grain wasted.

And yet her stomach barely showed it.

Nobody knew where she put it all.

When she stood, she patted Ye Wanwan on the shoulder. "Come with me."

Ye Wanwan glanced at Li Mingde and the others, but the elder smiled warmly. "Go on, child. She'll show you around."

Ye Wanwan gave a bow and was whisked away by Bai Jian — as if she were afraid Ye Wanwan might bolt.

Out of the dining hall, Bai Jian brought Ye Wanwan to see where disciples attended class, where they trained, the archive pavilion, the alchemy chamber, the artifact-forging chamber, and the disciples' quarters. Bai Jian even wanted to take Ye Wanwan to meet the other senior uncles on their respective peaks.

"Why?" Ye Wanwan asked.

Bai Jian turned at the unexpected question and looked at Ye Wanwan. The confusion in the girl's eyes was too clear to ignore. "I never said I was staying."

Bai Jian looked into her eyes. "You have nowhere to go."

Ye Wanwan froze slightly.

Bai Jian pointed at Ye Wanwan's chest. "In here, you're saying — you have nowhere to go."

Ye Wanwan's heart clenched.

Bai Jian smiled — a little warm, a little gentle and reassuring. "Here is good. Stay."

Ye Wanwan looked at Bai Jian. The young woman was two or three years older than her — but nothing about her felt worldly-wise or seasoned.

Bai Jian didn't seem like she was twenty. More like a girl of eleven or twelve.

She had been well protected.

Ye Wanwan moved into the disciples' quarters.

Since she hadn't yet formally taken a master, she would stay on the main peak for now. Once she did, she would choose a different mountain peak to live on.

After listening for a while, Ye Wanwan had pieced together the picture: the entire Tianyi Sect had fewer than twenty people in total.

Because Bai Jian said that she herself had an entire mountain peak — to herself.

For training purposes.

"Though I don't usually go to my own peak. I mostly stay here."

Ye Wanwan thought.

This sect didn't look like it was without means.

Even on a small peak like Qingyun, they couldn't afford to give every disciple their own mountain.

"We don't have much else, but land we have plenty of. If you want to grow something, you can grow it anywhere."

Ye Wanwan nodded.

Bai Jian: "I have something to take care of — I need to go report to Shifu. You rest. I'll take you somewhere this afternoon."

Ye Wanwan: "All right."

Ye Wanwan sat alone in the room. Through the open window, she looked out at the landscape. The sun was just right, falling on a plum tree ahead — dark branches, white snow, touched by gold.

Like a thread of light, dancing into her eyes.

Ye Wanwan was thinking.

Could she stay here?

Bai Jian was right — she really didn't have a home anymore.

Not in the modern world.

Not here either.

Ye Wanwan laughed softly at herself.

She sat cross-legged and began the day's cultivation. Large and small heavenly cycles completed, Ye Wanwan's realm had stabilized at qi refinement level one.

One step away from the second level.

Ye Wanwan drew some talismans, attached them to the walls of the room, and in one sustained effort, pushed toward the second level.

Two hours passed.

When the small current of energy expanded by one ring.

Qi refinement level two was smoothly entered.

"Done."

Ye Wanwan examined her dantian inwardly.

Five golden cores circulated nearby, following some pattern. And the five small wisps of energy — the red and blue currents were slightly larger.

The other three were comparable in size.

Fire root: peak of level two.

Water root: mid level two.

Metal, wood, earth: early level two.

Ye Wanwan nodded.

"Good enough."

When she surfaced from her trance, it was already late afternoon.

The time she had arranged with Bai Jian had long passed.

Ye Wanwan thought about it and stepped out of the courtyard door.

When she pushed it open, she found someone outside.

Li Wanzhi and Fang He'an were crouched in the courtyard — she had no idea how long they had been there.

Fang He'an said wistfully: "In all my years at Tianyi Sect, aside from Senior Brother, you are the most diligent person I have ever seen."

Li Wanzhi looked thoroughly baffled. "You just went straight into training? Honestly, is your life really this boring?"

Ye Wanwan rolled her wrist. "Nothing better to do."

Both of them said in unison: "You could have just slept."

Ye Wanwan: "......"

Fang He'an shook his head. "If I'd known, I would've dragged you to Xun Yin Senior Uncle's herb garden with me. At least it's something to do when you're bored."

Li Wanzhi simply jumped over the fence and entered the courtyard. "You're not seriously thinking of staying here, are you?"

Fang He'an looked at him. "And you're planning to run again? Sect Master Senior Uncle said — born a Tianyi Sect person, soul of a Tianyi Sect forever. You can't run."

Li Wanzhi sprang up and yelled back: "I've said it already — forget the refund on the tuition fees! Why are you still holding me here? It was my father who paid, not me! Go after him!"

Fang He'an said with absolute seriousness: "Money paid means obligations fulfilled — that's our sect's principle. You as a junior brother, we've claimed you. That's final."

Li Wanzhi was on the verge of exploding.

But Fang He'an paid him no attention whatsoever. He flicked his finger, sending a small pill flying into Li Wanzhi's mouth.

In an instant, the world went silent.

Li Wanzhi strained and strained and couldn't make a sound, flailing wildly at Fang He'an.

Fang He'an explained cheerfully to Ye Wanwan: "Just a failed pill. Extremely useful for shutting people up."

"Junior Sister, Second Senior Sister had something come up. She asked me to take you to the Marrow-Cleansing Pool."

Ye Wanwan was taken aback. "The Marrow-Cleansing Pool? I can go?"

That was a sacred place of the sect!

Even in the Supreme Sect, only disciples who placed in the top three at sparring competitions of the same realm were eligible to enter.

Ye Wanwan had almost made it every year in her second year and beyond.

But every time, because her senior brothers had never been, she gave up her own opportunity and let them have it — thinking there would always be another chance.

Until Ye Qian arrived, and she never had another chance again.

"Of course." Fang He'an smiled. "Every incoming disciple goes."

He pointed.

"Junior brother, too."

At those words, Li Wanzhi's whole body shuddered. Cold sweat broke out immediately.

Pure fear.

The Marrow-Cleansing Pool was right on the main peak. They didn't need to fly — they could walk.

Fang He'an led them through a purple bamboo grove. On the other side of the grove was a long staircase that could fit two people walking side by side.

Up the steps, stopping at the three hundred and seventy-seventh stair, then turning left onto a mountain path for another hundred or so paces — and there was a cold pool.

"Here we are."

He then walked around behind Li Wanzhi.

And gave him a firm kick straight into the water.

Then clasped his hands behind his back and said gently to Ye Wanwan: "Junior Sister, no need to worry. Girls get different treatment."

Ye Wanwan: "......"

Li Wanzhi, who had splashed in, opened his mouth — seeming to be screaming — but not a single sound came out.

Only silent howling.

Yet the cold mist rising from around him was proof enough that the pool's tempering effect on him was intense.

His entire body was steaming.

chapters.title: If They Didn't Start Taking Disciples Soon, There'd Be No One Left
chapters.content:
Cold mist billowed.

It swallowed Li Wanzhi whole in an instant.

Li Wanzhi sputtered out a string of bubbles and sank entirely. Fang He'an counted the time and then hauled him out.

"Stronger than before — sixty breaths this time. Twenty more than last time."

Li Wanzhi lay on the ground, eyes rolled back, not saying a word.

Ye Wanwan watched this and completely abandoned any notion of asking this person about cultivation methods for five spirit roots.

The current Li Wanzhi clearly didn't have the capabilities he would have in later years.

She had already mentally prepared for this.

But the gap was so enormous that it was still hard to accept.

Ye Wanwan was also curious, though.

What would Li Wanzhi go through to become the person he was in the future — cold, silent, and counting every coin to the last.

The current Li Wanzhi was just a money-grubber.
