A hundred years from now, would this person really become the master of intelligence?

Ye Wanwan thought the village gossip ring might have a spot for him.

A prominent spot.

"Junior Sister, come here." Fang He'an smiled warmly and amiably. But having seen the precision of the kick he had delivered to Li Wanzhi, Ye Wanwan didn't dare underestimate him.

This senior brother's foot had extraordinary accuracy.

Fang He'an spoke with warm gentleness: "This is the Marrow-Cleansing Pool. It can cleanse and refine your meridians. But everyone's constitution is different, so everyone reacts to it differently. Since it's your first time, you don't need to stay long — just go in and feel it out."

"If you feel uncomfortable, tell me. Senior Brother will come help."

He also handed Ye Wanwan a set of clean clothes.

And a purple ribbon — the mark of a Tianyi Sect disciple.

"You're a girl, so Senior Brother will wait for you at the bottom of the steps. If anything happens, just call out — I'll hear." With that, Fang He'an picked up Li Wanzhi by the collar and left.

Even Li Wanzhi's wet clothes hadn't been changed.

"You're already at qi refinement level five. You should have learned by now how to dry clothes with a technique."

"Mmmm."

"Why aren't you saying anything?"

"...... Aaah."

"Did the pool scramble your brain?"

Ye Wanwan considered: should she tell him that the pill he had fed Li Wanzhi was still working?

The two of them left the cold pool, descending the stone steps one by one.

Until Ye Wanwan could no longer see them.

She set the clean clothes on the ground.

But within moments, a stone platform rose and held her clothes gently aloft.

And translucent silken curtains drifted closed on all sides, shielding this corner of the pool from view. Even the chill from within was softened slightly.

Ye Wanwan's expression shifted. "A formation?"

Her treatment was nothing like Li Wanzhi's.

The girl removed her outer robe, kept her inner layer, and stepped in, barefoot.

She had expected the marrow-cleansing pool to be piercingly cold. It was not.

It was warmth.

Warmth that curled around her ankles and wound its way upward. Ye Wanwan felt no discomfort — only gentleness.

She tested it. It didn't feel bad at all.

So she simply jumped in.

Warmth!

That was Ye Wanwan's first sensation.

The warmth of the entire pool dispelled the chill of early winter — and the cold of having nowhere to go.

Her body and spirit fully relaxed.

She even suspected Fang He'an had been teasing her. This wasn't a Marrow-Cleansing Pool — it was a hot spring. But the threads of force that slipped into her meridians were real — healing the damage left behind from when she had destroyed her own cultivation.

Filling in every tiny crack.

Making the meridians as wide as a river channel — free for spiritual energy to surge through freely, and finally rush into the dantian with full force.

Strengthening those five wisps of mist.

Meanwhile, on another part of the mountain.

Yan Qu and Li Mingde were discussing something. "I want that child. Give her to me."

Li Mingde, whose face was usually wreathed in smiles, showed a rare expression of difficulty. "Martial brother, it's not that I won't give her to you. You're the first person in all our years together to ask me for a disciple — of course I'd try to satisfy you. But this child — you can't teach her."

Yan Qu's eyebrows shot upward immediately. "Can't teach her?"

Not won't give — but can't teach.

Now that was even more of a provocation.

Li Mingde: "Mm. Can't teach her."

Yan Qu crossed his arms, displeased. "Martial brother, use some other excuse to brush me off. But this one — I'd like to understand what you mean by can't teach."

Li Mingde rubbed his chin. "Have you noticed the girl's spirit roots are rather unusual?"

"Heaven-grade spirit roots," Yan Qu said, arms still crossed. "I noticed."

Which was precisely why he had come.

Such a fine seedling was extremely rare.

And that constitution and toughness she carried — rarer still.

A prodigy this exceptional — and the thought that no one from outside had apparently recognized it left Yan Qu genuinely stunned.

But since fate had brought her to Tianyi Sect, this child couldn't be allowed to fade into obscurity.

"Yes, heaven-grade spirit roots," said Li Mingde, his tone carrying a trace of deeper meaning. "But also five spirit roots."

Yan Qu went still.

"For a person to have one heaven-grade spirit root is already extraordinarily rare. And this girl doesn't have one — she has five."

Yan Qu was silent for a long while, staring at Li Mingde in astonishment. He knew his martial brother didn't make mistakes in his assessment.

But heaven-grade five spirit roots......

"You're right that I can't teach her." Yan Qu wasn't discouraged — he was genuinely puzzled. "But Martial Brother, why did you agree to let Little Bai keep her?"

Heaven-grade spirit roots were exceptional.

But heaven-grade five spirit roots — that was another matter entirely. There was a name for it: wasted spirit roots. No matter how one cultivated, it was impossible to ever break through the nascent soul stage. At best, one would remain at golden core for the rest of their life.

Unless four of them were destroyed, leaving only one.

But this method was forbidden in the immortal cultivation world.

Because no one knew whether the remaining root, after the other four were destroyed, would still be able to cultivate. Or whether the preserved root would maintain its original grade.

No one had ever tried.

And no one dared take the risk.

Tianyi Sect certainly would never do so — it would be destroying her talent, defying the natural law.

Li Mingde smiled warmly. "You and I can't teach her — but there is someone who can."

The moment Yan Qu heard this, he knew exactly who Li Mingde meant. He fixed Li Mingde with a look of deep significance. "Martial Brother — let that idea go."

"He has said, in this lifetime, he will never take a disciple."

Li Mingde chuckled. "Maybe there are exceptions."

Yan Qu raised an eyebrow and crossed his arms. "A wager?"

"All right." Li Mingde appeared to think it over briefly. "If you lose, you take Li Wanzhi as your disciple."

Yan Qu: "...... That is a vicious bet."

Li Mingde smiled and asked: "Do you concede, Martial Brother Yan Qu?"

"I'll bet you, because I don't believe he'll agree to it." Yan Qu stood and left the hall. Walking a few steps out, he said flatly: "I'll be off the mountain for a few days and back. The mountain is in your hands while I'm away, Martial Brother."

Li Mingde asked: "Something the matter?"

Yan Qu said: "The provisions in the kitchen have only three days' worth left. I'm going down the mountain to earn money."

"...... Thank you for your trouble, Martial Brother."

Yan Qu said coldly: "Martial Brother should also ask Xun Yin when he expects to grow crops. If he can't grow them soon, we won't be able to buy any."

Li Mingde was embarrassed. "We've all been in bigu for so many years, we've long since forgotten how to grow the five grains. Xun Yin has been trying his best these ten years."

"I'll try my best too."

Yan Qu said nothing more, turned, and left without looking back.

Raising a group of young ones — truly no easy matter.

These fellow martial brothers had never raised disciples before. Because one day, after years of secluded cultivation, they had suddenly realized — if they didn't start taking disciples soon, the Tianyi Sect would truly have no successors left!

The one hundred and first generation of disciples — there would be no one!

Who could have imagined that the thing to finally drive Tianyi Sect's elders out of their mountain seclusion would be this?

chapters.title: Marrow Cleansing and Spirit Infusion
chapters.content:
The Tianyī Sect was short on people.

Even after decades of searching for talented candidates, those who actually made the cut were few and far between.

So when a disciple with exceptional spiritual roots walked straight to their doorstep — why would they ever let him go?

Li Mingde stroked his beard. "A fine talent indeed. Of course we have to find a way to keep him."

......

Meanwhile, at the Marrow Cleansing Pool.

Fang He'an had been crouching on the stone steps waiting so long that his nerves were getting the better of him. He asked anxiously: "How long has she been in there?"

Li Wanzhi answered uneasily: "About a quarter of an hour."

Fang He'an shot to his feet. "A quarter of an hour? That long!"

Li Wanzhi: "It is pretty long."

He himself had wanted to get back out the moment he went in.

How was this little girl managing to soak for so long?

Fang He'an paced back and forth. "The person from our generation who stayed in the Marrow Cleansing Pool the longest on their first visit was Second Senior Sister — and even she only made it half a quarter of an hour. This one is almost at a full quarter."

Something was wrong.

"I have to go check."

If she'd fainted in there, that would be a disaster.

Fang He'an took the steps two at a time and rushed to the edge of the pool, ready to shout.

Just then, sounds came from within.

Rustling.

The kind of sound someone makes when putting on clothing.

Fang He'an immediately turned around.

Li Wanzhi, who had followed him up, asked, "What happened, what happened? Did she faint? Should we call someone?"

Fang He'an pressed a hand over his head and turned his face the other way. "It's fine. Junior Sister is coming out."

Yè Wǎnwǎn had indeed come out.

She'd changed into a Tianyī Sect robe, which earned nods of approval from both Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi. "Much better than before."

Before, Yè Wǎnwǎn had looked like a stray cat.

Distinctive bearing, yes — but the kind that said she had no home.

With this robe on, it was a completely different feeling.

A sense of belonging.

And as though the Tianyī Sect robe had been made for her from the start.

"Junior Sister has made a one–spirit-stone robe look like it costs a hundred," said Li Wanzhi, circling her with a golden jade abacus that had appeared in his hands from nowhere.

He flicked the beads. "If you sold clothes, you'd make a fortune."

Fang He'an shoved his head away. "Quiet, you money-obsessed creature. The robes aren't for sale."

Yè Wǎnwǎn clasped her hands in thanks to both of them, then explained: "Thank you, Third Senior Brother. I'm fine — it's my first time in the Marrow Cleansing Pool, so I was curious and stayed a bit longer than I should have."

Fang He'an understood.

So she'd been testing the waters from the edge, working up the nerve to get in.

He had experience with that.

Li Wanzhi had spent a full hour dithering before his first time, which was why Fang He'an had eventually lost his patience and just kicked him in.

The more Fang He'an looked at his Junior Sister, the more he liked her. He smiled. "My seniority in Tianyī is third. If you don't mind, call me Third Senior Brother. Senior Sister Bai is second. We also have a First Senior Brother — but he's away. I'll introduce you later."

"And this is Junior Brother Li — he's fourth, which makes you sixth. Little Six." Fang He'an pointed at Li Wanzhi.

Yè Wǎnwǎn thought: what about fifth?

Li Wanzhi voiced exactly what she was thinking. "You skipped over five."

"Fifth Junior Brother has been reserved by a Sect Elder, but the person hasn't been brought back yet. You probably won't meet him for a while."

Fang He'an said this while already leading the two of them down the stairs, heading for their next destination.

"Reserved? Not brought back yet? I don't like the sound of those words." Li Wanzhi drew a sharp breath. "Don't tell me he was kidnapped too?"

Fang He'an gave him a sideways look. "It's different from your situation. Fifth Junior Brother has a stubborn streak, so our Elder said it would take some coaxing — at least three visits before he could be persuaded, ahem, brought back."

"But you're different."

Fang He'an grinned. "You were delivered by your own father."

Li Wanzhi: "......"

Li Wanzhi had the distinct feeling Fang He'an was saying: you're the one who walked straight into the lion's den on your own.

Fang He'an led Yè Wǎnwǎn and Li Wanzhi away from the Marrow Cleansing Pool and into another building.

From the outside, it looked like no more than two or three stories.

Inside, there was only a single floor.

A single vast platform that stretched all the way up to the dome — more than eight zhàng from floor to ceiling.

Standing there, a person felt very small.

"We're here," said Fang He'an.

Li Wanzhi, upon arrival, showed no resistance at all. He found a spot and settled comfortably flat on his back, then told Yè Wǎnwǎn, "This is way better than the Marrow Cleansing Pool."

Yè Wǎnwǎn looked around.

She couldn't see anything particularly special about it.

Fang He'an stopped at the doorway and went no further. He smiled. "Just let yourself feel it."

As Yè Wǎnwǎn stepped onto the platform.

Light cascaded down from the dome far above.

Countless streams of spirit energy surged and swirled across the platform, condensed through a formation, and poured into the bodies of Yè Wǎnwǎn and the others.

Marrow Cleansing — followed by Spirit Infusion.

This was Spirit Infusion!

After Marrow Cleansing, the meridians expand. At that moment, if a powerful Spirit Infusion formation is used to condense the spiritual energy of heaven and earth, disciples can absorb it rapidly during that window, consolidating and strengthening their meridians.

In exceptional cases, a disciple's first Spirit Infusion can shatter the limits of an ordinary person entirely, carrying them straight into the Qi Refinement stage — creating what was known as a miracle.

Though Yè Wǎnwǎn and Li Wanzhi were no longer quite at the beginner stage, the effects of this formation were still immensely valuable to them.

The combined effects of Marrow Cleansing and Spirit Infusion were far greater than the sum of their parts.

But even the Marrow Cleansing Pool was extremely rare. The Spirit Infusion formation was rarer still.

Extraordinarily expensive.

Even a supreme sect like Wúshàng Sect, with all its resources, could only construct a small Spirit Gathering Formation near their Marrow Cleansing Pool — just enough to let newly cleansed disciples experience the enhanced absorption that came after tempering.

And yet the Tianyī Sect.

Were remarkably generous.

So generous that Yè Wǎnwǎn felt, truly and genuinely, wealthy.

Exceptionally wealthy.

Because they weren't using a Spirit Gathering Formation. They were using a massive Spirit Infusion Formation — one purpose-built within an ancient structure, which had absorbed the essence of sun, moon, and mountain range over countless years, and when needed, simply released it all at once.

To infuse their disciples with spirit.

Receiving this cascade of spiritual energy from every direction, Yè Wǎnwǎn murmured softly: "Tianyī Sect — your foundation runs very deep."

Nothing at all like what they showed on the surface.

Li Wanzhi grumbled, "Just living off old savings. Give it a bit more time here and you'll see how poor they really are."

"Even if they're poor — the fact that they put the two of us through the Marrow Cleansing Pool today, and then brought us into a Spirit Infusion Formation, tells you they are remarkably generous with new disciples."

In other sects, disciples who had been cultivating for a decade might never get this kind of opportunity.

Like Yè Wǎnwǎn herself — all those years at Wúshàng Sect.

And she had never once set foot in a Marrow Cleansing Pool.

Li Wanzhi, for once, didn't argue back.

Yè Wǎnwǎn didn't know how long the Spirit Infusion Formation would stay open. She seized the time — breathing, absorbing, the five spheres of energy inside her rotating swiftly.

With the reinforcement of both Marrow Cleansing and Spirit Infusion.

Her fire spirit root, which had already broken through to the third level inside the pool, was now under the additional outpouring of infused spirit — and was quietly charging toward the fourth.

Li Wanzhi beside her was no slower.

The aura of his fifth-level Qi Refinement was growing more concentrated, with the unmistakable signs of an imminent breakthrough.

But Li Wanzhi seemed entirely unaware of it. In this warm flood of spirit energy, he had already fallen fast asleep. Never mind deep breathing or guided meditation — he didn't even have the inclination to sit up and pretend.

Yè Wǎnwǎn: "...One who does not know their own fortune."

An hour later.

Fang He'an came to collect them, grinning cheerfully. The bits of grass and leaves clinging to him made it clear he hadn't spent the hour idly waiting.

"Time's up. Come on out."

By now, the sun was sinking in the west.

Fang He'an took them to the dining hall, and then saw them back to the disciples' quarters.

The sun had fully set by then.

Fang He'an said: "Today is Junior Sister's first day in the sect. You were also on the road all of yesterday. Tonight, rest well. Tomorrow I'll take you to start morning lessons."

At that, Fang He'an also smiled and offered Yè Wǎnwǎn a word of welcome: "Junior Sister — welcome to Tianyī Sect."

"I'm sure you'll look forward to the days ahead."

Li Wanzhi pressed a hand over his right eyelid. "Left twitches for fortune, right twitches for disaster. My right eye is twitching. This is a bad sign."

Fang He'an simply grabbed Li Wanzhi and hauled him away.

"Let's go, Junior Brother. Your room is next to mine. Long time no see — let Senior Brother catch you up on everything you've missed."

Li Wanzhi: "......"

The courtyard fell quiet. Only Yè Wǎnwǎn remained.

She went inside as she always did — alone.

Something was moving inside her qiánkūn pouch.

Yè Wǎnwǎn remembered. "Nearly forgot about you."

She took out the dark tortoise and found a basket. "Make do with this for now. Tomorrow I'll find you a proper home."

The dark tortoise looked at her for a moment, then slowly crawled into the basket without complaint and settled itself there — mainly because Yè Wǎnwǎn had thoughtfully tucked in a handful of xuán spirit grass.

Yè Wǎnwǎn sat down in quiet meditation.

Her first day at Tianyī Sect had passed without incident.

The next morning.

Bái Jiǎn came and knocked on the door.

chapters.title: Fang He'an, Killed by a Mob of Blades
chapters.content:
Yè Wǎnwǎn heard the knock and opened the door immediately.

"Second Senior Sister."

Bái Jiǎn's raised hand paused mid-knock. "You're up early."

She tilted her head and looked Yè Wǎnwǎn over. Seeing her already in her sect robe, alert and composed, she gave a fairly satisfied nod. "Come on. I'll take you to morning lessons."

Yè Wǎnwǎn had already prepared herself for a day of listening to instruction.

But Tianyī Sect's morning lessons were nothing like Wúshàng Sect's.

Because it wasn't a matter of listening to a master lecture, or sitting in breath-guided meditation — it was.

Fellow disciples hitting each other.

Yes.

Definitely distinctive.

Fang He'an said: "Junior Sister has misunderstood. This is sparring. Fellow-disciple sparring."

Li Wanzhi had already been dragged onto the practice field for round two of his daily refinement.

That gaze — full of longing and desperate pleading — fell on Yè Wǎnwǎn as he reached a hand out toward her.

Fang He'an pressed it back down.

Each knuckle of that outstretched hand being pressed back in sequence looked exactly like Li Wanzhi's will to be rescued being snuffed out, one flame at a time.

"I'm a pill cultivator, not a body cultivator. If you can't even take a punch from me, how are you going to cultivate at all? You need to train, Junior Brother Li."

Li Wanzhi wept.

Yè Wǎnwǎn's gaze lingered for a moment — she watched Fang He'an lead Li Wanzhi through a few exchanges, only for Li Wanzhi to dodge frantically and take a hit to the cheek in two moves. By the third and fourth move, he was already a wreck.

He clearly had no foundation at all.

"He won't die."

Bái Jiǎn's voice came from beside her. Yè Wǎnwǎn turned, and saw that Bái Jiǎn had also changed into training clothes. "Let me test your skills first."

Yè Wǎnwǎn nodded.

"Alright. Please go easy on me, Senior Sister."

The two of them moved to opposite ends and faced each other.

It was the early morning of winter's onset, and still slightly cold.

But when the two young women's eyes met, a few sparks seemed to fly between them, warming the practice field.

Not the kind born of hostility — but the kind born of two people who had found a worthy opponent.

They moved quickly.

Fists met.

The impact resonated from knuckle to wrist to forearm, and Yè Wǎnwǎn felt the full force of Bái Jiǎn's strength in that single exchange. In this one moment, she nearly couldn't hold her ground and stumbled backward.

But she caught herself after half a step.

Yè Wǎnwǎn: "You're very strong."

And yet the eyes she raised shone with excitement.

Bái Jiǎn, too, was eager to continue.

Having each gauged the other with one punch, the two of them launched into their second exchange. Fists whistled through the air, grazing past each other's knuckles.

In the midst of Yè Wǎnwǎn's constant evasion, she somehow managed to catch every one of Bái Jiǎn's sudden attacks.

Bái Jiǎn's strikes were simple — yet somehow never followed a predictable path.

Under these conditions.

They went one exchange, then another.

Three.

Four.

Five.

......

Their figures moved faster and faster, trading solid blows. The sound of real, unsparing hits finally brought Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi's exchange to a complete stop.

"This is the first time I've ever seen anyone make it past ten moves with the Great Demon without getting launched," Li Wanzhi said, sitting on the ground, his eyes vacant.

Only the afterimages of the two figures reflected in his gaze.

Fang He'an was equally stunned. Bái Jiǎn's strength was, among their generation, something only First Senior Brother could rival — and First Senior Brother himself had mentioned it: within the same cultivation stage, without using spirit energy to protect the body, in a pure test of physical strength alone, he was outmatched by Second Senior Sister.

And yet now.

How was there a Junior Sister who could keep pace with her too?

A genius.

Good.

Worthy of being a Tianyī Sect disciple.

When Yè Wǎnwǎn and Bái Jiǎn's sparring reached eighteen moves, Yè Wǎnwǎn conceded. "Stop."

Bái Jiǎn's fist halted one cun from Yè Wǎnwǎn's face, eyes still bright — but with a thread of confusion at her junior sister's action. Why stop?

Yè Wǎnwǎn pulled her lips into a smile. "I concede, Second Senior Sister."

Bái Jiǎn tilted her head. "Why?"

Yè Wǎnwǎn held out both fists.

Only then did Bái Jiǎn notice her hands were trembling.

"My hands hurt."

Fang He'an came over and sucked in a sharp hiss. "Bone fracture! Senior Sister!"

Bái Jiǎn's expression shifted.

Yè Wǎnwǎn smiled. "It's fine. A bit of rest and it'll be good."

Li Wanzhi nearly choked. "Bone fracture and you say rest a bit? You think you're a god? You're in Qi Refinement — an injury like that takes at least two weeks to heal."

Li Wanzhi fell into contemplation.

Hold on.

This person was clever.

Using fractured bones as an excuse — that meant two weeks off morning lessons.

How had he not thought of that?

He should've faked a serious injury from the start.

Fang He'an cut off his fantasy with a menacing tone. "Don't even think about it, Junior Brother Li. Your constitution is different from everyone else's. You could die and still come back alive."

Li Wanzhi: "......"

Yè Wǎnwǎn: "......?"

Die and come back alive?

Unkillable?

Bái Jiǎn took Yè Wǎnwǎn aside to apply medicine. Fang He'an dragged a whimpering Li Wanzhi back to continue the morning lesson.

"I... didn't control my strength."

Yè Wǎnwǎn saw the remorse in her eyes and offered reassurance: "It's alright, Second Senior Sister. It really will be fine in a moment."

Bái Jiǎn glanced at Yè Wǎnwǎn and asked carefully: "When it heals — will you still spar with me?"

So that was it.

Yè Wǎnwǎn smiled. "I will."

Bái Jiǎn let out a breath of relief.

The only person who could spar with her was Lí Yàn.

But Lí Yàn wasn't here. Without him, she had no sparring partner.

Life without an opponent for morning lessons was rather miserable.

Yè Wǎnwǎn rested to the side with her injury, watching Bái Jiǎn and Fang He'an work Li Wanzhi over. As she observed, she found that Li Wanzhi's constitution was indeed something special.

No matter how hard Fang He'an and Bái Jiǎn hit him.

His injuries recovered quickly.

His energy stayed inexhaustibly full.

He went down fast — but got back up just as fast.

And his rate of improvement was visible to the naked eye.

From withstanding only three moves against Fang He'an at the start, to four, then five — each session he progressed by a move or two. It didn't seem like much.

But in the fact that Li Wanzhi never appeared to tire.

Yè Wǎnwǎn began to think.

It seemed that in her past life, she hadn't known Li Wanzhi well enough at all.

An hour of morning lessons (which was really just a one-sided beating) came to an end. Bái Jiǎn led everyone to the dining hall — but Yān Jǔ wasn't there, and the kitchen was cold.

Fang He'an said: "It seems Senior Uncle has gone down the mountain to work. There are still steamed buns from before — let me go steam them."

Bái Jiǎn also went into the kitchen to help.

Yè Wǎnwǎn moved to pitch in, but the two of them refused on the grounds that she was injured.

Li Wanzhi just collapsed on the table and didn't move. The last breath left in him whispered weakly: "Food... food food..."

Fang He'an stacked five tiers of buns on the steamer, and said to Bái Jiǎn: "Senior Sister, the bottom four tiers are yours. The top one is ours."

Bái Jiǎn nodded and crouched down to start the fire.

Yè Wǎnwǎn watched her, and thought of the image that had flashed through her mind the other day.

But with Bái Jiǎn's ability — how could she have died so violently? With her temperament — who could she possibly have offended?

The woman before her was only two or three years older than she was.

And yet her way of thinking seemed to have stopped somewhere around the age of eleven or twelve.

A Bái Jiǎn like this.

Why would she end up dying such a terrible death?

Did the others in Tianyī Sect do nothing?

Yè Wǎnwǎn looked toward Fang He'an.

"Junior Sister, you must be hungry — here, eat this first." Fang He'an handed Yè Wǎnwǎn a baked flatbread. She reached out and took it — and in the instant of contact.

A new image appeared.

It was Fang He'an — being killed by a mob of blades.

chapters.title: The Black Book
chapters.content:
The dead of night.

Rain pouring in sheets.

Fang He'an stood in the downpour, his body covered in blade wounds. Blood from the cuts flowed in rivulets, washed down by the rain, pooling at his feet.

His eyes were open — as though looking in Yè Wǎnwǎn's direction. Within them was a trace of something like relief.

"...You're safe... that's enough..."

Yè Wǎnwǎn's pupils contracted.

She watched as the life left him, little by little — and all the while he looked at her, gently, right until the end.

The cold seemed to seep up from the soles of her feet and rise through her whole body.

She had never witnessed a scene like this before.

Yet in this instant, the grief and despair that seized her heart made every part of her go rigid with dread.

Fang He'an froze. He'd only handed her a flatbread. How had her face gone completely white in an instant?

Even powder couldn't work this fast.

"Junior Sister? Are you alright?"

Bái Jiǎn and Li Wanzhi also looked over with curiosity.

Seeing Yè Wǎnwǎn's face draining of color as though she'd been struck, Li Wanzhi was thoroughly puzzled. "Fang He'an, did you put something in the food again?"

"......"

Fang He'an was offended. "I didn't."

Though his confidence did waver slightly.

"My medicine pouch is banned from the kitchen. How could I have put anything in? Besides, these buns were left over from Senior Sister — she ate hers without any problem. There's no way they're bad for Junior Sister."

What bothered Fang He'an even more was that Yè Wǎnwǎn hadn't actually eaten any of it yet.

Even if there had been something in it, you'd have to eat it for anything to happen.

Yè Wǎnwǎn braced herself against the edge of the table and took a long moment to come back to herself. She looked at the flatbread Fang He'an had given her, still in her hand.

Two anomalies. Both times, immediately after one of them had given her something.

But what exactly was this?

Why was she seeing their deaths?

Was it the future?

Fang He'an swiftly took the flatbread back and tossed it away. "Don't eat it anymore, Junior Sister. Wait — you'll have hot porridge soon."

Fang He'an decisively began washing rice and starting a pot of porridge.

He also had Bái Jiǎn take Yè Wǎnwǎn out of the kitchen to drink hot tea while they waited.

When the porridge and buns were done, Fang He'an single-handedly carried five tiers of buns out.

Li Wanzhi had already gotten used to this impressive sight.

The group ate without much conversation.

Bái Jiǎn ate quickly.

When the meal was over, there were some small sect tasks to be assigned.

Fang He'an gave each of them one. Yè Wǎnwǎn was assigned to organize ancient texts. Li Wanzhi was to go with Fang He'an to Senior Uncle Xún Yǐn's plot to tend the spirit plants. Bái Jiǎn was to go reinforce the Mountain Protection Formation.

This was Bái Jiǎn's regular task.

Using the Mountain Protection Formation to temper herself, while also helping the formation grow stronger.

With the four tasks distributed, Fang He'an looked at Yè Wǎnwǎn's face. "Junior Sister, are you feeling better? If not, just go back to your room and rest — don't worry about the task today."

Yè Wǎnwǎn had long since restored her composure. "I'm alright. But Senior Brother — the organization of ancient texts is such an important task. Is it really fine for you to hand it to me?"

Even she, a complete outsider, knew that ancient texts were extremely valuable.

She was someone who had just been brought back, hadn't gone through any entrance ceremony, hadn't formally taken a master — for her to be trusted with organizing ancient texts just like that seemed a stretch.

Was Tianyī Sect really this casual about things?

"Of course it's fine. This is a task assigned by the Sect Master. Do it with peace of mind. Since you've come into Tianyī Sect, you're not getting away. We're not worried."

Fang He'an was completely unconcerned.

Li Wanzhi right there was a living example.

Those who tried to run were always brought back.

Yè Wǎnwǎn: "......"

Fair point.

Once outside, Fang He'an pointed her in a direction, and Yè Wǎnwǎn set off on foot.

The scripture repository was at the very top of the main peak.

Yè Wǎnwǎn walked the whole way up.

Over half an hour later, she entered the scripture repository. Not a soul was there.

Only ancient texts, strewn everywhere in complete disorder.

"......I can see this place hasn't been organized in quite a long time."

She began to sort through them, classify, and arrange.

But the thought from moments before still lingered at the back of her mind.

Why could she see their fates?

If these were Fang He'an and Bái Jiǎn's fates from her past life, how would she have witnessed them? She and they should have had no real intersection at all.

It was only in this life, because of Li Wanzhi, that she had been brought to Tianyī Sect and come to know them.

"Is it fate?"

"Or is there some kind of trigger?"

Yè Wǎnwǎn tapped the book in her hand, thinking. Both times, the common element had been a gift — something given to her. Perhaps next time, she could pay more attention to that.

Setting it aside, she turned her focus to organizing. She cleared through one entire cabinet quickly — but there were so many scattered texts.

Even half a day's work barely made a dent.

Yè Wǎnwǎn stretched.

Her eye was caught by an unnamed book wedged between shelves, its cover solid black.

At this angle, it seemed to faintly catch the light — a brief glimmer of gold.

She walked over and eased the book from the gap, then opened the first page.

Array diagrams.

And talismanic inscriptions.

But no detailed explanations.

A single torn page, however, caught her attention.

"Eye of Rebirth."

Yè Wǎnwǎn's gaze sharpened.

She quickly turned to the second page. It was gone — torn out. Blank. Nothing there.

She was puzzled.

She flipped through the entire book — nothing. She searched through the surrounding shelves — nothing. The remaining torn page simply wasn't there. "Was it always incomplete?"

Yè Wǎnwǎn looked back at the front page.

The text on it held only those four characters, and half a torn array diagram. Nothing else.

Then she felt it. Something strange.

She looked up abruptly. A pair of eyes was staring directly down at her from the crossbeam overhead. Yè Wǎnwǎn's expression went cold — the eyes were an absolute black, deep as a still pool.

As if watching her every move.

She reacted instantly, fire energy condensing in her palm.

But before she could release it.

The creature spread its wings and took flight.

In a moment it was gone, sweeping through the window and out of sight.

Yè Wǎnwǎn's gaze went cold. "A bird?"

Why was there a bird in the scripture repository?

She looked in the direction the black bird had gone and noticed one of the window lattices had been pushed half open — not fully closed.

So it had come in from there.

She pushed the lattice open wider. Sunlight fell onto the page bearing the words Eye of Rebirth, and Yè Wǎnwǎn's expression became unreadable.

The next day.

Yè Wǎnwǎn went to morning lessons as usual. This time in their sparring session, Bái Jiǎn held back considerably — but Yè Wǎnwǎn found it unsatisfying. "Go ahead and give it everything, Second Senior Sister."

Bái Jiǎn hesitated. "Your hands..."

"They're fine." Yè Wǎnwǎn struck out a punch and watched the force cleave the air cleanly, her fist completely unharmed. "Third Senior Brother gave me medicine yesterday. It worked very well."

"Alright."

Seeing this, Bái Jiǎn relaxed and let herself go without restraint.

Bái Jiǎn was a powerful body cultivator. Her defense and her offense were both exceptional tools for forging a person's physical form.

Ever since her golden core had been dug out, Yè Wǎnwǎn had been wanting to train her body.

Not to rival Bái Jiǎn — she made no such claim.

But at the very least, if her spirit energy couldn't be used, she wanted to be able to hold her own for a few moves — so that after Wúshàng Sect discovered her death-feint, she could run.

Bái Jiǎn, when sparring with them, had never used spirit energy once.

Morning sessions for fists and footwork. Afternoons for sorting texts. Evenings for inner cultivation and mind-tempering.

A month passed with Yè Wǎnwǎn settled into Tianyī Sect's rhythm. Then, after that month, Fang He'an seemed to want to say something but kept stopping himself. "Junior Sister, ah..."

Yè Wǎnwǎn set down her chopsticks. "What is it, Third Senior Brother?"

Fang He'an's words kept looping back from his lips, never quite making it out. Even Bái Jiǎn and Li Wanzhi looked over.

At last Fang He'an steeled himself and said: "The Sect Master wants you to go to Sword Mountain."

When the words fell, Bái Jiǎn and Li Wanzhi both went quiet for a moment, even the sound of their eating quieting.

chapters.title: Demonic Heart, or Conscience
chapters.content:
Sword Mountain.

Tianyī Sect's forbidden ground.

And the site of disciple trials.

Under normal circumstances, no trial began until a disciple had been in the sect for at least half a year. To be called this early could only mean one thing.

Yè Wǎnwǎn's talent was exceptional.

Yes.

Yè Wǎnwǎn could accept that.

In her past life, everyone had cursed her for ruthlessness, jealousy, cold-heartedness, betraying her sect and her roots — but no one had ever called her untalented.

Even after her golden core was dug out and she switched to the path of talisman cultivation, she had never been below the mark.

Her talent was legendary.

Seeing the furtive expressions the others wore, Yè Wǎnwǎn said: "Alright. I'll go now."

"No rush, no rush — finish eating first."

Fang He'an heaped food into her bowl, as though he felt genuinely sorry for her.

"Anyway, when you get there — hand the box to Elder Uncle Pèi Xuán, and then... be careful."

Yè Wǎnwǎn: "......"

Yè Wǎnwǎn agreed. "Alright."

She finished her meal and left.

Li Wanzhi immediately turned to Fang He'an in disbelief. "Her? Sword Mountain? Are you sure? I haven't been there, but my old man mentioned it once — Sword Mountain is only open to disciples who've been in the sect for a year. And she's only been here a month."

"One month. Can she actually pass whatever Sword Mountain puts her through?"

Fang He'an grumbled. "Do you think I'm the one sending her? It's the Sect Master. I'm just following orders."

"Fang He'an, you're brutal."

"Speaking of brutal — enter the sect for a year with no master willing to take you, and you'll have to leave."

Li Wanzhi perked up. "Really? That's wonderful."

"......Right. Perp-walk you down the mountain with broken legs."

"...Even with broken legs, I'm leaving."

"No backbone."

Li Wanzhi was indignant. "Would you, in my position — give up being a perfectly comfortable young master to come here and be someone's junior brother? And another thing — if I leave, my golden jade abacus comes with me."

"That is a mixed-blood beast that has inherited the blood of a great beast. You think you can take it? Abandon that idea."

Li Wanzhi cursed under his breath.

Fang He'an refused to budge an inch.

"She'll pass."

The sudden voice, coming from Bái Jiǎn's direction.

Li Wanzhi and Fang He'an looked at her in surprise. Bái Jiǎn's expression was unchanged. "Junior Sister Yè will pass."

Sword Mountain.

Also called Sword Tomb.

One of Tianyī Sect's forbidden grounds. Unauthorized entry was not permitted. Within lay the burial site of the spirit swords belonging to every Sect Master, Elder, and disciple across every generation of Tianyī Sect.

Regardless of how a person died.

After death, their sword would return to Tianyī Sect's Sword Mountain and join the others. More than a thousand swords gathered on a single peak.

Becoming one of Tianyī Sect's landmarks.

And the training ground for new disciples.

Yè Wǎnwǎn carried the lacquered box and stepped into the Sword Tomb. The moment she crossed the threshold, she felt a rush of sharp sword intent — sword will like wind, slicing past her on either side, one streak after another.

Grazing past her.

Severing the loose ends of her hair.

Yè Wǎnwǎn watched the strands drift to the ground. Her gaze lowered.

Her expression was calm.

Her steps were steady and practiced, moving one by one through the Sword Tomb. She felt the charged, readied sword intent pressing in from all directions. With every step, the young woman moved without faltering.

Not a single tremor.

The sharp clang of metal rang in her ears.

Countless voices gathered from all directions.

Yè Wǎnwǎn did not stop.

A talisman clutched in her palm, her expression unchanging.

Until the scene shifted. Yè Wǎnwǎn stood in a vast expanse of yellow sand. Ahead, a demonic beast came howling toward her — and a single figure stood before the city gates, sword in hand.

He stood there holding his blade.

Gazing toward what lay ahead without expression.

Ten thousand demon soldiers surged forward.

He raised his sword and cut them down.

Yellow sand, crimson blood, and the roar of countless voices — and still the man in his tattered dao robe stood at the city gates, unmoving.

Holding the line.

Then the scene changed.

The demon soldiers and their spears surrounding him had become the trembling, fearful faces of ordinary people.

"Don't blame us, Daoist. They said — if we kill you, they'll spare... spare the whole city. We just want to live."

"Daoist, you're an immortal. You won't die."

"We only need you to let us stab you once."

"Only when you die will they let us go. You've lived so long already — be magnanimous. Do this for us."

A notched kitchen knife came down against flesh and bone, dragging a sound that made the teeth ache.

And with each wound struck, blade after blade —

In moments, the young Daoist was a mass of blood and torn flesh.

Some of those striking him wept as they did it.

Some shouted forgive me and plunged their blades in anyway.

By the time he had fallen to his knees, the blades coming at him only kept coming — one person after another rushing forward, until someone threw open the city gates and screamed: "We've killed him — spare us!"

In that frenzy of voices, no one seemed to remember that this man had stood guard at those same gates for seven days and seven nights, keeping the entire city safe.

Yè Wǎnwǎn stood before the Daoist.

The young Daoist was perhaps in his mid-twenties. His face had once been clean-featured. Now it was impossible to make out. What remained was a formless mass of blood.

"Did I do wrong?"

That murmured question sounded like something wrung from the soul.

Yè Wǎnwǎn stood before him and heard his confusion.

"Did I... do wrong?"

The voice echoed in her ears, as though the question were being put to her. Yè Wǎnwǎn took a slow step forward, crouched down, and looked at the blood-soaked earth.

Her voice was detached.

"Act by your heart. Don't ask if it was right."

"If this was what you chose to do, then it wasn't wrong."

"Guarding the city is your Dao."

"Killing you is theirs."

That voice dropped. "Then is my Dao wrong?"

"Is it wrong?!"

It broke into a roar.

Yè Wǎnwǎn: "I don't know."

At that answer, the blood on the ground transformed into swirling demonic energy that tore upward into the sky, into every corner of heaven and earth, swallowing the city walls.

Blotting out the sun.

Demonic energy surged skyward, and the people cried out in terror. In this moment, inside and outside the city, there was nothing but demons. The only sanctuary had been destroyed by the very people within it.

The crying would not stop, and the demonic energy would not stop.

It swept toward everyone.

Including Yè Wǎnwǎn.

In this demonic energy was his resentment, his hatred, his incomprehension — every dark thing he had ever felt.

From it was born a heart-demon.

And within the heart-demon, Yè Wǎnwǎn saw that figure become herself.

Her brow tightened faintly.

"An illusion?"

"You were lying. This is your real answer." The voice was vicious, laced with dark satisfaction. "Return evil for evil — what else? Return kindness for evil — who does that?"

"Your heart is full of killing intent."

The voice laughed loudly.

As though mocking Yè Wǎnwǎn's hypocrisy.

This was Yè Wǎnwǎn's heart-demon.

Yè Wǎnwǎn's expression did not waver. She only took the blood-soaked flesh, buried it in a pit, as though maintaining some surface standard of morality — doing what a person of this position ought to do.

Burying the dead, raising a marker.

The black shadow twisted and warped, hovering beside her.

"You are full of hate."

"Hatred for the people who stabbed you in the back."

The surrounding townspeople abruptly became Jì Chánghuái, Dòu Míng, and Yè Qiàn. And blades came, one after another, each one straight through the heart.

Pain and suffocation welled up.

Yè Wǎnwǎn's color faded.

But the hand setting the grave marker did not stop.

"Clearly the most brilliant one on Qīngyún Peak was you. Clearly the most talented was you. Clearly the one who served the sect best was you — and yet no one has ever acknowledged your excellence."

"Everyone was biased toward the far more mediocre Yè Qiàn."

"You!"

"Were always the extra one."

Yè Wǎnwǎn's gaze went ice cold. "Shut up!"

"Ten years of cultivation and one golden core — they dug it out whenever they pleased. Your ten years of genius — they gave the title away whenever they liked. What did you get from any of it?"

"You got seven blades through the heart!"

"You should hate them far more than I do."

"Who are you pretending for?"

Yè Wǎnwǎn's eyes went cold, then gradually turned crimson. She dipped her fingers in the blood on the ground and began writing a name on the wooden marker — but what she wrote was not any person's name.

It was:

Conscience.

chapters.title: The Sword That Asks the Heart
chapters.content:
Conscience.

The black shadow faltered.

Yè Wǎnwǎn's expression was serene. "I have buried my conscience. From this point forward — a rebirth."

The shadow didn't understand.

But it watched as the young woman bent and picked up the sword that had fallen to the ground.

She raised it.

And stepped forward, one step at a time, toward those ghostly figures.

Ordinary people.

And the shadows of her sect.

She raised the sword.

She brought it down.

Kill.

The surging demonic energy, the piercing screams — none of it could stop the young woman who cut her way out from within the blood and mist.

"Guarding the city is your Dao."

"Killing you and turning to the demonic path is theirs."

"And slaying demons to uphold the right — that is mine."

Yè Wǎnwǎn stood beneath a rain of blood. Her voice was even. She looked back at the black shadow. "I won't save you. I don't know any art for saving souls."

"But I know one thing."

"The justice of this world does not stand on the side of the greater number."

"Do you see them as righteous?" Yè Wǎnwǎn pointed ahead at the townspeople, then laughed softly. "I see them as demons."

The shadow was silent for a long time.

Then its eyes began to slowly turn red.

"Kill," said Yè Wǎnwǎn.

Her lips barely moved.

"Killing can be a Dao as well."

Yè Wǎnwǎn raised her left hand, her fingers moving through the air. Talisman scripts manifested on their own — the vast force of a mountain-sealing talisman came crashing down from above, and in the blink of an eye, nearly a hundred figures were slain.

Among those hundred were the shadow of Jì Chánghuái.

The young woman did not flinch.

The sword swept through.

One by one they fell.

She walked across a mountain of bodies and a sea of blood, toward the opened city gate, pressing through the barrier of this disciple trial.

And as she stepped toward the gates, the entirety of Sword Mountain erupted.

Deep within the peaks, countless spirit swords began to vibrate in a frenzy. The surging demonic energy nearly tore past the suppression seals, threatening to consume the power of the mountain range itself.

Bái Jiǎn, who had been in the middle of practicing, went still.

Li Wanzhi and Fang He'an, who had been digging and planting, both stood frozen.

The mountain range trembled.

The Mountain Protection Formation, silent until this moment, activated on its own.

But the force it was responding to was not coming from outside.

It was coming from within.

"Something's wrong at Sword Mountain!"

Bái Jiǎn was the first to react. Without hesitation she ran toward Sword Mountain. Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi, equally alarmed, dropped everything and followed.

"Wait for me! I can't fly!"

Li Wanzhi was frantic.

Though he always felt Yè Wǎnwǎn had something weighing on her — she was still their junior sister. Li Wanzhi didn't want to see her come to harm.

Fang He'an called out his spirit tool, grabbed Li Wanzhi, and flew toward Sword Mountain.

Li Wanzhi spent a long moment staring at the spirit tool. Fang He'an's face darkened. "What are you looking at? Never seen such a distinctive spirit tool?"

Li Wanzhi muttered: "Haven't, actually."

Fang He'an: "......"

By the time they arrived, Bái Jiǎn was already there.

She was trying to break through Sword Mountain's seal and get inside.

But the formation was now fully activated.

Ten thousand swords trembled.

The earth qi shook.

Something extremely dangerous had been encountered within.

Bái Jiǎn couldn't get anywhere near it.

Yān Jǔ had arrived as well by now, brow furrowed deeply.

"Senior Uncle, hurry, look at this!" Fang He'an spotted him as though spotting a lifeline, quickly dragging him over. "Tell us what's happening!"

Yān Jǔ looked out at the demonic energy boiling over the mountain. "Who went in?"

"Junior Sister," Bái Jiǎn said quickly.

Fang He'an also rushed to explain that the Sect Master had sent Yè Wǎnwǎn into Sword Mountain. Yān Jǔ listened with a look of total bewilderment. "She's only been at Tianyī Sect — how long? And they dared send her into Sword Mountain?"

"Isn't she allowed? But the Sect Master gave the order."

"She can go — it's not that," Yān Jǔ's eyes flashed. "Sword Mountain holds the swords of every generation of Sect Masters, Elders, and predecessors. The Dao-force contained within them varies from sword to sword. Anyone who enters — if one of the ancestors' swords chooses them, having recognized their lineage in Dao, it's considered an inheritance. It's an opportunity."

"Then..."

Fang He'an stared at the scale of what was unfolding. "Was Junior Sister chosen by a sword?"

Yān Jǔ was quiet for a moment. "What I'm seeing is that she is being targeted by all the swords."

Three people: "......"

"What does that mean?"

Never mind Bái Jiǎn, who didn't understand the situation from the start — even Fang He'an was stunned. He'd been through Sword Mountain himself. But he hadn't caused anything remotely close to this.

His spirit tool had chosen him and he'd left. But right now...

Yè Wǎnwǎn's situation was clearly nothing like his.

"Being targeted by all the swords? Can Junior Sister still come out safely?"

The ancestral swords inside all carried Dao-comprehension within them. If they joined forces to attack — Fang He'an didn't dare think about what that would look like.

He only knew that the sword-formation array within was something even a Nascent Soul cultivator couldn't withstand, let alone someone in the early Qi Refinement stage.

Yān Jǔ was also curious. "I'd like to know — what did she do in there?"

To create this kind of commotion.

The disturbance at Sword Mountain drew every peak master to stop what they were doing and turn to watch.

"Haven't had this much excitement in years. Looks like the new talent the sect has taken in this time is something special. Quite the character."

"That damned demonic energy has frightened my seedlings half to death — did someone bring a demonic cultivator home? Compensate my seedlings!"

"Third Senior Brother, you're a technique master — can you stop trying to grow things? Leave the planting to people who are good at it."

"You think I want to? What the — "

A string of curses was cut off.

Everyone watched as the blood-cloud filling the sky above Sword Mountain was pressed down, only to surge upward again — rising and falling, again and again, refusing to stop. Several times the Mountain Protection Formation suppressed it.

But it kept surging back.

"This child's demonic heart is heavy."

"She'll never pass the Heart Asking Formation."

"Whether she passes is one thing. What I'm wondering is whether she can even come out alive."

Once killed by the Heart Asking Formation, not even the spirit soul could survive.

Opinions across the sect varied — puzzlement, astonishment, and murmured commentary — but not one person watching believed Yè Wǎnwǎn would make it through this trial.

Only Lǐ Míngdé, deep in his closed-door cultivation, said softly: "If this child passes this trial — she will soar to heights beyond imagining."

Another voice asked: "And if she doesn't?"

"Soul scattered. Nothing remains."

The sword in Yè Wǎnwǎn's hand had been soaked red with blood. The black shadow followed close beside her, watching her cut down every last one of those who had raised their hands against the Daoist.

Not one spared.

The demonic energy around the shadow was beginning, impossibly, to dissolve.

"That should be enough," said Yè Wǎnwǎn, tilting her head to look at it. "Is it really enough?"

"Since we've started — let's be thorough."

She looked toward the ten thousand demon soldiers outside the city. "Deal with all of them while we're at it."

The shadow: "......Wait."

"Who is the one going demonic here — you or me?"

Yè Wǎnwǎn gave a low laugh. "What's the difference between you and me?"

She looked up at the sky full of demonic clouds. "Here, you are me and I am you. And this isn't going demonic — this is the re-forging of our Dao-heart."

"One step forward — the sea is open, the sky is boundless. One step back — the angrier you get." Yè Wǎnwǎn flicked the tassel of her sword. "Since that's how it is — better one clean stroke, thought through to clarity, without a stain on the conscience."

"That is my Dao."

Yè Wǎnwǎn's eyes were completely clear. No trace of demonic energy.

Her actions proved what she meant — that killing was Dao, not demonic. And what she slew was not people. It was demons.

The shadow had returned to the form of the young Daoist. He floated in the air beside Yè Wǎnwǎn, murmuring quietly: "So my killing — was right."

Yè Wǎnwǎn met his eyes. "The sword in my hand has never taken a single innocent life."

The sword in my hand has never taken a single innocent life.

Those words floated slowly through the air, lingering at the city gates.

She looked back. The blood mist dispersed, and every fallen figure was one whose hands had been stained with blood — while huddled safely behind them, untouched, were the people of the city, clean and unharmed.

The young woman still stood at the city gates.

Behind her was light. Before her was the demonic horde.

She stood at the crossing between righteous and wicked paths — holding to her own Dao-heart.

And that was her Dao.

Neither purely righteous nor purely wicked.

The man in the blue-grey robe suddenly broke into laughter. It rang and rang through the air, and from deep within Sword Mountain, a green sword broke free — breaking out of the Sword Tomb, weathering the assault of ten thousand spirit-sword auras, crushing them all with the force of one, and erupting into the world.

Everyone in Tianyī Sect went pale.

"The Heart Asking Sword!"

Even Yān Jǔ was stunned for a moment.

She... had awakened the Heart Asking Sword.

chapters.title: Acknowledged by a Divine Weapon
chapters.content:
The Heart-Questioning Sword.

The personal sword of the second-generation disciple of Tianyi Sect, the ancestor known as Heart-Questioning — hailed as a once-in-a-thousand-years genius of Tianyi Sect, a mere step away from ascending to the upper realm. And yet in the course of a single trial, his Dao heart had been shattered, and he had died, his soul dispersing entirely.

No one had ever known why.

But his sword had remained behind from that day on.

Because it was soaked in blood and carried an overwhelming will to kill, it had always been sealed away in the deepest part of Sword Mountain — yet now, this divine weapon had broken its seal and flown free.

Not only did this astonish Yan Ju — even Bai Jian and Fang He'an could no longer make sense of what they were looking at.

"A divine weapon..."

"Has Junior Sister awakened a divine weapon?"

Yan Ju gazed at the Heart-Questioning Sword, which had suppressed the entire Sword Mountain formation and was now releasing its full radiance — its demonic energy crushing every other spirit sword, as though prepared to make enemies of ten thousand swords.

In order to protect the person inside the formation.

"What did she do in the Heart-Questioning formation?"

This question was not only Yan Ju's. Every elder watching was baffled.

At the summit of the snow mountain, a white-haired man with black eyes opened his eyes and looked toward Sword Mountain. A flash of light passed through them — nearly the colour of the blood cloud surging toward the sky.

"It returned..."

The murmur was scattered by the wind.

The Heart-Questioning Sword stood within the formation.

Inside the illusion, the yellow-sand city and walls had vanished entirely. The young Daoist floated in the air. "My heart's path is the righteous path."

Ye Wanwan tilted her head toward him, and answered without hesitation. "Yes."

"What I believe in is the Dao."

The young Daoist looked toward Ye Wanwan. "Young woman — is it the Path of Unfettered Freedom you wish to follow?"

Ye Wanwan shook her head. "No."

"I cannot transcend all things. I love money — even if I am not greedy, I carry resentment, jealousy, and desire. These are my negative feelings. I have never denied them."

"And I will not cut them away."

"Unfettered freedom of the heart is freedom — and yet it is not. I still do not know what it is. But I want to follow my own heart and seek out my own path."

"Whether it is righteous or shadowed, I am the one who decides."

"My path is not defined by anyone."

Ye Wanwan's expression was calm, her gaze fixed ahead. Even as yellow sand stretched endlessly before her, even as shadowy figures threatened to dissolve at any moment, her eyes never once wavered.

"Well said!"

The young Daoist called out in approval, his eyes bright as he looked at Ye Wanwan. "Then I will walk with you a while, and explore the path of this life together."

The yellow sand before her split open.

A sword came cutting through the air and fell before her. Not the one she had picked up at random earlier — this was an ancient blade, entirely blue from tip to hilt.

No ornamentation. Simply a sword.

And yet it radiated a powerful demonic energy.

Ye Wanwan glanced sideways at the Daoist. He raised an eyebrow in teasing challenge. "Afraid?"

The provocation tactic.

Far too low.

But undeniably effective.

"You said it yourself — your path should not be defined by others. And neither should that sword be defined as a demon sword or an immortal sword. It depends entirely on who wields it. The Heart-Questioning Sword asks not of your path — only of your heart."

Ye Wanwan reached out.

And gripped it.

The blue sword shuddered violently, as though trying to break free. But Ye Wanwan did not let go. One hand was not enough, and so she held it with both.

The five golden cores in her dantian spun at full force, five streams of spiritual energy pouring out from within, wrapping around the sword and around her, helping the fusion of one person and one weapon.

The young Daoist watched from the side, his expression serious, though touched with appreciation.

Every elder watched as the demonic energy on the Heart-Questioning Sword began to dissolve piece by piece. The five-element force coiled upward, transforming into a surge of brilliant white light that illuminated the entire Sword Mountain.

Li Mingde, Xunyin, and Yan Ju all straightened at once.

Radiant immortal light. The Heart-Questioning Sword formed a character.

It read:

"Immortal."

Fang He'an stared at the character hanging in the sky. "Immortal aptitude."

Li Wanzhi was blank. "What does that mean?"

"Mortal, spiritual, immortal — these are the aptitude rankings given by the Heart-Questioning formation. Mortal level is ordinary people with no capacity to cultivate. Those like us who can cultivate are usually ranked at the spiritual level, which is subdivided into the four tiers of heaven, earth, black, and yellow. I am earth-spiritual. Senior Sister is heaven-spiritual. And above heaven-spiritual, there is one more level called immortal. But..."

"In all these years, it has only appeared once in Tianyi Sect."

"That was the founding ancestor who has already ascended."

Li Wanzhi raised his fan to cover his face. "Does this mean Junior Sister Ye is extraordinary?"

Fang He'an said quietly, "Extraordinary does not begin to cover it."

Even the path she had chosen was extraordinary. Otherwise the Heart-Questioning Sword would never have acknowledged her.

"There's another character."

Bai Jian suddenly pointed it out.

Everyone then noticed, barely visible behind the character for immortal, a second character — faint, but impossible to ignore.

It read... demon.

Fang He'an rubbed his nose. This time he did not dare say a word. He had not expected their most well-behaved and obedient Junior Sister to also carry the potential to become a demon.

The disturbance at the top of Sword Mountain continued for some time, and then faded.

When the formation before them dissolved, Bai Jian found she could enter. She was the first one through, Yan Ju close behind.

Among the chaos of swords, Ye Wanwan stood alone. In one hand was a blue sword. In the other, the lacquered box.

Yan Ju stopped immediately.

"Junior Sister!"

Fang He'an's shout brought Ye Wanwan back to herself.

She turned and looked at Yan Ju. She clasped her hands in greeting, composed and unhurried. "Senior."

Even after a full month in the sect, Ye Wanwan had never changed how she addressed him.

Yan Ju had noticed.

She had still not fully accepted Tianyi Sect.

"Is this what a divine weapon looks like? Can't see anything special about it — can it be sold?" Li Wanzhi had moved before Fang He'an, and was already reaching toward the Heart-Questioning Sword.

"Don't touch it carelessly," Fang He'an said quickly.

The sword's energy immediately sent Li Wanzhi flying backward, landing him hard enough to see stars.

Everyone startled and immediately moved away from Ye Wanwan.

Ye Wanwan's brow furrowed slightly. Without any visible movement, she pressed her hand against the blue sword, and its imposing aura immediately retreated completely. By now Yan Ju had also noticed.

His expression grew even more complicated.

"Damn. The Heart-Questioning Sword actually acknowledged her." Third Senior Brother's voice-transmission sounded in their shared consciousness.

Yan Ju: "...Not only acknowledged. It is protecting its master."

Second Senior Brother: "We should come back."

Yan Ju: "If you think you can handle it, come yourself."

"Third Junior Brother, your sword path gets more and more timid the more you train — how can you not beat a little Qi Refining disciple?"

Yan Ju's expression did not change. "It is not the disciple I cannot beat. It is that sword I cannot beat. The moment I came close, it locked onto my aura. Hitting Li Wanzhi was a warning aimed at me."

"..."

"Is this not against the rules? That was the sword of our founding ancestor."

"Mm. A newly entered junior disciple, wielding a sword that outranks all of us — if she is considered Heart-Questioning's inheritor, should we not be calling her Ancestral Master?"

"...Fifth, shut up!"

"Damn, Fifth, when are you going to come back? I can't take care of your Qingcong Mountain anymore."

"It is fine as long as Third Senior Brother does not burn it down."

"That's about right."

Seeing the conversation drift entirely off topic, Yan Ju brought it back. "What do we do with this new disciple now? The Heart-Questioning Sword is sheltering her, but by the rules, once someone passes the Heart-Questioning formation they must take a formal master. If no one accepts her, she goes back down the mountain, and the sword must be retrieved."

But now...

The sword could not be taken back. So there was only one option.

Yan Ju was still thinking. "If none of the senior elders wish to take a disciple, then I will reluctantly..."

Before he finished, a light cough sounded. Third Elder Xunyin cut off Yan Ju's words. "Why not give her to me? I have yet to find an inheritor for my mechanism arts."

Fifth Elder Lu Qingxuan also rushed in: "I could also take her."

"Fifth, quiet — you can't even find time to take care of your little disciple Xiao An."

First Elder Gu Canglang, brief as always: "Give her to me."

"First Senior Brother, you haven't been seen in twenty years. Are you sure you have time to look after a child?"

Second Elder Luo Qingfeng considered. "First Senior Brother is too busy. I have time."

Yan Ju: "..."

Did you not all just call this child a demon cultivator?

chapters.title: The Sect's Acknowledgement
chapters.content:
Yan Ju gave a cold laugh. "Senior Brothers and Sisters, there are only three children in the current generation of Tianyi Sect. Besides myself and the Sect Leader, have any of you fulfilled your responsibilities as martial aunts and uncles? Taking a disciple is not just wearing the title of master and then walking away. It requires actual teaching."

And to teach Ye Wanwan, with the talent required to earn the Heart-Questioning Sword's recognition, was not something a casual effort could manage.

Everyone fell silent at that.

It was true — this could not be taken lightly.

"Send her to the snow mountain."

A sudden voice. Like jade cracking open, bright and clear, yet threaded through with a certain cool indifference. Unexpected, and the moment it rang out, everyone in the communication formation went still.

"Se... "

"Seventh Junior Brother?"

The shock was universal.

The one who never participated in their discussions had actually appeared.

Yan Ju's expression shifted. "Senior Brother, have you ended your seclusion?"

"Yes."

Li Mingde finally spoke, with a smile. "Do you want this child?"

Pei Xuan's voice was unhurried. "The item the Sect Leader had her bring — wasn't it meant for me?"

As he spoke, a stream of spiritual energy swept toward the lacquered box in Ye Wanwan's hands.

The box opened. Inside was a disciple token.

Ye Wanwan looked at what was happening and understood immediately.

Especially when she caught Yan Ju's expression — as though he was weighing something.

Watching the disciple token's spiritual resonance stir and flow, Ye Wanwan, who understood better than anyone what was about to happen, said immediately, "I am sorry. I cannot join Tianyi Sect."

Everyone at Tianyi Sect: ???

What? Their Seventh Junior Brother had been rejected?!

Everyone pricked up their ears.

"Reason."

That jade-clear voice, as though coming from mid-air.

Landing in every person's ear.

Ye Wanwan heard it too.

But the young woman kept her gaze fixed ahead, her expression calm. "I want to stay. But I am afraid to. Because I am someone who was... expelled from Wushang Sect as a traitor."

The word traitor.

Ye Wanwan said it with the utmost contempt.

In the communication formation, no one spoke.

Ye Wanwan continued. "In a match against my junior martial sister, I seriously injured her. Her golden core was shattered by me. For that offence, my own golden core was dug out and I was driven from Wushang Sect."

"Someone like me, so thoroughly disgraced — if I were to seek a master at a cultivation assembly, no one would accept me."

"Because no one would dare offend Wushang Sect."

Her voice was entirely calm as she said all of this.

Some things had to be spoken plainly.

Even if she did not say them herself, they would inevitably come out eventually. That would be even more troublesome.

"In order to avoid bringing trouble to everyone, I cannot join Tianyi Sect."

Ye Wanwan returned the disciple token to Fang He'an.

But Pei Xuan said in an unhurried voice, "And so what?"

Ye Wanwan paused.

Her expression shifted slightly. "I seriously injured a fellow disciple and betrayed my sect."

"In sparring and competition, injuries are common. If the path you have been following does not feel right to you, leaving to seek another is the most natural thing."

"But I shattered Ye Qian's golden core."

"If you, at the same cultivation level, were able to shatter an opponent's golden core — you are exceptional."

Ye Wanwan: "..."

No, how was the thought process of these Tianyi Sect people like this.

Pei Xuan's voice was still unhurried. "Did you want me to praise you?"

"...No."

Pei Xuan said, "Then that settles it."

Ye Wanwan did not understand, and asked, "What if someday, because of Wushang Sect, I bring serious trouble down on your sect?"

In the communication formation, the others laughed. "How serious?"

"What if I killed Yan Ding, or Wushang Sect's Sect Leader?"

The communication formation was silent for a moment.

Ye Wanwan thought: as expected.

But then Pei Xuan said in an unhurried voice, "You have no small ambitions, young woman. If pledging to me as your master comes with the condition of killing Yan Ding, I can set out right now."

Ye Wanwan went still.

"You are not going to scold me?"

The eight elders shook their heads. Li Mingde said soothingly, "Child, from the moment you came up the mountain, we had already guessed something of your situation."

"Your dantian has been torn apart."

Ye Wanwan's body went rigid. Her eyes reddened without her realising, and then a hand gently took hers.

It was Bai Jian.

Bai Jian looked at her with concern.

"We do not fully know what happened to you. But Bai Jian has never been wrong about people. You are a good child. Stay. What you are afraid of — it will not happen."

"You will not drive me away."

"Will not dig out my golden core, will not throw me in the Black Water Prison, will not punish me by kneeling on the Mysterious Ice Cliff, and will not kill me with a sword through the heart... is that right?"

Ye Wanwan asked.

In the communication formation, everyone was shaken.

They did that — to a disciple?

Even Yan Ju was stunned. Li Wanzhi had behaved outrageously since coming up the mountain and they had never made him kneel for anything. And this Ye Wanwan, barely in her teens — what on earth had she been through?

Even Li Wanzhi, who had been lying on the ground, looked up at Ye Wanwan in a daze.

Ye Wanwan did not cry. She only looked ahead. Her gaze had no focus, with nowhere to land — but she wanted an answer.

She did not dare lean on anyone.

Space split open. A silver light moved slowly out from the void. A man whose long hair flowed loose in silver-white was walking barefoot through it, snow and wind swirling around him.

He stepped into the light, and his deep black eyes looked toward Ye Wanwan.

"No."

Ye Wanwan looked at him, and in those beautiful eyes found sincerity. She thought for a moment, then said, "All right. But I have one condition. If in three years I still cannot accept this identity, I wish to leave. I hope that when the time comes, Tianyi Sect and you will give me my freedom."

The corner of Pei Xuan's lips moved. "Agreed."

The others thought: it will not be that easy.

—

Ye Wanwan formally entered Tianyi Sect as its one hundred and first generation disciple, ranked sixth, taking Pei Xuan as master. The moment the disciple token was in her hands, she was officially a member of Tianyi Sect.

Bai Jian and Fang He'an embraced her with joy.

"Junior Sister! Junior Sister!"

Ye Wanwan looked at the number on her ranking: six.

She closed her hand around it.

Would she be able to stay this time?

"Three days from now, come find me on the snow mountain." Pei Xuan's voice sounded.

"Understood."

After Ye Wanwan and the others left, Yan Ju spoke in a newly opened communication formation. "The cultivation method she is using is not from Wushang Sect's direct line."

"Unless I am mistaken, what she is cultivating is a basic low-tier outer disciple technique — the Qi Refining Art given to outer disciples. But with her talent, that should not be the case."

And to have come this far using only the most ordinary of Qi Refining arts spoke to how formidable Ye Wanwan's talent truly was.

"The current Sect Leader of Wushang Sect is Cheng Wen, isn't it?" said Xunyin.

"Yes. But I've met Cheng Wen myself, and he never seemed the type to be so ruthless to a disciple," said Sect Leader Li Mingde, stroking his beard. He could not make sense of it either.

Neither could the others.

"Regardless. She is my disciple now." Pei Xuan's voice was cold.

Everyone nodded. "That's right. Whatever she was before — she is Tianyi Sect's now."

And Tianyi Sect was famously protective of its own.

—

Ye Wanwan lay on her bed, turning the token over in her hands. Tianyi Sect's token was a little different from Wushang Sect's — both were tokens given to direct disciples.

But Tianyi Sect's token also had communication and positioning functions built in.

It could be used to transmit messages to disciples and send one's location in moments of danger.

Ye Wanwan considered this for a moment, then put the token away, closed her eyes, and began to meditate.

Having earned the Heart-Questioning Sword's acknowledgement, her primordial spirit had benefited greatly. Though her cultivation realm was still at the Qi Refining stage, her primordial spirit seemed to have surpassed the golden core stage.

Only because of the restrictions on her cultivation realm was she temporarily unable to break through.

"There will be an opportunity eventually," she said softly.

The Heart-Questioning Sword resting beside the bed lay quietly, not moving.

—

The next day, Ye Wanwan followed routine, rising at the mao hour and preparing to bring the sword to the practice ground.

She still wanted to test the Heart-Questioning Sword again.

But when she opened the door, Fang He'an, Li Wanzhi, and Bai Jian were all outside in plain clothes, waiting in the courtyard, waving her over. Ye Wanwan blinked. "What is this?"

"Martial Uncle has given us the day off. We're taking you down the mountain to have some fun."

chapters.title: One Spirit Stone Per Stalk
chapters.content:
On the way down, Bai Jian ferried them all on her sword, and told Ye Wanwan that this time their martial uncle's reason for sending them out was to help Ye Wanwan familiarise herself with the nearby mountain ranges and the lay of the land around Tianyi Sect.

And that after so much training, they all deserved a break.

Fang He'an talked a great deal on the flight down.

Ye Wanwan listened to everything.

Fang He'an had already reached golden core, but was still hitching a ride on Bai Jian's sword. Ye Wanwan asked, "Senior Brother Fang, with your level, you should have been able to fly on your own a while ago."

Fang He'an laughed awkwardly. "I can, technically, but I don't have my own life-bound spirit sword yet, so flying on my own is a bit inconvenient for now."

Bai Jian and Li Wanzhi both looked sharply at him.

Fang He'an glared back — he had not said anything wrong.

It was just not a sword.

"Although Tianyi Sect is not primarily a sword cultivation sect, according to sect rules, all disciples who enter must go to Sword Mountain and choose a life-bound spirit sword. Nurtured by one's own spiritual aura and resonance."

"This is both an inheritance of the sect's lineage and a fulfillment of the past masters' unfinished intentions."

Their Tianyi Sect, passing from one generation to the next.

Not only their will.

But also their sword spirits.

Ye Wanwan asked, "Every disciple?"

"Every one. Whether you are a talisman cultivator or an alchemy cultivator — everyone must go. Once Junior Brother Li passes his assessment, he will also choose his own sword, just as you did."

Li Wanzhi began to think. "Then I need to consider who to take as my master."

Fang He'an said, "Don't get ahead of yourself. Having anyone want you at all would be impressive."

Li Wanzhi: "..."

Fang He'an also offered a warning. "But I'd encourage you to start working on your body cultivation soon. Take advantage of the martial uncles and aunts all being at the sect right now. When it comes time for your Heart-Questioning, they might take notice of you. If they're all away by then, there really will be no one to accept you."

"Does it work like that?"

"Yes. Because the martial uncles and aunts are all very busy. Some enter seclusion for more than ten years at a stretch. Whether they'll even notice your existence is another question."

Li Wanzhi muttered something about not wanting to stay anyway if they wouldn't take him.

The others paid no attention.

This person was a weathervane — a different thought every day.

Bai Jian landed them one li outside the city walls.

"The immortal sects have rules: when passing through mortal cities, unless absolutely necessary, one must not fly on swords within city limits, so as not to disturb the ordinary people." Fang He'an said. "So, Junior Sister, we walk into the city."

"All right."

The four of them walked in on foot.

Before they reached the gate, everyone started asking Li Wanzhi for money.

Li Wanzhi gritted his teeth. "Didn't the Sect Leader give you money to take Junior Sister down the mountain?"

"...No."

"Then your monthly allowance?"

Fang He'an said honestly, "Our teacher said this year's allowance won't be distributed until year's end. So nothing right now."

Though Fang He'an privately thought the reason was — they had run out of spirit stones.

But spirit stones were not something they had much use for other than when going down the mountain. Fang He'an had decided not to worry about it.

Their daily cultivation supplies were all available on the mountain.

Nothing was lacking.

"It's just borrowing, not like we won't repay."

"Have you not heard of borrowing without returning?"

"I haven't."

Even if Li Wanzhi was unwilling, now that they were off the mountain, in the city, he was the only one among the four with any spirit stones, which naturally meant it fell to him.

Ye Wanwan touched the xuan spirit grass in her qiankun pouch.

In the past month on the mountain, she had grown some in her room and yard. She had picked some on the way down, and could sell it to get spirit stones.

Li Wanzhi noticed she had not said anything.

"Junior Sister, you don't need any?"

Ye Wanwan smiled. "Not for now."

But Bai Jian and Fang He'an, hearing this, promptly handed over the spirit stones they had taken from Li Wanzhi and gave them to Ye Wanwan. "You keep these."

Ye Wanwan: "...I truly don't need them."

She had spirit stones.

But it was too kind an offer to refuse.

In an instant, Ye Wanwan became the wealthiest of the four.

The stripped-clean Li Wanzhi: "...What am I."

Fang He'an led Bai Jian and the others into the city, introducing things as they went. "All the cities and towns in the mountain ranges nearby are under Tianyi Sect's protection. They pay spirit stones to the city lord's office, and the city lord's office pays tribute to us. In return, we handle the problems they cannot solve. I sometimes come down with Senior Sister to help."

Ye Wanwan said, "This is usually handled by outer disciples."

Fang He'an bought two bags of roasted chestnuts and gave one each to Bai Jian and Ye Wanwan. "Our sect has few people and doesn't divide into inner and outer. When things need doing, even our martial uncle comes down."

The moment the words left his mouth—

Ye Wanwan and Li Wanzhi spotted a familiar figure.

It was Yan Ju.

He was passing by with a sword slung over one shoulder and ten bags of grain in the other hand.

Fang He'an: "...Martial Uncle."

Yan Ju was unruffled. "You came down for the day?"

"Yes, bringing Junior Sister down to have a look around."

"Good, have fun." He said, then seemed to think of something, and reached into his robe to pull out a pouch of spirit stones, handing it to Ye Wanwan. "Young women ought to buy a few more sets of clothes. You look like a wandering nun."

Then he looked at Bai Jian. "You too."

And then Yan Ju was gone.

Leaving Ye Wanwan holding a spirit stone pouch with a hundred spirit stones inside.

And there was Yan Ju, going back to moving cargo.

"Is that... what he normally does?"

"Not entirely," Fang He'an said. "If there are demon beasts in the area, Martial Uncle handles those too. But a few years back, in order to provide for Senior Sister, he cleared out every demon beast within a hundred li that had been causing trouble. These past three years, no demon beast has dared come near Tianyi Sect's territory. With nothing to hunt, Martial Uncle had to find odd jobs."

"But doesn't the city lord's office pay tribute in spirit stones?"

"They do, but it's never enough to cover what the sect needs." Fang He'an said.
