Ye Wanwan thought of the marrow-cleansing pool she had been soaking in every few days, and understood where Tianyi Sect's money was going.

That pool alone was not something one could simply buy with spirit stones.

And the medicine Bai Jian and Fang He'an had given Ye Wanwan for her injuries was also top-tier — not commonly found on the market.

In other words.

If they were sold, they could be exchanged for money.

Fang He'an and the others simply did not have that mindset.

Sitting on a mountain of treasure without knowing it.

But there was one person who would not miss that.

Ye Wanwan looked at Li Wanzhi.

Li Wanzhi felt the hair rise on the back of his head. "What are you looking at?"

"Senior Brother Li, do you still have the medicine Senior Brother Fang gave you?"

Li Wanzhi used his medicine the most.

Because he was injured the most.

At those words, Li Wanzhi immediately covered his chest. "I do — what are you planning?"

"That can be exchanged for spirit stones, can it not?"

Li Wanzhi laughed awkwardly. "It can, but... there's no need."

Ye Wanwan also understood — using such rare medicines to exchange for spirit stones would be a waste. But the xuan spirit grass was different.

She glanced at the pharmacy nearby. "I'll go over here for a moment."

Bai Jian and Fang He'an moved to follow.

Ye Wanwan waved them off to go explore. No need for everyone to come.

Li Wanzhi, however, followed out of curiosity.

Inside the medicine hall, Ye Wanwan asked about the price of xuan spirit grass with practiced ease. She was told ten stalks for one spirit stone, and proceeded to take out one thousand stalks.

The shopkeeper looked up and blinked.

Ye Wanwan had already counted them neatly. "Check that against mine."

"Young lady, these cannot be sold at the rate of ten stalks per spirit stone."

Ye Wanwan frowned. "Cannot? Why not?"

That was a fair price.

She had sold before and had a rough sense of the going rate.

If they were saying they could not buy at that price, Ye Wanwan was not going to question the quality of her own goods. The only explanation was that the shopkeeper simply did not want to do business with her.

Li Wanzhi, hearing this, rolled up his sleeves and stepped in front of Ye Wanwan. "What is the meaning of this, are you trying to bully our Junior Sister?"

Ye Wanwan had not said a word yet.

Li Wanzhi already whispered to her, "Don't worry, I'm several cultivation levels above you. I'll make sure you get out of here safely."

Ye Wanwan: "...It hasn't come to a life-or-death situation yet."

The shopkeeper hurried to explain. "No no, there is a misunderstanding, honoured guests. The issue is that this xuan spirit grass — the price is not ten stalks per spirit stone. This grade of xuan spirit grass is worth ten times that."

"One spirit stone per stalk."

chapters.title: Free Refills on Noodles
chapters.content:
Ye Wanwan and Li Wanzhi exchanged a glance.

One spirit stone per stalk of xuan spirit grass?

Not a lowball price.

An inflated one?

In the xuan spirit grass market, low-grade grass generally sold at a hundred stalks per spirit stone. Mid-grade ran between thirty and forty stalks per stone.

The shopkeeper's opening offer to Ye Wanwan had been one stone for ten stalks.

That price, while not extraordinary, was not low.

Mid-to-high range.

Likely given because Ye Wanwan and Li Wanzhi's bearing was exceptional — hence a decent offer before even examining the goods.

But.

One spirit stone per stalk.

That was a high price.

Very high.

Even exceptional-grade xuan spirit grass did not command that.

Ye Wanwan could not quite make sense of the shopkeeper's meaning, and even Li Wanzhi — a businessman's son — found it strange. Was the man really doing business at a loss?

The shopkeeper watched the two of them say nothing, and spoke more carefully. "If the honoured guests feel it is too low, I can make it two spirit stones..."

Seeing the two of them still watching him without responding, the shopkeeper clenched his jaw. "Three. That is the absolute maximum. I cannot go higher."

Li Wanzhi had certainly seen three spirit stones before, but hearing this, he was still a little dazed. Was there something special about this xuan spirit grass?

Ye Wanwan considered for a moment, while the shopkeeper said with great difficulty, "This is truly the highest I can go, young lady."

Ye Wanwan relented. "Sold."

The shopkeeper's face brightened with delight.

He began settling the transaction immediately.

Ye Wanwan verified the count.

Both sides worked as fast as possible.

Each afraid the other would change their mind.

The shopkeeper said with a broad smile, "If you have more in the future, would the young lady consider coming to us again?"

Ye Wanwan thought for a moment. "If I chose exclusively to sell to your establishment, what can the shopkeeper promise me?"

"Any future purchases you make at any of our Wanbao Tower shops will come at a discounted price." The shopkeeper also handed Ye Wanwan a small wooden plaque.

Carved with a talisman pattern.

Ye Wanwan immediately understood — this was a form of identity recognition. The talisman pattern was low-grade, but sufficient.

"Agreed." Ye Wanwan said.

They left the medicine hall.

Li Wanzhi turned over Ye Wanwan's three thousand spirit stones in his mind. "Unless I'm wrong, Senior Brother Fang just said our martial uncle was at the wharf carrying cargo. He earns fifty spirit stones for a full day's work."

Ye Wanwan: "Yes."

So she had earned three thousand in a single day.

Li Wanzhi marvelled, "So the wealthy one here is actually you."

Ye Wanwan raised an eyebrow. "Indeed. So you had better hold on tight to this thigh."

Li Wanzhi looked at the young woman's smiling face and thought: just look at how lovely she is when she smiles. Curse that awful Wushang Sect.

Ye Wanwan walked further on, went down another street, entered a different medicine hall, and asked about prices. The rate she got was consistent with the first — one spirit stone for ten stalks.

But when they saw Ye Wanwan's xuan spirit grass, they all changed their offer. They gave a higher price.

Ye Wanwan looked at the xuan spirit grass in her hands.

"Is there something different about it?"

Li Wanzhi was also examining it. "It is extremely fresh."

"I picked it this morning, of course it's fresh." Ye Wanwan rested her chin in her hand, tore off a small piece, and chewed it thoughtfully. "Same clean, refreshing taste as always."

Fang He'an and the others found them eventually, looking puzzled.

"What happened? Why are you sitting out here?"

Though he asked, Fang He'an and Bai Jian both sat down too. All four of them sat on the steps, and Ye Wanwan and Li Wanzhi handed some to Fang He'an and Bai Jian.

"Here, have some grass."

Fang He'an: "..."

Bai Jian did not hesitate. She started chewing alongside Ye Wanwan.

Then Fang He'an went rigid and suddenly let out a yelp. "First-grade xuan spirit grass?! Junior Sister, where did you get this?"

Ye Wanwan and Li Wanzhi looked up at the same time.

"First-grade?"

"Xuan spirit grass can have quality grades?"

Two innocent pairs of eyes stared at him, and Fang He'an's urge to share what he knew surged. "Of course it can! But extremely rarely! Extremely rare!"

"Normal xuan spirit grass has no quality grade. Even high-grade xuan spirit grass is just considered excellent among ordinary spirit grasses."

"But having an actual quality grade is different. My teacher told me about it. Some naturally gifted spirit herb cultivators — because their spiritual energy is special — the herbs they grow are superior to those of ordinary cultivators in both strength and resonance, and can potentially break through the herb's existing ceiling, resulting in a mutation or a leap in grade."

"That is how first-grade xuan spirit grass comes to exist."

"It is extraordinarily rare."

"Where did you buy it? I absolutely must buy a few stalks." Fang He'an was agitated. "Medicine refined from this quality of xuan spirit grass would have a much higher purity."

He watched Ye Wanwan and Li Wanzhi remain silent.

Fang He'an asked, "Where did you buy it?"

Ye Wanwan smiled. "Senior Brother, if you want some, no need to buy it. I'll give it to you."

"No no no, how could Senior Brother accept something from you for free — you bought this too."

"I didn't buy it." Ye Wanwan pressed five stalks into his hand. "These are the ones with imperfect presentation. If you want more, when we get back to the sect, I'll pull some for you from the patch."

It took Fang He'an quite a while to process this.

"This..."

"You..."

"Grew..."

"...This yourself?"

Ye Wanwan nodded. "I just sold some. Now I have spirit stones. Shall we go for a proper meal?"

It was not until Ye Wanwan pulled Fang He'an into a fine restaurant that he started to come back to himself — still not fully recovered from the shock of the first-grade xuan spirit grass. Then the menu in front of him gave him a cold shock.

Seated in the main hall.

Fang He'an shuddered. "What the hell — plain noodles for twenty spirit stones? Martial Uncle could work half a day for that!"

Li Wanzhi pressed his head down. "Senior Brother, please keep your voice down."

Ye Wanwan smiled. "It's all right. Senior Brother, eat whatever you like. I have spirit stones."

She set her qiankun pouch on the table.

A solid thunk.

Very loud.

Fang He'an clutched his chest. "A fortune. An absolute fortune. Junior Sister, aren't you afraid of being robbed, walking around with this much on you?"

Bai Jian asked, "Can we order whatever we want?"

"Yes," Ye Wanwan said with a smile.

Bai Jian and Fang He'an both looked through the menu and pointed at the plain noodles.

Ye Wanwan thought for a moment. "Senior Sister, you don't have to save money for me."

Bai Jian said, "These come with free refills."

Ye Wanwan went still.

Li Wanzhi also looked. "That's true. It says right here: free refills on noodles."

Just very small print.

Ye Wanwan immediately understood what Bai Jian was thinking, and laughed quietly. "All right."

She ordered five dishes, and then one bowl of plain noodles each.

The serving staff at the restaurant had a very pleasant manner, all smiles — but an experienced Fang He'an said, "In a little while they won't be smiling."

Then he started regretting things. "I really should have bought everyone a face-covering before we came in."

Ye Wanwan propped her chin in one hand. "Since they've opened for business and written free refills on the menu, they certainly can accept it. Senior Brother, don't worry."

Fang He'an sighed. "Junior Sister, you are about to discover — the cruelty of the world."

When Bai Jian finished her fifty-eighth bowl of plain noodles and the main hall had gone utterly quiet, with only wave upon wave of scorching stares, Ye Wanwan was reminded of the first time she saw Fang He'an — how he had been nervously hunched in on himself. Clearly, experience.

But when Bai Jian finished the fifty-eighth bowl, Ye Wanwan still spoke. "Another refill."

The waiter stepped forward with a strained smile. "Honoured guest..."

Ye Wanwan said in a flat voice, "Your bowls are too small. Bring a larger one."

Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi both gave her a thumbs up.

Their Junior Sister! Deflecting blame with an unmoving expression — excellent.

chapters.title: The Person Following Them
chapters.content:
The staff of the fine restaurant had never in their entire lives seen anyone refill a noodle bowl a hundred times. Today they had witnessed it.

Fang He'an covered his face. "Senior Sister, I think that's about enough."

Bai Jian drank down the last of her broth. She was clearly still not quite satisfied, but she had the decency to know when to stop.

"The broth here is good."

Ye Wanwan said indulgently, "If you like it, we can come again next time."

The server's legs nearly buckled. The moment they went to settle up, he was going to take "free refills" off the menu immediately.

Once Bai Jian finished eating, Ye Wanwan paid the bill. The whole meal came to a hundred and twenty spirit stones. Bai Jian said quietly, "I should have eaten twenty more bowls."

It was then that Fang He'an understood — Senior Sister had been trying to eat back the full cost on Ye Wanwan's behalf.

Ye Wanwan realised it too. She paused, then looked back at her. "You didn't have to. Spirit stones — I can earn those whenever I need to. I'll make sure none of you ever go hungry."

Setting aside the xuan spirit grass, just her talisman skills alone could earn spirit stones.

Ye Wanwan had always been unconcerned about money because she had never lacked for it. She had the means to earn whenever she needed to.

But seeing Bai Jian still looking a little concerned, Ye Wanwan only smoothed her hair at her temple, "In the future, as long as I have food, Senior Sister will have food."

With the bill settled, they left.

But a group of people blocked their path. "I was just wondering who it might be — turns out it is the big eater from the Bai family. The moment I heard someone on the street talking about who was eating a hundred free bowls at the fine restaurant, I knew it had to be you lot."

An insufferably grating, arrogant voice.

When they looked ahead—

Expensive brocade robes, a dissipated air, dull yellowing around the eyes, an unfocused gaze. Clearly someone who had spent years wallowing in indulgence.

"Is that not the young master of the Ye family?"

"The Ye family."

Ye Wanwan raised her head and studied the person in front of her. She did not recognise him, but the jade plaque on his person—

Lingxi.

Ye Wanwan understood.

A branch of the Ye family.

The Ye family to which Ye Qian belonged was a first-tier great clan, its power matching or exceeding that of the major sects. In recent years, its growing influence and alliance with Wushang Sect had given it an edge over many other sects.

The sects were weakening. The noble families were rising.

And the Ye family was quietly positioning itself as the foremost among them — which was why Ye Congying held so much sway within Wushang Sect, and why Ye Qian's influence extended so far.

But Ye Qian and Ye Congying were members of the main family.

If this minor branch of the Ye family in a small town out here was already this brazen, one could imagine just how powerful the Ye family's reach had become.

That it even caused a minor branch in a minor place to act with such breathtaking arrogance.

Ye Yiran noticed Ye Wanwan's unfriendly gaze. He went cold. "What are you looking at?"

"Looking at how ugly you are."

Ye Wanwan said in a flat voice. As she said it, she gave him a slow, deliberate once-over. That provocation was enough to make Ye Yiran furious.

He raised his hand and summoned a technique.

Wind spiritual power!

Bai Jian immediately moved to act, but Ye Wanwan put one hand out and held her back. With her now-free right hand, she moved her palm.

Straight into the eye of the wind.

Everyone around them burst out laughing.

"What a fool. Who would try to block something like that with bare hands?"

"Clearly someone with no understanding of cultivation."

But then—

The young woman said quietly:

"Tear."

A soft sound.

Her hand split the wind coil directly in two.

The wind scattered around both sides of them.

Blowing open the two young women's hair.

And making everyone suddenly aware that they were remarkably beautiful.

Li Wanzhi was furious enough to jump, but he also knew he could not beat Ye Yiran who was at the Foundation Establishment stage. He noticed Fang He'an was not moving either, and Li Wanzhi grew annoyed.

"Senior Brother, are you a man or not?"

"Obviously I am," Fang He'an said, glancing at him. "You want to try?"

"...Then why are you just watching?"

"Who said I was just watching? I'm sitting here watching while keeping an eye on Senior Sister, and calculating whether we can afford the damages if a fight breaks out." Fang He'an had already thought through several scenarios.

But watching Ye Wanwan split Ye Yiran's wind technique with a single palm—

Fang He'an was still surprised.

"Junior Sister's physical strength has progressed so fast."

Training every day against Bai Jian — Ye Wanwan's physical body had already strengthened to the point where she could contest a first-tier spiritual technique with bare hands. Even if this Ye Yiran was clearly not particularly formidable—

It was still a first-tier spiritual technique.

She blocked it bare-handed.

Admirable technique.

Admirable humiliation.

Ye Yiran had noticed. He went rigid. "You didn't use spiritual energy?"

Ye Wanwan raised her eyes and looked at him without expression. "For you? Is that necessary?"

Ye Yiran leaned forward. This time he used a second-tier technique. Wind blades flew across the space between them, Ye Wanwan let out a quiet sound of contempt, and began using her hands to intercept them.

One palm, one wind blade.

As she moved, she closed the distance with Ye Yiran.

Crack.

She gave him a slap.

Then a backhanded one.

Crack crack crack.

More than ten slaps in rapid succession, driving Ye Yiran stumbling far back. He could not quite process the fact that Ye Wanwan still had not used spiritual energy — and the shock and fury of it showed all over him.

"You are humiliating me!"

"Does humiliating you require a particular occasion?"

Ye Wanwan looked Ye Yiran over. "Next time you see us, watch your mouth. All that rice you eat, and it has not done you a bit of good."

With that, Ye Wanwan prepared to leave.

But Ye Yiran was shaking with rage. "Bai Jian, you are my fiancée — the one sold to me by your Bai family! How dare you just walk away?"

All four turned back at once.

Even Li Wanzhi was staring at Ye Yiran.

"Fiancé?"

Li Wanzhi burst out laughing. "You qualify?"

Ye Yiran was incensed. "What are you all laughing at? Everyone knows the Bai family promised their daughter to me, Ye Yiran. Our engagement has been set since we were six years old. Bai Jian is my fiancée."

Bai Jian said, "I don't know you."

Fang He'an spat, "Did you hear that? My Senior Sister doesn't know you."

"But I know you." Ye Yiran fixed his gaze on Bai Jian, his eyes carrying a deep and intense want. Ye Wanwan felt something familiar in it.

Something like the way Ye Qian had looked at her before the golden core incident — restrained, controlled, yet unable to fully suppress a trace of covetousness.

Not affection.

But a craving for something on their body.

Ye Wanwan's fingers curled. Something was wrong.

Bai Jian frowned. "I have never seen you."

Ye Wanwan stared at Ye Yiran, studying his eyes, trying to find something there. The sharpness of that gaze made even Ye Yiran's heart stutter.

"You..."

Ye Wanwan took hold of his chin, staring into his eyes. "What is in there?"

Ye Yiran panicked. "What are you doing? Get away from me!"

Ye Wanwan raised her hand and covered his eyes. "These eyes, if dug out, would certainly be worth studying."

Ye Yiran was genuinely alarmed.

He shoved Ye Wanwan away. "You are insane!"

But Ye Wanwan had not missed a single change in his expression. And that brief strangeness she had seen a moment ago had vanished. She looked back toward Bai Jian.

Bai Jian also appeared somewhat confused.

A suspicion flickered through Ye Wanwan's mind. But Ye Yiran's companions had already surged forward to shield him, and Ye Wanwan fixed him with one long, searching look.

She smiled slowly. "I really do like your eyes."

"If you want to sell them — name a price."

Ye Yiran and his people went cold all over. They cursed and shouted, but Ye Wanwan paid no attention. She gave Ye Yiran one last meaningful smile, then took Bai Jian by the hand and walked away.

Leaving Ye Yiran standing there, face drained of colour.

Had she discovered his secret?

As soon as the four of them were clear—

Li Wanzhi said, "Someone is following us."

chapters.title: The Spirit Market
chapters.content:
"I know."

Ye Wanwan's expression didn't change.

Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi were both looking at her. Ye Wanwan considered for a moment, then said, "Why are you two staring at me?"

"Shimei, you just had a killing intent," Fang He'an said.

Ye Wanwan sighed lightly. "Shixiong, we are law-abiding citizens."

"And what does that mean?"

"Fighting and killing are prohibited within city limits," Ye Wanwan said.

Li Wanzhi clapped his hands. "Then we drag them outside the city and kill them there."

Bai Jian and Fang He'an both nodded.

Ye Wanwan stared at them. "...How are you all more demonic than I am?"

Fang He'an grinned. "Don't be angry, Shimei. That guy with the surname Ye is just throwing wild accusations. He wasn't scared off last time when Dashixiong went after him, so here he is again. When Dashixiong gets back, I'll tell him."

Ye Wanwan's expression shifted slightly. "This isn't the first time?"

"Not at all." Fang He'an bought four apples and handed one to each of them. "This is actually the third time. We run into him every time we come down the mountain."

"But Shijie doesn't even know him."

Bai Jian looked completely innocent. "I've never seen him before."

Li Wanzhi said, "He brought up the Bai family just now."

Fang He'an waved his hand. "That makes even less sense. Shijie has nothing to do with the Bai family. She's a foundling Dashixiong brought back — she has no family at all."

Bai Jian nodded.

Li Wanzhi looked baffled. "How does everyone here have a tragic backstory? You're all starting to sound like the main characters of some story."

Fang He'an said, "...You looking to die?"

The four of them shook off the people tailing them and headed to the docks to find Yan Ju, letting him know they were heading back to Tianyi Sect.

When Yan Ju heard that someone had been bullying Bai Jian, he set down what he was holding and said coldly, "Where are they?"

Fang He'an and Bai Jian looked completely unsurprised by his reaction. Ye Wanwan thought to herself — so this was a regular occurrence.

Fang He'an said, "Shishu, Shimei already taught them a lesson."

Yan Ju frowned. "Next time something like this happens, call me."

"Will do."

Since it was getting late, Yan Ju said, "Wait for me a moment — I'll head back with you."

None of them objected. Yan Ju even ordered a bowl of tofu pudding for each of them at a stall nearby, then finished up his last task and left together with Ye Wanwan and the others.

Ye Wanwan sometimes found herself curious.

With Yan Ju's abilities, he had absolutely no need to be doing this kind of manual labor. He was more than capable of earning far more spirit stones through other means.

"Shishu does it to look after us," Fang He'an explained. "This work is close to the sect and the hours are flexible — if he doesn't feel like working, he doesn't have to. If he took on missions like Shibo and traveled far away, he wouldn't be able to keep an eye on us."

"And don't underestimate Shishu — this isn't the only thing he does."

"He's very capable."

Except when it came to cooking.

Yan Ju led the four of them back to Tianyi Sect on his sword.

Bai Jian flew with Fang He'an.

Ye Wanwan and Li Wanzhi were lucky enough to ride with Yan Ju — and for once, Li Wanzhi expressed his sincere and heartfelt gratitude.

Because Yan Ju's sword-riding was exceptionally smooth.

This time, Li Wanzhi didn't throw up even once.

He was moved to tears.

Yan Ju looked at the four of them. "Next time you go down the mountain, let one of the sect's seniors know. And if you run into something you can't handle, send up a signal flare."

"Fang He'an — did you bring a flare?"

"I... brought one. Probably."

Yan Ju looked up at him. "Hm?"

"I brought one."

Fang He'an straightened up and answered with full conviction.

Only then did Yan Ju leave. But the look he gave Fang He'an on the way out left Fang He'an feeling deeply uneasy.

"What was that look Shixiaoshu just gave me?"

"The 'I want to stab you' look," Li Wanzhi said.

He'd barely finished the sentence before Fang He'an punched him.

"What a shame — if it weren't for that whole mess, we could've done some shopping," Fang He'an said wistfully.

Li Wanzhi shook his head. "What's there to be regretful about? Just buy it on the Spirit Market."

"The Spirit Market is expensive, you little brat. You've never had to worry about money a day in your life, have you."

Ye Wanwan paused.

"There's already a Spirit Market now?"

Fang He'an said, "There is, though not many people know about it. You need a password to get in. It was actually this little guy who brought us in."

Li Wanzhi clasped his hands together modestly. "You flatter me."

Ye Wanwan stared at Li Wanzhi. "I can't believe the Spirit Market already exists this early."

That same evening.

Li Wanzhi taught Ye Wanwan how to use her jade token to access the Spirit Market. He glanced at her disciple token and added, "Actually, Tianyi Sect's disciple tokens work even better — the spirit resonance is stronger, and the connection to the formation array is more stable."

"The downside is that it makes your identity easier to trace."

Ye Wanwan considered this. "Because it locks onto your aura?"

"Are you in?" Li Wanzhi asked.

"I'm in. Try sensing it with your spiritual consciousness."

Ye Wanwan immediately entered a vast spiritual network. It appeared pristine and empty at first, but as her mind began to stir, the scene shifted before her.

It transformed into an ancient, atmospheric street.

Along both sides of the street were all manner of small stalls, and the figures wandering between them were blurred spiritual projections — all of them identical, impossible to tell apart.

They looked more like NPCs in a video game. Copy-pasted, the lot of them.

Li Wanzhi told Ye Wanwan, "This is the Spirit Market. All kinds of goods and cultivation methods are traded here. You can buy and you can sell."

"As long as both parties are satisfied, a transaction can be completed."

Ye Wanwan withdrew from the network and asked Li Wanzhi, "Did you build this Spirit Market?"

Li Wanzhi stared at her like she'd grown a second head. He coughed twice, then said, "Shimei, I know you hold your Shixiong in very high regard, but your Shixiong genuinely does not have that kind of ability."

"I didn't build it. This Spirit Market has existed for years — it's only started becoming more widely known recently. Though I did play a small part in spreading the word." Li Wanzhi grinned.

Ye Wanwan understood. He'd been promoting it.

Li Wanzhi taught her how to enter, how to buy, and how to sell. "Smaller items can be transmitted directly to your hand through the formation array, but for larger items or especially valuable ones, they use Wantong Delivery instead — it gets sent straight to you. That's to ensure security."

Ye Wanwan said, "Understood."

"Alright, that covers just about everything. Don't stay in there too long — it's very draining on your spiritual consciousness."

Ye Wanwan nodded. "Got it."

The moment Li Wanzhi left, Ye Wanwan entered the Spirit Market.

She scanned the dazzling array of goods lining the street. Everything imaginable was on sale, and some vendors had items listed but weren't even there themselves.

Ye Wanwan thought it over. In her past life, she hadn't learned about the Spirit Market until after she'd met Li Wanzhi. Who would have thought it had existed this early all along?

She thought for a moment, then listed some of the Spirit Elixirs she had refined — along with a small quantity of Spirit Grass and two Ping'an talismans — on her stall.

The stall looked sparse, but Ye Wanwan was satisfied.

Pei Xuan had given her two more days. The following day, Ye Wanwan tilled the soil in the front courtyard and planted new Spirit Grass. During that time, Fang He'an came by to watch.

He wanted to learn how it was done.

Ye Wanwan taught him everything, but in the end they discovered that her spiritual energy was uniquely suited to the task — when Fang He'an tried the same method, he couldn't replicate her results.

He resigned himself to helping Xun Yin tend to his spirit plants and spirit crops instead, but still eagerly offered to come and weed Ye Wanwan's garden in the future.

All he asked was for a little Spirit Grass in return.

Ye Wanwan laughed and agreed.

That evening, Ye Wanwan logged back into the Spirit Market and found that still nothing had sold. She was about to log off when she heard a voice say —

"How much for the Ping'an talisman?"

chapters.title: The Ping'an Talisman
chapters.content:
How much for the Ping'an talisman?

Voices in the Spirit Market could be altered to conceal one's identity — but even so, the moment this particular voice came through, Ye Wanwan's eyelid twitched.

Because the sheer laziness of it — the tone of someone draped across a chaise lounge, being fed grapes by a handmaid without bothering to open their eyes — stirred an inexplicable sense of familiarity in her.

She had a feeling she might actually make a sale today.

Ye Wanwan named her price. "Ten thousand spirit stones."

"...Ten thousand?"

The languid voice spoke again. "And what exactly makes this Ping'an talisman so special? A standard attack talisman already goes for around a thousand spirit stones, which is considered high-end for talismans. A ten-thousand-stone Ping'an talisman — how does that work?"

At a time when most Ping'an talismans sold for five or ten spirit stones purely for psychological comfort, ten thousand was an astronomical price — a number pulled straight from thin air, one might say. The question carried a rather pointed edge.

But Ye Wanwan didn't flinch. "Expensive things are expensive for a reason. This Ping'an talisman can block one instance of damage."

"Hah," came the sound of a suppressed laugh. "I could just buy a defensive talisman and get the same effect. And for a lot less."

Ye Wanwan was unhurried. "It works against both magical attacks and physical ones."

"Physical?"

"Simply put — it can deflect the damage from blades and swords as well. And as for magical damage — possession, soul-stealing, hex attacks, even accidents and illness — it can protect you through all of it, one time. In short: comprehensive protection."

"A true Ping'an talisman, in every sense of the name."

The other party was silent for a moment. "...You're bluffing."

"Full refund if it doesn't work."

Another silence.

Ye Wanwan wasn't in a hurry. She'd put the talismans up mostly out of curiosity. These two Ping'an talismans were, in truth, her practice pieces from the past month.

After seeing the fates of Fang He'an and Bai Jian, and combined with what the Eye of Rebirth had shown her in the scripture pavilion, Ye Wanwan was ninety percent certain that those visions corresponded to what her shijie and the others had experienced in her past life.

Only in her past life, Ye Wanwan had still been an outer disciple clinging to Wushang Sect at that point. She hadn't known them, and so she hadn't witnessed how things unfolded.

She had no way to verify the truth.

But she knew one thing.

Fate had already changed. In this life, her cultivation had not been crippled — and she was now a disciple of Tianyi Sect.

And so Ye Wanwan wanted to try something.

If those were the fates originally meant for Bai Jian and the others — then this time, she wanted to change them.

The Ping'an talismans had taken her an entire month to draw. Her cultivation was still shallow, so two talismans had cost her a full month's effort.

But the effects were real.

They could block any form of harm.

The other party's voice took on a more measured tone. "Any level of damage?"

"Below the Golden Core stage — ninety percent. Above that, the effect diminishes. For higher levels you'd really have to test it yourself."

That was the limit of what Ye Wanwan could guarantee with her current Golden Core cultivation. She had tested it — the talisman could withstand her own strongest strike.

"Alright."

The moment the word landed, Ye Wanwan heard a distinct chime — the sound of a transaction completing — and then a cheerful notification rang in her mind:

"Congratulations, vendor! 'Big Spender' has purchased your Ping'an talisman. Seven thousand spirit stones have been deposited~"

Ye Wanwan stared.

They'd taken a thirty percent cut.

Absolute thieves.

"Why can I only buy one? The other one won't let me purchase it."

"Oh, it's limited to one per person."

"..."

Ye Wanwan said, "One Ping'an talisman only blocks damage once. One is enough — why would you need so many?"

"Because for me, one isn't quite enough."

Ye Wanwan said, "...Then come back for another one after you've used it."

"Fine," the buyer replied, sounding none too pleased.

No sooner had they finished speaking than another chime rang out — "Ding ding ding! Congratulations, vendor! 'Just Browsing' has purchased your Ping'an talisman. Seven thousand spirit stones have been deposited~ Keep up the good work!"

Ye Wanwan heard this.

And so did Big Spender.

Because the talisman that had been sitting on the stall had suddenly vanished.

"Where did it go?"

Ye Wanwan said, "Sold."

"Oh — there was another lab rat willing to spend like me? Fast hands. I was just thinking of recommending it to someone."

Ye Wanwan fell silent.

With her goods sold out, Ye Wanwan closed up her stall. The other party's projection faded from view and drifted toward other stalls.

Ye Wanwan packed up and looked around.

"Time to go home."

With a single thought, she vanished from the street — and found herself standing in an empty stretch of sandy ground. She clicked her tongue. "What a sorry state."

She didn't even have a home in the Spirit Market.

Sometimes Ye Wanwan thought that this Spirit Market bore an uncanny resemblance to a video game created by some programmer who'd dropped dead from overwork and transmigrated into a cultivation world.

The game had both a marketplace and housing.

Aside from a combat system that hadn't been implemented yet, all the basic functions of a proper trading platform were already in place.

If you swapped the code for cultivation world rune formations and teleportation arrays, then whoever built this — that programmer — had to be at least an Integrated Stage formation expert.

Because only a cultivator of that level would have the ability to construct a virtual space this vast, one that covered half the continent and accommodated untold numbers of powerful cultivators within its network.

Ye Wanwan measured out the available land for a while before realizing that building even a small home here wasn't going to be simple — the land itself cost money, and so did the house.

She opened her personal account.

"Fourteen thousand spirit stones."

These were stored in the Spirit Market vault, ready to be withdrawn at any time.

She opened the Cave Dwelling page.

The cheapest option listed was — fifteen thousand.

And it was nothing more than a thatched hut.

"...I can't afford property anywhere, can I."

Ye Wanwan transferred one thousand from her Spirit Grass earnings of the previous day, bringing the total to exactly fifteen thousand, and purchased a thatched hut exactly two square meters in size.

If Li Wanzhi had been there, he would've absolutely berated her for throwing money away.

Fifteen thousand spirit stones for that?!

But Ye Wanwan, who had accessed the Spirit Market and understood its secrets, knew one thing for certain — it was worth every stone.

Even if it was just a two-square-meter thatched hut.

She stepped inside her little cave dwelling. It was completely bare — nothing in it at all.

But Ye Wanwan didn't mind. She wasn't here to live. What she wanted was the dwelling's passive ability.

She sat cross-legged on the ground and began to cultivate.

The Qi Refinement technique cycled through its circuits, one full revolution after another. By the time Ye Wanwan had finished what would normally take a full day of practice —

She stepped out of the Spirit Market to find that only six hours had passed in the outside world.

Ye Wanwan gripped the jade token tightly. "One day outside, two days inside. Two-times time acceleration."

She stepped back into the Spirit Market and looked at the little thatched hut before her. "It's the cheapest place there is, but with this kind of effect, it'll do."

"Once I earn more, I'll upgrade the dwelling. The time multiplier should stack even higher then."

Ye Wanwan exhaled in relief.

The Spirit Market's existence would buy her a great deal of time.

Enough to push hard for the Sect Tournament next year.

She didn't want to miss what was coming.

Ye Wanwan immersed herself in cultivation, intending to spend both days inside the Spirit Market — but a force from the governing rules suddenly expelled her, sending her straight back out.

She gritted her teeth.

"There's even an anti-addiction mode? Are you serious?"

She'd only been inside for thirteen continuous hours before the Spirit Market kicked her out. Clearly the rules here limited occupancy to one day at a time in the outside world.

After a full day had passed, she could re-enter.

That was one of the drawbacks of using the Spirit Market as a cultivation space.

"Fine."

"It's time to go up the mountain anyway."

Ye Wanwan looked up toward the snow-capped summit, a glimmer of contemplation in her eyes. "It's time to meet the new Shifu."

chapters.title: Oh? A Familiar Face
chapters.content:
Once bitten, twice shy.

The bonds of discipleship at Wushang Sect had wounded Ye Wanwan far too deeply. So when it came to taking a master, she had no real expectations.

If she had to, she would. She didn't refuse outright.

But whether she was genuinely convinced — that, only she knew.

...

The snow mountain.

The coldest place in the entire Tianyi mountain range.

Tianyi Sect sat near the northern edge of the land, and in the depths of winter, the mountain range faded to pure white at its far reaches. At the very summit, the ice had not thawed in a thousand years.

The snow there had not melted in ten thousand.

Simply approaching it was enough to feel the cold seeping through every breath, cutting into the lungs with a sharp, aching sting — impossible to endure without shielding oneself with spiritual energy.

Ye Wanwan made her way upward from the foot of the mountain and quickly noticed how rapidly her spiritual energy was draining. She began to wonder — could anyone actually live up here?

By the time she reached the midway point, her five Golden Cores were already spinning at full speed, burning through their power to keep her going.

She dared not be careless any longer.

This place was not somewhere someone at the Qi Refinement stage could reach.

And since entering the sect, she had never once revealed that she possessed another five Golden Cores. No matter who was watching, she appeared to be nothing more than a Qi Refinement cultivator.

But now...

The look she directed toward the summit deepened by a fraction.

With her Golden Core power shielding her body, the cold became somewhat more bearable. But as she drew closer to the peak, her spiritual energy burned faster than she could have imagined.

By the time Ye Wanwan finally stood at the summit and caught sight of Pei Xuan seated on the stone platform — already merged with the surrounding wind and snow — her first thought was:

Is he still alive?

The man's shoulders were buried under a thick layer of accumulated snow. He hadn't moved in what seemed like a very long time. His entire figure had been swallowed by the snowdrifts.

If Ye Wanwan's eyesight hadn't been so sharp, she might not have spotted him at all.

There wasn't a trace of human warmth coming from him.

Come to think of it, when she'd first seen him step out of the void, she hadn't sensed much vitality from him either. He'd seemed more like an ice sculpture than a person.

"I'm not dead."

A voice suddenly rang out across the summit. Ye Wanwan's gaze stayed fixed on him — she watched his eyelashes give the faintest flutter as he opened his eyes and calmly looked her over.

"Not bad. Four hours to climb the mountain — that puts you around third in Tianyi Sect."

Ye Wanwan said nothing.

Li Mingde and Xun Yin, standing nearby: "...Shidi, do you have to be like that."

"Who was first?"

Pei Xuan languidly shook the snow from his left shoulder. "Me."

"And second?"

He raised his right hand and shook off the snow on that side. "Also me."

Ye Wanwan grinned. "You certainly have a sense of humor, Senior."

"I'm not joking." Pei Xuan's dark eyes turned to Ye Wanwan. A very faint expression crossed his lips — more of a sardonic edge than a proper smile. "In the same cultivation realm, my first ascent took two hours. The second time, an hour and a half."

Ye Wanwan held his gaze, and slowly let her smile fall.

He had said "same cultivation realm" — not her Qi Refinement stage.

He knew about her situation.

"Today's lesson ends here. When you can make it up in under two hours, come find me and I'll teach you."

With that, Pei Xuan resumed his original posture. This time he didn't even bother shaking off the snow — he simply closed his eyes and returned to stillness.

The summit felt, in an instant, as though only Ye Wanwan remained.

Along with the faint, lingering mockery radiating from the man before her.

Ye Wanwan clenched her jaw.

She said nothing. She turned and walked back down the mountain.

Back in her room, she skipped dinner entirely and went straight to sleep. The next morning, she got up and climbed again.

This time: three and a half hours.

Pei Xuan didn't even open his eyes. She hadn't met his standard, and she knew it — he wouldn't acknowledge her again.

The young woman carved a mark into the stone platform and walked back down.

For ten consecutive days, Ye Wanwan repeated this routine without pause. Four hours became three. Three became just over two.

But "just over two" was still not "within two."

Even Li Wanzhi could no longer watch in silence.

"Why aren't you running away?" He sat down next to her, rice bowl in hand. "What good is a master who just makes you climb a mountain every day? What's the point of keeping him?"

Ye Wanwan said nothing. She simply looked at him.

Li Wanzhi straightened his expression with great seriousness. "My desire to escape has not wavered."

Ye Wanwan said, "Mm."

Then she glanced at Fang He'an.

Li Wanzhi followed her gaze. Fang He'an was watching them from across the courtyard.

Li Wanzhi: "..."

Fang He'an smiled pleasantly. "Li Shidi, still haven't given up? Come on — finish eating and let's head over to Third Shibo's place."

Li Wanzhi's face fell. "Do we have to..."

"We do."

Ye Wanwan paid the two of them no more attention. She finished her meal and went back to her room to meditate.

The ten days of mountain climbing were brutal, but the effects were undeniable. Ye Wanwan could feel her spiritual energy growing denser with each passing day.

And the changes in her constitution were real.

After having her Golden Cores forcibly extracted, her constitution had been left weakened and frail. She had always felt the cold acutely in winter, relying on sheer force of will to keep anyone from noticing.

But after these ten days, Ye Wanwan found that — well, she'd grown immune.

The ordinary cold was nothing compared to what waited at the top of that snow mountain.

When you freeze long enough, you stop noticing.

With her body in its best state, and with time still left in the day, she began drawing talismans.

Over these ten days, she had entered the Spirit Market only to cultivate — but cultivating inside required burning through spirit stones. Even though she had earned fourteen thousand from her earlier sales, she'd already spent some on the dwelling, and with the current balance she had left from selling bits of Spirit Grass and Spirit Elixirs on the side, she was now sitting at about two thousand stones.

Nowhere near enough if she wanted to set up a spirit-gathering formation inside her Spirit Market dwelling.

Time to earn more.

Ye Wanwan steadied her mind, picked up her brush, and in a matter of moments had finished three talismans. She shook out her hand.

"Better. My speed has improved since last time."

After completing the talismans, she also carved two defensive formation stones — listed one for sale, kept one for herself, along with a single talisman.

At a price that was, naturally, far from cheap.

This time, she didn't even make it back to her room before someone appeared at her stall. "These talismans are different from last time."

She recognized the languid voice immediately. "These are Calamity-Dissolving talismans," she explained.

"Ping'an, Calamity-Dissolving — sounds like the same thing to me."

"It's not." Ye Wanwan's voice was even. "Those with no illness wear a Ping'an talisman for protection. Those already carrying wounds or internal injuries — wearing this one can ease half the pain."

"Half per talisman? So if I buy two, does that mean a full recovery?"

Ye Wanwan paused for a moment, then added, "...One person can only benefit from one talisman at a time. A second one won't do much."

"Your talismans really have their limits, don't they."

Before she could respond, she heard the familiar chime of a completed transaction. She thought to herself: fine. He's a paying customer. She could let it go.

"What about these formation stones?"

"Defensive."

"Oh... I don't need those."

With that, he was gone.

Ye Wanwan turned and went back into her dwelling to cultivate. While she was in closed cultivation, someone purchased the two defensive formation stones she'd left behind.

"Defensive formation stones — perfect timing. Shimei could use these."

Dou Ming tucked the stones into his pocket and left the Spirit Market.

Meanwhile, in stark contrast to Ye Wanwan's industrious cultivation inside the Spirit Market, the mood over at Qingyun Peak in Wushang Sect had grown heavy and still as a tomb.

chapters.title: Body Breathing
chapters.content:
Beneath Profound Ice Cliff.

Ji Changhuai was dragged out with red-rimmed eyes, and had been sitting at the mouth of the gorge for two full days, refusing to leave. "I won't believe she's dead until I see a body. Not for one day."

Another disciple said calmly, "Dashixiong, the bottom of Profound Ice Cliff is full of cyclone vortexes. If someone falls in, there won't even be bones left."

"What do you mean by that?" Ji Changhuai's eyes were bloodshot. "You're saying we stop looking?"

"Not that we don't want to — it's that we can't."

The disciples exchanged glances and looked toward Ji Changhuai, saying nothing more. It had already been two months, and Ji Changhuai had still insisted on keeping them here.

There had been dozens at first. Now only seven or eight remained.

Two months was a long time. Even these last few who had stayed out of loyalty were no longer willing to continue in vain. The updrafts at the bottom of the cliff were fierce and bone-piercingly cold.

For disciples below the Foundation Building stage, going in at all meant risking their lives.

For the sake of Ye Wanwan — who had defied the sect — they didn't think it was worth sacrificing themselves.

Ji Changhuai's red eyes trembled. "But Seventh Shimei, she..."

"Dashixiong, I'll stay with you. If we can't find Shijie today, we won't go back." A girl's stubborn voice pulled Ji Changhuai out of his thoughts.

He turned to find Ye Qian, her face ashen.

Little Shimei...

But wasn't it because of her that Seventh Shimei had been driven to this in the first place?

Ji Changhuai found he didn't know how to face Ye Qian.

Ye Qian's eyes were red. "I'll find Seventh Shijie myself. I'll explain everything to her in person. I truly never intended to take her Golden Cores."

With that, she turned and stepped toward the edge of the cliff.

Ji Changhuai snapped back to his senses and grabbed her.

Ye Qian looked back, tears streaming down her face. "I really didn't mean to hurt her."

"I know. I believe you."

Ji Changhuai was so distressed he could barely breathe.

Seeing the weight hanging over everyone present, his voice cracked as he said, "Come on. All of you — let's go."

"But Shijie—" Ye Qian started.

"We're done looking."

A month after Ji Changhuai brought Ye Qian back from Profound Ice Cliff to recover, Dou Ming had already moved on — far ahead of Ji Changhuai.

Seeing that even Dashixiong had finally come to terms with it, he remarked, "I've always said that girl pulled a perfect vanishing act on purpose. She's probably sitting somewhere right now watching us make fools of ourselves and laughing. You really fell for her little trick, Dashixiong?"

Ji Changhuai's expression was bleak. "If we really did wrong her..."

Recalling how resolute Ye Wanwan had looked in the moment she leapt from the cliff, Dou Ming's chest tightened briefly — but he shook it off quickly and laughed. "What are you talking about, Dashixiong? So many people saw her shatter Shimei's Golden Core. How could we possibly have wronged her?"

Ji Changhuai raised his head sharply. "Who actually saw it with their own eyes?"

"It was obviously..."

Dou Ming opened his mouth, and found he couldn't produce a name. The two of them looked at each other. They realized, at the same moment, the same thing.

The story had always been circulating. But when it came to naming someone who had actually witnessed it firsthand — no one had ever stepped forward.

Dou Ming laughed awkwardly. "Surely you're not suspecting Shimei. She's completely guileless."

Ji Changhuai averted his gaze. "No. But I'm beginning to wonder whether someone deliberately stirred up conflict between us."

Dou Ming lowered his eyes.

Come to think of it, he couldn't quite remember when he'd started disliking Ye Wanwan. It was all somewhat hazy now. Because before all of this, he had genuinely...

He had genuinely been fond of that shimei.

Dou Ming looked down at the formation stones in his hands. For once, he didn't immediately move to pass them along.

At the doorway, Ye Qian stood holding a bowl of medicinal soup that had long gone cold. She stood there for a long time, unable to bring herself to push the door open.

When she finally composed herself, she knocked softly. "Dashixiong. I've brought your medicine."

...

Ye Wanwan surfaced early from her closed cultivation inside the Spirit Market dwelling and examined the formation stone, now dim after use. She counted through what she had left — just over a thousand spirit stones.

She pulled up her stall page and found that the second talisman had also sold. The buyer's name was oddly familiar.

"Just Browsing."

She traced back through her previous sales record. Sure enough — the same person.

"What a coincidence."

She listed her last defensive formation stone and a few stalks of Spirit Grass, then exited the Spirit Market.

Back outside, Ye Wanwan closed her eyes and slept.

Cultivators at her level had long surpassed the need for sleep to restore themselves. But Ye Wanwan maintained that even immortals needed rest.

So — eyes closed, blanket pulled up.

Sleep.

Before dawn the next morning, Ye Wanwan scattered some seeds in the courtyard, then made straight for the snow mountain to keep pushing herself.

Half a month later.

She stood before Pei Xuan and held up two fingers.

"Two hours. Less a quarter."

"More precisely — one hour and seven quarters."

Ye Wanwan tilted her head, grinning. "That puts me in second place on the leaderboard."

Pei Xuan sat like a white spirit carved from snow. At her words, he said, unhurried, "That does sound like cause for some pride."

Ye Wanwan brushed off her sleeve. "Not really. I haven't reached first yet."

She looked at him. "Once I break the hour-and-a-half mark, I'll come find you again."

"But you've already met my requirement," Pei Xuan said, shifting his posture and sending the snow slipping from his shoulders. "So I'll teach you something now."

Ye Wanwan frowned slightly — she wasn't particularly eager to start just yet.

Pei Xuan said, unhurriedly, "You can learn it and simply choose not to use it."

"Fair point."

Ye Wanwan settled into a cross-legged seat and listened.

But Pei Xuan simply raised a hand. A memory condensed into a streak of light and landed between Ye Wanwan's brows. And just like that, a new cultivation method took root in her mind.

Unlike anything taught at Wushang Sect, and different again from what Bai Jian and the others practiced. "Is this a breath-holding technique? The Turtle's Rest Art?"

Pei Xuan noticed her curiosity. "Not quite. This technique still involves breathing — but the breath moves through the body."

Breathing through the body?

Ye Wanwan studied the practice method carefully.

She couldn't make sense of what that meant.

Pei Xuan said, "When your body becomes one with the natural world, you'll understand the meaning of those words."

"This is also one of the cultivation methods suited to those with multiple spirit roots."

Ye Wanwan froze. She looked up at Pei Xuan, a trace of surprise flickering in her eyes. He did know about her multiple spirit roots after all.

But had this technique been specifically sought out for her?

"I created this technique myself," Pei Xuan said, his tone offhand — yet the words that followed were quietly astonishing. "I also have multiple spirit roots."

Ye Wanwan's heart lurched. Pei Xuan was a Divine Transformation stage expert.

So the curse of the Golden Core stage for multi-root cultivators really could be broken?

She couldn't help it — her breathing quickened.

Pei Xuan said, without mercy, "It's too soon to say. Breaking through still depends on your opportunities and natural talent. Some people simply stay where they are for the rest of their lives."

Then he added one more line.

"I am the exception."

"..."

Alright.

You're the exception.

One day, I'll be one too.

Ye Wanwan said, "Should I start memorizing the technique now?"

Pei Xuan gave her a look that was almost amused. "The method is already in your head. Do you really need to ask?"

Ye Wanwan understood.

And so did Pei Xuan.

They were both playing dumb.

One wasn't quite ready to take a master. The other wasn't in any rush to take a disciple. So they left things as they were, neither saying it aloud.

Ye Wanwan was perfectly happy with that arrangement.

That day, she didn't rush back down the mountain. She stayed at the summit, working through the cultivation method Pei Xuan had passed to her. The first step was to master breath-holding, and only then would the "body breathing" he'd spoken of follow.

But the breath-holding alone nearly took half her life from her.

Which made it clear enough — converting internal qi circulation to external was no simple matter.

But then again, what in cultivation ever was?

And the harder the challenge, the more Ye Wanwan wanted to conquer it.

chapters.title: The Spirit Tempering Art
chapters.content:
When a second white figure appeared on the snow-capped summit — one that seemed to have merged with the drifts just like the snow itself — Pei Xuan couldn't help but open his eyes to look.

Ye Wanwan sat completely still where she had planted herself, as though she'd turned to stone.

She was still breathing — but barely. Faint, thread-thin breaths.

The aura around her was shifting, slowly and quietly.

Meanwhile, snow began to settle on her shoulders.

A soft, accumulating weight, gentle as a falling curtain.

Pei Xuan watched for a moment, then raised a hand and swept away the snow drifting around her. A small barrier formed, shielding her from the storm on all sides.

"Still works hard, this one."

The murmur was swallowed by the wind.

Ye Wanwan was deep in a meditative trance, entirely unaware of the world beyond herself.

Her whole being was submerged in this new cultivation method.

Pei Xuan's technique, at first glance, appeared to be a breath-holding exercise. But study it closely, and one would find that the breath-holding was the end result — not the process.

The true key lay in shifting from internal to external breathing. Moving the breath from the lungs and organs outward, into the body's surface.

Merging with the heaven and earth. Becoming one with the natural world.

Once that transition was complete, cultivation would never truly stop. Whether standing, sitting, or asleep — she would always be refining her spiritual energy, not losing a single moment.

This was the cultivation method best suited to those with multiple spirit roots.

And the fastest one.

The difficulty lay entirely in how to make that transition.

How to carry the internal qi outward.

And then allow both to circulate together, forming a new and complete cycle.

Ye Wanwan focused her mind on the qi cycling through her meridians, watching a strand of spirit energy enter from outside, travel along the channels, complete its revolution, and return to the golden core. She watched it slowly seep back out through the pores of her skin.

Only a fraction of a percent was retained.

This was the cycle every entry-level disciple knew. The foundation of all Qi Refinement techniques.

But what if one were to create a new circuit outside the body — one that interlinked with the internal meridians to form a complete cycle?

Ye Wanwan wasn't sure if it would work. But she'd thought of it, so she tried it.

Drawing on her spirit consciousness, she traced rune patterns around herself. Spirit-energy condensed into talisman-form, building a new circulation path outside her body. Under Ye Wanwan's guiding intent, it gradually resonated with her internal meridians.

And then, it became a new loop.

The effect was similar to a spirit-gathering formation, except that an ordinary formation required spirit stones as its anchor. Here, Ye Wanwan had made herself the anchor.

Spirit energy gathered from the world around her, poured into her meridians, then flowed back out through the external formation — and Ye Wanwan felt the moment the rune pattern and her internal cycle completed one full revolution together.

Even if that revolution came at considerable cost.

The spirit energy flooding into her was too vast. It tore at her meridians as it forced its way through, grinding forward painfully. Where she had once completed three major revolutions with ease, she couldn't even finish a single minor one now.

And the pain that came with it was beyond description.

Ye Wanwan gritted her teeth and pushed through until one small cycle was complete. When the energy finally settled back into her golden core, she saw it clearly — what remained in her core after this one cycle was more than ten times what a standard cycle had ever produced.

Naturally, the agony had been ten times what she was used to, too.

But the results were extraordinary.

Ye Wanwan exhaled slowly and surfaced from the trance. "Looks like I can't run that mode all the time."

This method was effective, but it still relied on an external prop. She needed to internalize it herself — to understand how to draw spirit energy directly from the world around her through her own perception.

That was the only way to truly make it effortless.

She flexed her fingers, noticed that Pei Xuan still hadn't stirred, and settled back in. She hadn't built up sufficient foundation yet — using shortcuts in the meantime was perfectly fine.

Once she had entered her trance again, Pei Xuan opened his eyes and fell into quiet thought.

The first time he'd used the Spirit Tempering Art to refine his constitution — how long had it taken him?

A month, if he recalled correctly.

This girl hadn't even needed a single day.

...

As Ye Wanwan drew on the rune patterns to absorb spirit energy at an accelerated pace, she was also, day by day, reducing her reliance on them. Using her primordial spirit, she reached outward to sense the rhythms of heaven and earth.

Little by little, she began to replace what the rune patterns had been doing on their own.

Until at last, she completed a true internal-external circulation — and successfully elevated the Qi Refinement Art into what would, a month later, Pei Xuan tell her was called the Spirit Tempering Art.

"Quite a formidable name."

By then, Ye Wanwan had also broken Pei Xuan's record, bringing her ascent time to within an hour and a half. But by that point, neither of them cared about the record anymore.

What she needed now was to be able to cultivate with her full attention — without interruption.

And so Ye Wanwan moved from the disciples' peak up to the snow mountain summit.

"I can grow spirit grass on a plot in the Spirit Market and harvest it whenever I need it. But I can't always be ducking into the Spirit Market for shelter. I need a proper place to live."

She rubbed her chin thoughtfully. She was going to have to build something up here.

But before she could even gather the materials, a slow, unhurried voice drifted over.

"Did it never occur to you that your Shifu might have his own cave dwelling?"

Ye Wanwan turned, surprised. "Shifu, I assumed your cave dwelling was that rock you sit on."

Pei Xuan: speechless.

Pei Xuan dissolved the concealment array, and only then did Ye Wanwan see what had been hidden nearby — a cave dwelling, cold and imposing, that she hadn't noticed at all.

She looked at the structure — deep blue from top to bottom — and laughed. "A cave dwelling worthy of Shifu. Looks only marginally more livable than sleeping on the ground."

It wasn't quite an ice palace, but it bore all the hallmarks of one. Cold, austere, severe.

Yet undeniably spacious.

Spacious enough that Ye Wanwan could have taken a different room every hour.

"Any room that's empty is yours to use," Pei Xuan said calmly. He rose from the stone platform for what was a rare occasion and led Ye Wanwan inside.

The gates swung open.

There was no biting cold as she'd expected. Instead, a wave of warmth met her — and the entire dwelling was done in deep blue and white, woven together in interleaving tones.

The whole place had the look of a particular kind of ore.

Ye Wanwan's heartbeat quickened. "Is this... Cyan Sea Soul Condensing Stone?"

Pei Xuan glanced back. "You have a decent eye."

Ye Wanwan's voice grew tight with barely contained shock. "The entire cave dwelling? This is one of the rarest ores found only in the deepest ocean. Master artificers have paid fortunes just to obtain a single small piece."

And here it had been used to build an entire cave dwelling.

"More or less. Where there wasn't enough, I filled it in with Blue Crystal," Pei Xuan said, unbothered.

"..."

A gram of Blue Crystal was worth more than a tael of Cyan Sea Soul Condensing Stone. And he'd used it as filler?

"Shifu — you're very wealthy, aren't you."

"I do alright."

"Then... could you lend me a hundred thousand to spend?"

Pei Xuan turned to look at his little disciple. That grin on her face — shameless and a little teasing — sat oddly with her otherwise cool eyes, eyes that seemed to hold the rest of the world at a certain remove, as though she never truly let anything in.

Yet here she was, stretching out her hand to ask him for money.

There was something in it that was, unexpectedly... amusing.

Pei Xuan flicked his wrist.

A small lacquered box landed in Ye Wanwan's hands. She startled.

"It's yours," Pei Xuan said, turning back toward the inner rooms. "If it's not enough, say so."

Ye Wanwan opened the box.

Her pupils contracted.

Inside, nestled in perfect rows — were spirit crystals.

Twelve of them, brimming full.

A single spirit crystal could be exchanged for one million low-grade spirit stones.

"Shifu really is very wealthy..."

Pei Xuan said, "The cave dwelling has plenty of empty rooms that I rarely use. Pick whichever one you like."

Ye Wanwan looked left, then right — then, grinning, she put forward a suggestion. "Actually — could I open up my own cave dwelling next door?"

Pei Xuan looked at her.

In the moment where Ye Wanwan expected nothing —

He said, "Yes."

Ye Wanwan's hand closed tight.

He...

He had actually agreed.

chapters.title: The Purple Spirit Cave Dwelling
chapters.content:
She had not known Pei Xuan for long, but cultivators of his level tended to have temperaments that were difficult to read.

Take Yan Ding, for example.

A single glance from Yan Ding was enough to keep all his disciples from daring to act out of line.

Even Ji Changhuai — the disciple Yan Ding trusted most — never threw tantrums in his presence. Always composed, always careful never to give offense. That was the aura of authority Yan Ding had instilled in them.

Yet in this exchange with Pei Xuan, she had put forward two conditions, one after the other.

Each more outrageous than the last.

And Pei Xuan had agreed to both.

He and Yan Ding were...

Different.

His cultivation was deeper, yet his temperament seemed far more easygoing.

Fang He'an: No, Shimei, that's just your imagination.

Ye Wanwan's desire to have her own living space was not said in jest.

She genuinely wanted a place of her own.

Pei Xuan's cave dwelling was magnificent, and the Cyan Sea Soul Condensing Stone could even nourish one's primordial spirit — but at the end of the day, it was someone else's home. Wanting to do things there never felt quite free.

She planned to look for materials in the Spirit Market and build her own cave dwelling.

Nothing grand was necessary — small would do.

But this wasn't something that could be solved overnight, and Ye Wanwan still needed time, because whether or not she had enough spirit stones was its own problem.

Just as she was considering whether to paint more spirit talismans or go hunting for a secret realm ore vein, Pei Xuan reached into his sleeve and produced a small, delicate spirit device.

Ye Wanwan stared at it for two beats.

Pei Xuan said, "I made this a long time ago, just idly refining — and it came out imperfect. Counts as a half-finished piece. Since finding materials to forge your own would take considerable time, you might as well use this in the meantime."

As he spoke, the spirit device was sent flicking into Ye Wanwan's palm.

Ye Wanwan's hand closed around it. She kept the grin on her face all the same. "You're really giving this to me? Shifu?"

"Is it strange for a Shifu to give a gift to his disciple?"

"Not strange at all."

Ye Wanwan smiled as she said it. But...

It was the first time she had ever received one.

Pei Xuan said in his unhurried way, "Shall I come with you to try it out?"

"Sure."

Ye Wanwan stepped out of the Cyan Sea cave dwelling and spent some time examining the small structure resting in her palm. Pei Xuan was patient. "A drop of blood will do it."

Ye Wanwan complied.

A moment passed.

The spirit device recognized its new master. The tiny house glowed in her palm, and with a single thought, the cave dwelling materialized right before her.

A small spirit dwelling — set down beside the vast and magnificent Cyan Sea cave dwelling — appeared, cloaked in purple from top to bottom, refined and quietly elegant.

Beside the imposing grandeur of its neighbor, this one was far more understated, far more delicate — and yet it carried its owner's style all the same.

Cold.

But the soft violet hue tempered that chill.

Ye Wanwan glanced at Pei Xuan.

Pei Xuan caught the question in her eyes and said, "It's yours. Do you really need my opinion before going inside?"

Ye Wanwan laughed.

"Shifu, come in with me."

Pei Xuan didn't move. "I forged it — you think I don't know what's in there? Go yourself."

Ye Wanwan watched him turn back into a streak of light and return to his stone platform. She paused, thoughtful, then stepped inside the cave dwelling.

She pushed open the gates.

A spacious courtyard spread out before her.

A protective barrier covered the courtyard, sealing out the biting cold of the mountain summit, carving out its own self-contained world. Around the perimeter of the yard were east and west wings.

One could serve as a pill-refining chamber.

One could serve as a device-forging chamber.

The rooms were generously sized and could be restructured and extended at will.

Past the outer courtyard, through the middle courtyard, was another yard, again flanked by two wings, four rooms in all.

Ye Wanwan walked further back, but found that after two courtyards the rooms ended — and in their place, a curtain of water formed by a barrier array appeared. Recalling that Pei Xuan had called it a half-finished work, she understood at once what that meant.

She returned to the outer courtyard.

Ye Wanwan found that the part she liked best was the courtyard itself.

Because this courtyard took up half the entire cave dwelling — and within the barrier, the wind and snow of the summit were shut completely out. Inside, the four seasons unfolded in miniature, with all four climates present.

For someone who wanted to grow a little Spirit Grass, it was everything she needed.

Add her talismans on top of that, and it was more than enough.

With the cave dwelling now in hand, Ye Wanwan moved her belongings over from the disciples' peak, leaving Li Wanzhi as the sole new arrival still living there.

Li Wanzhi was deeply aggrieved. "Even you're abandoning me now."

"I never claimed to want you around."

Ye Wanwan collected the last of her things and left without a backward glance. Li Wanzhi fumed for a long while afterward. "Got a Shifu and now Shijie doesn't matter anymore. Hmph."

Ye Wanwan thought about it. Dou Ming had said something similar once — and yet he was the one who'd gotten a shimei and forgotten all about her.

She shrugged, dry amusement coloring the thought.

What was the point of thinking about people like that.

A bunch of trash, the lot of them.

Living at the mountain summit, Ye Wanwan saved the time she used to spend climbing and descending each day. Two hours of seated meditation with Pei Xuan daily, practicing the Spirit Tempering Art.

Two hours of sword training.

Two hours of tempering her constitution in the ice spring.

Even when she turned her attention to drawing spirit talismans, her speed had improved considerably — though selling them at the same premium price as before wasn't quite so simple anymore.

Because Ye Wanwan had also noticed that the number of people who knew about the Spirit Market was still quite small.

That would need to spread further before the market for her work grew.

For this reason, Ye Wanwan kept a little talisman work going each day to maintain her skills, but devoted the bulk of her energy to cultivation.

The thirteenth layer of Qi Refinement was smoothly broken through, and she entered her second Foundation Building.

Ye Wanwan hadn't forgotten her goal either — she went straight into closed cultivation, pushing hard for the Golden Core stage.

Half a year later.

Boom!

A low rumble of heavenly thunder rolled over the snow mountain summit. Everyone in the sect noticed.

"Heavenly thunder," Sect Master Li Mingde said with a warm chuckle, stroking his beard. "These youngsters are moving along at a fine pace."

Xun Yin, hunched over his spirit crop fields, raised his head at the sound and muttered, "I still haven't figured out this spirit food recipe, and they're already making themselves obsolete. Half a year wasted."

Fang He'an pulled off his bamboo hat. "Where's that thunder coming from?"

Xun Yin turned and smacked the back of his head. "You little brat — your new little shimei has already formed her core and you haven't even done anything with yourself yet."

Fang He'an stumbled forward from the blow. "Shibo, I formed my core ages ago!"

"...Oh. Forgot."

"This is what gets me — if you've already formed your core, how are you supposed to freeload off your shijie's sword anymore?" Xun Yin fumed.

Fang He'an muttered darkly under his breath. "There's still that thing in the Sword Tomb. It's not like I can go face anyone."

He grumbled to himself and wisely didn't say it any louder.

He looked toward the snow mountain where the thunder was rolling, listening to the peals fall one after another.

"Little shimei's cultivation speed really is something. But isn't she Five Spirit Roots?"

Xun Yin's gaze drifted to a white flower that had opened on one of his spirit herbs. "Five spirit roots, yes — but five heavenly spirit roots, at that."

Thunder clouds churned overhead.

Ye Wanwan stood beneath them, her expression calm, though not without a thread of puzzlement. The last time she'd formed her core, there hadn't been anything like this.

Inside her golden core, all five cores were trembling faintly, as if affected by the heavenly thunder.

Her eyes lowered slightly.

Was there a formation array beneath Profound Ice Cliff blocking the heavenly mechanism from tracking her?

But idle thoughts aside, the tribulation lightning still had to be endured.

She looked up at the churning storm overhead. Her gaze did not waver. Only resolve.

"Come."

chapters.title: The Tribulation Lightning
chapters.content:
Boom.

The thunder clouds split apart. Lightning flashed across the sky in a blinding arc, cleaving through the darkness like a blade — utterly breathtaking.

In her past life, Ye Wanwan had walked the path of talisman cultivation, skirting the orthodox road, and had never needed to face a tribulation.

But she was not afraid.

Not a trace of fear showed in the young woman's eyes. She rose to meet the lightning. It swallowed her whole — and on the stone platform below, Pei Xuan sat still as before. But if one looked carefully, they would notice that his hand, resting in his lap, had curled into a tight fist.

She was, after all, his first disciple.

And the heir to the Asking Heart Sword.

Pei Xuan could not be indifferent.

Yet the young woman's gaze blazed as she stood bathed in lightning, letting the heavenly thunder crash against her body without resistance. A violent, numbing force pierced through her skin and left every limb suddenly drained of strength.

The hand gripping her weapon lost seven or eight parts of its power in an instant.

Ye Wanwan dropped to one knee.

"No wonder everyone dreads the tribulation."

Because the first thing it destroyed was your defenses — and your will.

It drove through every meridian in your body and pressed straight into your most vulnerable point: the golden core.

Ye Wanwan summoned the spiritual energy within her core. All five golden cores were pierced by the heavenly thunder now, and cracks seemed to form along their surfaces where lightning and core intertwined.

It felt as though the cores might shatter entirely.

And the other five cores, still in the process of forming, were spinning and colliding wildly under the force of the thunder — unable to complete their coalescence.

The tribulation lightning she hadn't endured at the bottom of Profound Ice Cliff had come for her all at once.

And this was only the first bolt.

Fang He'an frowned. "Little shimei's tribulation looks... rather large."

Xun Yin stroked his beard. "Somewhat out of the ordinary, yes."

But the scope of a tribulation was always proportional to the cultivator's talent. A grand and fearsome tribulation only meant one thing — that Ye Wanwan's talent was extraordinary.

Thunder rang out across the peaks.

The mountain range of Tianyi Sect was lit silver-white.

Ye Wanwan could barely stay upright. Pei Xuan's brow furrowed — he was already moving to rise.

But the young woman slowly straightened her back. Through sheer stubbornness, she hauled herself through the first bolt of heavenly thunder.

"Come again."

The lightning still clung to her body like a web of flickering threads, not yet faded — and the second bolt was already falling. Two bolts stacked together, and still Ye Wanwan did not resist.

Pei Xuan saw through to her intention.

Someone nearby marveled softly, "This little girl has real nerve — she's using the heavenly thunder to temper her body."

Pei Xuan didn't look back. He already knew who had come.

"My disciple," he said, "could not possibly be weak."

Li Mingde laughed. "True enough. I see a bit of you in her."

Ye Wanwan was not resisting because she was testing her own limits — she wanted to use the force of the heavenly thunder to reforge this body of hers, riddled as it was with old wounds.

To complete this baptism by lightning.

Her entire body was already pressed to the ground, yet the young woman held on. She forced herself into a seated posture, feet still touching the earth, channeling the heavenly thunder's force down into the ground below.

She was pushing her limits, yes — but she also knew exactly where those limits were.

A human body could not withstand thunder on this scale without the earth absorbing some of it. If she tried to take it all in herself, that small frame of hers wouldn't last.

Fortunately —

She could still hold.

First bolt. Second. Third...

Ye Wanwan endured them one by one.

By the seventh, all five of her existing golden cores had been successfully tempered — and the other five had at last taken shape. But by now, her body was in a wretched state.

And the seventh bolt came without warning.

Pei Xuan and Li Mingde both sensed what was different about it. They were already moving to lay down a barrier — when the young woman's hands flew up, forming seals.

"Five Element Formation — rise."

The moment the words fell, several spirit talismans emerged from around her body. Light threaded between them and rapidly solidified into a defensive array.

The massive bolt descended — and was divided by the formation into five separate streams, each absorbed by a different talisman, then discharged into the ground.

The young woman stood at the center of the formation.

Unharmed.

A flicker of surprise crossed Li Mingde's eyes.

This girl had come prepared.

Even Pei Xuan's furrowed brow gradually eased.

In the pause between the seventh and eighth bolts, Ye Wanwan moved quickly — drawing on the formation to restore her body's mobility — and swiftly tipped a vial of spirit liquid into her mouth.

She had prepared this in advance: Spirit Liquid refined from Spirit Grass — one mouthful after another, her eyes all the while calm as she looked up at the churning sky.

Half a vial went down. The young woman recovered sixty or seventy percent of her strength. She stowed the gourd, wiped the corner of her mouth, and as lightning blazed again overhead —

She picked up the Asking Heart Sword and rose to meet it.

To challenge the heavenly thunder, again.

This was the eighth bolt.

Li Mingde was quiet for a long moment.

"At her age, to face the heavenly thunder with this much composure and strategy — this child's mind is unlike any ordinary person's."

Brave and wise. Will of iron.

What a fool Wushang Sect was to have let a child like this go.

They would regret it to the bone.

Ye Wanwan raised her sword and met the lightning head-on. The heavenly thunder poured through the Asking Heart Sword. The cyan blade ran silver-bright — and under that blinding light, the old patina of bronze began to peel away, revealing snow-white radiance beneath.

Along with a pressure that had slept since ancient times.

Everyone present seemed to feel it — an ancient spirit stirring awake inside the blade.

"That is..."

Pei Xuan and Li Mingde both narrowed their eyes.

But in the very next instant, that immense pressure seemed to vanish.

The scale of the heavenly thunder pulled everyone's attention back.

The lightning swallowed Ye Wanwan and the Asking Heart Sword whole — yet the young woman's left hand never stopped forming seals. The Five Element talismans spun around her at speed, rapidly dispersing the force of the thunder. The Asking Heart Sword blazed with light.

And absorbed the last of it.

The ninth bolt was already coming.

Everyone was stunned.

"Isn't the gap between the eighth and ninth bolts way too short?!"
