It was. Almost no pause at all.

Fang He'an abandoned Xun Yin. "I'm going to check on Shimei."

But Li Mingde's attention was still fixed on the strange surge of ancient pressure from a moment ago — though it had been too brief. By the time he'd begun to process it, the ninth bolt was already there.

Li Mingde glanced at Pei Xuan. But Pei Xuan's gaze was locked on the final bolt of heavenly thunder.

The strongest one.

The pressure of the last bolt was immense — but Ye Wanwan had not come unprepared. When the first Five Element formation shattered under impact, the second array of runes surged to life at once, light blazing up.

The formation's radiance encircled Ye Wanwan alone, wrapping itself around her and absorbing most of the tribulation's force.

What remained — Ye Wanwan bore herself.

When the storm clouds finally scattered overhead and rain poured down, the sweet cleansing downpour after heavenly thunder began to nourish Ye Wanwan's body.

Feeding into her. Tending to her.

Ye Wanwan spread her arms and fell back against the ground, and she couldn't help but let out a laugh.

She'd done it.

She had successfully formed her core.

A cheer rose from the others nearby.

"Shimei! Shimei!"

Ye Wanwan turned her head. Standing not far off were Bai Jian and Li Wanzhi, Li Wanzhi waving two small flags in wild celebration.

Partway down the mountain, Fang He'an was running toward them.

Ye Wanwan lay there listening to all of them chatter and fuss — and amid all those voices, she heard another set of footsteps, measured and steady, drawing near. She followed the sound and slowly turned her gaze.

chapters.title: The Second Path
chapters.content:
It was Pei Xuan.

Pei Xuan said quietly, "You did very well."

Ye Wanwan could not suppress the curve at the corner of her lips. She nodded emphatically. "I'll be even better from here on."

Because this was not Wushang Sect.

This was Tianyi Sect.

After the tribulation.

Ye Wanwan rested for seven full days before she had fully recovered.

But when they saw the young woman again, Bai Jian, Fang He'an, and the others all went very quiet at the sight of her cultivation. "Why are you back at the Qi Refinement stage, Shimei?"

Li Wanzhi pointed at his own eyes. "If I hadn't watched you endure the lightning tribulation with my own eyes, I would have thought the whole thing was a dream."

Ye Wanwan touched her nose.

She'd discovered this on the second day after the tribulation. And Pei Xuan had already told her it would happen before the tribulation even began — so Ye Wanwan was not alarmed.

"When you face this tribulation, you'll have two choices. The first is to shatter your existing five golden cores and form them again from the beginning — building your foundation, condensing your core, and forming your nascent soul the conventional way. But for you, that path will be difficult. You'll hit the same wall as before, where your cultivation stagnates. You may overcome it. You may not. If you can't, this life ends here."

"And the second choice?"

"Keep forming cores. Don't look back. Push for the maximum number of golden cores, accumulate them, break into the Nascent Soul stage. With the Spirit Tempering Art I've taught you, walk a second path — one no ordinary cultivator has ever walked."

"Do you dare try?"

After Pei Xuan had laid this out, Ye Wanwan spent three days thinking. She turned over every detail of her past life in her mind.

Yan Ding had almost certainly known about her multiple spirit roots and the wall it placed on her advancement.

And so no matter how brilliantly she had performed at Wushang Sect, she had never truly been valued — because a genius who could never break into the Nascent Soul stage was not really a genius.

Not worth the investment.

Her father had sealed her spirit roots thinking he could buy her a way out. What he hadn't foreseen was that Yan Ding had seen through it — and had only felt contempt.

And turned that contempt into cruelty toward her.

Once she'd thought it through clearly, Ye Wanwan chose the second path.

Pei Xuan had asked at the time: "You've thought it through? This path is new to both of us — my guidance may not be correct. If I'm wrong, you may remain at the Golden Core stage for the rest of your life."

"Then I'll stay at Golden Core. The outcome is about the same either way — so I choose the second method."

At worst, she would return to the path of talisman cultivation.

Master and disciple held each other's gaze, and together, they stepped onto a path no one had ever walked.

"I will help you," Pei Xuan said.

And so —

That was the explanation behind what Li Wanzhi and the others were now seeing.

Ye Wanwan smiled and said, "Yes — I'm starting over from the beginning."

"Something's not right. Something's very not right." Li Wanzhi circled around Ye Wanwan and stared at the top of her head. "Were you body-snatched?"

Ye Wanwan laughed softly. She raised a hand, formed a seal, and let her Golden Core cultivation pour outward for a moment.

Li Wanzhi's eyes lit up. "That's... Golden Core stage!"

Ye Wanwan reined in the golden core's aura and concealed her cultivation again. "My spirit root situation is a little unusual, so my cultivation method is different from others. Don't worry, Shixiong — Golden Core or Qi Refinement, it's all still me. I still have the ability to protect myself."

Fang He'an asked, "Has Seventh Shishu spoken to you about the secret realm?"

This was why Ye Wanwan had come down the mountain. The secret realm was opening in a month.

"She did." Ye Wanwan nodded. "I'm going with you all this time."

Before the sect tournament, they'd go scour the secret realm for treasures first. Their odds in the tournament would be better for it.

Fang He'an said, "Done then. You, Shijie, and me — the three of us set out together."

"What about me?" Li Wanzhi called from the side.

Fang He'an pushed his head away. "You haven't formed your core yet. Get out of here."

"..."

Li Wanzhi stretched out his hand in protest. "I'm one step away."

"We leave in half a month. Form your core before then, and you can come with us." Fang He'an said it, and sure enough, Li Wanzhi deflated on the spot.

But to say Li Wanzhi lacked talent would be entirely false.

He had entered the sect alongside Ye Wanwan, and while he couldn't compare to her, in that one year he had already reached Foundation Building stage at full circle — just one step from core formation.

Ye Wanwan was fast only because she was absurd about it.

Ye Wanwan thought to herself — if not for the time dilation inside the Spirit Market, her speed wouldn't be this extraordinary either. Five Spirit Roots meant her cultivation required five times the effort of a single-root cultivator. Even with strong natural talent, cultivation still demanded real, uncompromising time.

"Let me come. I know I'll break through," Li Wanzhi was still pestering them stubbornly.

"If you hit your tribulation out on the road, we'll have to babysit you through it. Stay in the sect and behave yourself."

Fang He'an grabbed him by the collar and dragged him off. The two shimongous went straight to sparring — because over this past year, at least, there had been no more talk of Li Wanzhi trying to run away.

After the two of them left, Bai Jian pressed a bag of spirit stones into Ye Wanwan's hands.

She opened it. Inside was ten thousand spirit stones.

Ye Wanwan was startled. "Shijie."

Bai Jian's eyes curved into a smile. "A congratulatory gift."

Ye Wanwan's hand tightened around the bag.

Bai Jian patted her on the head. "Keep going."

The four of them gathered, settled on what to bring, and then Ye Wanwan returned to the snow mountain.

Pei Xuan was not on the stone platform — he must have been inside his own cave dwelling.

The gates of the Cyan Sea cave dwelling were shut.

Ye Wanwan went into her own and dove headlong into the Spirit Market. Inside, the cave dwelling was still that thatched hut — a small room where there was barely space for a bed.

With spirit stones in hand, Ye Wanwan opened the city page of the Spirit Market. For a higher-grade dwelling and a faster time multiplier, she would need to spend spirit stones to upgrade.

The previous thatched hut had cost fifteen thousand.

The bamboo house was thirty thousand.

Counting what she'd earned from selling talismans, plus what Bai Jian had given her, plus her disciple stipend — she had just barely scraped together thirty thousand and a bit more.

Without hesitation, Ye Wanwan spent every last stone.

Before her eyes, the tiny thatched hut upgraded in an instant into a small bamboo house. Ye Wanwan tested the time multiplier.

Three times.

One day outside, three days inside.

And this time, she wasn't ejected after a single day.

The time she could remain in the Spirit Market had grown considerably longer.

Ye Wanwan ran her hand along the battered little bamboo house. "I wonder what the highest-tier dwelling gives, in terms of time multiplier — and how much it costs."

Even in her past life, she had never upgraded all the way to the top.

Her curiosity about whoever stood behind this Spirit Market grew a little deeper.

For now, though, there was nothing to do but earn spirit stones. Three-times speed was not enough on its own.

Ye Wanwan sat cross-legged and began to cultivate, pushing to raise her cultivation as fast as she could — and just as Pei Xuan had warned her, the further along she went, the slower her progress would become.

The rate at which she absorbed spirit energy was increasingly consumed by her golden cores, leaving less and less for rebuilding her foundation and condensing new ones. It was not easy.

But it made sense, if she thought about it.

Not every dantian could hold this many golden cores. And her bottleneck, in all likelihood, would come at the eleventh core.

Or possibly at the next Foundation Building stage.

But there was still a long way to go before any of that.

For three days inside the Spirit Market, Ye Wanwan did nothing but cultivate the Spirit Tempering Art, using it to draw in spirit energy from a radius of ten li in every direction.

Borrowing the technique's extraordinary effect to compensate for the slower pace of cultivation.

The two forces offset each other.

After three days.

Water and Fire spirit roots: Qi Refinement, second layer.

Metal, Wood, and Earth: stabilizing at the first layer.

Ye Wanwan turned her gaze inward to her dantian, composed herself, and continued to cultivate. After fifteen days had passed inside the Spirit Market, she was expelled.

Fifteen days inside. Five days outside.

Ye Wanwan calculated. "About right. Looks like I still need to spend a day outside before I can go back in."

She waited out the day, then went straight back in without delay.

During all of this time, good news arrived from the disciples' peak.

Li Wanzhi had formed his core.

chapters.title: Illusion
chapters.content:
Perhaps because Fang He'an had been so uncompromising — no core formation, no leaving the sect.

Li Wanzhi knew he had no other chance. He threw himself into cultivation with singular intensity over those two weeks and, four days before their departure, finally formed his core.

The tribulation lightning descended on the disciples' peak without warning.

It caught Xun Yin, Li Mingde, and the other sect elders entirely off guard.

"Another core formation."

"Wonderful, wonderful — these children are all doing this sect proud."

But compared to Ye Wanwan, who had Pei Xuan guiding her, Li Wanzhi had cobbled together his instruction by borrowing a bit from one person and a bit from another — and his tribulation, as a result, was a thoroughly miserable affair.

Chaotic and undignified to watch.

Under the falling thunder, he screamed and flailed wildly, scrambling in every direction to dodge.

Several bolts in, he'd destroyed a handful of buildings on the disciples' peak, and the spirit grass in the courtyard had not been spared. By the time Yan Ju and Fang He'an arrived, Li Wanzhi had barely survived the fifth bolt — and only thanks to his spirit tools.

After that, Yan Ju summoned the Third Elder, who was well-versed in formation arrays, and they helped Li Wanzhi weather the remaining bolts. Afterward, it was said that Yan Ju had given him a thorough and blistering scolding.

Ye Wanwan asked, "Why?"

"Because our Shidi over here walked straight into his tribulation without a single preparation — not one. If Xiaoshishu hadn't sensed something was off and gone to check, he might have genuinely become the first disciple in Tianyi Sect's history to be struck dead by a nine-tier lightning tribulation."

Even Bai Jian extended a thumb. "Remarkably bold."

Li Wanzhi sat bolt upright in bed. "I had no experience! No experience! How was I supposed to know the thunder would just come down in the middle of cultivating? I didn't know!"

Fang He'an stuffed an orange segment into his mouth. "Now you do. There's always next time."

Because of Li Wanzhi's injuries, they delayed their departure by three days — and set out with three days to spare before the secret realm opened.

Of the four of them, Fang He'an was the only one not flying on his own sword — he was hitching a ride with Li Wanzhi. Ye Wanwan and Bai Jian flew their own.

Li Wanzhi held his head up with great dignity. "See, Shixiong? You still need me."

Fang He'an gripped Li Wanzhi's shoulders, face ashen. "Shidi, Shixiong is asking you — please, get down. Let me fly the sword."

"Shixiong, this is my sword. You can't control it. Trust me — I will get you to Mengze Mountain safely." Li Wanzhi declared with full confidence.

"No — I'm afraid I'll die before we get there."

"..."

Li Wanzhi had only retrieved his spirit sword from the Sword Tomb before they'd left. He wasn't quite attuned to it yet.

For Fang He'an, one sword flight was nothing short of a death-defying ordeal. By the time the three of them dismounted at the foot of the mountain and entered the nearest city to Mengze Mountain —

Fang He'an was clinging to a tree, retching more dramatically than Li Wanzhi had ever done on his very first ride.

Li Wanzhi patted his back with a look of deep suffering. "Is it really that bad? I didn't even throw up."

Fang He'an raised a trembling finger and pointed at Li Wanzhi.

"You did that... on purpose."

Li Wanzhi immediately denied it with righteous indignation. "I would never do something like that. I'm your beloved little Shidi."

Fang He'an: "..." Absolutely on purpose.

Ye Wanwan looked up at the city gate ahead of them.

Mengze City.

Once Fang He'an had recovered, all four of them entered the city.

But the moment they stepped through the gates, something felt wrong.

Even Fang He'an, still hiccupping faintly from the nausea, immediately went quiet. Not one of them spoke. They all stared at the street ahead.

There were people. Plenty of them.

Mengze City was one of the rare cities with a population of a hundred thousand — even on a quieter day, there would be dozens or hundreds of figures passing through. But the people here wore expressions of hollow blankness.

Cold. Empty. Utterly without life.

The aura drifting from each of them was gray and dim and inert.

"Death qi," Ye Wanwan said suddenly.

Li Wanzhi's desire to explore and sightsee vanished instantly. He drew close to Fang He'an. He wasn't foolish — he understood what Ye Wanwan meant. He just needed to be sure he hadn't misheard.

"Shimei, what did you just say?"

Death qi?

Even Bai Jian and Fang He'an turned to look at Ye Wanwan.

Ye Wanwan's gaze remained on the people in the street. She didn't elaborate further — she simply said to Fang He'an, "Shixiong, where is the meeting point you were told about?"

This secret realm trial was not organized by Tianyi Sect alone.

It was an invitation from Xuanming Sect.

Before they'd set out, Li Mingde had specifically instructed Fang He'an — as the group leader for this trip, all communication would go through him.

Fang He'an said, "East district, Seventh Street. The YuéLái Inn."

Ye Wanwan nodded.

"Let's go."

Ye Wanwan led the way. Bai Jian walked at her side. Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi followed behind the two girls. Li Wanzhi had briefly wanted to suggest that perhaps the men should be out front —

Then he thought about Ye Wanwan and Bai Jian's respective capabilities.

Never mind.

Sect tradition.

The shimeis charged ahead. As long as they didn't drag everyone else down, that was enough.

They wound through one street after another. There were plenty of citizens along the way.

But every single one of them wore a face emptied of expression.

They seemed not to see the four cultivators at all.

Even the rare instances where two people stood near each other and exchanged words, something was stiff and wrong about their faces.

Li Wanzhi was curious enough to try talking to a few of them, wanting to observe their condition and ask someone for information. But every time he opened his mouth and met the target's hollow, glassy stare, the words died in his throat.

After several encounters with those dead-eyed looks, Li Wanzhi couldn't bring himself to try again.

They reached the east district and found the Yuélái Inn.

All four of them exhaled, quietly, without quite meaning to.

Fang He'an said, "Something about this secret realm invitation is off. Everyone stay sharp."

Ye Wanwan said nothing. She was staring at the inn's front gate.

"An inn — in broad daylight — with its doors shut?" Li Wanzhi asked aloud.

The unease in Fang He'an's chest deepened at those words.

When Bai Jian and Ye Wanwan moved to step forward, Fang He'an said, "Let me."

Ye Wanwan looked at him and didn't object.

Bai Jian had been about to say, "What do you need to go for?" — but seeing that Ye Wanwan had already stepped back, she followed suit without another word, waiting beside the young woman.

Fang He'an steeled himself and knocked.

Knock, knock.

It was broad daylight — and yet Fang He'an felt as though this was a darkness deeper than any night. On either side of the street, figures still moved. There were even voices.

But in this one moment, Fang He'an felt as though the entire world had been emptied out, leaving only himself.

The door in front of him seemed like the mouth of some enormous beast.

If it opened, it would swallow them all.

That feeling grew and grew. Cold sweat began to prick at his skin. And yet, in that very instant, Fang He'an gritted his teeth and shoved the door wide open.

He called out in a loud, clear voice: "Innkeeper — are you in? We're looking for someone."

The call rang out and echoed through the inn.

The moment the door opened, the people inside all turned to look.

And the moment it swung open, the uncanny sense of wrongness outside vanished — the sounds of the street flooded back in, voices and noise and all the ordinary life of a city.

Fang He'an blinked in surprise.

Bai Jian and Li Wanzhi turned to look back at the street, equally confused, sensing something was still not quite right.

Ye Wanwan's expression didn't change. She heard a burst of laughter ring out from inside.

"Ha! Another one who fell for my illusion!"

chapters.title: Oh, They're Dead
chapters.content:
"Idiot! Hahaha!"

The laughter rang out, and the rest of the inn erupted along with it.

"Which sect walked into Qi-brother's trap this time? Not that they can be blamed — Qi Shixiong's illusion arts have reached such mastery that even we couldn't tell anything was off."

"That's right, that's right."

"Their robes look unfamiliar — I don't think I've seen that sect before."

"Neither have I."

"Check their disciple tokens."

But disciple tokens weren't something anyone could simply demand to see, and Fang He'an and the others hadn't displayed theirs.

The cultivators in the inn ran their eyes up and down the new arrivals, their gazes carrying a thread of mockery and contempt.

It was the sort of look that said: we don't think much of you.

And when they noticed one of the group was still at the Qi Refinement stage, their disdain sharpened.

"Sure, this trial is open to anyone below core formation, but bringing a Qi Refinement cultivator? That's asking to get killed. A little too full of themselves, don't you think?"

Ye Wanwan's lips curved faintly. Talking about her, were they?

The one being praised — Qi Minglu — shot a taunting look their way, as if asking, well? How did that feel?

Li Wanzhi bristled and moved forward. "These little punks — what's a core formation cultivator got to swagger about? We have four of them!"

Fang He'an wasn't pleased either, but he pressed a hand down on Li Wanzhi's shoulder. "Situation's unclear. Don't be rash."

Li Wanzhi gritted his teeth and held back.

Fang He'an scanned the room and spotted an empty table tucked in the corner. He steered the group over and they all sat down.

The four of them exchanged a glance — Fang He'an, Bai Jian, and Ye Wanwan.

"That wasn't a real illusion," Fang He'an said.

Ye Wanwan lowered her eyes and smiled quietly. "Shixiong doesn't disappoint."

He'd seen through it.

Fang He'an said, "I've never witnessed that Qi fellow's illusion arts firsthand, but with his cultivation level, he couldn't sustain an illusion over an entire city."

A single core formation cultivator couldn't possibly control a city-wide illusion.

"Something in this city isn't right."

Fang He'an turned it over in his mind but couldn't pin down exactly what.

The thinking in this group of four generally fell to Ye Wanwan. Bai Jian didn't bother with strategy. Li Wanzhi was impulsive by nature. And though technically all four of them were deliberating, Fang He'an's attention was squarely on Ye Wanwan.

His Shibo had told him before they left: if you don't understand something, ask Xiaoshimei.

Fang He'an hadn't understood why his Shibo would say that.

But now he looked at the wide-eyed, guileless Bai Jian, and at Li Wanzhi who was already muttering about going after Qi Minglu — and he thought: Shibo was absolutely right.

Ye Wanwan asked, "Who is Xuanming Sect's contact person?"

"Didn't see one." Fang He'an looked around again. "The invitation came from Xuanming Sect three months in advance, sent to all the sects. The letter said this was a trial open to disciples at core formation and below — Shibo thought it would be good for us to get out and see the world, so he sent the four of us. But I've looked around and I don't see anyone from Xuanming Sect."

Whoever was organizing this should have been circulating among the disciples, managing things. But right now, the gathering was leaderless and scattered — and that Qi Minglu had conveniently set himself up as the cock of the roost.

"That said, Shimei — even if someone from Xuanming Sect does show up, they won't be above the Nascent Soul stage. Small trials like this generally have one elder accompanying at most."

Which was precisely why their Shishu had been comfortable letting just the four of them come.

The thinking had been: nothing serious would happen.

But the way things looked now, it seemed the situation wasn't as simple as Fang He'an had assumed. At minimum, the strangeness they'd encountered entering the city didn't look normal no matter how you looked at it.

Ye Wanwan thought for a moment and asked, "What do you know about the secret realm itself?"

Fang He'an relayed what he knew. "The realm is called Huanmeng Xingze — the Dreamstar Marsh. Its origins can't be traced. They say it existed before Mengze City was built. Some believe it was a spiritual pocket realm left behind when a Mahayana-stage cultivator failed their ascension — and after their death, the space slowly contracted. It ultimately attached itself to Mengze Mountain and has persisted there, some speculate, for thousands of years. It simply went unnoticed for a long time."

"Five hundred years ago, a Divine Transformation cultivator stumbled in by accident and found immortal herbs, rare treasures, and heaven-grade spirit tools inside. After that, the place was made public. But centuries of plundering have picked it mostly clean — what's left is ordinary spirit grass and ore, nothing of interest to anyone above the Nascent Soul stage. There are still some ancient restrictions and cultivation insight records left inside, though, which makes it useful to core formation cultivators like us who haven't yet broken through to Nascent Soul."

He paused, then added, "Xuanming Sect took control of Mengze City three hundred years ago and claimed the Dreamstar Marsh. At the time, their sect wasn't large or powerful — they were worried about others taking the realm from them, so they began inviting disciples from other sects to come for training on a fifty-year cycle. This will be the sixth opening under Xuanming Sect's stewardship."

And another thing: "Nothing has ever gone wrong before."

Ye Wanwan nodded.

Li Wanzhi had by now caught enough of the conversation to understand what they were discussing. "Shimei thinks there's something suspicious about Xuanming Sect."

"Not certain yet. Let's watch a little longer."

Li Wanzhi, now properly cautious, said, "I'll see what I can find out."

Fang He'an rolled his eyes. "And where exactly would you go to do that?"

Li Wanzhi said nothing.

Ye Wanwan, however, knew Li Wanzhi had his methods. She didn't ask — she simply waited quietly for information. Fang He'an said under his breath, "By schedule, someone from Xuanming Sect should have appeared by now."

Ye Wanwan said softly, "It would be good if someone comes. The problem is — they may no longer have anyone who can."

Fang He'an was about to ask what she meant — when the inn door was struck by a rapid series of knocks, fast and desperate, like a storm that would not stop.

Urgent beyond bearing.

Every head in the common room turned.

Twenty or thirty cultivators in the hall all froze at the sound.

Eyes shifted instinctively toward Qi Minglu. "Qi-brother, is this another of your illusions?"

Qi Minglu's expression shifted through several changes. Faced with everyone's expectant looks, he could only laugh awkwardly — because inwardly, his heart was hammering. He hadn't set anything up.

Could it be a residual effect from before?

Seeing the knocking grow more frantic, someone finally said, "Qi-brother, enough joking around. Drop it — something sounds wrong."

The others agreed.

The urgency of that knocking — no one pounds a door like that unless their life depends on it.

But in the very next moment, the door was slammed open from outside. Wind and rain swept in, and the gust knocked several cultivators stumbling back by more than a dozen steps.

"What powerful wind spirit energy!"

Ye Wanwan quietly activated a spirit talisman.

A formation array rose around the four of them.

All four were unscathed.

In the doorway, soaked by wind and rain, were two young cultivators — faces white, bodies bearing injuries. They had barely crossed the threshold before they cried out:

"Help us!"

"Those are Xuanming Sect disciples!"

Someone recognized their sect robes.

The room surged to its feet. Everyone looked past the two toward the open door — and then, stepping forward one slow footfall at a time, came their pursuer.

A figure wrapped entirely in black robes.

A corpse.

chapters.title: Shen Nanzhou
chapters.content:
The reason he could be called a dead man was simple.

The aura that wreathed his entire being was death qi — much the same as what they had sensed when first entering the city, only the figure in the black robes was far more powerful than any of those city dwellers. One look was enough to tell that he must have been a high-ranking cultivator in life.

Fang He'an gripped his teacup, tense.

The others noticed too. One by one, their expressions shifted as they fixed their gazes on the doorway. But every person gathered here was the pride of their sect. A moment of alarm, yes — but composure returned quickly.

The two fleeing Xuanming Sect disciples stood in the middle of the common room. No one stepped forward. Everyone watched the scene unfold, minds working rapidly.

No one moved rashly.

The Xuanming disciples' faces were ashen. Seeing this, one of them shouted, "What are you all doing just standing there?! This man is a demonic cultivator — help us!"

"Says who? How do we know you're not trying to use us?" Qi Minglu sneered.

Xuanming Sect's Zhao Jianming flushed crimson with fury.

"This thing grievously wounded our Third Elder and injured every one of our disciples. Now it's followed us into Mengze City to steal our secret realm quota. We fought with everything we had just to escape here and warn everyone — if no one deals with it, once this dangerous creature gets into the secret realm, it won't only be Xuanming Sect that suffers."

Qi Minglu thought it over briefly, but still made no move to act.

Zhao Jianming bellowed, "This is a demonic cultivator!"

"How interesting." A low, quiet laugh drifted through the wind and rain. "You ran all this way only to come and slander me in a room full of people."

A flash of white light swept past. A new figure appeared by the door.

White robes, patterned with green bamboo and plum blossoms. Refined and graceful, with features so strikingly beautiful they blurred the line between male and female.

Someone nearby breathed, very softly, "How beautiful."

The young man crooked a finger, and the black-robed figure stepped forward two paces.

Zhao Jianming screamed in terror, "You dare?! This room is full of heroes from every sect — you puppet-wielding demonic cultivator, how dare you cause a scene here!"

"They won't let you walk away from this!"

The young man looked up and let out a short, contemptuous laugh. "Then come."

Ye Wanwan's eyelid twitched — harder and harder, until she pressed at it with her fingers. But when she saw his face, she couldn't suppress her reaction any longer.

Oh no.

Why was it him?!

If she had to name the person who had left the deepest impression on her in her past life — besides Yan Ding — it would be the Tianyuan Devil Lord: the demonic cultivator who had united the entire demon realm through force alone.

A madman more unpredictable than any ordinary rogue cultivator.

But the young man before her now was worlds apart from the Devil Lord in her memory. He was still young, still unpolished. The murderous edge and cruelty that would one day define him had not yet set into his features. What remained was only the hot-blooded resentment and disdain of a young man who despised the world.

A rebel without a cause.

Compared to the black-robed corpse beside him, Shen Nanzhou at least looked the part of the living — his energy still vigorous and unmistakably vital.

He raised a hand and flicked it, and the black-robed figure lunged at the two remaining Xuanming Sect disciples.

The moment the two looked certain to die in a spray of blood, a clear, urgent voice rang out: "Fellow Daoist, stay your hand."

Ye Wanwan dropped her gaze. He would stop? Not a chance.

Sure enough — the black-robed figure struck at Zhao Jianming. Zhao Jianming dodged back in a desperate scramble, and in his panic, grabbed the junior disciple beside him and shoved him forward to take the fatal blow.

Then he threw himself behind Qi Minglu and the others, trying to use the crowd as cover to carve out a path to survival.

The room erupted in fury.

"He used his own junior disciple as a shield! What kind of creature does that?"

Zhao Jianming tried to run, but no one lifted a finger to help him. He fled in desperation, yet even so, the black-robed figure closed in.

"No!"

At the brink of life and death, a figure burst in through the window. The aura of a perfect core formation stage erupted outward — a pressure so close to breaching the Nascent Soul stage that it drew more than a few stares.

And it forced the black-robed figure back.

The newcomer thrust out a palm to intercept the dead man's strike, then shoved out a heavy blow. Under the force of that strike, the corpse and its robes flew outward together — the black shroud was torn away, exposing the figure beneath.

Everyone saw the face. And the robes he wore.

Xuanming Sect's robes.

"He's a Xuanming Sect disciple himself!"

With the black robe stripped away, the corpse crumbled on contact with open air and disintegrated — leaving the room full of shaken, bewildered cultivators, and a deeply rattled Zhao Jianming.

Qi Minglu and the others couldn't even follow what had just happened. Why was the puppet chasing Xuanming Sect a Xuanming Sect disciple?

Zhao Jianming jabbed a finger at Shen Nanzhou and screamed, "He's the one who made Junior Brother Li into a puppet! Him!"

Shock rippled through the room.

A flash of dangerous fury crossed Shen Nanzhou's eyes. "Not afraid to die, are you?"

Ye Wanwan glanced at Shen Nanzhou and understood perfectly well what would happen if his temper fully ignited — but she had no intention of intervening. What captured her attention far more was the core formation cultivator who had made that move.

Another familiar face.

Ji Changhuai.

Ji Changhuai hadn't noticed Ye Wanwan's presence. He simply planted a kick square into Zhao Jianming's side and snapped, "Shut your mouth."

Zhao Jianming spat blood.

"Dashixiong, well done!"

With a sweep of wind and rain, a man and a woman appeared in the doorway together. A ripple of recognition moved through the crowd. "It's disciples from Wushang Sect."

Ye Wanwan's eyes went cold.

Two more.

Like ghosts that never quite leave.

Ye Qian stood sheltered at Dou Ming's side. She turned her gaze to Shen Nanzhou and said, with soft reproach, "Why didn't you listen to me and stop? Now look — everyone's misunderstood you."

Ye Wanwan stared. These two had a prior connection?

Shen Nanzhou glanced at Ye Qian with cold indifference. "Who are you?"

Ye Wanwan: Good.

In her past life, Shen Nanzhou had been the one person she might loosely have called a kindred spirit. If he now turned out to have any connection to Ye Qian, that feeling of having been failed by the entire world would come rushing back.

But, fortunately.

Shen-xiong remained as consistent as ever.

Ye Qian's expression flickered with a brief, barely concealed embarrassment — but she recovered quickly and introduced herself to the room with open composure. "I am Ye Qian, disciple of Qingyun Peak, eighth in seniority under the tutelage of the Venerable Yan Ding. The one who acted just now is my Dashixiong, Ji Changhuai. This is my Third Shixiong, Dou Ming."

The room stirred. Cultivators cupped their fists in greeting, one after another.

"Liu Han of Cangyun Gate."

"Lin You of Fuquan Valley."

"Qi Minglu of Xinghuan Pavilion."

Shen Nanzhou alone said nothing, showing no interest in any of it. His gaze swept lazily across the crowd — and landed, briefly, in the direction of Ye Wanwan's table.

Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi exchanged a murmur. "Is he looking at us?"

Ye Wanwan considered. "It seems... like it."

Shen Nanzhou pulled his gaze away just as quickly, as though he'd only been looking at nothing in particular.

Qi Minglu, his tone softening slightly at the sight of Ye Qian's face, said, "Ye Shimei, what exactly is going on here?"

"Qi Shixiong, it's a long story." Ye Qian sighed softly. "My Dashixiong, Third Shixiong, and I arrived in Mengze City early. We noticed right away that the city's inhabitants were behaving strangely — their bodies carrying a persistent death qi that would not disperse. In some streets, there were no living people left at all."

"Sensing that something was wrong, we began investigating quietly."

"And then, earlier today —" Ye Qian's finger shot out to point directly at Zhao Jianming, her voice rising with indignation, "when we entered the city, we saw this Zhao-shixiong and Xuanming Sect's Third Elder together, commanding puppets and draining the life essence of living city residents."

A sharp collective intake of breath filled the room.

"More than half the city's residents are now plagued with illness. Many others are already dead. And all of this was their doing."

Zhao Jianming's face darkened to a deep, furious red. "You... you're lying."

Ye Qian spoke with unshaking conviction. "All three of us saw it with our own eyes — and this gentleman acted because he, too, witnessed what you did."

"The Third Elder was killed when his own puppets turned on him. You were pursued by puppets of your own creation. This is the consequence of your actions. How dare you have the audacity to accuse someone else!"

Zhao Jianming's face went white. "I... I've been wronged."

But no one was listening. Every person in the room had fixed their attention on Xuanming Sect's use of city residents to forge puppets — conveniently overlooking the detail that the Third Elder had originally set those puppets on Shen Nanzhou, only to fail and be killed by him in return.

And that Shen Nanzhou himself could also —

Control puppets.

"This fellow Daoist is innocent," Ye Qian declared to the room, clearing Shen Nanzhou's name. As she said it, she turned toward him and offered a look of open goodwill.

Shen Nanzhou didn't even deign to acknowledge her. He simply turned and walked into the common room — heading directly in the direction of Ye Wanwan's table.

Ye Wanwan: ?

What exactly are you doing?

chapters.title: Little Shimei Is the Most Impressive One
chapters.content:
Ye Wanwan kept her gaze fixed on Shen Nanzhou.

No flinching. No looking away.

She looked at him directly.

Their eyes met in midair — one calm and composed, the other sharp and probing. But Ye Wanwan couldn't tell from that look whether this person carried memories of a past life.

It was the only explanation she could think of for why he would walk toward her.

Shen Nanzhou's movement drew attention from more than a few onlookers.

Ji Changhuai and Ye Qian both turned to look, their eyes tracing the line of his approach.

But then Shen Nanzhou walked all the way to the table beside theirs — and sat down at the empty one next to it.

A few awkward smiles rippled through the room.

He just wanted a seat, then.

Which made sense — the common room was packed, all the good spots taken by the disciples of whichever sect had arrived earliest. If you wanted somewhere to sit, you went to the corners.

Li Wanzhi, Bai Jian, and Fang He'an all turned to stare at Ye Wanwan. Since when had she been wearing a veil?

Ye Wanwan gave them a small smile.

"Shixiong, have some tea."

After a year together, they all understood one another well enough to know that Ye Wanwan never did things without reason.

One by one, they composed themselves and pretended not to notice anything.

Li Wanzhi, meanwhile, cast a carefully casual glance in the direction of the Wushang Sect disciples.

So it's them.

Fang He'an and Bai Jian understood as well.

So that's who they are.

The people from her former sect. The ones who had wronged her.

Back when Ye Wanwan had first entered the inn, Qi Minglu and the others hadn't paid her much attention — and even now with her face concealed, they might not recognize her at all. Even if they did, they wouldn't spare her a second thought.

There were more pressing matters demanding their attention.

A Xuanming Sect elder using city residents to forge puppets — that was an enormously serious issue. Because if the elders were capable of this, what did it say about the imminent secret realm? What would they find waiting inside?

Was it even safe to enter?

Were there traps set within?

That was the question of the hour.

Around the room, cultivators began reaching out to their sect's senior members, relaying what had happened here and waiting for further guidance.

And as for the one who had exposed the truth of the puppets — Ye Qian — she was receiving unanimous praise and admiration from all sides.

Her meticulous observation and the courage it had taken to step forward and reveal what she knew had left a strong impression on everyone in the room.

"That's the youngest core formation cultivator from Wushang Sect, isn't it? A heaven-grade spirit root — formed her golden core at sixteen, and she's from the main Ye family line. A true daughter of heaven."

"Indeed. A heaven-grade spirit root is one in ten thousand — perhaps rarer. To find a single perfect one among ten thousand cultivators is considered extraordinary, and Ye Shimei formed her core so young. Can her future be anything but brilliant? They say Wushang Sect may be about to produce its youngest Divine Transformation cultivator yet."

The last person to break the record for youngest Divine Transformation was Yan Ding himself.

And now it might be Yan Ding's own disciple who broke it.

Admiring murmurs spread through the room.

A single sect, full of exceptional people.

Ye Qian demurred with practiced grace, "My master's talent is without equal — I would be more than content to have even one ten-thousandth of his gift. How could I possibly dare compare myself to him?"

The humility only made people like her more.

Dou Ming stood nearby looking insufferably proud. This was their shimei — nothing like that wooden, expressionless Ye Wanwan who could barely get two words out of her mouth.

Utterly insufferable, that one had been.

Li Wanzhi clicked his tongue. "What's so impressive about one heaven-grade spirit root? My shimei has five. Five!"

Fang He'an gave a short, agreeing huff.

True enough.

A single spirit root was what qualified as a heaven-grade root — the more roots a cultivator possessed, the greater the interference between them, which muddied the quality and complicated cultivation. But Ye Wanwan's spirit roots were different from anyone else's.

Both their Xiaoshishu and Sect Master Shibo had said as much long ago: Ye Wanwan's five spirit roots each individually reached heaven-grade quality. It was only because of their number that people overlooked what they were.

If she sealed four of them and kept only one, that remaining root would undoubtedly be a heaven-grade spirit root.

Five heaven-grade roots. Not one in ten thousand — more like one in a million. The only difficulty was that cultivation with so many roots was incredibly demanding.

But to those who seemed to think Ye Wanwan had formed her golden core in a single year through natural ability alone — they didn't know the half of it.

Pei Xuan Shishu had laid down a seventh-level spirit-gathering formation across the entire snow mountain.

The resources silently poured into it, as well as the spirit food prepared daily for Ye Wanwan, all came from Pei Xuan's own stores.

Of course, he hadn't mentioned any of this to Ye Wanwan.

And Ye Wanwan herself didn't seem entirely aware of it.

Hearing Li Wanzhi's childish declaration, Ye Wanwan suppressed a laugh. "More spirit roots isn't better, Shixiong."

"Doesn't matter — she's still better than her either way."

One golden core per formation. Ye Wanwan had formed five in one go.

If that wasn't something to crow about, what was?

Ji Changhuai had taken no part in Ye Qian and Dou Ming's moment of triumph. He stood slightly apart, looking out of place.

He simply bound Zhao Jianming in spirit rope and sent up a signal flare, waiting for Wushang Sect to send someone.

Ye Wanwan had no interest in any further contact with Wushang Sect. When the opportunity arose, she slipped out of the common room.

Li Wanzhi and Fang He'an remained behind to keep watch and wait for news.

It wasn't until evening that Li Wanzhi came rushing back with Fang He'an, demanding water the moment he walked in the door. "Tea — quick, tea! I'm dying of thirst."

Ye Wanwan handed him a cup.

Li Wanzhi drank, then startled. "Is this spirit tea?"

Ye Wanwan asked with a smile, "Shixiong doesn't like it?"

"That's extravagant, Shimei." Li Wanzhi smacked his lips in appreciation, then launched into his report. "After you and Shijie left, someone from Xuanming Sect finally showed up, and the nearest sect — Cangyun Gate — arrived too."

Ye Wanwan raised an eyebrow. "How did it go?"

"An absolute fight broke out."

Li Wanzhi's eyes lit up with barely contained excitement. "I wouldn't have believed it — who knew that when elders start arguing, they're no better than squabbling commoners in the street."

Bai Jian tilted her head. "Squabbling commoners?"

"Exactly. They were one step short of grabbing each other by the hair," Li Wanzhi said, taking another long sip of tea. "This whole thing came down to a Xuanming Sect elder acting on personal greed — they nearly used every disciple sent by every sect as a living sacrifice. Xuanming Sect claims it wasn't intentional, but if it hadn't been discovered in time, who knows how it would have ended."

"The other sects' elders tore into Xuanming Sect. Xuanming Sect knew they were in the wrong, so they couldn't exactly argue back — all they could do was offer apologies."

"Verbal apologies? The others wouldn't have accepted that."

Li Wanzhi grinned. "Not at all, as expected — those elders aren't people you can appease with words. Sincerity is what counts."

Li Wanzhi rubbed his fingers together in the universal gesture.

Ye Wanwan understood immediately.

"How much did they give?"

"Every disciple who came for the secret realm gets ten thousand spirit stones. Those who were injured get thirty thousand each, plus one third-grade beast core. And everything found inside the secret realm is theirs to keep — no more handing thirty percent of the take to Xuanming Sect."

Ye Wanwan was genuinely surprised. "That really is a heavy bleeding."

Each time Huanmeng Realm opened, Xuanming Sect's thirty percent cut had been enough to fund half a year of their sect's resources.

Now they were not only giving it all up — they were paying out of pocket on top of it.

"Exactly. The Xuanming Sect elders looked sick to their stomachs. I could see it in their faces — if there hadn't been so many people around, it might have come to blows."

Fang He'an stepped through the door just in time to catch that last remark and rolled his eyes. "You think everyone's like you — ready to start a fight at the drop of a hat."

"These people would never actually come to blows."

"Xuanming Sect paid to make the problem go away. They got off easy."

Ye Wanwan had been about to ask Fang He'an why he'd come in separately from Li Wanzhi when a new voice caught her off guard.

Fang He'an grinned. "Look who's here."

Stepping around Fang He'an were Yan Ju — and an elderly man Ye Wanwan had never met in person. But from the elder's blue robes, the wooden hairpin holding his hair in place, his air of refined otherworldliness, and the faint, clean scent of herbs and wood that drifted from him, she could guess exactly who it was.

"Third Shibo."

chapters.title: So There's a Little Shidi Too
chapters.content:
Xun Yin ranked third among the sect's elders — in seniority above even Sect Master Li Mingde. He was gifted in formation arrays and mechanical arts, and had been pressed into an unwanted second role as a medicinal alchemist ever since Fang He'an's master had disappeared.

These days, he spent his time on Crimson Mist Peak researching spirit herbs and spirit food.

His burning ambition: to solve the food problem for their roughly one hundred and one disciples.

Progress had been slow. The spirit food remained uncracked. But under Xun Yin Shibo's formation arrays, the sect's spirit plants had been flourishing magnificently.

Medicinal herbs for wound treatment were never in short supply.

As for pills, with Fang He'an's master absent and no one else capable of proper alchemy, Fang He'an had taken it upon himself to refine basic healing pills and the occasional first-grade poison pill.

Second-grade and above remained out of reach — room to grow.

Li Wanzhi had once mocked Fang He'an for this and taken a thorough beating for it. "You try entering a sect and having your master disappear on the second day — and then teaching yourself from books until you're a first-grade pill master and a core formation cultivator all at once! Go on, try it!"

After learning the full, harrowing story, Li Wanzhi never mocked him again.

Because according to Fang He'an, all three of the disciples who had entered the sect before the others — himself, Bai Jian, and the senior shixiong who still hadn't shown his face — had been raised in what could only be called a free-range fashion.

A disciple was taken in, then left to fend for themselves up on the mountain. Whoever happened to have a free moment would teach them something.

Bai Jian was the exception — she'd been so frail as a child that Sect Master Shibo had personally looked after her for a few years. The rest had survived on self-reliance.

Disciples like Ye Wanwan and Li Wanzhi, who had Yan Ju and Pei Xuan guiding them step by step — that was a new wind that had only started blowing this year. Unheard of before.

"Master — what are you doing here?"

At the sight of Yan Ju, Li Wanzhi visibly straightened up, both hands and feet suddenly awkward as he stood ramrod-stiff by the table.

For the past half year while Ye Wanwan had been in closed cultivation on the snow mountain, Li Wanzhi had spent most of his time under Yan Ju's instruction, with Xun Yin and occasionally Li Mingde filling in the rest.

Though the master-disciple bond between him and Yan Ju had only been formalized after Li Wanzhi chose his spirit sword in the Sword Tomb, they had already been something like master and disciple-in-training for a while now.

And yet these two still looked thoroughly unaccustomed to each other.

Because Yan Ju was severe.

Li Wanzhi shot to his feet and offered his seat to Yan Ju. Yan Ju settled into it with his sword in his arms, cool and expressionless. "You move fast, I'll give you that. Now — the Swiftwind Thunder Taming Art I taught you. How much of it have you learned?"

Li Wanzhi's face crumpled instantly. He looked on the verge of tears. "Master, the Swiftwind part is fine, but the Thunder Taming is a core formation technique — I only just formed my core two days ago, I haven't even started on it yet..."

"Slacking off and you still have the nerve to say it out loud?"

Li Wanzhi hugged his own head, the picture of wronged misery.

Xun Yin chuckled warmly. "You've all come out — no need to frighten the children."

Fang He'an said, "...Shibo, it's exactly that sudden warmth that frightens me. I'm not used to it."

Xun Yin's eyes went wide. "You little brat!"

Fang He'an grinned shamelessly.

Li Wanzhi and Bai Jian greeted the elders in turn with proper bows. Xun Yin waved them off. "We're not so formal around here. Sit down. I came down the mountain with your Xiaoshishu because we'd heard what was happening here."

All four of them nodded like good children.

Xun Yin stroked his beard, looking them over — these four little ones. He hadn't come to the wrong place, had he? They all looked so tense.

"Don't be nervous. Your Xiaoshishu and I have already spoken with Xuanming Sect. The puppet business is being handled by your elders. All you four need to worry about is going into the secret realm."

He paused, then added: "We'll be waiting for you outside when you come out."

Li Wanzhi laughed awkwardly. "There's no need for that, surely..."

If Shibo was here, that meant Yan Ju would also be staying in Mengze City. Which meant for him...

Yan Ju looked up, his voice flat. "I'm not welcome?"

"Of course you are!" Li Wanzhi said at full volume. "With Master here, my back doesn't ache, my legs don't hurt — I could eat two extra bowls of rice. How could anyone not want Master here?"

He slithered close to Yan Ju's side and began kneading his shoulders with dedicated enthusiasm. "I just didn't want Master to tire himself out! You have such important responsibilities to attend to."

Those responsibilities being: keeping them financially afloat — which had always been Yan Ju's unofficial burden.

Though ever since the end of last year, when Sect Master Li Mingde had reclaimed the spirit stone tributes from the two cities under the sect's protection, they'd had no shortage of funds.

Yan Ju no longer needed to pick up odd jobs everywhere.

But he still moved through ancient ruins and dense forests like a ghost, surfacing unpredictably and vanishing again.

And every time he returned, he brought resources with him. Monster carcasses, forging materials, rare medicines, even the occasional immortal herb. It wasn't just Yan Ju either — several of the other shibo had also started sending things back to the sect.

The younger generation didn't know exactly what treasures were being gathered. But they had a sense of it. Starting from the beginning of this year, when Sect Master Shibo changed their annual stipend to a monthly stipend —

Ten thousand spirit stones every month.

After that, they understood: Tianyi Sect was no longer short of money.

The elders were working hard for them.

Their master was working hard for them.

Yan Ju had no patience for flattery. He grabbed Li Wanzhi by the collar and hauled him to his feet. "Several days apart. Let's see how your footwork's held up."

Li Wanzhi nearly cried.

The two of them left. Xun Yin, still smiling, said he would be going too.

"Get some proper rest tonight. Tomorrow morning after the hour of Chen, once the goods are delivered, we'll talk about the secret realm."

"Yes, Shibo."

They saw the two elders off. Fang He'an exhaled with relief. "Well, now I can relax. Shimei, why are you still frowning?"

Ye Wanwan said quietly, "It's because things have gotten more serious."

Fang He'an looked surprised. "What do you mean?"

Ye Wanwan turned her gaze toward the door, as if looking out over the whole of Mengze City. If Yan Ju and Xun Yin hadn't come, that would have meant nothing too serious was going on.

But they had come. Which meant things were not simple.

They only came down the mountain when lives were at risk — when their disciples needed protecting.

"Shixiong — be careful when we go into the secret realm tomorrow."

Fang He'an thought Ye Wanwan might be overthinking it, but he took the warning seriously all the same.

The next morning.

Everyone gathered at the foot of Mengze Mountain. Xuanming Sect sent three Nascent Soul elders. The moment they saw Yan Ju and Xun Yin, their expressions became markedly subdued — and they came forward to pay their respects almost immediately.

Yan Ju said nothing, cold as ever.

Xun Yin greeted them with a pleasant smile, but his hand was firm as he took four qiankun pouches from them and distributed one to each of Ye Wanwan's group.

"That's the compensation, I take it?" Ye Wanwan asked.

Li Wanzhi looked inside — then snapped his hand up and tucked the pouch away immediately.

Fang He'an rolled his eyes. "What are you skulking around for? People will think we've never seen money before."

Then he looked inside his own. And just as quickly yanked it shut.

Ye Wanwan studied their expressions and had a fairly good guess. She opened hers.

Sure enough — the spirit stones inside were ten times the promised amount.

"Did they give us the wrong ones?" Li Wanzhi whispered. Ten times — that was a hundred thousand spirit stones. Even Li Wanzhi, son of a wealthy family, had never seen this kind of generosity in one sitting.

"Impossible that they got it wrong," Fang He'an said firmly.

Shibo had handed these out himself.

Yan Ju said, coldly: "Pathetic."

Xun Yin chuckled. "The people harmed by Xuanming Sect just so happened to be Tianyi Sect disciples. Naturally, our compensation is going to look a little different from everyone else's."

Li Wanzhi and Ye Wanwan both looked up.

"Sorry?"

When had they been harmed?

But a bad feeling had already begun to take root in Ye Wanwan's chest.

"Nanzhou — come and meet your shixiong and shijie."

chapters.title: Otherwise Shijie Could Hold That Pose All Day
chapters.content:
Ye Wanwan had always known her seniority would eventually rise. She'd always known the day would come when she'd have a junior shimei of her own. But just as an only child resents a new sibling who appears to steal away all the affection that used to be entirely theirs — Ye Wanwan, with the shadow of Ye Qian casting its long and bitter pall over the very concept of "shimei," had developed an intense and deeply-rooted aversion to the idea of suddenly gaining one. Aversion wasn't even strong enough a word for it.

But right now —

It wasn't a shimei.

It was a shidi.

Still.

Same thing. Insufferable either way.

Shen Nanzhou stood by a large boulder not far off. When Xun Yin called out, the young man turned toward them. His expression was cool and haughty, radiating a clear keep-your-distance energy — but under Xun Yin and Yan Ju's watchful eyes, he still made his way over. He lifted his chin at Ye Wanwan and the others in the barest possible nod.

That counted as a greeting, apparently.

Li Wanzhi: "..."

Fang He'an: "..."

What an unbearably arrogant little shidi.

Li Wanzhi took one look and immediately decided he didn't like Shen Nanzhou. He muttered under his breath, "What kind of attitude is that? Since when does a shidi greet his shixiong like this?"

Bai Jian, for her part, was entirely unbothered. She sat quietly eating her snow fruit — grown by Ye Wanwan in the Purple Spirit Cave Dwelling, and brought down the mountain in two small bags for her. Sweet and refreshing, perfect for nibbling between moments.

Bai Jian treasured them deeply. She allowed herself one per hour at most. But now, with a new little shidi appearing before her, her gaze drifted thoughtfully toward the bag.

Maybe she could offer one?

Fang He'an asked, with some uncertainty, "Shibo — is this... our shidi?"

Xun Yin smiled warmly. "He's the new disciple taken in by your Qingfeng Shibo."

Fang He'an's eyes went wide. "Fifth Shixiong?"

Li Wanzhi and Ye Wanwan both remembered at once — the fifth slot that had been claimed but never filled. The shixiong who'd joined the sect's roster but never actually appeared.

If he was Fifth Shixiong...

Ye Wanwan turned this over.

She could live with that.

Xun Yin stroked his beard, amiable as ever. "Well, yes and no. He joined after all of you, so seniority still falls in line with when you entered. He'll be Sixth — Little Six. This is your shixiong and shijie — get acquainted."

The smile Ye Wanwan had just been about to put on quietly disappeared again.

Shidi.

Was there something wrong with being a shixiong?

Shen Nanzhou's brow furrowed slightly. He looked somewhat displeased — but as if something had occurred to him, he introduced himself anyway. "Shen Nanzhou."

Fang He'an could already see this man had no interest in saying anything more, and with Li Wanzhi and Ye Wanwan both wearing expressions of obvious displeasure, he stepped up to ease the awkwardness.

"I'm your Third Shixiong — Fang He'an. This is Second Shijie, Bai Jian. Fourth Shixiong Li Wanzhi. And Fifth Shijie... Wanwan-shimei."

Shen Nanzhou looked through them one by one, and his gaze landed last on Ye Wanwan. "Shijie?"

Ye Wanwan: "..."

Ye Wanwan pressed her fists together and said, with complete seriousness, "Shixiong was the first disciple Qingfeng Shibo chose — he entered the sect a full year before me. By rights, your seniority is above mine. You may call me Xiaoshimei."

Shen Nanzhou said flatly, "That old man said I'm Sixth."

"No, no — Shixiong is an outstanding person in every regard, it wouldn't do for you to be last. Please, the title is yours."

She was done with this whole 'shijie' business. She wanted no part of it.

Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi watched the exchange going back and forth.

Xun Yin and Yan Ju had already slipped away to deal with the Xuanming Sect elders and open the secret realm — leaving just the five of them, watching Ye Wanwan and Shen Nanzhou politely and persistently push the title back and forth at each other.

"Shixiong, you're clearly Fifth."

"Shijie, there's no need to be modest — since Shishu said you're Fifth, then you are my Shijie."

"Shixiong, Shibo only said that to make me feel better. But in my heart, I sincerely admire your character and bearing. Please — the title of Shixiong should be yours."

Everyone could see it plainly. Ye Wanwan simply did not want to be the shijie.

She just wanted to be the youngest.

Shen Nanzhou had figured that out too.

The young woman in front of him had been hovering quietly at the edge of the group the entire time, barely visible, her expression one of supreme and unshakable indifference — the look of someone who could watch a mountain collapse and not blink.

Whatever anyone said, she wore the same air of 'this has nothing to do with me.'

It had been the same way back at the inn yesterday.

But the word 'shijie' — that was the one thing that cracked it. When she heard it, her expression fractured for just a split second, a flash of something like deep revulsion, as though the two characters themselves reminded her of something unbearable.

Even with the veil, he'd caught it clearly in those eyes of hers — that visceral rejection of the title.

Hates it that much, does she?

All the more reason to use it.

The title meant nothing to Shen Nanzhou either way. Shixiong or Shidi — they were just labels. He'd come to Tianyi Sect mostly to pass the time.

But now, for some reason, he found himself oddly attached to this particular label.

"Shijie — does Xiaoshidi displease you?"

Ye Wanwan ground her back teeth and turned her head as if she hadn't heard him. But Shen Nanzhou leaned in with a faint curve at his lips. "Shijie, you look very unhappy."

"Shijie..."

A snow-white fruit was held out from the side. Shen Nanzhou startled and looked up at the young woman offering it.

"Little Shidi," Bai Jian said simply. "Here."

Shen Nanzhou stared at her for a long moment and didn't take it.

But Bai Jian kept her arm extended, steady and unhurried, and didn't retract it either.

Fang He'an remarked, "Little Shidi, you'd better just take it. Otherwise Shijie will hold that pose all day."

"..." Shen Nanzhou reached out and accepted it.

A snow-white fruit the size of a longan, faintly traced with gold veining, its skin thin enough that the juice inside was almost visible, just waiting to burst free at a bite.

A second-grade spirit fruit.

Shen Nanzhou was surprised.

A minor disciple of Tianyi Sect carrying a second-grade spirit fruit as a casual snack — something that could instantly restore the cultivation of a Qi Refinement stage cultivator, and still offered meaningful benefits to Foundation Building and Golden Core cultivators alike.

Tianyi Sect was turning out to be rather different from what he'd imagined.

Bai Jian saw him take it. She smiled, her eyes curving into crescents, then linked her arm through Ye Wanwan's. "Xiaoshimei," she said, enunciating the syllables one by one. "You are Xiaoshimei."

Ye Wanwan's expression stayed gentle. She nodded softly. "Yes."

No matter how many new disciples Tianyi Sect took in, Ye Wanwan would always be Bai Jian's Xiaoshimei.

A breeze stirred high overhead.

Light bloomed in the air before them.

Under the combined effort of the Xuanming Sect elders, the secret realm entrance opened.

One blue-robed elder channeled his voice outward: "Huanmeng Xingze opens once every fifty years. Each opening lasts one month. You are free to explore within that time — but Xuanming Sect must caution all present: though the realm has shrunk to a third-grade secret realm, with no creature inside exceeding the third rank, the danger within the forests is beyond counting. All those who enter must sign a life-and-death covenant."

"Life and death by heaven's will."

A sheet of gold paper appeared before each cultivator.

Ye Wanwan looked at hers.

A contract.

She extended her soul force outward and pressed her aura into the paper. The contract was sealed. Two hundred gold sheets returned to the Xuanming Sect elders.

"Xuanming Sect wishes all of you a fruitful journey."

"The entrance — open!"

At the signal, cultivators began leaping into the entrance one after another, disappearing before the eyes of the crowd.

Ye Wanwan's group wasn't the first in. Before they stepped forward, Ye Wanwan handed each of Li Wanzhi and the others a small silk pouch.

"What's this?"

"A protective talisman."

Everyone knew Ye Wanwan made talismans. They tucked the pouches away without overthinking it — though each of those talismans might, at the critical moment, be the thing that saved their lives.

"Let's go."

Fang He'an and Bai Jian led the way. The group flew into the entrance together. At the last moment, something made Ye Wanwan glance back.

Shen Nanzhou was following five steps behind her, unhurried and composed.

When he noticed her looking, he offered her a slow, deliberate smile.

Ye Wanwan's hand tightened at her side.

This person... did he carry memories of a past life?

chapters.title: The Core Condensation Fruit Tree
chapters.content:
At the thought of past-life memories, Ye Wanwan noticed that her own were beginning to blur. She could still hold onto the turning points of her former life — but the details were fading, slipping away little by little.

She didn't know whether it was because she had strayed so far from her past life's path that the memories were dissolving along with it.

After all, her past self at this point in time was still at Wushang Sect, an outer disciple being ground down day by day.

She wouldn't even have been allowed to leave the mountain, let alone compete for a secret realm slot.

And yet here she was, one of two hundred elite disciples who had secured a place in this trial.

"What are you thinking about, Shijie?"

Ye Wanwan heard the word 'shijie' and shot Shen Nanzhou a sideways look. The young man still had a faint curve on his lips — and even with that, his fundamental coldness showed through. His smiles tended to look more like mockery than anything else.

Ye Wanwan changed the subject. "We're here."

Passing through the secret realm entrance, she felt the token at her waist flicker with a brief glow. Then she was through, stepping into another world.

It happened in the blink of an eye.

Yellow sand surged from all directions, sweeping over her.

Ye Wanwan frowned, keeping the Asking Heart Sword from veering off course as she pushed through the sandstorm. When it cleared, she landed — and found herself in a stretch of open sand.

Not a single person in sight.

Bai Jian and the others were nowhere to be found.

Ye Wanwan brushed off her sleeves. She wasn't alarmed.

Before departure, Li Wanzhi had gotten hold of a map of Huanmeng Xingze for all of them. Each of the four carried one — and the disciples from other sects had long been given the same by their own seniors.

This kind of separation was expected. Ye Wanwan unrolled the map and read the terrain, determining that she had been dropped somewhere called Yangtou Slope.

"The whole of Huanmeng Xingze is shaped like a wild ram whose head and body have been separated. The head and body are positioned in two different directions, connected in the middle by a massive lake."

"In the ram's head region lie precious third-grade spirit herbs and Core Condensation Fruit — and if obtained, it can raise the odds of a Foundation Building cultivator forming a golden core by fifty percent."

"Refined into a Breakthrough Pill, that rises to ninety percent."

"One of the most sought-after things for anyone coming here."

Last night's conversation with Li Wanzhi came back to her.

"But the majority of people entering this time are at core formation stage. Core Condensation Fruit wouldn't interest them very much, would it?"

"Well said, Fang Shixiong — you've asked exactly the right question. But you seem to be overlooking something: core formation cultivators might not need it, but Foundation Building cultivators do."

"And if a core formation cultivator brings some back, their sect can exchange it for Pei Yuan Pills — that's useful for breaking through to the mid core formation stage. Nothing to sniff at."

"You know a lot about this."

"It's you who knows too little, Shixiong."

"..."

Last night's exchange rang softly in her ears as Ye Wanwan murmured to herself, "Core Condensation Fruit."

Wasn't that practically made for her?

Other people formed one core at a time. She needed to form countless.

Well then.

This fruit was going to be hers.

She confirmed her bearings and set off directly toward the head region.

The yellow sand swept past her on both sides. She flew fast, and in almost no time had arrived at the mouth of a valley. Unlike the open slopes of the mountain, this valley was thick with spirit mist and heavy with moisture.

As she drew closer, she saw it: a dan tree in full bloom at the center of the valley, its branches loaded with fruit — some as large as a fist, others no bigger than a longan.

Core Condensation Fruit ripened once every eighty to a hundred years.

She'd come at a fortunate time. It happened to be a ripening year.

Ye Wanwan's eyes lit up.

Delivered right to her door?

She made her approach — a few swift leaps through the trees — closing in on the dan tree rapidly. But just as she neared it, she felt a thread of killing intent.

She froze on a branch and didn't move.

A tree this laden with ripe and near-ripe fruit, some of the older ones still hanging after nearly a hundred years — given the secret realm's fifty-year cycle, that shouldn't be right. There should have been far fewer by now.

Ye Wanwan thought it over and decided to wait and observe before doing anything.

She wanted the fruit. But she also wanted to keep her life.

She concealed herself without a sound nearby, extending her spiritual sense outward to quietly map the valley around her.

Her cultivation stage couldn't advance from Golden Core to Nascent Soul — but the Spirit Tempering Art that Pei Xuan had taught her was not only for tempering the body. It also cultivated the primordial spirit.

As her body was being refined, the art had been steadily strengthening her primordial spirit as well.

Once her physical tempering was complete, the Spirit Tempering Art's true potential would reveal itself — a technique for cultivating the primordial spirit, capable of elevating its realm.

That full potential hadn't unfolded yet, but the results were already impressive.

So while her cultivation stage had not risen, her primordial spirit had already reached the peak of the Golden Core stage — one step short of breaking into the Nascent Soul.

When that wall would fall, she still didn't know.

But for now, it was more than adequate.

Her spiritual sense swept rapidly across the valley. Just as she sensed something distinctly unusual — three figures entered from the valley's outer edge.

"Found it, just like I thought! Shixiong, the dan tree's here!"

Dan tree — named for the fruit that hung from its branches, round and golden, like oversized golden cores. The name had stuck.

Ye Wanwan quieted her breath and concealed her presence completely.

None of the three newcomers noticed her.

They were disciples from Yunlang Stronghold — two at the early core formation stage, one at late Foundation Building. The three of them came sailing in through the sand and wind.

They're eager. No caution at all.

How convenient. Test subjects.

"Shidi, wait!"

The elder of the two shixiong called out just in time to stop the younger disciple from reaching for the fruit.

The younger one looked baffled. "Shixiong, what's wrong?"

"Be careful."

"Shixiong, you worry too much. We haven't run into any danger the whole way here — if there really were something powerful lurking about, it would have shown itself already. It's been completely quiet."

The shidi talked as he reached forward, his hand already closing around a Core Condensation Fruit —

And passed straight through it.

He blinked.

He tried again, fingers swiping at the same spot. Again, nothing. His hand moved right through it as if through air, as though the fruit were nothing but a projection.

The other two shixiong stepped closer to try for themselves — and the fruit vanished, reappearing two steps to the left.

They lunged. The fruit moved again, this time appearing three steps away.

"It's running!"

A tree that could run sounded like a joke.

But that was precisely what was happening.

Right before their eyes, the dan tree wrenched itself free of the earth, unfurled its roots, and sprinted — fleeing into the depths of the valley.

Ye Wanwan: ?

The three disciples stood there dumbfounded.

"After it!"

They gave chase. But the dan tree was fast, and extraordinarily agile. No matter what they tried, they couldn't catch it — and after enough failed attempts, their frustration boiled over. One of them drew his sword.

"Stop right there!"

Sword qi tore through the air, sweeping in all directions. The valley shook with it, the ground trembling underfoot — and the disciple brought his blade down in a single devastating arc.

Aimed directly at the dan tree's roots.

If that blow landed, the entire tree would be destroyed beyond any possibility of saving.

Ye Wanwan's eyes went very still.

chapters.title: A Thief Never Leaves Empty-Handed
chapters.content:
Destroying a spirit plant's roots while raiding its fruit — it was one of the most contemptible acts in the cultivation world. Even the most ruthless cultivators drew the line here. You could take what you wanted, but you didn't slaughter the goose that laid the golden eggs. You could harvest, but not uproot. Among cultivators, there was an understanding: leave something behind. Always give the next person a chance.

But this Yunlang Stronghold disciple, desperate not to lose the Core Condensation Fruit, had thrown all of that aside.

The sword strike was poured full of sword qi, slashing out across a hundred meters to cut off the dan tree's escape route — and to try to obliterate it entirely. But the tree proved surprisingly cunning. It veered sharply and plunged straight into the earth.

Gone.

The three Yunlang Stronghold disciples stood there blinking.

"What kind of tree was that?"

Ye Wanwan lowered her gaze, the corner of her mouth curving faintly.

"What a fascinating little spirit."

Among the creatures of the cultivation world there were feral beasts — those with powerful bodies but no awakened intelligence — and there were spirit beasts and nature spirits: those who had awakened awareness but possessed little strength. What she'd just seen, the force animating that running dan tree, was the latter.

And whether the fruit hanging from that fleeing tree had actually been Core Condensation Fruit — that was another question entirely.

Ye Wanwan suspected it wasn't.

She waited and watched.

With the three of them gone in pursuit, she moved in the other direction. The valley was dense with trees and thick with spirit herbs underfoot.

The whole way in, Ye Wanwan had already identified a great many first and second-grade spirit herbs.

She hadn't been idle.

Since she was here anyway.

Why not take them along?

As for the morality of destroying spirit plants while pillaging — that wasn't her concern. She wasn't doing this to be a good person.

Besides, she wasn't destroying anything. She was just relocating these plants to a different home.

Before departure, Pei Xuan had given her a purple storage ring — vastly larger than an ordinary qiankun pouch, which held only three or four cubic meters. And unlike a standard pouch, this one could store living things.

Something like that would fetch a fortune even at auction.

And yet Pei Xuan had handed her three to choose from.

All three were fifth-grade storage rings, each with a different function.

The first had a capacity approaching ten thousand cubic meters and was ideal for ordinary goods and spirit herbs of the fourth grade and below — but couldn't hold living creatures or high-grade spirit plants.

The second had a smaller capacity, but could store living creatures and low-grade spirit beasts, though its space was only half that of the first.

The third was a growth-type ring.

Its interior space would expand as the owner's spiritual consciousness grew. Until Ye Wanwan's primordial spirit reached a higher level, it held roughly the space of a small house.

After weighing her options, Ye Wanwan chose the third.

And then borrowed the other two as well.

Pei Xuan had said nothing. He'd simply stared at her.

"This trip into the secret realm is full of unknowns — better to be prepared. I'll return them to Shifu when I get back."

At the time, she'd been thinking only about capacity. Now she could see she'd had good instincts.

Everything she passed, she collected.

She gathered three hundred and seventy stalks of second-grade Spirit Root Grass — excellent material for cultivating a foundational base.

Five hundred stalks of second-grade Rain Swallow Grass — perfect for Bai Jian, being just the kind of herb suited to her cultivation.

And three saplings of third-grade Black Sour Fruit trees.

Only one had fruited — but it had over thirty berries on its branches.

"Too slow, picking them one by one."

Ye Wanwan looked at the spirit trees and something clicked in her mind.

"What if I just take the whole thing?"

She thought it, and she did it. There was no time for lengthy deliberation. She pinched five talismans from her hand, used the power of the five elements to form a formation array, and pressed her fingers into a seal before the trees.

"Earth spirit — move."

"Collect."

The spirit tree shifted, but there was a moment of resistance — a force pushing back, refusing to yield.

Ye Wanwan pressed her lips together. She held her concentration without allowing a fraction of it to slip.

Then —

In an instant, the spirit tree before her was drawn into the purple ring.

Into the third ring — the one meant for living things.

Ye Wanwan exhaled. Her gaze settled on the two remaining, still-fruitless Black Sour trees. "I'm already taking one — might as well take all three."

With a thought, the talismans flew to the other two trees.

Moments later, all three short, broad-branched Black Sour trees had taken root in the space inside the ring, standing gracefully and bringing a small breath of life to what had been an empty space.

Ye Wanwan surveyed the whole valley around her.

"Since I'm already here..."

She smiled. Her footsteps carried her forward, and the range of the five talismans expanded rapidly to encompass most of the valley. The power in her primordial spirit hummed faintly.

"An element this weak in primordial spirit has the audacity to try to take an entire valley of spirit plants. I'd say she really doesn't value her own life." A young man hidden in the void nearby shook his head slowly, clicking his tongue.

But even as he watched, he didn't interrupt.

Ye Wanwan didn't stop either.

The five talismans' power continued to spread outward. The moment the formation came together, Ye Wanwan felt the resistance surge. "Not quite enough."

The talismans reversed their rotation and contracted back, settling into the smallest safe perimeter she could manage.

"Now."

Moving as fast as she could, Ye Wanwan opened the second storage ring.

And transplanted every spirit plant within the talisman's range inside.

After the first success, and then the second, Ye Wanwan grew bolder and went for a third — and then kept going, growing more practiced with each attempt.

By the time she was done, the ground she had passed through was stripped clean.

Ye Qian's luck on this trip had not been good. She'd been dropped into the body region of the realm when she entered. Everyone knew the treasures of Huanmeng Xingze were concentrated in the head region — specifically in the head valley. So the moment she'd identified her location, she'd been pushing hard to get here.
