She finally exhaled when the valley entrance came into view ahead.

Dou Ming was happy for her, even as his tone stayed light and dismissive. "Shimei, I told you — nobody's going to have found everything here in such a short time. Even if people beat us here, they can't possibly have swept the whole valley clean in one go."

"Not a chance," Dou Ming said, still looking perfectly relaxed.

Ye Qian's eyes flickered briefly before she concealed whatever was behind them. She said prettily, "Third Shixiong, I'm just worried that the Black Sour Fruit Second Shixiong wanted has already been taken. I'd hate to fail him."

"A single Black Sour tree can drop fifty to eighty fruit per season. Even with bad luck — say thirty at most — a few people could split it between them and still leave enough. Second Brother didn't specify a quantity. Get him a few and the job is done. The real prize here is the Core Condensation Fruit."

Dou Ming's expression darkened slightly.

Core Condensation Fruit wasn't especially useful to core formation cultivators, but Wushang Sect had no shortage of Foundation Building disciples — someone in the sect would always have a use for it.

Their objective before heading north had been clear: come back with Core Condensation Fruit. That was part of their mission.

Ji Changhuai had the same goal.

Neither of them said it aloud — but they both harbored the same thought. If she hadn't died. If, somehow, she was still out there —

A golden core that had been pried out could be restored with Core Condensation Fruit, couldn't it?

Whatever she'd lost — they could give it back to her.

Why had she had to be so stubborn? Why choose death over that?

Dou Ming didn't know what Ji Changhuai was really thinking, but the moment he'd heard there was Core Condensation Fruit here, both of them had volunteered to come.

Ye Qian had come purely for the spectacle.

"Shimei," Dou Ming said, "time to go in."

"Alright."

The two of them flew into the valley at speed, closing the distance quickly. The valley's entrance shimmered into view ahead, still wreathed in spirit mist that obscured the full view of what lay inside.

Their spirits lightened with every step.

Then they descended past the mist.

And neither of them could manage a smile anymore.

The valley ahead was still green, still verdant in color — still alive. But where the spirit herbs and rare plants should have been, there was nothing.

Not a single one remained.

Not a trace.

chapters.title: Nascent Soul Fruit
chapters.content:
Who had done this?

Dou Ming's expression turned ugly beyond all reckoning. He landed his sword and walked forward at a quick pace. But the further into the valley he went, the more desolate his heart became.

Gone.

All of it, gone.

Aside from ordinary weeds, every spirit herb with any value had been uprooted — pulled out from the soil, root and all, leaving nothing behind. All that remained was the turned earth itself. Scatter a few seeds here now, and perhaps in fifty years a new herb garden might take shape.

But right now it was barren.

Well — the weeds remained.

Ye Qian's face had gone through several shades of white. The high spirit mist that had clung to the valley's upper reaches had disguised the true state of things below, creating a false impression of abundance. Who could have imagined that walking inside would reveal nothing at all?

They'd have done better going to the body region.

"Third Shixiong..." Ye Qian called out tentatively. "Did we come too late?"

However furious she felt inwardly, Ye Qian didn't dare let it show in front of Dou Ming.

Dou Ming reassured her. "Don't worry. Even if someone got here first and swept the obvious spots, a valley this size — they couldn't have taken absolutely everything. They wouldn't have had the time, and they wouldn't have had the ability."

Ye Qian thought about it and supposed he was right.

The Yangtou Valley was rich with spirit energy, and the variety of spirit herbs and spirit beasts growing inside was considerable. Beyond the Core Condensation Fruit, there were countless other rare plants. Her Second Shixiong Lianxin was an alchemist — Ye Qian had planned to gather extra spirit herbs as a gift, in hopes of trading with him for Nourishing Soul Pills to stabilize her core.

If she left empty-handed, the whole trip would have been for nothing.

The two of them pressed on deeper into the valley.

But everywhere they looked was barren wasteland. Not just the Black Sour Fruit and Blood Swallow — those rarer resources — but even the most basic first-grade medicinal herbs had vanished entirely.

It had been picked absolutely clean.

When they reached the spot marked on the map as the Black Sour Fruit tree's location, they found nothing but an upturned hole in the ground.

The tree had been dug up by the roots.

Dou Ming's fury finally boiled over. Even Ye Qian fell silent.

"They even took the trees."

"Who would do something like this?"

Dou Ming was so furious he wanted to smash something — but there weren't many trees left standing nearby to receive his anger. The valley was stripped and empty.

Then, from somewhere ahead, came a flurry of movement. Dou Ming's head snapped up.

Someone was there.

"Move in," Dou Ming said immediately.

Ye Qian followed.

As they drew closer, voices drifted out from inside the mist: "Grab that thing — don't let it escape! That's the Core Condensation Fruit!"

Two bursts of sword qi rang through the air. The sound of a struggle.

Dou Ming wasted no time. He raised his sword and drove it into the mist, slashing through it.

A clash of steel.

His sword was blocked and came flying back into his grip, followed by an outraged shout from inside.

"Who's attacking from behind?"

Dou Ming charged in with a cold laugh. "Attacking from behind? You're the ones who should be dead."

Uprooting spirit plants and leaving nothing for anyone else — utterly shameless. They deserved exactly what was coming.

Inside the mist, neither side could clearly see the other — but they'd already exchanged several blows, and Dou Ming's fury was looking for somewhere to go.

Ye Qian pressed close to Dou Ming's side, not daring to stray an inch, while she spread her techniques to help pin the opposing side down. "Shixiong, there are three of them."

"Good. No wonder they moved so fast!" Dou Ming gritted his teeth. "Now let them give everything back!"

The Yunlang Stronghold disciples seethed in response. "So you're here to steal!"

They had been chasing this dan tree for a full day and night. They'd only just managed to corner it inside the formation array, success within their grasp — and now, at this exact moment, someone had come to take the spoils.

All three of them refused.

"Don't let them leave alive."

The three exchanged a glance. Killing intent flashed in every pair of eyes.

Most of all in Foundation Building stage Li Qun, who had set his sights on this Core Condensation Fruit for himself. He only needed this one fruit to break through to the Golden Core stage.

Li Qun quietly slipped his hand into his robes and drew out a concealed treasure — a Thunder Ball, a third-grade spirit tool capable of delivering the full force of a mid core formation cultivator's strike.

When the opening came, in the chaos of a three-way exchange, he hurled it directly at Dou Ming and Ye Qian.

Thunder exploded outward, driving straight toward them. Dou Ming lunged in front of Ye Qian and formed a seal with one hand. "Earth flow, hasten — earth draw, come now."

An earth wall rose up in front of them, stacking layer upon layer as a shield.

But the thunder bolt scaled two zhang of earthen wall and came crashing down on Dou Ming before the wall fully closed. Half his body went numb — but at the critical moment, he plunged underground, escaping through earth flight.

Li Qun came after him.

His shixiong Sun Qu pulled him back. "The dan tree is what matters. He won't get far. We'll give chase — you stay here and pick the fruit."

Li Qun swallowed his rage and pressed it down. "Shixiong — don't leave any witnesses."

"Understood."

If word got out that they'd caught the Core Condensation Fruit tree, Yunlang Stronghold would face its own troubles. An entire tree of Core Condensation Fruit — Sun Qu also wanted to return to his sect having accomplished something. He had every reason to see this through quietly.

"Second Shidi, you stay with Little Shidi."

"Understood."

Sun Qu went after Dou Ming alone.

But however far he followed the trail, Dou Ming and Ye Qian were nowhere to be found. "Something's not right — I followed the trace of the earth flight technique straight here, so how could they just... vanish?"

The tracks in the earth had broken off halfway.

Sun Qu frowned and examined the ground for a long while. Then his heartbeat began to quicken. He jerked his head up, sweeping the area — and his voice came out in a startled gasp.

"Something's wrong. This valley..."

"Why is it empty?"

"No, that's not the key point." Sun Qu's mind moved fast. He spun around. "We've been had."

He ran back at full speed, grateful he'd left one person with Li Qun. But by the time he arrived, it was already too late.

Dou Ming had driven a sword through one man's chest.

The golden core, shattered.

Only Foundation Building Li Qun remained.

Li Qun stared at the fallen shixiong at his feet. His voice pitched high and sharp. "You dare kill my shixiong?"

Dou Ming sneered. "Survival of the fittest. Save your words." He raised his hand to deliver a finishing blow, aiming to end it in a single strike.

But Li Qun had something left. He hurled another Thunder Ball.

Dou Ming's expression shifted. But at the critical moment, a jet of water surged forward and intercepted the lightning's force, redirecting the ball's power to one side.

It slammed into the earth.

Ye Qian's face had gone white from the effort.

Dou Ming's expression darkened. "You dare hurt my Shimei!"

Li Qun had already turned and fled — but he wasn't fast enough. Dou Ming's sword caught him through the heart. Li Qun's eyes flew wide open. They went glassy as he crumpled slowly to the ground.

And in the final moments of his gaze, cast toward the thick mist ahead, a blurred figure stood at the edge of the fog.

Dou Ming had already turned to Ye Qian. He didn't notice.

"Shimei, are you alright?"

Ye Qian was breathless. "I... I'm fine."

Dou Ming fed her a Xuanling Pill. "Absorb it properly."

"Yes, yes."

Ye Qian swallowed the first-grade pill immediately and let it take effect.

When her color began to return, Dou Ming helped her toward the formation array that had trapped the dan tree.

"These people actually had some skill."

The formation holding the dan tree was a third-grade array. Normally, only disciples of major sects would ever encounter first or second-grade arrays, let alone a third. Third-grade arrays were the province of inner disciples and elders.

Dou Ming, as one of Yan Ding's inner disciples, had some familiarity with formation arrays — but his strength wasn't in them. The highest he typically worked with was second-grade.

This one in front of him was going to be a challenge.

"If only Dashixiong were here," Dou Ming thought to himself.

Ye Qian asked, "Shixiong, can you manage it?"

In front of Ye Qian, Dou Ming would never say no.

"It'll just take some time."

Ye Qian stood. "I'll stand guard for Shixiong."

She quickly formed seals. "The spring river floods to meet the sea's breadth — above the sea, the bright moon rises with the tide."

"Water spirit — gather."

Droplets converged from all directions, encircling Dou Ming and Ye Qian in a shell of water, forming a natural liquid barrier. And at the front, the rising moisture coalesced into a new layer of mist, concealing their figures. When Sun Qu returned and entered the fog, he found himself wandering in circles.

Dou Ming's expression warmed slightly. "Thank you, Shimei."

"Shixiong, focus — we need to save time."

Dou Ming complied.

As he began working on the formation, Ye Qian stopped hiding the ambition in her eyes. Her gaze burned as it fixed on the heavily laden branches of the dan tree.

And on the single fruit at the very top — the one that had been slowly, unmistakably, ripening to gold.

A Nascent Soul Fruit.

chapters.title: The Realm Spirit
chapters.content:
The Core Condensation Fruit tree had lived inside Huanmeng Xingze for over a thousand years. And a dan tree that crossed the threshold of a millennium had a certain probability of producing a single Nascent Soul Fruit.

This was something even Xuanming Sect itself didn't know. Her father, Ye Conying, had dug up this information specifically for her.

"When you formed your golden core, the core cracked and failed. The golden core now inside you is Ye Wanwan's. We've used certain methods to transform that exceptional fire core into a water core, but for you to advance beyond it — past the Nascent Soul barrier — will be extraordinarily difficult. Unless you can use the power of the Nascent Soul Fruit, combined with assistance from two Ye family elders and your master, you might still have a chance."

"And if I can't get the Nascent Soul Fruit?"

"Then you will remain at the Golden Core stage for the rest of your life."

No.

Absolutely not.

Ye Qian had seen what happened to Ye Wanwan — the prodigy who had once been the talk of all of Wushang Sect, discarded and driven out the moment her cultivation stalled after core formation. By Yan Ding. By Ji Changhuai. By all of them.

Pushed step by step until she had nowhere left to go.

She would never follow that path.

She would never allow it.

In this world, she was the only one who could be the protagonist.

Ye Wanwan was nothing but a stepping stone.

The Nascent Soul Fruit had to be hers.

Encircled by the water barrier, Dou Ming worked at breaking the formation while Ye Qian sat cross-legged, standing guard. But whenever her gaze drifted upward to that single gold fruit at the highest branch, the hunger and certainty in her eyes became impossible to conceal.

And when she turned that gaze on Dou Ming —

A flicker of wariness entered it. Something calculating.

If Shixiong wanted it too...

She wouldn't give it up.

Not to him.

Hidden in the mist nearby, a small paper bird was watching. Its eyes — twin dots of cinnabar — spun in their sockets like something alive.

And a li away, Ye Wanwan was digging up the last Blood Swallow plant.

She brushed the soil from her hands and turned her attention toward the thick mist ahead. The silence that had settled over it told her that whatever fight had taken place inside was finished.

And her clearing of the valley was finished too.

"Only that last dan tree left."

But she didn't move toward it. That tree had been leading the Yunlang Stronghold disciples on a chase through the valley for a full day and night, buying her all the time she needed. But she still had questions about whether what it carried was real.

She'd covered every corner of the valley and found no second dan tree. If the fruit hanging from this one wasn't Core Condensation Fruit, then where was the real thing?

Ye Wanwan tapped one foot lightly on the ground.

This Core Condensation Fruit tree had existed inside Huanmeng Xingze for many years, but true Core Condensation Fruit had been obtained only twice in the five times Xuanming Sect had opened the realm — and only one fruit each time. Yet this one tree was loaded with dozens.

Did that mean every cultivator who'd ever reached it had been too principled to take more than one? Too restrained by conscience to be greedy?

Ye Wanwan laughed quietly.

"Impossible."

If it had been her, she would have taken the whole thing — roots and soil and all — and left nothing behind. Not one fruit.

So something was wrong.

The question was where.

Ye Wanwan stood thinking. Her gaze dropped to the ground, then lifted slowly toward the sky above.

High overhead, thick mist rolled across everything.

Even through it, the sky was pitch black. No stars. Nothing.

Huanmeng Xingze.

That was this realm's name.

But where were the stars?

And for that matter — where was the marsh?

Ye Wanwan bowed her head, turning this over. The name bore no obvious relationship to the realm around her. If anything, the two seemed entirely unconnected.

So — was this really the realm?

She turned suddenly to look at the lake not far away.

The only lake in the valley.

It was also where the dan tree had first appeared, before it ran off with those disciples and never came back.

Ye Wanwan walked toward it.

She reached down and let her hand enter the water.

The lake was cold. Fine threads of spirit energy burrowed into her skin — a sign that the spirit energy here was so saturated it was overflowing, spilling outward to nourish the entire valley.

Ye Wanwan's eyes deepened. Without another word, she took a breath and dove in headfirst, holding her breath as she descended toward the dark heart of the lake.

The further she went, the darker and more ordinary it seemed. She was beginning to think she'd been wrong — when a light appeared ahead.

One point, then two.

Then more and more.

Until they spread into a sky full of stars.

Ye Wanwan stopped where she was, staring.

And then she took two more steps forward, passed through a curtain of water — and the world flipped.

She was standing on the surface of the lake.

The water below her was perfectly still, mirroring a brilliant, star-filled sky. For a moment she couldn't tell which was water and which was sky. She stepped across the center of the lake, and ripples spread outward from beneath her feet.

A few rings, then stillness again.

Not far away, a spirit tree blazed red — its branches twisting gracefully, its leaves deep crimson, its fruit the size of apricots. There were pale red ones, pink, deep red, and at the very top — a single, resplendent golden fruit.

Ye Wanwan's gaze fixed on the gold fruit.

It was small — barely emerged from its blossom, like something that had only just broken free of its bud. Even its muted color carried a faint rawness, like something unfinished, not yet ready.

And yet that single gold fruit held more concentrated spirit energy than everything else on the tree combined.

If the deep red ones were Core Condensation Fruit, then that one had to be...

Nascent Soul Fruit.

Ye Wanwan's eyes darkened.

If Core Condensation Fruit was something she wanted but didn't urgently need, the Nascent Soul Fruit was different. She had to have it. Worth taking risks for.

Her path to the Nascent Soul stage — if left entirely to her own efforts — was something she would likely never achieve in this lifetime. But with outside help, there was still a chance.

Pei Xuan was already looking into the whereabouts of Fang He'an's master, hoping to bring him back to refine a Nascent Soul Pill for Ye Wanwan.

But the materials required for a Nascent Soul Pill were extraordinarily rare. Even if their Fifth Shibo was truly capable of making one, gathering the ingredients would be another problem entirely.

Especially given how many golden cores were inside her — how many pills would that take?

The thought made her scalp prickle.

So this Nascent Soul Fruit — Ye Wanwan would take it first, and see if it could help her break through. It was worth trying.

And as for the Core Condensation Fruit itself — the benefits to her were enormous as well.

True, someone of her natural ability didn't technically need Core Condensation Fruit to form a core. But if she could save some effort and not have to slog through the same old road again — why insist on doing it the hard way?

Without hesitation, Ye Wanwan walked toward the dan tree.

Up close, it was nothing like the scrawny little sapling she'd seen above ground. This was a vast, flourishing tree, deeply rooted, with branches spreading in every direction. If the one above looked a thousand years old, this one looked ten thousand.

Its roots spread across nearly half the lake bed, burrowing down to depths she couldn't measure.

"This is going to be a problem to uproot."

She sized it up. Pulling it out root and all wasn't going to be easy.

"Maybe I should just pick the fruit first."

Ye Wanwan eyed the full branches and moved immediately.

She reached for the gold fruit first.

The fruit shuddered.

The realm itself seemed to notice the intrusion. The lake surface erupted in sudden ripples — then the water itself burst upward, a column of it rocketing straight toward Ye Wanwan.

She swatted it aside with her staff and dove behind the tree trunk. The water column crashed down past her, turned to fine mist, and scattered — but made no further immediate move against her.

Ye Wanwan was briefly surprised.

Then she felt a hostile gaze from above her.

She looked up.

Perched right beside the gold fruit was a child.

He was glaring at her with open fury.

You could practically read it on his face: Thief!

chapters.title: One Life or Ten — It Still Knew How to Choose
chapters.content:
Someone was there?

No.

The light in Ye Wanwan's eyes shifted. Not a person. A spirit.

The child before her had no physical body — he existed by drawing on the spirit energy of the dan tree. The lake's water he'd unleashed against her had simply been borrowed power from this star marsh, turned into a weapon.

The realm spirit?

Ye Wanwan began circling the tree, weaving between the water arrows, and then moved swiftly — scaling the spirit tree, closing the distance between herself and the child in the shortest possible time.

"What are you doing?!"

The boy vanished from his spot and reappeared five steps away.

Ye Wanwan was faster.

The boy bristled, furious. "You want Core Condensation Fruit?! Fine — take them! Those are mine to give! But you can't have that!" He pointed at the gold fruit. That single fruit contained the concentrated essence of the entire dan tree.

It was his life.

Ye Wanwan laughed softly. "I've come all this way — why limit myself to a few pieces of fruit? I want everything, naturally."

The boy's eyes went wide. He felt her gaze land directly on him and couldn't believe what he was hearing. "You want to take me too?"

"I wouldn't call it taking — just giving you a different place to live." Ye Wanwan moved like a wolf circling a child into a trap, step by measured step. "Come now, little one. Let big sister show you what it feels like to be free."

The Realm Spirit: "..."

"How dare you!"

Ye Wanwan's hand had already closed around his wrist. "I can dare a great deal more."

The boy threw himself backward in a full roll, wrenching out of her grip — but a force from below caught him mid-air and launched him forward instead.

He looked down. Beneath him, a spirit talisman had appeared without his knowledge.

It ignited on its own.

Rune light bled outward from the talisman, encircling the dan tree in a ring of luminescence.

Snap.

Another burst of light from a different direction.

He looked. Flames were flickering in four separate spots around him — four more talismans, burning.

Four streams of rune light converged and closed inward, catching the boy and the gold fruit together in the center.

Like a net drawing shut.

The boy flailed both arms wildly, and the wind above the lake screamed down, a barrage of blades hammering at the rune barrier. He darted into the branches with the gold fruit clutched to his chest.

And vanished.

Ye Wanwan's expression didn't shift. She reached one hand through the rune barrier — the runes bent like a golden hoop around her wrist. Bracing the other hand on a branch, she leapt down from the tree.

Wind and water column came crashing toward her simultaneously.

But the rune barrier around her wrist suddenly expanded outward, encasing her and deflecting the water column entirely. She ignored the screaming wind and the crashing water and walked calmly to the base of the tree.

She crouched, and brought her palm down hard.

"Five-element force — open!"

Wood, water, fire, metal, earth — five beams of spirit light poured from her palm into the ground. With the dan tree at the center, five spirit pearls expanded outward at speed.

Surrounding the dan tree.

The boy's eyes went wide, and he nearly broke apart in panic. "What — how can a golden core leave your body like that?! What are you?!"

Her golden core.

She'd used golden cores like weapons, sending them out from her body.

And there were — one, two, three, four, five —

Five of them.

Why were there five?!

What cultivation technique was this?!

Ye Wanwan changed her posture from palm-flat to closed fist, and began pulling upward — slowly, steadily, dragging the entire dan tree out of the ground.

The realm spirit felt the space it had been hiding in begin to destabilize. The entire spirit let out a wail.

"What do you think you're doing?!"

Ye Wanwan spoke in the same unhurried tone she might use to discuss the weather. "Taking you outside."

"You lunatic!"

The dan tree came up inch by inch. The entire lake, the entire realm, trembled with it. It was as if something foundational was being disturbed. The realm spirit shrieked, "The dan tree is the heart of this entire star marsh realm! If you pull it out, this place will collapse!"

"Doesn't matter. It's not mine."

The realm spirit: "...Have you no conscience?"

"None at all."

Ye Wanwan bore down and kept pulling. The tree came free of the earth — but even dozens of meters off the ground, the root system still hadn't ended.

The roots really did go that deep.

Ye Wanwan sighed faintly. "This really is annoying."

The realm spirit assumed she would give up. But the young woman's golden cores spun faster and rose higher outside her body — and she still had enough attention to spare for something else.

She opened the entrance to the Purple Cloud Ring.

The realm spirit finally reached its breaking point. Its home was about to be sacked wholesale. It exploded at her: "Wait — the dan tree needs the spirit lake to survive! If you take only the tree, it won't live long!"

For the first time, Ye Wanwan's resolve showed a crack. "Then..."

The realm spirit said, heartbroken: "Either take the whole lake, or put it down, and I'll give you all the fruit on it."

It added quickly: "Including the gold fruit."

It was done caring.

It was a parasitic spirit — it existed only because the realm existed. If the realm collapsed, so would it.

One life against ten. It still knew how to choose.

Better to wait a little longer, as painful as that was.

Even if it burned with resentment.

Ye Wanwan considered for a moment. "No need to make things so complicated. If the lake has to come with it, I'll just take the lake too."

The realm spirit: "?"

"Do you know what you're saying? This isn't just any body of water. This is the Star Marsh — a spirit lake born from the concentrated essence of heaven and earth, nurtured over ten thousand years."

"A single drop could add a year to an ordinary mortal's lifespan. A bowl of it could restore life to someone on the very edge of death. It's a source of spirit energy that cultivators spend their lives trying to obtain. No matter how severe the wound, a few days submerged in it will heal you completely. And you're telling me you'll just — take it?"

Ye Wanwan felt the pull of complicated emotions. "Thank you for making sure I know I need to take it."

The realm spirit screamed. "That wasn't what I meant!"

Ye Wanwan reached into her robes and produced three gold talismans. "I only have three. One can only be used once — I was saving them for real danger. Looks like I'll have to use one now."

The realm spirit stared. "What are those?"

Ye Wanwan didn't answer. She channeled her spirit energy into the gold talisman and it ignited without flame, golden runes blooming like a flower at the heart of the lake.

And with them came a pressure — enormous, fundamental.

The realm spirit felt its voice leave it entirely. "What is this..."

The power of it was terrifying.

Like something that could unmake the world.

Ye Wanwan's brow furrowed slightly. Her cultivation was too low — she could only force a temporary elevation of one stage. But for now, that was enough.

The rune patterns wrapped around her, then dispersed and sank inward, settling into her meridians, flowing through her from the inside out. Like armor plating being fitted over her.

It built a layer of defense — and simultaneously drew heaven and earth essence toward her at tremendous speed, her aura climbing without pause.

In an instant, Ye Wanwan's presence had surged to the edge of the Nascent Soul stage.

Nascent Soul — mid-stage.

Ye Wanwan clenched her fist. "Good enough."

The five golden cores floating outside her body surged with new power, and Ye Wanwan gathered herself with a single low shout. The five cores shot outward and surrounded the spirit lake on all sides, lifting it.

The boy's jaw dropped completely.

What was this technique?

Had this woman decided to use the entire star marsh as her dantian?

Under Ye Wanwan's will, the entirety of the star marsh realm began moving toward the open Purple Cloud Ring.

But at that moment — a small problem.

The Purple Cloud Ring's interior couldn't hold a spirit lake this size.

Ye Wanwan paused.

"I didn't think of that."

If she let go now, the lake and the dan tree would both dissolve. But drawing on her focus to upgrade the Purple Cloud Ring's interior capacity — there was no time for that.

The standoff held.

The realm spirit also felt the approach of death and dissolution.

It screamed at her: "I knew this would happen! You absolute madwoman!"

Ye Wanwan said, almost thoughtfully, "I didn't think it through."

Still — if she couldn't take all of it, half might still work.

She made an immediate decision and moved to contract the range of the golden cores.

The realm spirit roared: "Don't you dare."

Ye Wanwan said, "If I stop, the realm really will collapse."

The realm spirit gritted its nonexistent teeth. "Then let me!"

"Let me do it!"

chapters.title: Is That Ye Wanwan?!
chapters.content:
"Don't let go — let me handle it!"

The shout was sharp and frantic.

As if in terror that Ye Wanwan would act impulsively and ruin everything. The realm spirit moved with startling speed, and at the brink of life and death, condensed itself into a streak of light and hurled itself straight at the Purple Cloud Ring.

The Purple Cloud Ring flickered with shifting light, its aura rising and falling.

Ye Wanwan immediately saw what was happening — the realm spirit was merging with the Purple Cloud Ring.

She raised an eyebrow. "I thought you didn't want to leave?"

The realm spirit ground out the words. "You've already looted my home and carried it off wholesale. What choice do I have?"

The voice was young — but it radiated the exhausted indignation of someone who had suffered every available affront.

Ye Wanwan shrugged, but her technique didn't waver.

"I only want the dan tree and the lake. You don't have to come with them."

"...Those two things are the foundation of my survival. You're taking both. If I don't come with them — you want me to just die?"

Ye Wanwan smiled. "I was worried you'd be too stubborn to come."

The realm spirit stopped talking to her.

Its aura began to fuse with the Purple Cloud Ring. The ring had been blood-bonded to Ye Wanwan — it was connected to her consciousness, and she could feel it changing.

The interior space was shifting.

The exterior was shifting.

As the internal space expanded, the realm spirit called out: "Ready."

Ye Wanwan had been holding on through this entire stretch, burning through most of her spiritual energy. Her dantian was verging on depletion.

At the word, she didn't hesitate. She summoned everything she had left and drove the lake and the dan tree inward. When the very last drop of the spirit lake had entered the ring's interior —

From every direction came a massive sound of shattering.

Like an enormous mirror — cracks spreading in an instant in all directions, then —

The boy's voice: "Run!"

Ye Wanwan didn't pause. She flew toward the entry point she'd come through — the exit. But the space behind her was collapsing with terrifying speed.

The crashing roar closed in without stopping.

Three meters.

Two meters.

One meter.

Half a meter.

One body-length away.

The realm spirit screamed: "That's a void collapse — if it catches you, there won't even be ashes left. Run!"

Ye Wanwan wiped the blood from the corner of her mouth. The backlash from forcing a cultivation elevation was significant, and the exhaustion of depletion was rolling over her in waves.

But at the sound of that scream beside her, Ye Wanwan still managed to laugh. "Perfect — saves on coffin costs."

The realm spirit: "..."

Freak.

Ye Wanwan laughed again, low and soft. The void behind her collapsed, and from the black abyss poured a relentless tide of annihilating energy. She didn't look back — she could feel it closing in without turning around.

Like a beast opening its jaws to swallow her whole.

She kept moving. And at the last critical moment, her spiritual energy erupted in a sudden burst. Right before the realm spirit's eyes — pale with terror — she ignited the second gold talisman and detonated the power of a mid Nascent Soul stage cultivator from within.

At the same moment, she drove herself through the exit.

Lake water flooded the space around her on all sides.

She was back in the valley lake. And she didn't stop — she broke the surface and surged back onto dry land.

"Out!"

But she didn't stop there either.

The realm spirit looked back — and saw that things weren't over yet.

The valley lake behind her was sinking. Fast. The collapse spread outward from the lake as its center, swallowing everything on all sides at tremendous speed. Anyone who hesitated even a moment would be gone.

The realm spirit's heart nearly leaped into its throat.

"Oh no."

Ye Wanwan laughed softly. "Exciting, isn't it."

Boom boom boom.

The ground shook violently.

Inside the mist where Ye Qian and Dou Ming had been working through the formation, and where Sun Qu had been trying to track them down — all three were jolted by the impact.

Ye Qian was still piecing it together when she felt the earth lurch beneath her feet, and the black void spreading through the valley sent her voice pitching into sharp, frantic alarm.

"Shixiong! Something's wrong!"

Dou Ming had just managed to break the formation. The entire dan tree was in his hands. He turned back — and his pupils contracted.

"Run!"

Ye Qian was already moving. She didn't look back even once.

Dou Ming kept pace, grabbed a handful of Core Condensation Fruit from the tree, then seized Ye Qian by the hand and ran with her.

The concealing mist they had conjured around them was being swallowed up by the collapsing space, drawn inward and dissolved into nothing.

The landscape behind them was going dark, piece by piece.

Sun Qu was also running. And in the chaos of that retreat, he spotted the bodies of Li Qun and the other disciple near where Dou Ming and Ye Qian had been — and his eyes split wide with grief and rage.

"You killed my shidi!"

Dou Ming didn't spare him a glance. He ran at full speed. The devouring force was moving too fast.

Sun Qu's heart was torn in two — but he didn't dare stop. As the void storm swept closer, all three of them saw Li Qun and the other man's remains, left behind on the ground, swallowed completely by the darkness.

Not even fragments remained.

All three felt their backs go cold.

Dou Ming didn't dare ask what had happened.

There was no time to ask.

Both of them ran for the valley mouth with everything they had. Then, in the corner of Ye Qian's eye, she glimpsed a figure moving alongside them in their escape.

Just off to their right. Very close.

She tried to look more clearly — but the moment she turned her head, her pace slowed.

Dou Ming snapped at her: "Shimei, what are you doing?!" You couldn't afford to be distracted at a moment like this.

The warning jolted her back into focus. She didn't look again.

She poured every last bit of herself into running.

But the entire valley was being pulled backward with them — their speed dragging in the suction of the collapsing space. With their lives on the line, they had no choice but to use whatever they had left.

Sun Qu burned through his bloodline power to boost his speed, moving to overtake Ye Qian and Dou Ming. Ye Qian was sharp enough — one look at the hatred blazing in Sun Qu's eyes told her exactly what he intended to do if he passed them. She called out immediately: "Shixiong, he's going to make a move on us!"

Dou Ming understood at once. He bit through his own tongue, burning his vital essence, and pulled ahead of Sun Qu. But Sun Qu lunged and caught hold of Ye Qian's long skirt.

"If we're dying, we're dying together."

Ye Qian's expression went cold in an instant. She spun, drew her spirit sword, and slashed through both his arm and her own skirt without a moment's hesitation.

Decisive. No mercy.

In the same instant, they leapt through the valley mouth.

Sun Qu fell one step short and was left inside, swallowed by the dark forever.

Outside the valley, once the consuming void stopped expanding, Dou Ming finally stopped moving. His heart was still hammering. He turned to look at Ye Qian, and his expression was slightly strange. "Shimei, just now you..."

That ice-cold gaze. That instant, merciless kill. Nothing like the gentle, soft-spoken Ye Qian he knew.

Ye Qian's eyes grew red. She stared at her own fingers and said in a small, trembling voice, "Shixiong — did I do something wrong? I... I didn't want to, but if I hadn't, both of us would have died."

Dou Ming turned it over and felt a flash of guilt. Why had he even questioned his shimei over something like that? Sun Qu would have taken them both if she hadn't acted. She'd saved both their lives.

He reached out and ruffled her hair. "Shimei did nothing wrong. You did exactly right. If you hadn't been so quick-thinking, neither of us would have made it out."

Ye Qian sniffled and managed a smile through her tears. "And the dan tree..."

Dou Ming's face broke into a grin. "Still right here. When we leave, however much you want, Shixiong will give you."

Ye Qian brightened. "That's a promise, Shixiong — no going back on it."

"When have I ever gone back on my word?"

They talked and laughed as they went. Dou Ming glanced once more at the black void where the valley had been and shuddered. "No reason to stay here any longer. Let's move."

"Alright."

They walked away quickly. Ye Qian had already pulled her gaze forward — but as it swept back, she caught a glimpse of a figure standing near the valley mouth not far away.

Ye Qian stopped.

Her eyes fell on a familiar set of features, and her pupils shrank.

"Ye Wanwan...?!"

chapters.title: I Have More Golden Cores Than Other People
chapters.content:
Ye Qian's eyes were fixed wide open, staring at the young woman who had escaped from the valley. If she had not been mistaken earlier, the figure hidden in the thick fog had also been her.

But she had been right behind them not far back — how had she only emerged now?

Ye Qian clenched her jaw. Though the young woman's face was covered and not clearly visible, Ye Qian had an instinct: it was Ye Wanwan.

The brows and eyes were too similar.

Even the build was identical.

But if it truly was Ye Wanwan, she could not let Dou Ming see.

Ye Qian turned her head and ran off alongside Dou Ming.

"Senior Brother, I can hear the commotion growing behind us. Let's move faster."

Dou Ming had no reason to suspect anything and immediately picked up the pace.

Ye Wanwan felt Ye Qian's gaze of hatred, but did not give chase. She only swept a calm glance in their direction, and without slowing her hands, dragged the person out.

It was Sun Qu.

"Why did I have to save him?"

If she had not gone back to pull someone out, Ye Wanwan would have emerged sooner.

The little creature inside the Ziyun ring said, "I felt just now that this person carries an aura I recognise. He should have something I want."

"What kind of thing?"

"I'm still thinking."

The absorption had happened too quickly for proper analysis. For now, all it could do was have Ye Wanwan rescue the person first and figure the rest out later.

The absorption inside the valley was still ongoing, but the stone walls provided a temporary barrier — it had not completely collapsed yet, though it was still not safe.

Ye Wanwan dragged Sun Qu out and pulled him several metres away from the valley entrance. She scanned the surroundings, brow slightly furrowed, as though searching for something.

Her complexion was an unnatural pale.

The little creature noticed. "Well, well. Overexerted yourself, didn't you? Drained dry."

Serves you right for showing off.

Ye Wanwan said flatly, "I need to find somewhere to close off and recover my energy. Can you stand guard?"

Two golden talismans had completely wrung out the spiritual energy inside her. She needed somewhere to restore herself.

Otherwise there was no way to get through the next twenty-odd days.

The little creature's mouth twitched. "Why go to all that trouble? Just go into the Xingze realm."

Xingze realm...

Ye Wanwan immediately thought of that spiritual lake within, and looked down at the ring on her finger. "Go into the ring?"

Could a storage ring hold its own owner?

The little creature immediately understood what she meant and explained. "Now that this ring has me as its inhabiting spirit, it's nothing like that cheap storage ring of yours anymore. You only need to focus your intent and you can enter."

Cheap?

Storage rings had never been cheap.

"And then what?" Ye Wanwan asked. "Leave the ring lying on the ground for someone to pick up?"

"I can create an illusion. I am now the ring's inhabiting spirit — I can transform the ring into a speck of dust and hide it in the soil. That way you won't have to worry about anyone finding it."

Ye Wanwan's brow smoothed. "That doesn't sound bad."

"But you should still move further away first. If that absorption force leaks out, it's all over."

Ye Wanwan: "...Thank you for the reminder. I'm not an idiot."

Ye Wanwan dragged Sun Qu and flew a distance away. Once she confirmed she was well clear of the valley entrance and the surrounding area was safe, she threw Sun Qu in first.

Then she entered the Ziyun ring herself.

The inside of the Ziyun ring had now become an entire starfield expanse.

A spiritual lake ringed a fertile patch of land at the centre.

On the land grew that ten-thousand-year pill fruit tree, as well as the Grade Three sour black fruit tree and over a dozen Grade Three spirit herbs Ye Wanwan had placed inside.

Other spirit herbs were scattered around the base of the pill tree as well.

Everything was thriving.

Growing even more vigorously than before she had transplanted them from the mountain valley.

Ye Wanwan's gaze deepened slightly.

The little creature materialised as a spirit form and perched in the pill tree, arms folded, looking down at Ye Wanwan from above. "These low-grade spirit herbs actually get to enter the Xingze realm. They must have been accumulating good fortune for a lifetime."

If it were up to its own taste, it would never have let such things in.

Ye Wanwan lifted the hem of her skirt and sat down cross-legged. "In my view, you and all of them are the same — all going into medicine eventually. Don't make distinctions between noble and humble."

The little creature charged up to Ye Wanwan's face in a fury. "I am a great formation spirit! The most precious companion spirit in this entire world! I govern an entire realm! And you dare say I'm the same as these weeds!"

Ye Wanwan closed her eyes.

The little creature was deeply aggrieved. "Quickly, apologise to me! Or I'll be angry! I won't play with you anymore!"

Ye Wanwan said flatly, "I'm recovering. Go play on your own."

Ye Wanwan raised a hand and lightly swept the Xingze to one side, while around her the five golden cores floated, forming a protective array that enclosed Ye Wanwan within.

Xingze stared at the golden cores and fell into a long, deep reverie.

A cultivator's golden core... why could it leave the body?

This question had been puzzling it endlessly.

Of course Xingze could not work it out. Even Pei Xuan, the first time he witnessed it, had nearly lost his composure.

No one had imagined that Ye Wanwan would use the unique properties of the Spirit Refinement Art — using the method of circulating spiritual energy both inside and outside the body — to lay out five expanded meridian pathways externally.

It was as though a larger version of Ye Wanwan surrounded the real one at the centre, and within the meridian range of this outer projection, her golden cores could travel outward through those meridians and roam freely — even be arranged to cover attack ranges that an opponent could not anticipate.

When Ye Wanwan explained this idea to Pei Xuan, he had looked at her for a very long time, and then said, "You are a genuine genius."

As for the word genius — Ye Wanwan had heard it so many times she was tired of it.

She simply wanted to be stronger.

If the method worked, that was all she needed.

"Though this technique does have a flaw. If someone manages to strike your golden cores down, you would very likely lose them and be severely injured. Hardly worth the risk."

Because golden cores were too important to a cultivator.

Regarding Pei Xuan's concern, Ye Wanwan responded, "Master, don't worry about that. I may not have much, but I have more golden cores than other people."

Pei Xuan: "..."

Fair enough.

Absolutely no issue then.

Ye Wanwan ran the Spirit Refinement Art, drawing spiritual energy from the surrounding heaven and earth. It channelled through the Ziyun ring and surged rapidly into the Xingze realm.

Five streams of spiritual mist drifting down from the void also left Xingze dumbfounded.

What kind of person was this?

Even just cultivating could trigger an Xingze phenomenon — and with this much heaven-and-earth spiritual energy, she absorbed it so effortlessly.

Watching Ye Wanwan's body become like a vortex endlessly pulling in the energy of heaven and earth, Xingze drew a sharp breath. "This new master... is extraordinary."

Even the realm's former owner, that dead old man, had not possessed this kind of talent at golden core stage. And yet a person with five spiritual roots — someone fated for a difficult cultivation path — had this ability.

Xingze's eyes went through many shifts before it finally reached a decision: it could follow along and observe. Perhaps this person could truly help it.

Help it escape its imprisonment in the Xingze realm and never be free.

Xingze crouched nearby and watched for a while, then suddenly remembered the dragged-in Sun Qu. It slapped its head, hurried over, and began rifling through the man's belongings for examination.

Five days later.

Ye Wanwan emerged from her meditation, opened her eyes, and felt every meridian in her body flowing freely. When she raised her hand, she immediately found she had broken through.

The third stage of Qi Refining second layer had broken through to the third layer.

Wood spiritual root: Qi Refining fourth layer.

Water, fire spiritual roots: Qi Refining third layer.

Metal, earth: second layer.

Ye Wanwan's brow lifted slightly. The wood attribute here was unusually rich — it had sent the wood attribute leaping two full levels directly to the fourth.

By no means a slow progression.

chapters.title: Senior Sister, We Need You!
chapters.content:
At this pace, she would reach Foundation Establishment again in under half a year.

Ye Wanwan withdrew her spiritual energy and rose, walking toward Xingze. She found the little creature sitting beside Sun Qu, staring at his belongings with a grave expression.

"What is it?"

"Look." Xingze pointed at everything that had been emptied out from Sun Qu's qiankun pouch.

Sun Qu was an elite disciple of Cloud Wave Fortress, but his belongings were not particularly impressive.

He had a Grade Two sword, a few pills of xuan spirit elixir — all ordinary quality, none even reaching first-grade — and the most valuable thing was a few hundred spirit stones.

Everything else was worthless.

"Mm?"

Very quickly, however, Ye Wanwan's gaze fell on a different stone. It resembled a spirit stone somewhat, though its hue was deeper. Despite appearing to hold no spiritual energy, it was distinctly different from an ordinary stone.

Low-grade qiankun pouches had no binding ritual.

Ye Wanwan flicked her hand and drew the stone over, studying it carefully. It was threaded with faint blue, and when held up to the light, it seemed to carry talisman patterns within.

Xingze's expression was serious. "This is a Dream Illusion Stone."

"A Dream Illusion Stone from the Dream Illusion Xingze?" Ye Wanwan thought carefully. "I've heard these stones can help a person comprehend illusion realms and cultivate illusion arts."

"That would be an ordinary Dream Illusion Stone." Xingze's voice was grave.

Ye Wanwan raised an eyebrow and weighed the stone in her hand. "This one isn't ordinary?"

"No. This is a stone from within the Dream Illusion realm. Think of it as a formation stone — something as important to the Dream Illusion realm as the Xingze's spirit lake." Xingze braced its hands on its knees and stood, expression still grave. "If refined and absorbed, it can give a person a temporary grasp of illusion abilities and allow them to comprehend the methods of constructing a secret realm."

Ye Wanwan's heart stirred. Methods of constructing a secret realm?

That was essentially creating a spatial world.

That was quite remarkable.

"This stone no longer has much spiritual nature left. And it's only an edge stone — it can only be used once before it loses its power and offers no more comprehension." Xingze's tone was extremely heavy. "But its appearance here means the formation stones inside have already been extensively damaged."

Ye Wanwan began to follow its reasoning. "You mean the Dream Illusion realm has had something happen to it as well?"

"The Dream Illusion Xingze is called a single secret realm, but it is actually divided into two. In the past, when cultivators like yourselves entered, you were always entering the first-layer Dream Illusion realm. Only you..." Xingze glanced furtively at Ye Wanwan, "...discovered the Xingze hidden behind the Dream Illusion realm. That is, me."

Xingze puffed out its chest.

"But with the Dream Illusion realm's secret realm maintenance, it should have been able to run for at least seven or eight thousand years. Yet if even the formation stones have been excavated, and then the Xingze itself collapsed..."

Ye Wanwan did not need it to continue. She already understood the problem.

This secret realm was collapsing.

This trial had been a trap.

Without another word, Ye Wanwan said, "Go out."

She flashed out of the Ziyun ring. The ring returned to her finger, and Sun Qu was left behind where he lay.

"Do we need to bring that person?" Xingze asked.

Ye Wanwan glanced at Sun Qu lying by the riverbank and kept walking. "No need. A disciple like this won't know much. Better to go see for myself."

Ye Wanwan mounted her sword and flew toward the middle of the sheep's belly.

Wind rushed past as she flew. Her mind was rapidly analysing the situation. The Cloud Wave Fortress disciples had rushed toward the valley the moment they entered.

While it was true that everyone knew the Ram's Head Valley was where the pill fruit grew — and so those who needed it would head there first — Cloud Wave Fortress had arrived suspiciously fast.

Even Ye Wanwan had only ended up in the Ram's Head slope area because she had been transported there by accident, and had simply chosen what was closest. But Foundation Establishment cultivators would more often be drawn to the sheep's belly where resources were richer.

And there had been three of them.

That did not fit the transport rules.

Unless they had already known in advance that this secret realm could not hold much longer, and someone had simply told them: go for the pill fruit first when you enter, worry about the rest later.

If that was the case, a treasure-hunting group like Sun Qu's would not be the only one in here.

There were certainly more in the sheep's belly.

Ye Wanwan increased her speed, breaking through the cloud layer and charging toward the vast open terrain of the sheep's belly. As she did, she also noticed that faint black cracks were flickering in the sky above.

Xingze said, "As expected."

Ye Wanwan's eyes flashed. "Based on your estimate, how long can this realm hold?"

"If closed off, another eighty or a hundred years without issue. But if there's fighting — that's harder to say. The bigger the commotion, the faster it collapses. Under normal circumstances, a month shouldn't be a problem."

"Good."

The Heart-Questioning Sword accelerated.

In moments, Ye Wanwan plunged into the perilous dense forest.

At this same moment, two groups were also fleeing frantically through the trees. At the front was a young woman shouldering an enormous colourful stone taller than the trees themselves.

She charged head-first through the dense forest.

Everything she passed was left in astonishment at her sheer brute strength.

Behind her, at a somewhat greater distance, was Fang He'an. "Senior Sister! Senior Sister! Can you just put it in your ring for now!"

Bai Jian was grey with dust, but her eyes were bright. She heard this and looked a little confused. "My qiankun pouch is full."

Fang He'an heard that and almost slapped his own thigh.

The ring! The ring Martial Uncle Pei Xuan had lent them before they set out!

"I tried," Bai Jian said. "But it said it needs time."

Now Fang He'an understood why Bai Jian was running with it on her back — it needed time. Which meant the rainbow ore was of too high a grade for Senior Sister's current spiritual sense to move it immediately.

Fang He'an was running so hard his soul felt like it was trailing behind him. But behind them was a group that was not letting them stop.

"Li Junior Brother can't hold them off much longer. I'll buy some time — you get it in."

Bai Jian nodded but did not slow down, quickly veering toward a more secluded area and beginning to transfer the stone.

This was something she was bringing back for Junior Sister.

No one was taking it from her.

Fang He'an skidded to a halt. He quickly rummaged through his qiankun pouch and pulled out two vials, moving swiftly to pour them across the ground.

He was not even sparing the medicinal powder he normally would not use carelessly.

He used all of it.

A hissing white smoke rose from the ground and dissolved into the thick fog. Fang He'an took the antidote he had prepared for himself, then quickly stepped back.

He melted into the forest.

He still had one porcelain vial in his hand.

The vial was transparent, and inside were several tiny ant creatures.

Fang He'an took a deep breath. "Come on, don't let me down." He uncapped the vial and let the tiny poison ants out.

The poison ants crawled to the mouth of the vial, then spread their wings and took to the air.

They could fly.

Fang He'an retreated slowly into the depths of the forest, while Li Wanzhi's voice grew gradually closer. "You bunch of people raised with no manners whatsoever — we were the ones who found that spirit stone vein. We were generous enough to give you room, and you dare chase after us demanding we hand things over."

"Shameless."

In mid-sentence, several blood-red arrows came flying out.

Li Wanzhi leapt upward, barely dodging them. When he saw the purple marks on the arrowheads, his cursing grew even fiercer.

"Blood Rainbow Pavilion thinks I don't know your Pavilion Master's name — just because you're all wearing masks doesn't mean I don't know your dirty little secrets."

"Your Pavilion Master killed his own brother and father, stole his own elder brother's position, and abducted his own sister-in-law, and all the disciples in your sect not only refuse to condemn their own leader, they actually join him in bullying men and dominating women, running rampant wherever you go!"

"When I get out of here, I am absolutely going to act in the name of heaven and bring justice down on all of you!"

"I will destroy every last one of you!"

"What the—!"

"What is this smell, why can't I use my spiritual energy?"

"There's poison! I'm going down!"

And yet even as the young man pretended to collapse, he shot out several ice arrows.

Everyone cursed furiously.

"Ha ha ha — here come my hidden weapons!"

The young man's insufferable voice gave everyone a splitting headache. One by one they chased after Li Wanzhi, longing to finish him off.

But only Li Wanzhi knew: the situation was bad.

Without Senior Sister, they could not win this.

"Senior Sister!"

We need you!!

—

At that same moment, Ye Wanwan broke through the tree line and plunged into the forest.

chapters.title: Excellence Is Its Own Original Sin
chapters.content:
Li Wanzhi had just recently broken through to golden core, and his mastery of techniques was limited.

Though Yan Ju had been responsible about things — during his Foundation Establishment period he had given Li Wanzhi three cultivation manuals to choose from: the Azure Cloud Sword Art, the Chaotic Blade Sword Art, and a basic combat technique manual for cultivators.

Li Wanzhi had chosen the Azure Cloud Sword Art and the combat technique. But he had been lazy, and neither was fully mastered yet. He had always thought it did not matter.

Yet now, in actual combat, he finally understood exactly where his weaknesses lay.

He—

Was too weak!

But it was too late for regret now.

"If I make it back, I will study until I drop dead!"

Fortunately, while he had cut corners on everything else, Yan Ju had forced the Swiftwind Art into Li Wanzhi's head personally. After a full year of it, his escape speed was actually quite impressive.

At the very least, Li Wanzhi had managed to kite five people through the forest — and successfully drawn them away!

Except now—

He could not keep going!

A dense volley of blood arrows came shooting from every direction, sealing off all of his paths forward. If Li Wanzhi kept running, there was only death ahead.

He had to stop.

He watched the five people closing in on him and let out an awkward laugh. "Brothers, is it too late to admit I was wrong?"

"Go and die!"

The lead cultivator swung a blade downward. The blade energy, driven by a golden core cultivator's power, was ferocious. Li Wanzhi raised both arms and blocked with a thud.

Everyone now saw what was on his arms.

Li Wanzhi broke out in a cold sweat. "Good thing, good thing — at least I learned this one technique."

Spirit Shield.

The best thing there was for blocking attacks.

But the force on the other side was too powerful. Li Wanzhi was still driven backward several steps by the momentum. The blade fighters closing in from behind swung at him. Li Wanzhi rolled into a forward tumble, arms pressing down to push off, rolling quickly out of the encirclement, and then threw back his head with a desperate, throat-tearing cry.

"Senior Sister, help me!"

Fang He'an watching from the side was anxious. "The Earth Escape Art, you idiot!"

Li Wanzhi reacted instantly. "Right, right — Earth Escape Art!"

Damn.

What was the Earth Escape Art incantation?

At this life-or-death moment, Li Wanzhi finally remembered. His whole body transformed into a streak of light and shot into the ground with a whoosh.

At the same time, Fang He'an cast his technique. A swift wind swept through the forest, picking up the dense fog hovering across the ground and sending it toward the five Blood Rainbow Pavilion members.

But a stronger gale swept back from the opposite direction, blowing the poison fog back toward Fang He'an's position.

Fang He'an was all right — he had already taken his antidote. But Li Wanzhi, who had just popped back up from the ground, took a full breath of it. "I'm going to suffocate."

In the very next moment, he thought: actually, suffocating might be better than this.

Countless bubbles broke out across the surface of his skin, spreading in a rapid purple-black tide. He stretched out his hand in despair. "I'm... I'm dying."

Fang He'an dropped into a sliding stop and rushed over, slapping what was in his hand into Li Wanzhi's mouth. "Swallow it!"

The antidote was shoved down Li Wanzhi's throat, saving his life at the critical moment. But Li Wanzhi was completely incapacitated, and Fang He'an could only hoist him up and run.

The five people were already in pursuit from behind. But not far into it, a series of screams rang out.

"Poison ants!"

"That pretty-faced one who ran is a Poison Master!"

Fang He'an sprinted with everything he had. When he heard that, he still found time to yell back, "Your grandfather is the Poison Master — I'm an Alchemy Master!"

The direct disciple who inherited his teacher's greatness as an Alchemy Master!

Even if his teacher had always said never to tell anyone he was his disciple — poverty could not change one's integrity, and one's profession could not be changed!

Li Wanzhi was being jostled so hard his bile was rising. The numbness in his limbs was fading, but his overall discomfort was only growing stronger. "Senior Brother, I think I can see mushrooms flying."

Fang He'an's head throbbed.

This one, of all things, had inhaled the most potent variety of Cyan Ink Poison. If the antidote had been even slightly delayed, he would have gone down. But the aftereffects were also severe.

"Just hold on. I'll clear the remaining poison for you in a bit."

"Oh, a mushroom flew into my mouth, Senior Brother, let me take a bite."

Fang He'an heard the sound and sensed something wrong. He spun around and raised his arm, catching two plum-blossom throwing darts — and one already halfway in Li Wanzhi's mouth.

Fang He'an: "..."

Li Wanzhi spat it out. "Too old — can't bite through."

Fang He'an had not even had time to check whether the darts were poisoned before the hesitation had already let two people catch up.

One came around from behind and swung at Li Wanzhi.

Li Wanzhi was still oblivious, not sensing the danger approaching at all.

Fang He'an saw this, shifted his stance, and used his own body to take the blow in Li Wanzhi's place. With that movement, his right side was completely open with no defence — one more hit and Fang He'an would be heavily injured for certain.

Not to mention attacks closing in from both left and right simultaneously.

At that precise moment, the golden core pressure on Fang He'an's body condensed into a technique, transforming into a burst of golden light that forced both attackers back.

It had only been around ten steps. But the Blood Rainbow Pavilion disciples' faces had already changed completely.

"Late-stage Golden Core!"

This young?

Fang He'an was barely past twenty. And the one he was carrying, Li Wanzhi, was eighteen or nineteen — yet both of them were already at the Golden Core stage.

And Fang He'an was at late-stage golden core!

By the normal pace of cultivation in the immortal cultivation world, breaking through to golden core before fifty was considered promising. Breaking through before forty was above average.

Breaking through before thirty was one in ten thousand.

As for the Junior Sister at Wushang Sect who had broken through at sixteen — that was once-in-a-generation rarity. And how did you tell a cultivator's age? Quite simply: upon breaking through golden core, a cultivator's lifespan extended to five hundred years, and their appearance could be completely fixed at the age they were at the time of breakthrough.

This meant whatever age you appeared to be when you broke through golden core was how old you looked — though one could also use a youth-restoring pill to change appearances, since such pills were precious and very few people actually spent the money.

So Fang He'an's young face had led them to assume at most Foundation Establishment late-stage. But now it was clear that neither he nor Li Wanzhi was simple at all.

Meanwhile, every single one of their opponents was in their mid-thirties.

That sting. And the envy.

Why were these two so gifted?

"We cannot let them get away."

Too excellent. All the more reason to eliminate them.

Only three Blood Rainbow Pavilion members remained standing. The other two lay poisoned behind them. A third now came forward with a bow on his back, eyes carrying nothing but cold killing intent.

He drew the bow.

Fang He'an stepped slowly backward. The hand he kept hidden at his side was dripping blood.

But he could not hide it — all of them were golden core cultivators. Blood dripping into the grass could not escape anyone's eyes.

The remaining three smirked. Blood arrows were already forming.

Fang He'an turned and ran.

"Restrain."

A wave of binding force fell over Fang He'an's body, slowing his steps. At this moment, if he abandoned Li Wanzhi, Fang He'an could still break through the binding and escape.

But Fang He'an did not.

"What deep brotherly loyalty!" one of the Blood Rainbow Pavilion disciples sneered. "Kill him. Blood Drink."

A blood arrow was released.

Fang He'an still did not let go of Li Wanzhi. The blood arrow hit him head-on, piercing his defences — but it did not strike him directly in the chest.

Because a spirit talisman, burning without flame, had transformed into a protective spirit mark and shielded both of them.

Fang He'an was startled.

So were the three opponents, halting for a fraction of a second.

The three of them sensed something was wrong and shouted: "All of you, together!"

But before the words had fully landed, two streaks of sword light came from above and from directly ahead — moving fast!

One carried the breath of a heavy brute-force sword.

The other was the Heart-Questioning Sword.

Both swords arrived together before Fang He'an, blocking the two ferocious blade energies. And two slender silhouettes appeared along with them.

chapters.title: I Don't Know How, But I Can Learn
chapters.content:
One in blue. One in white.

Arriving one after the other.

A young woman in blue robes, still carrying the freshness of youth, looked utterly without guile. Her thrown sword arrived carrying a faint fragrance, landing before Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi.

Just like that, without a second thought, she stood in front of them.

Her small face was drawn tight, expression very grave.

"Senior Sister."

Fang He'an was on the verge of tears.

The first to arrive was Bai Jian.

She had thrown her heavy sword forward first, then ran up behind it — while from another direction, the Heart-Questioning Sword arrived, and its owner followed in its wake, stepping through the air.

It was Junior Sister!

Blood Crow stared at these two new arrivals. One had an aura he could not read — clearly a cultivation level above his. The other... was at Qi Refining.

But what Qi Refining cultivator could walk through the air?

Ridiculous!

Yet when both young women's gazes swept over him, every hair on Blood Crow's body stood on end. Years of living on the edge of a blade had sharpened his instincts.

"Something is wrong."

Blood Crow called to Blood Drink and the third person and immediately ran. But Ye Wanwan and Bai Jian moved simultaneously.

Bai Jian's attacks were always direct and straightforward. She drew her heavy sword and made a single horizontal slash forward. The immense blade force from a golden core cultivator slammed all three of them heavily backward.

She was already in pursuit, locking on to the strongest of them — Blood Crow. Blood Drink and Blood Winter, feeling the weight of who they were up against, seized the opportunity and bolted.

Ye Wanwan gave a quiet laugh. "You hurt my Senior Brother. And you think you can just leave?"

She raised her hand and formed a seal. A formation array was projected outward. In moments, it had covered the entire area.

Blood Crow shouted, "Run!"

Blood Winter tried to break through. The formation force bounced him back. His face went pale. "A formation master!"

"Quite perceptive."

And in an instant, the young woman appeared before him.

Blood Winter's face went through a dramatic shift. He slammed out a palm, wanting to catch Ye Wanwan off guard and wound her while she was unguarded.

But the palm passed straight through.

A phantom.

"Blood Winter, Senior Brother! Behind you!"

Blood Drink's warning came loud and urgent.

Blood Winter turned. There was the young woman, standing in a thin mist. Her expression was one of utter indifference and dispassion. The sword in her hand was entirely unremarkable.

Her aura was nothing beyond the lowest level of Qi Refining.

And yet when the sword energy penetrated through his body, Blood Winter could not understand why. The Heart-Questioning Sword was embedded in his heart.

It was as though a voice was asking.

"What is the greatest regret of your life?"

Blood Winter opened his mouth. "My greatest regret is..."

That he never broke through to Nascent Soul. Never went home and told his parents that from now on, his entire clan had him to rely on.

Thud.

Blood Winter crumpled to the ground.

The sound drew the attention of Blood Drink and Blood Crow. Both men's eyes turned red. Blood Drink raised his bow. "Die! All of you die!"

But the one he was targeting was not Ye Wanwan.

It was Fang He'an.

Clearly he understood who in this group was the most exploitable.

Ye Wanwan swept her hand outward. The Heart-Questioning Sword split from one into a hundred, forming a circular net of blades that blocked the spiritually condensed blood arrows Blood Drink had launched.

Ye Wanwan herself stepped forward until she was face to face with Blood Drink. Seeing that the ambush had failed, Blood Drink shifted his target to her.

A blood arrow in the air split into eight.

Each aimed at a vital point on Ye Wanwan's body.

But the young woman's hand was like an impenetrable shield. She raised it with a light gathering motion and caught all eight blood arrows in her palm.

Then—

She crushed them.

Blood Drink's pupils contracted.

"What are you?"

Ye Wanwan raised her eyes. "The person who ends your life."

Blood Drink cried out and released a sky full of blood arrows — this time too rushed to use his spirit bow, instead drawing on the blood in his own body to condense a killing strike.

With his golden core cultivation level, unleashing his absolute strongest attack!

Enough to heavily wound a late-stage golden core cultivator!

"This is my own self-created killing technique. Dragon Emerges from the Deep. One final time — can you still dodge?"

By sacrificing his own blood, offering himself up to execute the most extraordinary technique and drag the enemy down with him — Blood Drink's expression carried pride and wild elation.

Especially when he saw the beast-shaped shadow formed from condensed blood droplets, the enormous blood dragon soaring toward the heavens, the golden core late-stage oppressive force crashing down!

The entire dense forest trembled.

He was proud of himself!

This was the strongest strike he, as a Blood Rainbow Pavilion genius, had ever created. Even his own master had been shaken by it, and praised it endlessly.

Right now, in this secret realm, before these sect geniuses, he would finally make a name for himself. Win this battle, and he — Blood Drink — would be renowned across the world.

He stared at Ye Wanwan.

Wanting to see amazement in her eyes, see confusion and panic.

But there was none.

The young woman looked at the wheeling blood dragon and seemed to be asking Blood Drink: "Is that it?"

Blood Drink's smile slowly disappeared.

Even Fang He'an nearby was puzzled. "What dragon? That's a blood dragon, not a Azure Dragon."

"..."

"And with that big a spectacle, how much attack force actually remains?"

Blood Drink turned furiously toward him. "What do you know?"

Ye Wanwan said flatly, "All show."

Her spiritual energy flowed through her fingers, slowly taking shape at her fingertips as a talisman pattern. The pattern gleamed brilliantly in the sunlight.

Smaller than the blood dragon in the sky. But far more striking.

The blood dragon's gaping maw unleashed a ten-thousand-piercing attack at her. The young woman's protective formation talisman stopped it completely — and she did not even show so much as a flicker of strain or exhaustion.

She simply stood there, effortless as a breeze.

Like a goddess looking down upon all creation.

Blood Drink completely broke. "Who... who are you?"

Ye Wanwan looked up without expression. "Tianyi Sect. Ye Wanwan."

Ye Wanwan — that name was strangely familiar. She had heard it somewhere before...

But Blood Crow's face had gone white. "Wushang Sect's Azure Cloud Peak — Ye Wanwan! The Dao Venerable Yan Ding's youngest disciple! The Ye Wanwan who broke through Core Formation at fifteen?!"

"Senior Brother, it was sixteen!"

Blood Crow's voice shook. "No — sixteen was the other one. She was the first."

Although Ye Qian had publicly allowed people to assume she was the one who had reached Core Formation at fifteen, among the elite disciples of the various sects, the name passed around as the first true genius was not hers.

It was Ye Wanwan.

"But you... aren't you..."

Dead?

How had she become a Tianyi Sect disciple?

Blood Crow wanted to ask, but the words would not come — because the young woman was frowning. "Are you asking too many questions?"

She turned the blood arrow back with a flick of her hand. The arrow pierced through Blood Drink's chest, and Ye Wanwan did not spare Blood Crow either.

Blood Crow cried out, "We won't tell anyone!"

But the young woman did not stop.

When the blood arrows had consumed both men, when both brothers' auras had faded from the dense forest, Ye Wanwan's voice came, quiet and unhurried.

"Only the dead can keep a secret."

She had not particularly cared about keeping it secret anyway — but they had hurt Third Senior Brother.

Blood Crow's eyes stayed open for a long time before they could close.

Ye Wanwan walked in the other direction.

Bai Jian and Fang He'an called out anxiously, "Where are you going?"

Ye Wanwan pointed ahead. "There are two more. Might as well deal with them all."

The two of them let out a breath of relief — they had genuinely been worried she would just walk off and not come back. Ye Wanwan went quickly and returned quickly.

She came back carrying two more bodies, and laid them out beside Blood Crow and the others.

Then, as though remembering something, she turned and looked at the three of them. "Do you know how to bury bodies?"

Fang He'an thought it over. "I don't — but I can learn."

Bai Jian nodded firmly.

Right!

Learn!

chapters.title: This Voice... Sounds Like Junior Sister
chapters.content:
Ye Wanwan brought Fang He'an and Bai Jian along to finish digging the hole together, burying all five of them. As for their qiankun pouches, she naturally collected every one.

Low-grade qiankun pouches had no owner seal.

Just open them and everything came out.

Ye Wanwan divided the contents into four shares — one per person — and even the still-murmuring Li Wanzhi got his portion.

The four of them, having dug a pit together, buried people together, and split the spoils together, seemed to have grown considerably closer. When their eyes met, Fang He'an broke into a broad, goofy smile.

Comparable to Li Wanzhi's current state.

Ye Wanwan reminded him. "Third Senior Brother, let's check on Senior Brother Li."

"Right, right — almost forgot."

Fang He'an quickly pulled out his medicine pouch and started compounding an antidote for Li Wanzhi. Li Wanzhi sat there cooperatively and let Fang He'an work.

Bai Jian and Ye Wanwan stood watch.

Ye Wanwan glanced at Li Wanzhi, gradually coming around, and at Fang He'an, focused on the medicine. She said to Bai Jian, "Senior Sister, wait here a moment."

"All right."

Ye Wanwan stepped onto her sword and flew into the depths. She circled around and came back with a handful of herbs. Fang He'an recognised them. "That's blood-staunching grass."

Ye Wanwan nodded.

She ground the blood-staunching grass into a paste. "Senior Brother."

Fang He'an made a sound of acknowledgment. "What is it?"

"Hand."

Fang He'an held out his hand in confusion, and Ye Wanwan gripped his forearm and pressed the herb paste over the wound on his right arm.

Fang He'an went briefly still.

The cool herbs brought sensation back to the numb wound — but it was not pain. It was an indescribable burning warmth.

"It... it's just a small wound."

Ye Wanwan: "Don't be careless."

Fang He'an nodded quickly.

Ye Wanwan put away the remaining blood-staunching grass. When Li Wanzhi came around, he asked blearily, "What happened to me just now?"

Ye Wanwan saw they were mostly recovered. She went straight to the point.

In a few short sentences, she relayed what had happened with the Ram's Head Valley collapse, and included Xingze's hypothesis, stated obliquely. The three listened for a while.

Li Wanzhi looked stunned. "Junior Sister means the secret realm is a trap? Someone deliberately drew everyone in here to catch all us talented youngsters in one net?"

He had just been drifting along in a dream, swimming through a sea of mushrooms. How had he woken up to consequences this serious?

Ye Wanwan: "Not necessarily. But there is definitely something wrong with the realm."

Fang He'an thought for a moment. "This is a serious matter and cannot be taken lightly. But Martial Uncle and Third Martial Uncle are both outside the realm. If something has truly gone wrong in here, they will certainly notice in advance."

Ye Wanwan nodded.

Fang He'an reassured everyone. "So we don't need to be too tense. If something seems off, the four of us will run first — we should have enough time. But from now on, we cannot separate."

Bai Jian and Li Wanzhi both nodded emphatically.

Ye Wanwan said, "The danger isn't what concerns me. But since we're already here, we can't let what's inside go to waste."

Three pairs of eyes lit up at once, all turning to Ye Wanwan.

It was about to collapse.

Which naturally meant — take whatever you can carry!

Ye Wanwan gave a low laugh. "Senior Brothers and Sister, how many storage pouches did you bring?"

Three hands shot out simultaneously.

Each wore a ring on one finger.

Ye Wanwan: "..."

"The Sect Leader borrowed these from Martial Uncle Pei before we set out, so that if we came across high-grade treasures, we'd have somewhere to put them."

"...Very good."

All Grade Three rings — each could hold several hundred cubic metres worth of contents.

Bai Jian said, "I brought you a lot of shiny stones."

"Oh right, I almost forgot," Fang He'an suddenly smacked his head. "Junior Sister, we just found a rainbow stone vein earlier. We were halfway through digging it out when people noticed us. They're all down there fighting over it now. We need to hurry."

Ye Wanwan: "No rush."

She spread out her map.

Fang He'an looked at it. "Junior Sister, your map has several more markers than ours."

Well, because she had threatened Xingze until it told her.

Ye Wanwan circled the nearest marker. "Is this the rainbow stone vein you're talking about?"

Fang He'an and Bai Jian could not place it immediately. Li Wanzhi called out, "Yes, that's it — shaped like a rooster, but the comb's been taken off by Senior Sister."

Bai Jian patted her ring. "It's in here."

Ye Wanwan smiled. "The most important rainbow stones have already been taken by Senior Sister. The rest aren't that significant."
