Ye Wanwan's finger moved, landing on a mountain peak. "We go here."

Cloud Mountain Cave.

No one questioned Ye Wanwan's suggestion in the slightest.

They put away the map, and Ye Wanwan and Bai Jian each took Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi and set off.

The young woman stepped onto her sword to fly, and suddenly — as though struck by a feeling — looked back.

Li Wanzhi asked, "What is it?"

Ye Wanwan thought for a moment. Since emerging from the valley, she had been feeling as though someone was following her. But the person had not shown themselves...

She would have to be more careful.

"Nothing. Hold on tight."

Ye Wanwan increased her speed and caught up with Bai Jian. The four of them stopped at the top of a mountain peak, where clouds and mist swirled. When the mist parted, there was an ancient cave dwelling.

Bai Jian and Fang He'an had arrived just before them.

In front of the cave dwelling, apart from the four of them, there was a crowd.

Ye Wanwan took a quick look. Seven or eight cultivators, all top practitioners from various sects, alert to the point of wariness — and among them, Ji Changhuai.

The group was clearly paying him a great deal of deference, with everyone naturally taking him as the leader without making it obvious.

Ye Wanwan considered: regardless of anything else, Ji Changhuai was Wushang Sect's Azure Cloud Peak's senior disciple, and by skill and ability, he was certainly qualified to lead a group and to be sought out by others.

Ye Wanwan stopped.

Li Wanzhi caught sight of Ji Changhuai and exhaled through his nose in contempt.

Ji Changhuai looked at a loss.

It seemed that from the very first time they had met, this group had shown strong hostility toward him.

"Junior Sister."

Fang He'an spoke up.

Ye Wanwan gave a small nod, signalling patience. She then brought Li Wanzhi back to the others at an unhurried pace. Cloud Mountain Cave had other visitors — Ye Wanwan was not surprised.

Good things in the secret realm were concentrated in only a few locations. Everyone converging here made perfect sense.

But then someone stepped forward from the other group, breaking the silence. "Fellow cultivators — are you also here to explore Cloud Mountain Cave?"

Fang He'an said, "No. We're here to move in for a few days."

The fellow cultivator who had spoken went blank. "What?"

Li Wanzhi curled one side of his mouth. "You asked a pointless question, so my Senior Brother gave you a joke answer."

A flicker of irritation crossed Li Yun's thoughts, though he kept it concealed. If he had not seen that these four were young but possessed notable cultivation levels, he would not have been so accommodating.

His tone stiffened considerably. He abandoned pleasantries entirely and went straight to the point. "We found this Cloud Mountain Cave first."

"So? Are you going to fight us for it?" Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi asked simultaneously.

Li Yun sneered. "First come, first served."

Ye Wanwan said flatly, "First come first served — I have no objection to that. But I would like to ask everyone: you've been here so long. Has this door opened yet?"

At those words, several faces in the group instantly went red. "You—!"

And then Ji Changhuai's head snapped toward Ye Wanwan. "This voice..."

chapters.title: I'll Wager With You
chapters.content:
Had he heard wrong?

The young woman's face was covered. Her build was slight, but she was a little taller than the person he knew. Her brows and eyes were colder, too — and the gaze she turned on people carried a detachment and indifference that he was not used to.

No.

This was absolutely not Seventh Junior Sister.

Seventh Junior Sister was gentle and sweet, her eyes always holding a soft smile. She was the most considerate and thoughtful disciple on Azure Cloud Peak. How could she possibly say something so sharp-tongued and provocative?

And yet Ji Changhuai found that he could not take his eyes off the young woman. She was genuinely... too similar.

"Master Ji is of course a direct disciple of Azure Cloud Peak's master, most well-versed in the ways of formations and seals. The seal on this door is precisely what we invited him here to break."

Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi both looked toward Ji Changhuai simultaneously.

And exhaled loudly through their noses.

"So impressive!"

It was common knowledge that the Dao Venerable Yan Ding of Azure Cloud Peak had two areas of supreme mastery: formation arts, and sword arts — unmatched in both sword and formation, strong enough at the Spirit Transformation stage to challenge a Void Refinement cultivator on even footing.

Naturally, his disciples would also have inherited his formation arts and mastery of seals.

Li Yun had found the right person to ask.

Ji Changhuai was indeed the most gifted in formation arts among Yan Ding's seven disciples. Of course — aside from Ye Wanwan.

Ye Wanwan looked at Ji Changhuai with something between a smile and none at all. "So Wushang Sect also wants the treasures inside Cloud Mountain Cave?"

Ji Changhuai felt that needle-like remark land somewhere unpleasant. "There is a Wood-Fire Spirit inside. I want to retrieve it for my Junior Sister."

"This is what we agreed upon." He said this last part to Li Yun.

Li Yun quickly replied, "Of course. Whatever Master Ji wishes to take, we will certainly not stand in his way."

Ye Wanwan let out a short laugh. "If I recall correctly, your Peak's Junior Sister cultivates a water spiritual root. What do you need a Wood-Fire Spirit for?"

Ji Changhuai's expression darkened. He stepped forward and released his pressure, sending it directly at Ye Wanwan. "What I want is my business. Does it require an explanation to you?"

Ye Wanwan did not answer. But Bai Jian had already stepped in front of her.

Their auras clashed.

But Ji Changhuai did not back down. His gaze pressed downward, his presence fully unleashed — and it sent a terrifying pang through everyone's chest!

"Golden Core Great Completion!"

Only a hair's breadth from Nascent Soul.

No — perhaps Ji Changhuai had already comprehended Nascent Soul, and was deliberately suppressing his cultivation to search for treasures for Ye Qian.

Sensing Ji Changhuai's power, Li Yun and the others felt both alarm and elation — alarm at Ji Changhuai, who was probably the strongest person who had entered the realm in this entire group, and relief that they had not offended someone this powerful. But Ye Wanwan's group, on the other hand...

"I saw their elders last night — they appear to be from Tianyi Sect."

"Tianyi Sect? That former top-three sect that hasn't participated in a sect competition for a hundred years and has been delisted?"

"That would be them."

"Some say their sect collapsed long ago. These few seem to have been taken in fairly recently. Nothing much to them."

No one dared follow up on the last part. Nothing much to them? Nothing much to them — and yet one of them was matching auras head-on against Ji Changhuai?

Bai Jian was late-stage golden core — only somewhat below Ji Changhuai.

Bai Jian furrowed her brow, her palm shifting, wanting to summon her sword and strike. But a hand settled on her shoulder, and Ye Wanwan said quietly, "Senior Sister, I'm fine."

Ye Wanwan looked up and met Ji Changhuai's gaze, undaunted. "Since we both want the Wood-Fire Spirit, let everyone rely on their own abilities."

Ji Changhuai said with contempt, "You wish to fight me?"

Ye Wanwan's expression did not change. "No need for a fight. There is a seal on this door. Whoever breaks through it in the least amount of time gets the Wood-Fire Spirit."

Ji Changhuai felt even more like laughing. "You want to compete with me in formation arts?"

"Yes — shamelessly wishing to request a lesson from Senior Brother Ji." Ye Wanwan's eyes were serene. "Do you dare agree?"

Ji Changhuai frowned.

He had originally been searching for Ye Qian and Dou Ming, and was invited along by Li Yun midway. Thinking about the unique properties of the Wood-Fire Spirit and how it might be useful for Seventh Junior Sister, he had come along to retrieve it.

He had not expected to run into this presumptuous young woman.

Ye Wanwan's golden core had been dug out. Her cultivation path would certainly be difficult going forward. But with a Wood-Fire Spirit, she could still become an alchemist.

Who could have known she would encounter someone this overconfident?

In Ji Changhuai's memory, he had always refused to believe that Ye Wanwan had died — had died because she lost faith in all of them and thrown herself from a cliff. He only believed that as long as he paved every road smooth for her, his Junior Sister would certainly come back. She definitely would.

"Fine. I accept."

"Agreed."

Li Yun suddenly had an idea and cut in. "Just a wager like this seems like the stakes aren't high enough. After all, the Wood-Fire Spirit was already going to be Master Ji's regardless of whether any of you came. But now, because of you, Master Ji still has to spend time competing alongside you. Shouldn't you show a bit of good faith?"

In between his words, he shifted from addressing Ji Changhuai as "Master Ji" to "Senior Brother Ji" — subtly closing the gap between them.

Ji Changhuai did not object.

He also wanted to see what this young woman would bring out.

The Ziyun ring had no shortage of things inside, but to produce something capable of moving Ji Changhuai — none of those could be brought out.

Because the moment she did, they would deduce that she had already been to the Ram's Head Valley first.

A thought suddenly came to her, and Ye Wanwan turned her hand over to reveal it.

The onlookers were preparing to snicker before they even looked clearly. "You think you can exchange these Grade Three spirit herbs for the Wood-Fire Spirit that every alchemist wants? You're dreaming."

In Ye Wanwan's hand was a Jade Dew Flower.

Its effect was to nourish and refine a golden core. Appropriate for cultivators with an unstable golden core, but naturally useless for Ji Changhuai who had already reached late-stage golden core.

But for Ye Qian, it was useful.

Ye Qian was using Ye Wanwan's golden core — a forced spiritual transfer, with no small impact on her. Even with all the rare materials the Ye family and Azure Cloud Peak had used to stabilise it, there would still be moments of stagnation during cultivation.

This Jade Dew Flower, once refined, could be made into Jade Dew Pills — taken regularly to nourish and stabilise the golden core.

Precisely the right remedy.

And so, regardless of what Li Yun and the others were saying, Ji Changhuai's eyes had already fixed on the Jade Dew Flower, carrying surprise and a quiet certainty of intent.

Ye Wanwan's eyes held contempt. She had known.

The moment it was about Ye Qian, Ji Changhuai lost every trace of the intelligence he otherwise possessed.

"Well? Is this Jade Dew Flower acceptable to Senior Brother Ji?"

"It is."

With the agreement secured, Ye Wanwan put it away. "Who goes first?"

Ji Changhuai said coolly, "You just arrived. You go first."

Ye Wanwan gave him a light, amused look. "Senior Brother Ji, if I go first, and I open the door first — how exactly would that be counted?"

The onlookers burst out laughing. "She's guarded against someone opening it on her first turn? You've been standing here three days and none of us could budge this thing, and you — one little Qi Refining girl — are going to talk big like that?"

"First time out in the world, is it? Must think it's still that tiny backwater Tianyi Sect."

Ye Wanwan ignored the laughter around her and only looked toward Ji Changhuai.

Ji Changhuai said flatly, "There are three layers of seals here. You break the first. I break the second. Whoever does it the fastest gets to break the third. At that point, they may choose whatever they wish from inside — and no one may object."

"Agreed."

Ye Wanwan said this and walked toward Cloud Mountain Cave.

Li Yun and his people were full of mockery. "Disgracing herself. If I were her Senior Brother, I'd pull her down from there instead of letting her parade her limited skills in front of everyone."

chapters.title: Ji Changhuai, Formation Arts Prodigy
chapters.content:
Fang He'an and the others heard the remark aimed squarely at them. Li Wanzhi spat, "You don't have the qualifications to be her Senior Brother."

Thinking about being Junior Sister's Senior Brother?

Worthy of it?

"All of you combined aren't worth a single hair on Junior Sister's head." Li Wanzhi sneered.

Li Yun's expression turned angry. Was that what they meant? They had been commenting on Ye Wanwan overreaching herself — who was talking about wanting to be her Senior Brother?

But ultimately they were wary of their cultivation levels. Li Yun threw out a cold parting remark and let it go. "Ridiculous lot."

Li Wanzhi very much wanted to throw a punch. But he watched Bai Jian and Fang He'an both standing there without moving, and could only follow suit, grinding his teeth as he asked, "How can the two of you stand this?"

"Can't stand it, but have to." Fang He'an lowered his voice. "We can't ruin Junior Sister's business."

Li Wanzhi heard this and looked toward Ye Wanwan at the door. True — if a conflict broke out between the two groups right now and a fight started, it would only delay things.

And they knew perfectly well that Ye Wanwan was racing against time to gather as much of the realm's resources as possible. If they could not get what was in Cloud Mountain Cave, they had more places to be.

There truly was no time to waste on these people.

Endure it.

Li Wanzhi exhaled sharply. Even if he would not start a fight, he would not lose the verbal battle. "I understand — you're all just jealous."

"Don't push your luck."

"We're already pushing it — come and do something about it."

"You little—!"

Li Yun held people back. "Don't let them distract us. She is right here — whether she can break the seal or not, we'll know soon. Some people are just waiting to make fools of themselves."

"Exactly!" Everyone raised their voices. "We want to see how a little Qi Refining girl is going to break a high-grade seal. Don't get yourself reflected and severely injured — might even lose your life."

"What's the use of running your mouth? Show some real skill — bring out your real abilities!"

"Come on then — a group that has to bring in outside help, and you dare mock us? Cowards. Go ahead and try it yourselves if you've got the nerve. What right does someone who doesn't even know which side the seal's left edge is on have to mock anyone?"

"Losers." Li Wanzhi gestured rudely.

Both sides erupted into argument. Li Wanzhi alone took on the whole group in a war of words and did not falter in the slightest.

Fang He'an and Bai Jian listened with their eyes going glassy, raising their hands to applaud.

"Well said."

No wonder it was Junior Brother Li.

The two sides clashed and argued until their faces were red.

But Ji Changhuai paid no attention to any of it. His focus was entirely on Ye Wanwan alone. The young woman had been standing at the cave entrance for a moment without moving.

Ji Changhuai said coldly, "If you cannot break it, you may concede."

Ye Wanwan glanced at Ji Changhuai, then raised her hand and pressed it to the cave entrance.

Li Yun cried out sharply, "Stop! That's a killing formation!"

Others screamed, "Get back!"

Li Yun and five others mounted their swords and ran. But Ji Changhuai and Li Wanzhi's group stood exactly where they were.

And in front of Ye Wanwan, a red formation array had indeed sprung out — a Grade Three annihilation formation. But at this moment, the formation had not fully expanded.

Instead it looked like a smooth sphere, trapped between the young woman's palms.

Those countless flowing talisman patterns — like fish darting in a lake — began to separate and dissolve under the movement of the young woman's fingertips. The Grade Three annihilation formation that had been holding all of Li Yun's group at bay dissolved quietly in her hands.

By the time the last trace of light scattered away, no one had processed what had happened.

"Is it... is it broken?"

How long had that taken?

Everyone stared at each other.

"Impossible. Let me check."

Someone who did not believe it stepped forward. They started by testing with a sword. The cave entrance did not react.

When they walked up themselves, pacing back and forth in front of the cave entrance, and even used brute force against the cave door — all they received was a rebound deflection. The killing intent from before was completely gone.

Li Yun stood speechless. "What kind of technique is that?"

"Is that how formations are broken?"

The normal method of cracking a formation involved allowing the formation to fully activate, manoeuvring within it to find its weaknesses, and then seizing the opening. A technique like hers — pulling the talisman patterns out of the formation and holding them in one's palms to dissolve them by hand — looked positively casual.

"Wait, I think I understand. Just now Senior Brother Ji said there are three seal layers total, and this first layer is certainly the simplest. Senior Brother Ji was being magnanimous in letting her go first."

"A small seal like that, she obviously could manage."

"Exactly!"

Li Wanzhi, still in a state of some shock himself, immediately latched on when he heard this. "Look in a mirror before you say that. Are you not ashamed of yourselves?"

"A seal that you've been standing here for days and couldn't break — my Junior Sister broke it at Qi Refining stage — and you not only refuse to admit your own weakness, you refuse to acknowledge someone else's strength?"

Li Yun's group refused to acknowledge it.

It must have been a lucky fluke.

"Chances are we'd already weakened the formation by hammering at it for so long, and now the thing was just barely holding on. Your Junior Sister just got lucky and cleaned up the scraps. What is there to be proud of?"

Everyone nodded vigorously in agreement.

Li Wanzhi: "..."

Ye Wanwan paid no attention to the others. She only looked toward Ji Changhuai. Unlike the rest of them scrambling to salvage their dignity, Ji Changhuai had not said a single word.

"Well?"

Ji Changhuai said coldly, "I underestimated you."

Ye Wanwan curved her lips. "You are indeed arrogant."

Li Yun and the others flared up. "What are you being so cocky about!"

Ji Changhuai extended a hand to hold them back. He stepped forward. "But I have not conceded."

He raised his hand and struck the cave entrance. The second-layer seal sprang outward and pushed his force back hard, but Ji Changhuai met it with a counter-press, threading a thread of spiritual energy into the seal.

It activated the entire formation array.

A rush of sound.

Blue-white talisman patterns materialised.

Every pair of eyes went still.

Ji Changhuai's bearing was composed and unhurried.

Li Wanzhi looked at that confident air and had a quiet exchange with Fang He'an beside him. "This one looks easier than Junior Sister's, doesn't it?"

Li Wanzhi's original intent was to rebut those people — to argue that Ji Changhuai had not been lenient at all, that he had kept the easiest layer for himself. Just look at that composed manner.

Scheming.

But Fang He'an shook his head. "No."

Li Wanzhi glared at him. "Why are you boosting his confidence and undermining ours? Though actually — if it's hard, then he's destined to lose." Li Wanzhi quickly consoled himself and broke into a goofy grin.

Fang He'an's mouth twitched.

"The three seals of a cave dwelling formation are generally stacked in difficulty at a ratio of three-three-four, and because of the seal's special nature they can persist even longer than formation arrays. What they test a formation breaker on is those talisman patterns."

Fang He'an explained, pointing to the blue patterns before Ji Changhuai. "Those are the key to the seal. It is said they are also simplified versions of the rules of heaven and earth — though that is just a rumour."

"Only by comprehending these seal talisman patterns can one break through. The layer he is facing is the same difficulty as the killing seal Junior Sister broke — both Grade Three."

"However, his is a Ward seal."

"In general, a Ward seal is more complex than a Kill seal. The time needed to break through is correspondingly longer. So even though they are the same difficulty, his will take more time than Junior Sister's did."

Fang He'an paused, then said, "He probably thought that since Junior Sister's cultivation level was low, letting her go first was giving her a head start."

Then added with irritation, "Or he figured Junior Sister couldn't break it at all, so he let her go first, only to have the stone he picked up drop on his own foot."

The three of them looked at each other and nodded in unison. "Right."

Either way, people from Wushang Sect were never a good sort.

That was a shared understanding among their group.

Li Yun and his people were already anxious. "Senior Brother Ji isn't actually going to lose, is he?"

This one looked considerably more complicated than the last.

chapters.title: He Would Not Concede!
chapters.content:
Even as everyone told themselves that Ji Changhuai, as the Dao Venerable Yan Ding's direct disciple, could not possibly lose to an unknown young woman — the method Ye Wanwan had used to break the seal was entirely unlike anything they had seen before.

None of them had ever seen anyone hold talisman patterns in their palms like that.

Not even Fang He'an. But all four of them had a quiet understanding about not revealing their full abilities, which was precisely why Fang He'an would not say aloud that he could not understand how his Junior Sister had broken it.

Let them guess.

So now Li Yun's group could not make up their minds either.

Someone was frustrated. "Senior Brother Ji was just too much of a gentleman. Why did he let that young woman go first? If he had gone first, none of this would be an issue."

Though none of the others said it, they all felt the same.

Ye Wanwan watched on without expression.

She did not think Ji Changhuai would lose. His formation arts had been personally taught by Yan Ding. A mere Grade Three seal — if that could give him trouble, he would not be Ji Changhuai.

But in no time at all, the seal dissolved.

Everyone heard the cave door give a click.

Li Yun's group was overjoyed!

"It opened!"

They were ecstatic, practically wanting to rush over to Li Wanzhi and celebrate in his face.

But Ji Changhuai's first instinct was to turn toward Ye Wanwan, as though seeking approval. The exhilaration of having just cracked the formation was still visible on his face, and without thinking he blurted out, "Junior Sister, did you see—"

But the next instant, he met Ye Wanwan's eyes.

And the sudden quiet that had fallen all around.

Ji Changhuai snapped back to himself.

Right — she was not his Junior Sister.

Li Wanzhi and Fang He'an both immediately stepped in front of Ye Wanwan. "What do you mean by that? Are you trying to poach our Junior Sister?"

Li Wanzhi raised his voice. "I said it before — not just anyone qualifies to be her Senior Brother."

Li Yun's group went pale with anger.

"Senior Brother Ji only mistook someone else from Wushang Sect's Junior Sister Ye for being here — do you really think he was calling your little nobody? Their Junior Sister Ye reached Core Formation at fifteen. Yours..."

"Tsk tsk tsk tsk..."

That unutterably expressive face, making everyone furious.

Li Wanzhi gritted his teeth. Endure...

He would endure!

No, he could not.

Before he could, a white figure shot out beside him. Bai Jian launched a single punch that sent the person sailing off the cliff edge. If they had not summoned their sword in time, they might have been killed by the fall.

Bai Jian: "Shut up."

Everyone went silent.

Late-stage golden core.

Right, forget it. We cannot fight them.

Ye Wanwan gave a quiet laugh. "Senior Sister, don't waste your anger on them. A bunch of second-generation nobodies — I don't even look at them. Master Ji — shall we begin?"

Ye Wanwan turned to Ji Changhuai.

She was well aware of Ji Changhuai's confusion. And she was aware of his loss. Before Ye Qian's arrival, it had been her who accompanied Ji Changhuai through those long, gruelling years of comprehension.

It had been her who stayed by Ji Changhuai's side as he pushed through Yan Ding's relentless trials.

It had been her who encouraged this elder-brother-and-father figure through his time of uncertainty, and who ultimately stepped into the formation herself to help him break through.

She had been like Ji Changhuai's devoted admirer, looking up at him as he became Azure Cloud Peak's number one prodigy in formation arts, a rising star in the cultivation world, and someone everyone believed would be Azure Cloud Peak's successor.

But it was also he who, with one hand, had pushed her into the abyss.

Ten years.

This body was only seventeen now. Not counting the previous life, nearly two-thirds of its existence had been spent at Wushang Sect. How much she had come to depend on them.

The more she had, the deeper the wound when it was finally inflicted.

And the more desperate the despair.

Ji Changhuai came back to himself. Out of awkwardness, his voice came out stiff. "The time I took and your time were comparable. There is no way to determine who won."

"Then what do we do?" Li Yun's group started to worry.

Ji Changhuai looked at Ye Wanwan. "So I have a proposal. You and I break the third seal together."

"Absolutely not!"

Li Wanzhi and Fang He'an spoke in unison.

Even Bai Jian turned to look sharply, watching Ji Changhuai like a hawk guarding against a thief, making sure to keep Ye Wanwan firmly behind her — as though deeply concerned that Ji Changhuai was about to steal the person away.

Ji Changhuai frowned.

The way these people were acting...

Something very strange.

Li Yun's group sneered. "Senior Brother Ji himself hasn't said no — what right do you lot have to speak?"

Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi kept their faces dark.

They had absolutely no interest in Ji Changhuai spending any time alone with Junior Sister.

Ye Wanwan watched everyone's reactions, stunned beyond words — but once she understood, a feeling stirred in her that she could not quite name, somewhere between helplessness and a warmth she had not felt in a very long time.

She reassured them. "Senior Sister, since Master Ji has proposed this, we may as well hear out his terms. How would the things inside be divided after we break the third seal?"

Ji Changhuai kept his lips pressed together. "Proportional to each of our contributions during the break."

"So Master Ji wants me to compete with you over contributions while breaking the seal at the same time?"

Ji Changhuai's expression went cool. This person was absolutely not his Junior Sister. His Junior Sister would never be this unreasonable. "I am not the kind of person who schemes in the shadows."

"Fine."

Ye Wanwan said flatly, "I don't want to waste time either. We go in together. Whoever breaks through it first takes the lead. Whoever opens it, it's theirs."

"Your meaning..." Ji Changhuai furrowed his brow. This was not a collaborative arrangement.

"Each works independently."

Ye Wanwan said this and stepped forward first.

Ji Changhuai's expression shifted. He immediately moved to intercept her, extending his hand — his intention being to tell this young woman who had no idea of the odds that the third-layer seal was no simple thing.

But Ye Wanwan reacted with lightning speed and brushed his hand aside, eyes cold. "Don't touch me."

Ji Changhuai's hand hung in the air, his eyes carrying anger. "You—"

"Fine! Everyone on their own merits!"

Ji Changhuai said this, then moved to take the first step.

Ye Wanwan's eyes deepened. She matched his pace — but Ji Changhuai turned to block her. Ye Wanwan sidestepped, and without pausing, slapped a palm water arrow technique directly into the cave entrance.

The third-layer seal was triggered.

The entire formation array expanded outward!

Spreading across the entire mountain cliff.

Ji Changhuai's expression went dark. "You really don't care about anyone else as long as you can win."

Ye Wanwan: "Same goes for you."

With the seal activated, this Grade Four difficulty was far beyond the single-attribute Grade Three seal — fire surged in from both sides and Li Yun's group were screaming.

"Run your qi and defend!"

But Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi had already obediently ducked behind Bai Jian, using her spiritual energy as a shield against the fire.

"Senior Sister really is the best."

Ji Changhuai stared at Ye Wanwan. The two of them were at the centre of the seal's activation, engulfed by flames — but neither retreated. The key to breaking this seal was at the entrance itself.

There was only one chance. Whoever yielded would lose.

Ji Changhuai threw a punch. Ye Wanwan reached back and caught it. The two of them exchanged over ten moves in the doorway, all footwork and technique. Ji Changhuai could not believe it no matter how he tried — this Qi Refining cultivator was holding her own against that many of his strikes.

"You are hiding your cultivation level?"

Ye Wanwan said coldly, "What of it if I am? What of it if I'm not?"

Ji Changhuai condensed his spiritual energy and sent a sweeping, crushing wave of pressure straight at Ye Wanwan. She was struck and sent flying back. Ji Changhuai did not look back — he went straight for the beast head at the cave entrance and poured spiritual energy into it!

But Ye Wanwan had already launched a spirit talisman.

"Bind!"

In an instant, the talisman patterns wrapped around Ji Changhuai's wrist. The young woman's toe struck the ground and she shot forward like a swallow skimming water, reaching the beast head before Ji Changhuai and pressing her hand down on it with force.

Spiritual energy poured in!

A cascade of water rushed down from above.

Li Yun and the others screamed. "Now what is this?!"

First fire, now water — what is happening?!

But Ye Wanwan had already turned the beast head, and the second mechanism behind the cave door clicked open. The door swung inward before the two of them. Without another word, Ye Wanwan ducked inside.

Ji Changhuai roared. "You dare!"

Ye Wanwan laughed coldly. "You said it yourself — everyone on their own merits."

But Ji Changhuai was not willing to accept this. He refused to lose to this young woman whose name he did not even know!

In moments, he followed her inside.

But behind Ji Changhuai, another shadow also turned into a streak of light and slipped through. Not a single person saw it — only Bai Jian caught it.

"That looked like..."

Fifth Junior Brother?

chapters.title: The Treasure Room
chapters.content:
Inside Cloud Mountain Cave, everything was pitch black.

Not a trace of light.

Entering first was a long passageway.

The moment Ji Changhuai was inside, he followed Ye Wanwan's trail. He moved quickly and grabbed her shoulder, intending to slow her down.

But Ye Wanwan stepped aside as though she had seen this coming all along and avoided him. She turned back and the two of them traded blows inside the corridor.

The sounds of impact rang back and forth — neither yielding an inch to the other.

Their footwork was actually quite evenly matched.

Even Ji Changhuai was mildly surprised. Remarkable technique.

But Ji Changhuai was two full cultivation stages above Ye Wanwan, and the moment he used even a touch of spiritual energy, he could control her easily. His elbow pressed against her shoulder.

One restraint — and he slammed her hard into the stone wall.

A thud.

Rock fragments crumbled and fell. There was a muffled sound of impact, and the young woman's shoulder struck the stone wall — yet she had done it using the strength of her physical body alone, no spiritual energy defensive layer at all, and still cracked the stone.

Ji Changhuai paused briefly.

But seeing that her eyes still held nothing but refusal to give in, Ji Changhuai felt his own frustration rise. He said coldly, "I was going easy on you because of your age, and yet you show no appreciation."

Said she was coming in. Then came right in.

Said she would fight. Then fought.

Ye Wanwan gave a quiet sneer, her gaze mocking. "The great Senior Brother of Azure Cloud Peak going back on his word — that makes you a gentleman?"

Ji Changhuai was incensed. "I never said I wouldn't give you the Wood-Fire Spirit."

Ye Wanwan looked up directly at Ji Changhuai and said with cold clarity, "Then get out."

Ji Changhuai's hand tightened. These eyes were too bright, the brows and face too clean and clear. She looked so very much like that person — one movement of his hand was all it would take to pull away the veil.

And see her true face.

But the young woman had just used a water-element technique. His Junior Sister had a fire spiritual root and should not be able to.

Ye Wanwan observed his expression carefully, watching every shift in his thoughts with complete clarity.

She gave nothing away. She was waiting for the right moment.

Ji Changhuai's frustration broke through. "You are so young and already so arrogant! Has your teacher not taught you the basics of propriety? I am your elder — I should go first."

Ye Wanwan let out a short laugh.

Ji Changhuai raised his voice. "Fine! Let me teach you, in your teacher's stead, what shame is!"

"Idiot."

Ji Changhuai: "What?"

But Ye Wanwan had already twisted free in a single motion and pushed him aside. She stepped back several paces, putting distance between them. Ji Changhuai's eyes went dark, and a bright flame ignited in his palm.

Ye Wanwan laughed.

"Why are you laughing."

Ji Changhuai's words were barely out before he felt something was wrong. In the air around him, something seemed to be clinging to him. Ji Changhuai tried to move forward, but his meridians ached.

Even his movement had begun to tremble.

His expression changed. He watched with his own eyes as the flame in his palm was wound shut by invisible threads and extinguished with a crackle.

"Spirit-Binding Thread."

He looked around the corridor. "You cannot use spiritual energy in here!"

No wonder — when she had hit the stone wall, she had not used any spiritual energy at all.

Ye Wanwan laughed. "The proud Senior Brother of Azure Cloud Peak, and you did not even notice a trap like this. Truly the height of arrogance."

"How did you notice?" Ji Changhuai said sharply.

They had entered at the same time. How had Ye Wanwan noticed?

Ye Wanwan turned and walked away.

Why should she tell him?

She ran into the depths of the corridor, communicating with Xingze inside the Ziyun ring as she went. Xingze told her, "There are two more seal layers inside this cave dwelling. The first is a spirit-binding."

"Aside from not using spiritual energy, also do not run any cultivation techniques."

"The stronger your power, the higher the restriction imposed."

"Just walk straight forward and you will leave the spirit-binding range."

Ye Wanwan complied and ran straight ahead. In a little over a quarter of an hour, she had left the binding force behind.

But ahead was also a three-way fork.

"Which path?"

Xingze sat in the tree and looked toward the fork. "Pick any one."

"That old man" — the realm's former owner — "liked playing treasure-hunting games. Each path leads to something at its end. Even if you don't find the Wood-Fire Spirit you're looking for, you'll find other things."

Ye Wanwan said, "I want them all."

Xingze: "...Greedy."

Ye Wanwan chose a path first. "Greed is human nature. Since I'm already here, why should I leave anything behind for others?"

But she had no time to waste on deliberating. Even as she spoke to Xingze, she was already moving toward the first fork.

She went smoothly all the way to the end.

A stone room.

There was still a seal on the door.

Xingze said, "This again — it's a four-layer seal. If you want to break through, it could take an hour or two. And by then, that one from the corridor will have caught up."

Ye Wanwan said, "It won't take that long."

She reached into her pouch and produced a talisman.

Xingze: "..."

It might not know talismans, but it knew the character for "explosion."

Ye Wanwan pressed the talisman against the door, poured in spiritual energy, and the talisman paper began to flash with light. She turned and ran immediately.

Xingze's voice shook. "You're using an explosive release talisman on a four-layer seal — that's throwing an egg at a boulder! A restriction this powerful can't just be blown open by brute force. If anything, your force will trigger its strongest response and activate it fully!"

Ye Wanwan said, "I know."

Xingze: "?"

Then why are you doing it?!

Boom!

When the massive explosion rang out from the first fork, the entire Cloud Mountain Cave — and the cliff face itself — shook. Everyone was startled, and even Ji Changhuai's expression changed.

"What is she doing!"

Xingze stared blankly as the young woman who had been hiding in a crevice of the stone wall emerged. Ye Wanwan walked out, looked at the blown-open stone door, and then at the formation patterns still moving across it.

The door was open, but the seal was still active.

Ye Wanwan: "I can't go in, but you can."

Xingze: !!!

Ye Wanwan pointed at the doorway. "Go."

Xingze made sounds of protest. "Who said I could — I never said that."

Ye Wanwan picked up a rock. "Trees can move, rocks can move too."

Xingze went quiet.

Ye Wanwan smiled. "Coming?"

"..."

The palm-sized black rock sprouted two tiny legs, its expression indignant and aggrieved. "I am the great inhabiting spirit of a secret realm..."

Ye Wanwan pointed at the stone door.

"Don't waste time."

Xingze could only stand. "Throw me in — quickly."

"All right."

Ye Wanwan held the stone in her palm and tossed it through. The seal only reacted to living things, but whether it would trigger aggression toward a parasitic spirit like Xingze — Ye Wanwan genuinely did not know.

But between letting herself take the risk and letting Xingze take it, having Xingze go first was clearly the safer option.

She aimed the stone carefully through the opening and into the stone room.

Ye Wanwan asked, "Did you make it in?"

Xingze's excited voice rang out. "Made it in! This is the old man's treasure room — you chose the right path!"

She had walked directly into the treasure room on the very first try!

Ye Wanwan lowered her voice. "Is there a Wood-Fire Spirit?"

Xingze muttered, "Wood-Fire Spirit isn't exactly a rare thing, what do you want this for anyway?"

Ye Wanwan, leaving no room for refusal: "Look for it."

chapters.title: It Has Developed Its Own Awareness
chapters.content:
A Wood-Fire Spirit was truly not a particularly rare thing.

But for alchemists, it was useful.

For those with cold afflictions, it was also an excellent spirit medicine.

And the higher the grade, the better the effect.

Ye Wanwan had not held overly high expectations for whatever treasures the Dream Illusion Xingze might contain.

But when Xingze mentioned that Cloud Mountain Cave had a Grade Five Wood-Fire Spirit, she had come regardless.

The image of the man always sitting on the snow mountain stone platform in cultivation floated through her mind. Ye Wanwan thought: she really ought to bring some kind of gift for this teacher she had acquired so conveniently.

"Found it!" Xingze's voice came, bright and eager.

Ye Wanwan nearly stepped into the seal at the sound — fortunately reason stopped her. She asked, "Where?"

"Found a Grade Two Wood-Fire Spirit."

Ye Wanwan's brow furrowed. "Grade Two? I thought it was Grade Five?"

"It is Grade Two. There are also some cloud pearls and spirit shells, as well as some refining materials."

Xingze — a small black stone — stretched out two tiny arms and held out a lacquered box larger than its own body, asking Ye Wanwan through the seal. "Do you want it?"

Ye Wanwan did not hesitate. "Yes."

"Which parts?"

"All of it."

Ye Wanwan said calmly, "You are now the Ziyun ring's inhabiting spirit. You should be able to open up an access point and take everything in, shouldn't you?"

Xingze and Ye Wanwan stared at each other.

"Right!"

"How did I forget about that!"

Without delay, Xingze expanded its body. A vortex formed at the stone's centre, and in moments, every last treasure had been absorbed into the Ziyun ring.

It then turned and walked quickly toward the exit.

But when it touched the seal, it was violently bounced back.

Xingze cried out, "This is bad!"

"Something in the treasure room triggered the seal. I can't get out!"

But a hand reached into the seal's talisman patterns, grabbed the stone, and pulled it free. At the same moment, the seal roared and expanded, a devastating force of destruction surging toward Ye Wanwan.

Intent on obliterating her.

But Ye Wanwan did not pause at all. She entered the Ziyun ring. The Ziyun ring transformed into a speck of dust and fell to the ground, blown far away by the storm.

The person and stone inside the Ziyun ring, caught in the edge of the blast, were both badly shaken.

Xingze looked at Ye Wanwan.

Her left hand was covered in blood.

There were talisman patterns drawn on it — clearly, at the critical moment, she had used herself as a vessel for the formation, reaching in to grab it and pull it out. Xingze felt a little awkward. "Are you all right?"

Ye Wanwan wiped her wound with a cloth. "Fine."

She said it as though it had been nothing at all.

Xingze found itself wondering: she was so young — how had she ended up with such an old-soul, calculating manner? She hardly ever smiled.

Though to be fair, every time Ye Wanwan did smile, it always seemed to happen right when she was calculating something at someone's expense.

Sigh.

Outside, the commotion was enormous. Ye Wanwan did not rush out immediately. While resting inside the Ziyun ring, she did a rough survey of the treasures Xingze had brought in. There was a fair amount of it, but Ye Wanwan's focus went straight to the Wood-Fire Spirit.

Indeed Grade Two.

"There should still be a Grade Five one somewhere." Xingze said.

Ye Wanwan murmured, "I'll check the second path next."

Once the storm outside had subsided for a while, Ye Wanwan exited the Ziyun ring. The ring settled back on her finger, with Xingze also coming along.

A small black stone perched on her shoulder.

"Completely destroyed."

The stone room ahead had been entirely demolished.

So her shortcut method had angered the local master. The seal had fully activated, and everything was obliterated.

Ye Wanwan thought it over. "I'll need a different approach next time."

Xingze nodded. "Definitely."

The two of them retraced their path back, and Ye Wanwan stood at the junction between the second and third forks. Without hesitation, she chose the second. But compared to the first, the terrain of this second path was far more complex.

It was a circular corridor.

Ye Wanwan walked for a while, then stopped.

Xingze said, "We've looped back to the start."

Ye Wanwan lowered her eyes, gaze flickering. "When we entered from the fork, there was only one path going straight ahead. There were no additional forks anywhere along the way. So how have we looped back?"

Xingze rocked its feet. "That is a good point."

Ye Wanwan said nothing.

She simply walked forward again.

This time she walked every step slowly and carefully, feeling the subtle changes in spiritual energy beneath each footfall. She noted every tiny detail.

Xingze tilted its head and watched Ye Wanwan.

Her eyes were focused, a flow of light moving through them above the thin veil — sometimes sinking into deep concentration, sometimes brightening with sudden understanding.

In those eyes, Xingze saw many things.

And then it heard:

"I understand now."

Ye Wanwan raised her head. "Seven-Star Illusion Formation." She gave a soft laugh. "So that is what this is."

"What is that?"

Ye Wanwan said, "A type of formation technique."

Xingze watched as she stepped through with an unusual pattern of footwork, and this time there was no obstruction at all. They reached the stone room at the end with complete smoothness. This time, there was no seal on the door.

It seemed the illusion formation itself had been the test.

Ye Wanwan entered the stone room without trouble.

The spacious stone room held only a single lacquered box.

Ye Wanwan looked around, and her gaze finally settled on the box. She reached out to touch it — but a surge of powerful spiritual energy pushed her back. Without any sense of danger, though.

Ye Wanwan stepped back half a step.

"Well, well, well. Someone has actually made it through the second trial and come to my presence. A person with real potential."

Ye Wanwan looked at the phantom that had appeared before her, the last golden talisman already held ready in her palm.

"A spirit body?"

Xingze spoke up immediately. "No — a residual memory."

Ye Wanwan studied it for a moment and confirmed there was no danger. Only then did she release her defensive posture. She looked steadily at the grey-robed old man before her. The old man gazed back at her as well.

As though separated by thousands of years, he was actually seeing her.

"Child, you must have come for the Wood-Fire Spirit. So let me ask you: do you wish to become a great alchemist?"

Ye Wanwan: "I do not."

"If you wish, that is exactly right! Think of it — I, the Dream Illusion Elder, lived a life of unmatched pride, without equal in the alchemy world, and yet in my old age I found I had no one to pass my legacy to. Such a regret! Now at last someone has passed through my first and second trials and come before me. You — you are the one destiny has chosen as my inheritor!"

"..."

Ye Wanwan stared at the grey-robed old man. "Is this progress fixed? Are there no options to choose from?"

The grey-robed old man looked at her with benevolent and "approachable" insistence, seemingly saying: you have no right to refuse.

Ye Wanwan said flatly, "I accept."

The grey-robed old man exclaimed with joy, "If you accept, that is exactly right! Think of it — I, the Dream Illusion Elder, lived a life of unmatched pride..."

Ye Wanwan: "Be quiet. Get to the point."

But a fixed sequence was a fixed sequence — it could not proceed to the next stage without completing the current one. This was a residual memory left behind by the realm's former owner, and its awareness was limited.

As Ye Wanwan moved through each of the choices step by step—

Another item appeared beside the lacquered box.

A spirit pearl.

"This is the fruit of my life's work in alchemy. Now... I give it to you."

Ye Wanwan's expression paused slightly. She studied the grey-robed old man carefully, and in the hopeful gaze he turned on her, Ye Wanwan saw something else.

He...

Had developed his own awareness.

chapters.title: Doing Good Deeds Has a Price
chapters.content:
The grey-robed old man's eyes held a meek and cautious light, as though afraid Ye Wanwan would refuse. Yet for someone who had reached the Mahayana stage, this level of humility was unnecessary.

And a mere memory with no awareness, one that only knew how to run its programmed sequence, should not have been capable of this kind of emotion.

Accept?

Or refuse?

Ye Wanwan looked into the old man's eyes, and as his gaze gradually dimmed in anticipation, she reached out and took the memory spirit pearl. "Fine."

The grey-robed old man's eyes immediately lit up. "You accepted?"

"Yes, I accepted."

Let her do one good deed for the day.

"A drop of blood will bind it to you," the old man reminded her.

"I have things to do. I'll handle that later."

The old man hastened to add, "This memory spirit pearl contains not only alchemy techniques — it also holds a full map of this cave dwelling and the memories of the entire secret realm. You will only know everything once you have absorbed it."

Ye Wanwan paused.

Xingze thought it over and said, "That should be true. Dream Illusion Elder was the master of the entire secret realm. Some things he would know more clearly than me, a mere parasitic spirit."

"All right."

With only a brief consideration, she did it.

Blood dripped.

The memory was received.

A vast flood of memory crashed into her mind. Ye Wanwan dropped to one knee, her complexion slightly pale. And only then did she understand — this was not merely alchemy knowledge. It was also the cultivation insights of a Mahayana stage cultivator.

The problem was—

She could not withstand it!

At the critical moment, the Heart-Questioning Sword's light flashed, and a thread of cold sword energy pierced through her temple. Her mind cleared in an instant. Ye Wanwan raised her head, eyes cold, locking onto the old man. Her left hand grabbed the Heart-Questioning Sword, and her right hand launched a talisman.

Ye Wanwan stepped up onto the table and pursued him, saying in a cold voice, "You ambushed me?"

The grey-robed old man immediately said, "I did not!"

The Heart-Questioning Sword's energy was already primed and ready, and Ye Wanwan had the old man's memory spirit form in her grip — one squeeze and she could shatter it.

The young woman's killing intent was immense.

The old man called out, "Your primordial spirit and cultivation level are still too weak to receive this much insight at once — that is perfectly normal! Just a little while and it will be fine!"

Ye Wanwan said with cold clarity, "Stop talking rubbish."

"If it were just ordinary alchemy memories, I would not be unable to withstand them. But what you have hidden inside carries your own private desires." Ye Wanwan tightened her grip on the Heart-Questioning Sword, enunciating each word. "Memories saturated with emotion passed as a transmission — you want to interfere with my Dao heart?"

The grey-robed old man's spirit form went visibly dim. He offered Ye Wanwan a wary, negotiating tone.

"Young woman, I can give you the most important things and the full inheritance of this cave dwelling — but I only have this one small wish of my own."

Ye Wanwan gave a cold laugh. "You think I will be generous a second time?"

The grey-robed old man said with complicated feeling, "But this emotional memory genuinely will not influence you. With your nature, you will absorb all memories eventually — sooner or later."

Ye Wanwan glanced at him, not bothering to deny it. But her attitude remained unmoved. "Whether I can or not is my business. The fact that you had things left unsaid and then ambushed me — that is an entirely different matter."

Ye Wanwan reached into the Ziyun ring and produced a spirit pearl.

Her right hand moved rapidly, forming patterns.

Her speed was so fast that even Xingze could not track the motion clearly.

But the old man saw it.

"A Soul-Locking Talisman!"

"In you go," Ye Wanwan said flatly.

She struck the old man's spirit form into the pearl. The Soul-Locking Bead was complete, and Ye Wanwan heard the old man's protest. "You little girl, where did you learn that? I am half a teacher to you, after all."

"Sorry — I am rebellious by nature, and my favourite hobby is killing teachers. Say one more word and I will slaughter you."

The grey-robed old man went silent.

Though he knew Ye Wanwan was joking, he could tell the young woman was in a very bad mood.

Ye Wanwan steadied her emotions. The grey-robed old man had held no malice — but the emotional turbulence inside the memory spirit pearl had been so violent it had pulled her own mind along with it.

A person's memories were heavy things.

All the more so for a creature that had lived for thousands of years.

His life had been full of slaughter and strife, without a moment of true peace.

Even though this was only a small portion of those memories, it was still more than enough to keep Ye Wanwan occupied for a very long time. She silently recited the Clear Heart Incantation, and then applied two Clear Heart Talismans on herself.

"When the opportunity arises, I still need to get some Clear Heart Pills."

Ye Wanwan pressed down the sharpness that had come over her, and quickly looked toward the lacquered box. When she opened it, there was indeed a Grade Five Wood-Fire Spirit.

A warm, gentle flame — without the burning heat of fire, but carrying instead a nourishing quality for the spirit.

This eased her mood considerably.

Ye Wanwan put away the Wood-Fire Spirit, storing it alongside the Grade Two one.

The grey-robed old man quickly called out, "Now that you've taken my things, don't forget my inheritance!"

Ye Wanwan acted as though she had not heard him. Having collected everything, she swept the stone room with her eyes. She spotted a few formation stones by the doorway and carried those off as well.

Xingze: "..."

Old Man: "...You really do not let anything go."

"The formation stones of a Seven-Star Illusion Formation are very useful things. Why would I leave them behind?"

Having cleared out the formation stones, Ye Wanwan hurried toward the third path.

Seeing her move at this speed, the old man realised he did not even need to remind her.

The third fork truly did hide the most precious things in Cloud Mountain Cave.

It was also the very core of this secret realm.

Ye Wanwan moved without pause — but she also knew that even racing against time, time was still passing. Ji Changhuai would free himself from the spirit-binding thread sooner or later. So what she could do was make his journey a little more troublesome.

Ye Wanwan ran into the third path. After about ten paces, she buried the Seven-Star Illusion Formation stones she had taken in the ground. Then she took one long, hard look at the corridor ahead.

And went in without looking back.

"Have you considered that if he has already passed through, the illusion formation you buried might end up blocking you?"

"He hasn't. At Ji Changhuai's level, he needs another quarter of an hour to break free." Ye Wanwan paused, then said flatly, "And even if he breaks free early, I won't be the one it traps."

Both Xingze and the old man were won over by the young woman's confidence.

But Xingze, perched on her shoulder, still could not resist asking, "How can you be so sure?"

Ye Wanwan glanced at the spirit pearl hanging at her waist and said with a slight smile, "That is where Dream Illusion Elder's memories come in."

The grey-robed old man puffed up with pride, ready to show off a little.

Ye Wanwan looked straight ahead. "If anything in those memories turns out to be wrong, I would not mind sending this tiny little memory form of yours to its complete obliteration."

Old Man: "..."

Xingze also sat quietly on Ye Wanwan's shoulder, watching the young woman run into the end of the corridor. But with one step forward, the path suddenly shook.

Xingze immediately looked at Ye Wanwan.

Ye Wanwan also looked at the old man.

The old man's eyes went wide. "I am just a memory form — I have no ability to shake heaven and earth!"

The tremor was not just one wave.

The storm that suddenly came crashing down the corridor from ahead was not something that would end after one blast.

Clearly, this was only the beginning.

Almost immediately, the grey-robed old man shouted loudly, "Run!"

But Ye Wanwan had already moved a step ahead of his warning, entering the Ziyun ring. The speck of dust drifted in the storm, centred on the end of the corridor ahead.

It detonated.

Then swept through the entire cave dwelling. Including the cliff face.

Unlike the earlier explosion, this was a blast that consumed the entire cave structure in one go. Even Ji Changhuai, who had just broken free of his bindings, was caught in the shockwave.

The cave dwelling collapsed. A massive vortex appeared in its place, swallowing everyone on the cliff face.

Including one particular speck of dust hidden in the air.

chapters.title: Is It a Dream, or a Past Life?
chapters.content:
Even sheltered inside the Ziyun ring, Ye Wanwan could feel the violent shaking. The tremors from outside extended inward, affecting her within the ring.

Xingze quickly detached itself from the stone and stabilised the Xingze realm.

The grey-robed old man, now inside the space, immediately noticed the spirit lake.

"You absorbed the Xingze secret realm?!"

Ye Wanwan said flatly, "I thought you had already guessed that when you heard the little creature's voice."

The grey-robed old man drew a long breath, then gave a quiet, heartfelt sigh. "My judgement was right this time. I chose well."

Ye Wanwan furrowed her brow. "This must be the first time anyone has ever entered Cloud Mountain Cave."

The grey-robed old man went silent.

Ye Wanwan: "Did you even have another choice?"

The grey-robed old man went silent again.

Ye Wanwan: "Ha."

The grey-robed old man wiped his face. Fine, he knew what she was getting at and what she was sarcastically implying. He had used the inheritance memories to pour his own recollections into Ye Wanwan.

That had genuinely not been a proper thing to do.

But Dream Illusion Elder also knew — without doing it that way, Ye Wanwan would never have agreed to accept the inheritance.

In principle, Dream Illusion Elder could have chosen someone else.

Because no matter who heard that a Mahayana cultivator's insights and experiences were being offered, they would take them without caring what else was included.

But people who would take anything without questions — Dream Illusion Elder no longer trusted them.

Ye Wanwan's "I don't want to" had been the correct answer.

Precisely because she did not want it, he needed to make her want it.

Suddenly, the secret realm began to spin rapidly. A powerful vertigo affected everything inside the Ziyun ring, as though something was gripping the ring from outside.

Xingze said loudly, "There is something outside absorbing spiritual energy. I am losing control!"

Ye Wanwan asked, "Can I see what is happening outside?"

Xingze said, "I will open a water mirror for you."

The words had barely left when a water mirror opened ahead.

Ye Wanwan saw the collapsed corridor, and at its end, an enormous vortex. The vortex expanded, pulling in the speck of dust that was the Ziyun ring's illusion.

Along with the Seven-Star Illusion Formation she had planted and the nearby stone rooms.

And the range was still expanding.

Within the vortex's pull, Ye Wanwan also saw Bai Jian and Fang He'an at the cave entrance trying to resist the force. But the power of this spatial collapse was too overwhelming.

All three of them were pulled in.

Ji Changhuai and his group along with them.

Ye Wanwan's pupils contracted.

But she had absolutely no time to help them — because Xingze was saying, "It's no good. I can't hold steady anymore. Hold onto something."

Only a moment later.

The entire inside of the Ziyun ring flipped upside down. Ye Wanwan rolled as though inside a spinning sphere — but she quickly grabbed the pill fruit tree and steadied herself.

Xingze sat in the branches, looking a little apologetic. "Sorry. I'm still too weak."

Even though it was a companion spirit, it had only been born after Dream Illusion Elder had perished.

By the reckoning of a companion spirit's age, it was barely a newborn.

Ye Wanwan glanced at the disordered space around her. "If I go outside, wouldn't that help?"

Xingze nodded, then shook its head. "But if you go outside, you would have to bear all the pressure out there directly."

Ye Wanwan said, "I'll go."

The moment the words left her, she exited the Ziyun ring.

The ring returned to her hand. Xingze's voice sounded, "Be careful!"

Ye Wanwan: "Yes."

She let the suction pull her into the vortex. The vortex landscape was pitch black, but she made no resistance at all, letting herself be drawn to wherever it ended.

The dark passage was completely silent.

No sound. No silhouettes.

Even Bai Jian and Fang He'an, who had been visible moments ago, were gone.

Ye Wanwan did not move recklessly. She let herself feel the stillness of the place.

Until—

A sharp, clear ring.

The sound of a blade leaving its sheath.

"Kill!"

Ye Wanwan's eyes snapped open, fixed on what appeared before her. It was a residence hung with festive lanterns — but a group of cultivators with killing intent thick on their bodies came surging inside.

"Kill the demon seed — save all living beings!"

"The Shen family is harbouring a demon seed — their entire clan must die!"

Those countless cultivators stormed the residence, killing anyone they found. If not for the proper cultivator robes they wore, one might have taken them for the demon tribe themselves.

The scene shifted — a residence where all candles had gone out.

A three-year-old boy crawled out from a well and walked through a ground covered in bodies, dazed and bewildered. "Mother, Father... Aunt..." No matter how he called, none of them would wake.

Then the front gate creaked open. The boy trembled, but he did not hide. He stared blankly at what was ahead.

From this angle, Ye Wanwan could not see who was at the door.

But she heard a voice.

"How terrible."

A soft, low sigh. A wisp of smoke curled the boy away.

The memory shifted again. Back to the same destroyed mountain settlement.

"Tianyi Sect shelters a demon seed — are they not defying all of the righteous cultivation world?"

"The righteous and the demonic cannot coexist. Since Tianyi Sect has protected this creature, they can all die together!"

The mountain summit was covered in flowing fire.

Deeper in the mountain range, a young man's voice rang out, hoarse and breaking, "Come at me! You want to kill me — come at me!"

And yet those grey-haired elders in their dao robes stood before him one by one. Their faces held a compassionate gentleness, looking at all living things with a kind of benevolent acceptance as they moved quietly toward death.

The young man sobbed, "Come back!"

But a white-robed elder said softly, "The way of the world is harsh. This is not something a child can bear alone."

"Master!"

"Ah, you never wanted to call me Master before, and yet you finally say it now. For that one word, child — your Master will surely shield you from all hardship."

But the scene shifted.

Two people were digging up bodies in the mountain. The sound of collapse and weeping made Ye Wanwan's entire body go rigid. It was Li Wanzhi...

"Senior Sister! Senior Brother! Master!"

The crying was broken — but another young man remained unmoved, his voice low: "I want revenge."

"We will have our revenge!"

The scene shifted again. Ye Wanwan saw the immortal-demon great war of her past life. She also saw, within the demon ranks, a man who raised his hand with easy detachment and took the lives of ten thousand cultivators as though dispersing clouds.

That was the Demon Lord of the Abyss.

A face that wore the same features as Shen Nanzhou.

She also saw herself — pierced through by seven swords from Yan Ding and the others, standing outside the crowd.

Her eyes were blood-red.

Her chest was full of killing intent.

But the Heart-Questioning Sword trembled, and that cold sword energy shot through her mind again. Ye Wanwan snapped awake, and her gaze sharpened like an arrow, seeing through the illusion before her.

The images shattered.

Ye Wanwan saw the one standing behind the illusion.

A young man in blue robes stood there, quietly, undisturbed. His gaze held none of the effortless, commanding authority of someone who took lives in the images — only calm, looking steadily at Ye Wanwan.

His voice was even cold. "How were you able to enter my dream?"

Ye Wanwan's face was pale. The two of them looked at each other. A thought passed through Ye Wanwan's mind — had the past life truly been a dream?

No.

It was not.

She stepped forward toward Shen Nanzhou and looked directly into his eyes.

"Who are you?"

chapters.title: The Past
chapters.content:
The young man in blue curved his lips and said in a low, beguiling voice, "I am your Junior Brother, Senior Sister."

Ye Wanwan gave a short, contemptuous laugh. "Junior Brother?"

"I don't think so."

Ye Wanwan suddenly closed the distance. As the spiritual energy around her surged, she struck a palm toward Shen Nanzhou. He shook his head and stepped aside at an unhurried pace.

"You are..."

His words caught. Shen Nanzhou looked down and saw a small stone graze past his chest and fly away.

It was the stone Xingze had been inhabiting.

The stone had hit the target.

And passed straight through.

Xingze: "It's a phantom."

Ye Wanwan's brow lifted. "Oh? Is that so, Junior Brother?"

A drawn-out note of mockery at the end.

The figure's expression shifted slightly, and he said with an odd curiosity, "How did you know?"

Ye Wanwan gave a short laugh. If Shen Nanzhou truly had memories of his past life, he would not have just asked how she got into his dream — he would have simply moved to kill her on the spot.

The phantom sighed, and as it sighed, its features changed — becoming Ji Changhuai's. "Junior Sister, you make it very heartbreaking."

Ye Wanwan's eyes darkened. She launched a fist. "I said never call me Junior Sister!"

The punch flew — but the phantom did not flinch, because as a spirit form it should have been beyond Ye Wanwan's ability to hurt it. Yet it had miscalculated.

Because when a fist slammed hard into its face—

And dragged it bodily down onto the ground beside Ye Wanwan—

The dream spirit went blank.

"How is this possible?"

It was a spirit body — how could Ye Wanwan possibly harm it?

Ye Wanwan gripped it by the throat. Now she understood why antagonists in stories liked grabbing people by the throat. Pulling someone's hair was unsightly, and pressing down on their chest lacked presence.

But the throat was different.

One hand was enough to hold it.

And the air of dominance was more than sufficient.

"Because I am not an ordinary person." Ye Wanwan laughed quietly, and the laugh made the spirit's whole body prickle. Only when it finally came back to its senses did it notice that five golden cores had locked onto it from all around.

And within the range of those five golden cores, the space answered to Ye Wanwan!

The dream spirit could not believe it. What kind of cultivation method allowed this? And how could anyone's golden cores operate outside the body? Weren't those supposed to be in the dantian?

"You're cheating!"

The dream spirit screamed.

"That doesn't count! Do it again!"

It had only been careless — let it be caught off guard by Ye Wanwan and it would never let it happen again.

Ye Wanwan's voice went cold. "Where are the others?"

"Why would I tell you..."

A stone rolled over from the side. It had sprouted two tiny hands and feet — Xingze had taken up residence in the stone again.

It perched on Ye Wanwan's shoulder and said with the wisdom of someone who had seen things, "As a more experienced spirit, I would strongly advise you to tell the truth. Otherwise you will not be so lucky next time."

The dream spirit choked, staring wide-eyed at this companion spirit. "You... a companion spirit? You accepted her as your master?"

"Mm-hm."

Xingze wanted to deny it, then thought better of it. It tossed the answer back. "What do you think?"

The dream spirit's expression was full of fury and reproach. "A dignified companion spirit, and you accepted a human cultivator as your master — even the master of this secret realm could not make me submit, and you, a useless creature, bend the knee."

"Is that so?"

Ye Wanwan's expression was bland.

"Then die."

The golden core range contracted. Flames surged — and laced within those flames was an attack on the primordial spirit. The dream spirit's expression changed. As the young woman's wrist was about to release it, it grabbed hold of her wrist and thudded to its knees.

"Master."

Xingze: "..."

Dream Illusion Elder: "..."

"They're behind me — I didn't move them." The dream spirit pointed backward.

Ye Wanwan looked into the darkness and saw nothing.

The dream spirit was perceptive enough to wave its hand and open a gap in the space, letting Ye Wanwan see Shen Nanzhou, who was trapped in the dream. But the young man's aura at this moment was surging with killing intent — come no closer.

If Ye Wanwan had genuinely encountered this Shen Nanzhou, death would have been certain.

"His will is too powerful. I tried to get close and absorb some of his memories, but I could not bear even a little of what I got." The dream spirit was a touch embarrassed.

Ye Wanwan looked at it coldly. "The images you showed me just now — that was his dream?"

The dream spirit gave an awkward laugh. "More or less. Part of it I made up — hey, hey hey, don't squeeze — it is a dream after all, close enough, the key is to find who he cares about and then destroy them. Hee hee hee."

Xingze threw itself at the spirit. "Stop laughing. You sound like something out of a crypt."

Ye Wanwan still had the images from her last moments of her past life on her mind. Those were not things anyone could have fabricated. "The immortal-demon great war at the end — did you make that up as well?"

The dream spirit's expression was strange. "That one..."

"Speak."

The dream spirit raised its voice. "No — I was peering through his memories and that fragment genuinely exists. But it's just that one broken piece. In those memories there is someone who looks like you, and then..." It glanced at Ye Wanwan. "It seems he has been looking for you all this time."

Ye Wanwan's brow furrowed.

Shen Nanzhou had also been reborn?

But judging from their first encounter, that did not quite seem to be the case.

The Shen Nanzhou of this life still appeared to have a certain simplicity and harmlessness about him — though still cold and off-putting to others. Nothing like the explosive volatility and murderous presence he had carried in the previous life.

The current Shen Nanzhou was, by comparison, far more gentle.

And yet this memory — who else could have it except someone who had been reborn?

She needed to probe further.

Ye Wanwan's gaze settled on Shen Nanzhou. "Can you bring me into his dream?"

The dream spirit's expression twisted with conflicting feelings, tinged with barely-suppressed glee. It almost could not contain its joy. "Really?"

Inside a dream realm, it was invincible.

It could also use the dream to absorb the life essence of cultivators and grow stronger. And naturally, if it could consume Xingze, the companion spirit, that would make it stronger too.

Xingze aimed a kick at it.

"Put away your drool."

Ye Wanwan said flatly, "Bring me in. I want to see."

"Of course, of course, no problem at all." The dream spirit was overjoyed. It did not even need to drag Ye Wanwan into the dream — the person wanted to go in herself. How could anyone walk right into a trap like this?

The dream spirit bared its teeth in a wide grin. "Just walk forward and you will enter."

Ye Wanwan strode forward.

But she also reached back and grabbed the dream spirit as she went, swinging her left hand lightly to form a Soul-Locking Incantation, which resolved into a cage trapping the spirit inside.

It stared at her, then at the cage, and yelled, "What are you doing?"

Ye Wanwan did not look back. "Since we're going in, of course we go together."

She looked down at the companion spirit she had also brought along, and smiled. "Isn't that right?"

The dream spirit shuddered.

Somehow these two entities, one after the other, both managed to be absolutely terrifying.

Ye Wanwan raised her hand and stepped lightly through what appeared to be a water curtain, entering Shen Nanzhou's dream. She found herself in mist. Within the mist, her footsteps rang with unusual clarity.

Step by step.

Then ahead — slow steps, hesitant.

They sounded twice, and then were gone.

Ye Wanwan stood still without approaching further. The mist gradually thinned. A three-year-old boy stood there. He seemed to have heard something, and raised his eyes to look at Ye Wanwan with puzzled curiosity.

In those large, clear black-and-white eyes was the clarity of a child — and wariness.

"Shen... Nanzhou?"

chapters.title: Wanwan, I'm Still Alive Too
chapters.content:
It was three-year-old Shen Nanzhou.

The boy looked at Ye Wanwan, seemed to find the person before him strange, then turned and ran. Ye Wanwan took long strides in pursuit — but in the dream, the boy kept growing older as he ran.

From three, to four, to five...

Ye Wanwan witnessed Shen Nanzhou's growth.

And she saw his younger self covered in wounds, saw the young man stepping through a sea of blood one step at a time, saw him fighting on the battlefield — a path completely different from his past life, yet still moving step by step toward death.

"Shen Nanzhou!"

Ye Wanwan called out.

Shen Nanzhou did not look back. Ye Wanwan's eyes deepened. "What did you do?"

The dream spirit looked genuinely put-upon. "I didn't do anything — he blew up the dream realm himself, and then it became like this. The dream right now is his own."

"Oh, and I forgot to mention something."

The dream spirit said in a creeping tone, "If he does not wake up, you cannot leave either."

In this moment, Shen Nanzhou was deep in his own dream.

And Ye Wanwan had walked in of her own accord.

As long as Shen Nanzhou did not wake, the dream would not dissolve, and Ye Wanwan would never be able to get out.

Ye Wanwan looked long and hard at the dream spirit until its smile slowly faded and it did not dare laugh anymore.

Ye Wanwan looked calmly toward Shen Nanzhou, who was still running. She did not pursue.

She stopped.

"Why have you stopped chasing?" the dream spirit asked.

"You said he was looking for me. I will wait for him to come find me." Ye Wanwan pressed a finger to the Soul-Locking Incantation. The incantation shrank to the size of a lantern, and the dream spirit was compressed into a ball of light.

Ye Wanwan pulled a branch from somewhere in the space and held it like a lantern, using the faint glow the dream spirit emitted to light her way as she walked in the opposite direction.

Dream spirit: "..."

She was using it as a lantern?

Fine — I'll go dark!

But in moments, the light faded from its body.

Ye Wanwan said in a cold voice, "Your only use to me right now is to show me the way. Try going dark and see what happens."

Dream spirit: "..."

It slowly began to glow again, with great reluctance, lighting the way for Ye Wanwan as she traced back the path she had come — and making more visible what was unfolding in this young man's dream.

"Where is the night when his family was killed, when he was three?"

The dream spirit pointed forward.

"I know you have a way to get there directly."

The dream spirit said nothing.

Xingze climbed down from Ye Wanwan's shoulder and sat on the red lantern. It took a deep breath, and a stream of powerful energy was drawn into it. Xingze grew excited. "Master, I can eat it!"

Feeling its energy being drawn away, the dream spirit let out a shriek. "Little brat, what do you think you're doing?! How old are you, daring to try to devour me?! Outrageous!"

It frantically shielded itself.

But Xingze was thrilled.

It had only thought the creature smelled delicious, but had not expected absorbing it would actually strengthen itself. Xingze licked its lips. "Master, if you don't want it, can you give it to me to eat? I will be very tidy about it."

The dream spirit felt deeply unwell.

It flared with a burst of bright light.

The entire path was illuminated.

As if in stern protest, it declared, "Tell me where you want to go and I will take you!"

Ye Wanwan: "The night the Shen family was killed."

"This way."

A green staircase appeared one step ahead. Ye Wanwan stepped forward and was instantly before a residence, the ground covered in bodies.

Three-year-old Shen Nanzhou crawled out of the well, searching through the field of the dead for his family, calling their names, unable to wake any of them.

Small and helpless, he tried to drag the adults' bodies together, but the sounds at the front gate were growing louder. Amid the creaking of hinges, Ye Wanwan and the boy stopped simultaneously.

Ye Wanwan looked toward the gate.

But she did not notice — the boy was looking at her.

"Is it Tianyi Sect people who have come?"

This murmur from Ye Wanwan seemed to fall into the boy's ears. He suddenly darted toward the well, jumped in without hesitation. Ye Wanwan was thrown off by this rapid chain of events.

And then the scene cracked.

"Dream spirit!" Ye Wanwan called.

"His memory ends here — I cannot hold this much longer."

The illusion cracked like a spider's web. Before Ye Wanwan could see who had come through the gate, it shattered. But in that final instant as it broke apart, Ye Wanwan saw a blood mist sweep Shen Nanzhou away.

Ye Wanwan's pupils contracted.

Not white smoke.

Blood mist.

It had changed.

Ye Wanwan fell out of Shen Nanzhou's dream, stumbling back three steps before steadying herself. She looked up — and there was the small boy.

"Why did it change?"

She asked in a cold voice.

If she was right, the Shen Nanzhou of her past life had been taken in by Tianyi Sect. Why had he been swept away by blood mist?

The boy looked at Ye Wanwan. "You."

Ye Wanwan was puzzled. "Me?"

The boy walked slowly toward her. "I have been looking for you... for a very long time."

Ye Wanwan stiffened.

Xingze leapt up. "Watch out!"

Ye Wanwan raised her fingers and formed a seal. Five golden cores arranged themselves in a defensive formation — but in doing so also shattered the illusion. The small boy disappeared. But Ye Wanwan's heart did not settle at all.

No.

She had to understand this.

She had to know whether what had just changed was the dream — or reality.

Ye Wanwan asked, "Does my entering this dream change anything in the real world?"

Neither the dream spirit nor Xingze had anticipated this question. Both were momentarily taken aback. "How could it? This isn't travelling back in time — this is just an illusion."

Only what exists in a person's heart — what they think of, crave, and long for — is woven into a dream that satisfies their own desires.

How could that affect reality?

Ye Wanwan murmured quietly, "Then what is it that Shen Nanzhou wants?"

Ye Wanwan held the lantern and followed the path of Shen Nanzhou's dream. She watched his younger self rise from a battlefield of the mortal world, step by step — and she could not help but look on in a different light.

The path Shen Nanzhou was walking in this life was not the same as the one he had walked before.

She walked for a long time, and then the mist ahead broke open. Ye Wanwan saw the young man sitting on the ground.

Ye Wanwan held the lantern and did not move.

Then the young man's eyes slowly opened. They were threaded with red, and his emotions did not seem stable — and yet he still smiled, curving his lips with a teasing quality.

"Senior Sister, are you so interested in my past? You've been watching over and over."

Ye Wanwan studied the young man before her and said flatly, "I didn't want to watch. I just cannot leave."

Shen Nanzhou raised a hand. Between his fingers wound a strand of blue silk thread. "How could that be? If Senior Sister wanted to leave, you could certainly leave. After all — you are Senior Sister."

Ye Wanwan very much wanted to roll her eyes, but held it back.

Heaven knew how much she loathed those two words.

The dream spirit was already shaking. "The blue thread in his hand — it's dream silk from the dream realm. It pulls on every person's desires and emotions who enters. If it snaps, a person will lose their mind."

Ye Wanwan paused slightly, her gaze dropping to his fingers.

"Whose dream silk is that?"
