Yu Chun: "......"

So as long as you didn't announce your sect affiliation, you weren't considered part of Tianyi Sect?

Pei Xuan flicked the snowflake off his palm. The single flake landed on the lava — and still did not dissolve. From that one small detail, Yu Chun could feel just how terrifying this man's mastery over spiritual power truly was.

Yu Chun was genuinely terrified.

Because he understood one thing with complete clarity —

If Pei Xuan wanted to kill every disciple on Qingyun Peak, it would take him no more than the snap of a finger.

Qingyun Peak would not survive.

"This is Wushang Sect's domain! Fellow Daoist, stand down!"

Three elders arrived on sword-light, each striking a blow to shatter the lava lake as they bore down on Pei Xuan.

Yet without any visible movement from Pei Xuan, a great earth dragon surged up from within the lava and slammed into their swords. Right before everyone's eyes, a hundred-zhang fire dragon and earth dragon engaged the three elders in fierce battle.

Pei Xuan said lightly: "Haven't heard anyone praise me like that in several hundred years."

He raised his eyes, cold and unmoved. "So what if I stand down? And what if I don't?"

As the three elders found themselves tangled up by the fire dragon and unable to break free, every disciple on the mountain peak went pale as paper. Someone burst into tears: "The three elders can't win — they actually can't win!"

These were all elders at the peak of the Nascent Soul stage!

And they couldn't defeat someone who looked barely past his mid-twenties!

"Run!"

"Fellow Daoist Pei, is this really necessary?" A streak of white light pressed the earth dragon back. Cheng Wen appeared in midair, his expression complex.

The three elders went ashen. "Sect Master."

Yu Chun was overcome with relief as well.

"Sect Master!"

Pei Xuan stood tall, watching Cheng Wen, his expression unchanged. "I made a promise to my Senior Brother. I would not kill anyone on this trip down the mountain."

Cheng Wen's expression eased somewhat. "Then you..."

"I'm looking for someone."

"Who?"

"Yan Ding."

Everyone: "......"

Cheng Wen was taken aback. Did Pei Xuan have some kind of grudge against Junior Brother Yan?

Yet the several elders exchanged glances and none of them could figure it out.

"Junior Brother Yan has been in closed cultivation for half a year and has yet to emerge. I'm not sure what grievance you two have." Cheng Wen asked with genuine puzzlement.

But Pei Xuan let out a low laugh — and hearing that laugh, everyone's nerves pulled tighter than ever.

Pei Xuan said calmly: "No grievance. But his disciple has wronged my only disciple. As a master, shouldn't I go and claim some justice on behalf of my own student?"

The elders looked at one another in bewilderment. No one could make sense of it — he had come all this way for this?

And since when had Pei Xuan taken on a disciple?

And when had their respective disciples ever come into conflict?

But Cheng Wen already had a guess forming in his mind. "Your disciple is...?"

"The genius, Ye Wanwan."

Pei Xuan looked at Cheng Wen, and curled his lips. "The greatest genius in the cultivation world today — Ye Wanwan."

"She is my disciple."

Qingyun Peak fell utterly silent.

chapters.title: No High Ground? Then Make Some
chapters.content:
"Ye Wanwan."

The three words echoed in everyone's ears. It was a very long time before anyone came back to their senses, until at last someone asked in a low voice: "This Ye Wanwan — is she the same Ye Wanwan we know?"

"It seems like......"

If there were many people sharing the same name, the phrase "greatest genius" could only apply to one.

Qingyun Peak's Seventh Junior Sister — Ye Wanwan.

The one who had shattered Ye Qian's golden core, been punished to kneel on Xuanbing Cliff, yet who had destroyed her own cultivation the very next day and in the end leapt without hesitation from Xuanbing Cliff.

That Ye Wanwan.

Dou Ming's entire frame went taut.

The Ye Qian on his back also lifted her head sharply, her eyes burning with a cold and vicious hatred. Through tightly clenched teeth, she silently forced out three words.

Ye Wanwan.

She is my disciple.

Pei Xuan added lightly: "My only one."

Those three supplementary words fell upon Dou Ming's heart like the blow of a heavy hammer.

The sole disciple of Daoist Pei Xuan.

Cheng Wen, Yu Chun, and the three sect-guarding elders immediately read the meaning that lay behind the man's words.

He — valued this disciple enormously.

Even immeasurably so.

"My little disciple doesn't go out much. This was her first time leaving the mountain to go through trials, and your people gravely injured her. She's been bedridden ever since. As her master, I've turned it over many times — and I still had to come and do something about it."

"After all, my little disciple is soft-hearted and thin-skinned. There are some things she always feels too embarrassed to do herself. But I don't mind," Pei Xuan said indifferently. "I have no shame whatsoever."

Cheng Wen and the others were speechless for a long moment, unable to produce a single appropriate response.

One elder couldn't help himself and started: "That traitor..."

But Pei Xuan's gaze swept coldly over him, and in that instant the very air seemed to congeal. The frost that sealed the air hovered right between the man's nose and mouth — one moment more and it could solidify his blood and bone.

Shatter him with a single palm.

Pei Xuan — ice and fire dual spirit roots. There were rumors that he had a third spirit root as well, though no one knew what it was.

There were also those who said it was best never to force this man to use his third spirit root.

Because that was when he would begin to kill indiscriminately.

The elder who had spoken went pale, but before long a far deeper terror set in.

Because his cultivation — appeared to have been sealed as well.

"I......"

"Wùxū!"

Before the words were out, the elder who had spoken — Wùxū — was already encased in ice. Curling around his ankle was a tiny tongue of flame, like a viper coiling upward, ready to strike.

No one doubted that when that flame crept higher, it would swallow Wùxū whole in an instant and dissolve him into the mist of steam that still hung in the air.

Pei Xuan said serenely: "I'm petty. I don't like hearing people speak ill of my disciple."

Everyone: "......"

Expletives rose to the tip of the tongue and simply couldn't be uttered.

Cheng Wen stopped the two elders who had moved to intervene and let out a sigh. "In that case, Fellow Daoist Pei, tell us how you'd like to resolve this. With Junior Brother Yan still in closed cultivation, I will make the decisions on his behalf."

"Sect Master!" Elders Wùjìng and Wùxīn both panicked.

Cheng Wen cut them off.

Pei Xuan lifted his gaze with an air of complete indifference. "Two options. Return a person, or return medicine."

His gaze drifted over Ye Qian with quiet deliberateness.

Before the hatred in Ye Qian's eyes could fully rise, her body was already shaking uncontrollably.

Pei Xuan... wanted to kill her.

Cheng Wen sighed. "What exactly do you want?"

Pei Xuan had come prepared. He raised a finger and sent out a stream of spiritual light. Cheng Wen reached out and caught it — and found himself holding what appeared to be a list. No, not a list — a scroll.

When Cheng Wen unrolled it, the scroll dropped and kept dropping, unspooling nearly seven or eight meters across the ground before it finally stopped.

Several expressions shifted.

Elder Wùjìng burst out: "Are you robbing us?! What disciple's injuries could possibly require this many spirit herbs?!"

Three hundred-odd varieties of first-grade spirit herbs was one thing.

There were over a hundred varieties of second and third grade as well.

But what they truly could not accept was the two fourth-grade spirit herbs listed within.

Fourth grade!

Even the elders themselves didn't have many of those to spare.

Pei Xuan's expression was one of contemptuous dismissal. "Robbery? Everything on that list barely scratches the surface. My disciple deserves the finest things this world has to offer."

Cheng Wen looked it over for a long time, a clear picture already forming in his mind.

"Yu Chun."

Yu Chun, who had been standing to one side the entire time, started at the sudden summons. "Sect Master."

"Go and prepare it."

Yu Chun paused. "This......"

Cheng Wen waved a hand. "Go. Don't keep our guest waiting too long."

Yu Chun hurried away with the scroll.

Pei Xuan, for his part, surveyed Qingyun Peak with great patience, his gaze occasionally landing on Ye Qian in a way that filled her with dread.

Cheng Wen drew closer to the remnants of Miao Lake. "Shall we sit inside?"

"No need."

The entire group stood in attendance around Pei Xuan, not daring to breathe too loudly, every person anxiously watching, silently willing Yu Chun to return soon.

Every second was an eternity.

After a very long wait, Yu Chun finally returned.

He carried a qiankun pouch along with two lacquered boxes.

"The fourth-grade spirit herbs are too precious for a qiankun pouch to contain." Yu Chun added quickly.

"Mm."

Pei Xuan took the items, and as he turned to leave, he looked once more at Ye Qian. This time Ye Qian trembled violently from head to toe, even her teeth chattering.

Pei Xuan said: "As long as she doesn't make a move against you, I won't touch her. But one thing — and you know this in your heart — whatever you owe her, however she chooses to collect it, you will take it."

Ye Qian's eyes filled with tears. "I never......"

Pei Xuan had no interest in hearing her explain. He turned and walked away. "How a whole and intact golden core was shattered, I didn't see with my own eyes. But I'm not blind. A withered spirit root cannot produce a flawless golden core."

Only his clear, cold voice lingered in the empty air.

Again and again it echoed across Qingyun Peak.

Every disciple looked at Ye Qian with a complicated expression.

Tears streamed down Ye Qian's face.

"I really... didn't......"

But before she could finish, another voice drifted down from above.

"Nearly forgot — I'll leave a mark."

At those words, every heart on the peak lurched.

In the next instant, the highest stone peak of Qingyun — Qingshi Peak — was encased in ice. The frost spread across the entire mountainside in a great rushing wave. And upon it, using the power of the Dao itself, two characters were carved.

Pei Xuan.

Everyone: "......"

Elder Wùjìng erupted: "This is outrageous!"

Even Wùxīn's face had gone iron-dark. "Sect Master, are we truly going to swallow this humiliation?"

Neither Wùxīn nor Wùjìng could hold back any longer. This was too much. Far, far too much.

Yu Chun and the others didn't dare say a word, everyone struck silent as cicadas in winter.

But Cheng Wen said nothing. After a long pause, he asked: "And what would you like to do?"

"That traitor — she clearly betrayed our Wushang Sect, and yet this Pei Xuan treats her like some precious treasure. Is he simply that foolish?" And besides, the one who had been injured was their disciple — even now, Elder Wùzhēn was still bedridden from severe injuries — yet Pei Xuan had shown up at their door to extort them!

Cheng Wen gave a cold laugh. "Do you think he doesn't know?"

Wùjìng: "Perhaps, if we found the right opportunity......"

"If any of you want to die, then by all means make your move."

Cheng Wen finished speaking and vanished from where he stood without another word.

What a pack of fools.

Pei Xuan had been looking for exactly this kind of excuse. Had Li Mingde not given him instructions before he set out, Pei Xuan would have started killing long ago. Anyone who handed him a pretext at a moment like this — Tianyi Sect's people would have a perfect opportunity to perform at their absolute best.

Standing on the moral high ground, they would stomp their enemies into the dust.

No high ground available? Then they would manufacture it.

That was their guiding principle.

A group of lunatics — but lunatics who still operated within a certain logic.

The remaining disciples exchanged helpless looks, none of them daring to speak again — especially not with the sight of Wùxū still unable to break free of the ice seal and the utter wreckage of Miao Lake before them.

Everyone sighed.

As the two elders seethed in silent misery, Cheng Wen's voice drifted down from somewhere above. "Wait until Junior Brother Yan Ding emerges from closed cultivation. We'll discuss it then."

Both of them looked up, eyes brightening at once. It seemed the Sect Master had his own calculations in mind after all.

Good.

They would wait.

chapters.title: Innate Spirit Bone
chapters.content:
Elders Wùjìng and Wùxīn took the still ice-sealed Wùxū with them as they left, intent on finding a way to break the seal. Before long, Yu Chun departed as well.

Miao Lake was left with only Dou Ming and Ye Qian and the other disciples.

The building that had been suspended over the lake was already on the verge of collapse.

After Pei Xuan's departure, it came crashing down with a great rush of noise.

Reduced to rubble.

Dou Ming stood at the lakeshore with Ye Qian on his back, staring at the collapsed structure at the lake's center and the devastation all around them. For a very long time he said nothing. Finally, a hoarse single syllable escaped him.

"Little......"

Dou Ming had wanted to ask — did you really frame Ye Wanwan by sabotaging your own golden core? But the words caught in his throat. What if she had?

So what.

Things had already come to this.

In truth, many of them had guessed the answer, to some degree or another. They simply hadn't been willing to believe it.

And that person had proven it with her life.

She had done nothing wrong.

They were the ones who had.

Dou Ming changed course. "Let me take you somewhere to recover from your injuries. We'll think of another way once our master comes out." Regardless of anything, he couldn't abandon Ye Qian again.

But Ye Qian suddenly grabbed his shoulder. "The scripture tower."

Dou Ming frowned. "What are you going to the scripture tower for, in this state?"

Ye Qian's eyes were red as blood. "Take me."

She tightened her grip, her voice dropping cold and hard. "Take. Me. There."

A jolt of unease went through Dou Ming's chest. This Ye Qian felt deeply unfamiliar to him.

The Wushang Sect's scripture tower had five levels. The first and second could be freely browsed by disciples in the Qi Refinement and Foundation Building stages.

The third level required a Golden Core cultivation base or the status of a personal disciple.

The fourth required late Golden Core stage at minimum, and the fifth was off-limits to anyone below the Nascent Soul stage — only there were the higher-level cultivation techniques housed.

Ye Qian dismissed Dou Ming and went in alone on the first level. She didn't go to the second, nor to the third that was restricted to personal disciples.

Instead she went to the very back of the scripture tower, to a corner, opened a hidden door, and passed through a passage leading downward.

She moved slowly, her steps unsteady. With every stride, the wound in her abdomen seeped blood. But her feet moved toward the descent without the slightest hesitation. She was going down.

Reaching the vast open space below, Ye Qian called out loudly: "Come out!"

"I know you're in here!"

Black mist surged, slowly encircling Ye Qian.

"Heh heh. Why so angry all of a sudden?"

Ye Qian snatched a book from within the black mist. The book shuddered and tried to fly away, but Ye Qian seized it and held on. "A withered spirit root?"

"Was it you who drained my spirit root!"

"Wasn't it?!"

Ye Qian's voice rang out furiously. The reason she had failed to condense her golden core was because of this — because of it!

"I brought you up from the riverbed. You absorbed my spirit root's power, and yet you never told me my golden core failure had nothing to do with me. It was you!"

"You're the one who destroyed me!"

Ye Qian flung the black book to the ground and stamped on it frantically. "Why would you do this to me? It was I who broke the seal on you. It was I who brought you out. It was I who placed you in this scripture tower with its abundance of spiritual energy so you could nourish your soul. Why would you do this to me?!"

Ye Qian's tears came without stopping. She sank to her knees on the ground and broke down sobbing. She was no worse than Ye Wanwan — she was simply unlucky.

Just unbearably, catastrophically unlucky.

Ye Qian wept and wept.

Black mist drifted up from within the book, and a voice sounded — low and eerie. "Little girl, you had better be clear on something. Without my help, how could you possibly have formed your golden core at fifteen years old?"

"But I failed!" Ye Qian screamed.

"Your talent was insufficient. You attempted to condense the core by force — of course you'd fail."

Ye Qian's eyes burned with hatred. "Pei Xuan said my spirit root was withered. He doesn't lie. So it was you! It was you!"

The black mist drifted around her playfully. "To become a genius, one naturally has to pay a certain price. To become the protagonist of this world, one naturally has to give certain things up. What do you think you are — Ye Wanwan? Born with a full set of spirit roots, innately suited to everything she studies. You're not~"

The mocking lilt in that voice sent Ye Qian completely over the edge.

She seized the black mist in a fierce grip, hatred blazing from her eyes. "Give me back my spirit root. Give me back my golden core! Give it back! Or I'll dig up the bones buried here and burn them — grind you down in the pill furnace, piece by piece."

She was consumed with hatred. She tightened her grip on the black mist and her movements were swift — she gathered spiritual energy at her fingertips and cut out a sword strike, splitting open the ground.

There, half a skull surfaced — emanating a dense, sinister black aura, buried deep in the earth.

Ye Qian stared at it fixedly.

That was the thing that had changed her life — and ruined it.

At the age of eight, she had found it at the base of Wushang Sect's mountain. From that day on, it had set Ye Qian upon the path of a genius. But by the same token, it had also severed any possibility of her ascending to immortality.

The black mist's tone loosened. "Girl, you can't really blame me. I told you at the time — don't try to force the golden core, wait two more years, and the circumstances will be more favorable to you. But you insisted on challenging Ye Wanwan's record. Records set by a genius — do you really think they're so easy to break? Even your master Yan Ding can't keep up with her natural talent. What possessed you to compare yourself to her?"

"She isn't the only one who condensed a golden core at fifteen!" Ye Qian screamed, refusing to hear this thing praise Ye Wanwan for another second. She couldn't bear to hear it!

She didn't know there was such a thing as praise used as a weapon — that the black mist wasn't praising anyone at all, but stoking the fire of Ye Qian's hatred for Ye Wanwan.

"Oh? Another genius like that actually exists?" The black mist seemed to perk up with interest. "Who?"

Ye Qian's expression went cold and lethal. "My golden core has been extracted. My cultivation is already beginning to unravel. Within a month I'll have fallen back to the Qi Refinement stage. I want you to find a way out of this for me. Otherwise we die together."

Ye Qian reached into empty space with one hand — retrieval from a distance — and seized the skull. She turned to leave the scripture tower.

She was going to tell Yan Ding and Cheng Wen everything.

Tell them that Wushang Sect had been harboring a thing like this.

The black mist sighed. "What's the rush? I never said there was no way."

"Speak."

"Then look."

From within the black mist, a spirit root appeared — golden in color, faintly threaded through with black energy.

Ye Qian frowned. She could feel the immense power emanating from it, yet there was also something she couldn't name — an ominous foreboding she couldn't shake.

The black mist said: "Do you know what exists above a Heavenly Grade spirit root?"

"What?"

"An Immortal spirit root."

Ye Qian was slightly taken aback. "An Immortal's spirit root?"

"That's right~" The voice carried a smile. "This is a spirit root even stronger than Ye Wanwan's. As long as you possess it, in less than half a year you'll not only return to the Golden Core stage — you'll go even beyond that."

Ye Qian's heart stirred. "Truly?"

"Of course — though this thing does have one drawback." The black mist spoke like a demon making its pitch, its voice low and beguiling. "Because it is too powerful, your physical body cannot withstand it. To merge with it perfectly, you must first obtain an Innate Spirit Bone."

"What is that?"

"Heaven plays favorites — there are always a few people it is particularly generous to. A genius like Ye Wanwan is one. There is another kind as well — children born with an innately extraordinary constitution. These are children with an Innate Spirit Bone. They are born with boundless divine strength, which is quite remarkable."

"Without any body-tempering cultivation, their flesh alone rivals a top-grade spiritual instrument in power. And once the spirit bone is developed to its fullest potential, it can even reach for the path of an immortal."

"It is the physical vessel best suited to bearing an Immortal spirit root."

chapters.title: It Must Be Taken While Alive — Dead, It's Useless
chapters.content:
Ye Qian's heart blazed with desperate longing. "Where would I find someone like that?"

The black mist laughed with a sound like rustling leaves. "That would be for you to discover. Such people are one in a million — even rarer to find than a Heavenly Grade spirit root. But if you truly manage to locate one, your path to immortality may not be beyond reach after all."

Ascension to immortality.

Ye Qian seized the golden spirit root in a firm grip, her voice dropping low. "I'll find one."

"The spirit bone must be taken while the person is still alive. Once dead, it's useless." The black mist gave a quiet cackle, said its last word, and then, carrying the skull, sank back into the earth and vanished.

Only Ye Qian remained, alone in the space, beginning to fuse with the spirit root.

"Ambition — and the drive to act on it. The talent is a little lacking, but she'll do."

The black mist murmured to itself, its voice low and coaxing.

Moments later, a finger extended from within the black mist and gave a light tap. Spiritual power surged in torrents into the skull's forehead. A face began to take shape — nearly formed — but it held for only a moment before dissipating.

"Still... not enough."

Far from enough.

Geniuses...

The more, the better.

——

Tianyi Sect.

Ye Wanwan's heart gave a sudden violent lurch. She pressed her hand to her chest, but it did nothing to ease it. The others saw her complexion going paler by the moment and their expressions changed at once.

"Little Junior Sister!"

Shen Nanzhou's brow furrowed. He looked above her head, then reached out and grasped at the empty air above it. The others watched the motion with some surprise.

Shen Nanzhou's expression remained unchanged. "Warding off bad energy on her behalf."

The three of them: "......"

"Does that work?"

But seeing Ye Wanwan's color genuinely begin to improve, all three of them rushed over and started waving their hands above her head with great enthusiasm, chanting as they went: "Away, away, away! Bad energy go away! Good fortune come, come, come!"

Ye Wanwan: "......"

Shen Nanzhou had lowered his head, quietly laughing. In his hand, he turned a thin black thread over between his fingers, his eyes dark and deep.

A curse.

What a base thing — resorting to such base methods.

He rubbed it between two fingers, and the curse shattered in an instant. The young man's expression was mild as he looked up and found Ye Wanwan watching him. He smiled lightly. "What is it, Senior Sister?"

"...It's Junior Sister."

"Right. What does Senior Sister need?"

"......" Ye Wanwan stared at his hand. Shen Nanzhou extended his palm toward her. "Is Senior Sister going to read my palm? Then tell me — will I die young?"

Ye Wanwan heard this and studied Shen Nanzhou's palm earnestly, then looked at his face and said: "You won't. Because I'll go before you."

The smile on Shen Nanzhou's face vanished.

His hand curled closed.

"Don't say that."

But before he could finish, Fang He'an cut in: "Quick, spit three times — we're all going to live long, healthy lives."

Ye Wanwan smiled and said: "Right. Fifth Senior Brother and I are both going to live long, healthy lives."

Shen Nanzhou: "Mm. All of you are."

Fang He'an caught the odd phrasing. "What do you mean, 'you all'? Including you — it's 'we all'!"

Shen Nanzhou smiled. "Right. We're all going to live long lives. A scourge lasts a thousand years."

Li Wanzhi snickered too. "Then I'm definitely going to be the wealthiest person in the entire cultivation world."

"Wishing you every success."

The group joked around for a bit longer, which smoothed over the interruption entirely. Seeing that Ye Wanwan was fine, Fang He'an took Li Wanzhi and Bai Jian and headed back.

"Little Junior Sister, rest well. We'll come see you in a couple of days."

"Alright. Fourth Senior Brother, don't forget what I mentioned."

Li Wanzhi: "Relax, leave it to me."

Get a few spirit market tokens?

What did Little Junior Sister call it again?

Oh right — alternate accounts.

Li Wanzhi thumped his chest with a promise.

After they left, it was just Ye Wanwan alone. The discomfort had faded, but she still had that strange sensation from before lingering in her mind.

It hadn't felt like mere physical discomfort. It had felt more like something clinging to her.

"It was a curse."

The spirit pearl inside the Ziyun Ring rolled out. The voice of Elder Huanmeng, who had been residing within the pearl, sounded: "Someone used their blood essence to cast a curse on you. Not a high-level one — that young man helped you deal with it."

Ye Wanwan was puzzled. "A curse?"

"Something like this requires your date of birth along with a personal item of yours to work. Under normal circumstances it wouldn't affect a cultivator. But you're severely injured and your constitution is weak right now, so it had some effect on you for a while."

Ye Wanwan: "...The harm is minimal, but the insult is considerable?"

Elder Huanmeng: "...Fitting."

"Something Ye Qian would stoop to." Ye Wanwan reduced it to two words. "Petty."

Still, since the person had gone to the trouble, Ye Wanwan wasn't about to fail to return the gesture.

She turned her hand over and produced talisman paper, using water as ink and drawing three talismans in rapid succession. The spirit talismans floated in midair. Ye Wanwan swiftly formed the hand seals, and the fire-attribute golden core she had retrieved rose into view.

The talisman paper enclosed the fire-attribute golden core, absorbing the energy from it, locking onto it bit by bit.

Elder Huanmeng watched, transfixed. "What are you doing?"

"Have you heard of spiritual energy flow locking?"

Elder Huanmeng knew perfectly well — "The energy that circulates through the body is called the spiritual flow," he began automatically, then caught himself. "Who do you think you're talking to, one of your junior disciples?"

Even newly initiated disciples knew this.

Ye Wanwan lowered her head with a quiet smile and reached out a finger to lightly tap the golden core from a distance. "This golden core still carries the pattern of her spiritual energy circulation. It belongs to her."

"I use spirit talismans to disrupt the circulation pattern. Can you imagine what that would mean for Ye Qian back at Wushang Sect?"

The realization hit Elder Huanmeng like a jolt. "...Good lord."

This was far more sophisticated and vicious than any curse.

Ye Wanwan said calmly: "She won't die from it. But as long as she cultivates, everything will be twice as hard for half the result. Everything she attempts will meet with interference. It won't last very long — but it will make her thoroughly miserable for a month or two."

"This is my return gift."

Courtesy demanded reciprocity.

If she wanted to play that game with her, she couldn't blame Ye Wanwan for playing it better.

Elder Huanmeng, Xingze, and Mengling all crouched behind a pillar at a distance, watching Ye Wanwan from afar. "This girl......"

Mengling: "...Never cross her. Not ever!"

Xingze said in its little voice: "I'm going to follow her for life!"

Then Xingze thought of something and looked at the other two. "Wait — why am I hiding back here with you two? I have a master now!"

And with that, it proudly transformed into a small stone and rolled toward Ye Wanwan.

"Master~"

Mengling: "......"

Elder Huanmeng: "......"

Sycophantic little spirit.

Ye Wanwan hadn't restricted their freedom — but Mengling's freedom only extended to a small five-element cage, and Elder Huanmeng remained in the spirit pearl. Only Xingze could inhabit its little stone form and move freely throughout the cave residence, keeping watch over the other two — one companion spirit and one fragmented soul memory.

After Ye Wanwan told Xingze not to leave the cave, she began circulating her cultivation technique to assess her condition.

Her conclusion: somewhat bad.

But not catastrophically bad.

She had taken the full force of Wùzhēn's palm head-on.

All five golden cores had sustained damage, but none had shattered — and after some repair, they would still be functional. Better than she'd expected. She had thought none of the five would survive.

But repairing them would require Core Stabilization Pills.

Ji Changhuai had given her one out of guilt before — that one would come in handy. But it wasn't enough. She would need at least five Core Stabilization Pills.

"Core Stabilization Pills are still too limited in effect. Better to see what else there might be."

Ye Wanwan had been mulling over which medicinal ingredients she'd need, but when her gaze landed on Elder Huanmeng, she suddenly remembered the memory inheritance — and swiftly turned her focus inward to search for methods to repair golden cores.

She found two — Rain Dew Nourishing Core Pill and Xuanjing Core Stabilizing Powder.

But both required two fourth-grade spirit herbs as primary ingredients. She had obtained some third-grade herbs from the Huanmeng Secret Realm, but none at the fourth grade.

Elder Huanmeng sighed. "In the old days, never mind fourth grade — fifth, sixth, even seventh grade herbs were all available in the secret realm. But now..."

Long since stripped bare.

Ye Wanwan considered. She had to find a way to obtain them.

The injury had to be treated.

Five golden cores, after all.

All of a sudden, "Someone's coming." Both Elder Huanmeng and Mengling flashed back inside the Ziyun Ring in an instant. Ye Wanwan pulled Xingze close to her as well.

She looked up — and found Pei Xuan standing at the door.

chapters.title: Wanwan Pays Respects to Her Master
chapters.content:
Pei Xuan stood alone in the courtyard before the entrance. In this space where all four seasons had their place, winter snow was in full reign — snowflakes drifted through the air everywhere, and he seemed to blend into them seamlessly.

Cold. Without emotion.

Like a block of ice.

Or like a snowflake with nowhere to land.

He seemed close, yet felt very far away.

But in this moment, Ye Wanwan could see on Pei Xuan's face a trace of something — contemplation, and a rare flicker of concern.

Remarkably new.

Ye Wanwan rose and slowly walked toward him. "Master."

Pei Xuan heard her and turned, gave a slight nod, and looked at her. "Are you better?"

Ye Wanwan: "Much better."

The two of them stood on either side of the threshold. Ye Wanwan felt it was rather odd. "Won't you come in, Master?"

Pei Xuan didn't enter. He said: "Hold out your hand."

Ye Wanwan held out her hand in puzzlement.

A qiankun pouch and two lacquered boxes settled into her palm — heavy, solid, like a wordless instruction from the person before her.

"This is fourth-grade Rain Dew herb and fourth-grade fire Xuanjing crystal. I knew you would be trying to repair your golden cores once you woke up — these two spirit herbs can help you mend your water core and your fire core. The remaining three are less urgent. Fifth Senior Brother is already on his way back. He'll bring three fourth-grade spirit herbs with him. That will take care of everything."

Ye Wanwan's hand closed tight. "Master......"

Pei Xuan said simply: "As for the rest — keep it and use it. If there is anything you lack, tell me."

"Master!"

Pei Xuan paused. Perhaps sensing the turbulence of emotion the young woman was trying to hold back, he added a few more words. "I don't often spend time with people. Among my eight martial siblings, we each go our own way as a rule. Taking in a young girl as a disciple has come without much experience on my part. But there is one thing — a disciple of mine, Pei Xuan's disciple, is not someone who can be pushed around by just anyone."

"From now on, go wherever you wish in the outside world and do as you please. If anything happens, your master will bear it."

"Whatever you want to do — do it."

"Don't worry about implicating the sect." Pei Xuan said with composure. "We can handle it."

Ye Wanwan's eyes grew red at the rims. She could feel the traces of having just come back from outside that still clung to Pei Xuan — and those medicinal herbs... and the pattern on the lacquered boxes.

That was Wushang Sect's pattern. He had gone there.

Just saying thank you — those two words were too light.

Ye Wanwan brushed aside that small surge of sentimental tears and took out a lacquered box from her Ziyun Ring. With both hands she offered it respectfully to Pei Xuan, and said with sincerity: "Master, this is for you."

Pei Xuan was slightly taken aback. "For me?"

Ye Wanwan: "Yes. A fifth-grade wood-fire spirit."

Pei Xuan's fingers curled slightly. "You......"

Ye Wanwan said quietly: "Some time ago I heard the Sect Master mention that you possess ice and fire dual spirit roots, yet you have always remained on the snow mountain and never come down. If my guess is right, your fire-attribute power is likely too strong and requires the ice and snow to suppress it. A wood-fire spirit is the gentlest of its kind and can neutralize fire poison."

She looked up, her smile bright. "I believe it should be useful."

Pei Xuan looked at the lacquered box in the young woman's hand for a long moment. Then he took it. "Yes. It is useful."

Ye Wanwan said: "This is only fifth grade. If I happen to come across a higher grade one in the future, I'll find one for you."

Pei Xuan: "Do your best. Don't force it."

Ye Wanwan: "I won't."

Silence fell between them, but Ye Wanwan was already learning to fill it herself. "Then I'll also accept what Master gave me. I can use it however I like, is that right?"

Pei Xuan said: "It's yours. Even if you toss it around for fun, that's your prerogative. I won't interfere."

"I won't toss it around for fun. I'll put it to good use."

As she spoke, the young woman seemed to think of something. She stepped back two paces, sank to both knees, pressed her hands together and touched them to her forehead in a deep, full bow. "Wanwan pays respects to her Master."

Pei Xuan was quiet for a long while. Ye Wanwan did not rise.

Across the wind and snow of the courtyard, the young woman knelt straight and still — but with a reverence that was entirely genuine.

On the other side of the threshold.

Pei Xuan's figure also remained motionless for a long while. He met this bow from Ye Wanwan with equal solemnity.

Because both of them understood — this bow carried extraordinary weight.

It was Ye Wanwan's recognition, offered from the heart.

After a long silence, Pei Xuan said softly: "Rise."

Ye Wanwan stood, eyes curved into a smile. "Master."

Pei Xuan answered and departed with the gift.

Ye Wanwan watched him go with quiet respect, and only when Pei Xuan's figure had disappeared entirely from view did she lower her gaze to the lacquered boxes in her hand. She raised her hand and gently ran her fingers over the Wushang Sect's markings on the surface.

"It's all in the past now."

The quiet murmur seemed meant for no one but herself.

Like the markings she had just smoothed away.

Everything — was in the past.

Leaving the Ziling Cave Residence, Pei Xuan sat on a stone platform and stared at the wood-fire spirit for a long time, thinking at length. Then he tucked the box away and headed to the main peak to find Li Mingde, who was in the middle of experimenting with a new recipe.

"Senior Brother, there's something I want to show you."

Li Mingde was surprised. "What sort of thing would bring you all the way down the mountain to find me?"

Pei Xuan solemnly pushed the lacquered box forward. "Take a look."

Li Mingde opened it, saw the warm glow of the wood-fire spirit within, and looked up with genuine surprise. "A fifth-grade wood-fire spirit, and quite fine quality too — a little below your seventh-grade wood-fire spirit, but still a solid piece. So what are you planning to......"

"My disciple gave it to me."

Li Mingde: "......"

He stared at Pei Xuan. "Little Wanwan gave it to you?"

Not given to Little Wanwan?

Pei Xuan inclined his head. Repeating: "She gave it."

Li Mingde felt aggrieved. "What a good disciple."

Satisfied with this response, Pei Xuan took the lacquered box and left. He went next to Qingcong Mountain, found Xunyin, and told him everything. Xunyin: "......"

From Qingcong Mountain he went to Jian Peak and found Yan Ju.

Yan Ju was seething. "Are you here looking for a fight?!"

Knowing perfectly well he'd taken in a troublesome disciple.

Pei Xuan considered. "If you'd like a pointer or two from me, I'm willing."

Yan Ju's eyes lit up instantly. "Really?"

It had been many years since Pei Xuan had made a move.

"Really."

Pei Xuan opened a virtual battlefield. "Come in."

Yan Ju followed at once.

Two hours later, Yan Ju lay spread-eagle on the ground. Though covered in injuries from head to foot, his eyes were bright and alive. "Satisfying! Come again next time!"

Yan Ju had a feeling — fight Pei Xuan two more times, and he'd be able to break through the bottleneck of Nascent Soul and step into Deity Transformation.

"Hey, fight me again next month, will you."

Pei Xuan paid no attention to the request and turned a communication stone over in his hand, as though deep in thought.

Suddenly, Yan Ju felt his communication screen snap open of its own accord.

A purple communication signal!

Second only to red in terms of urgency.

Yan Ju: "......"

Everyone in Tianyi Sect was startled.

Senior Brother Gu Canglan asked gravely: "What's going on — has something happened to the sect?"

Second Senior Brother Luo Qingfeng was also urgent: "Did someone bully us? Wait for me — I'll finish this secret realm and be right back!"

Sixth Senior Sister Liu Menglan was thoroughly bewildered: "Did Seventh Junior Brother send this? Did the snow mountain collapse? Or did Seventh Junior Brother wipe out a sect? Was the enemy strong? Did you get rid of them cleanly? Any loose ends? Do I need to come help clean up?"

Senior and Second Brother: "...Sixth Junior Sister?"

Sixth Senior Sister immediately straightened: "I'm joking."

It was Fifth Senior Brother Lu Qingxuan who cut to the heart of the matter: "A few days ago, Seventh Junior Brother wrote to say Little Six got hurt. And now suddenly this signal — don't tell me Little Six has taken a turn for the worse?"

All four senior siblings began asking questions at once, desperate for an answer.

Only Yan Ju and Xunyin buried their faces in their hands in silent anguish.

Damn.

chapters.title: Are You Sure You Want to Upgrade?
chapters.content:
Li Mingde spoke from within the communication array: "Everyone, don't panic. Nothing serious has happened to the sect, and Little Six is perfectly fine."

Sixth Senior Brother Liu Menglan didn't believe it. "Who sends a purple signal just for fun!"

Pei Xuan said calmly: "Nothing serious has happened. I only wanted to show everyone something."

The image flickered to reveal a lacquered box.

Liu Menglan recognized it at once: "A fifth-grade wood-fire spirit."

Lu Qingxuan was also puzzled: "This is a fine item, but enough to warrant a purple signal?"

Pei Xuan: "My disciple gave it to me."

Everyone: "......"

A beat passed, and then the entire communication array erupted.

They wanted to curse him, but on second thought — this was Seventh Junior Brother. You didn't provoke him. Yet — the indignation!

Before Senior Brother and Second Senior Brother could even speak, Fifth Senior Brother had already exploded.

"What do you mean?! Your disciple gives you something this valuable! Why does she get to?!" Fifth Senior Brother Lu Qingxuan roared. "Seventh Junior Brother — give me your disciple!"

Everyone: "......"

Pei Xuan: "Fifth Senior Brother, you already have one."

"Oh... I suppose I do. Haven't been taking care of them properly."

Xunyin was grinding his teeth. "When are you coming back?!"

"Within half a month."

"Get here faster!"

The group descended into comfortable chaos, but beneath the jostling banter ran an undisguised current of envy and indignation. Yan Ju gave a cold laugh: "Little Six was someone I had my eye on originally."

Pei Xuan: "You couldn't have taught her."

Yan Ju: "......"

Everyone covered their faces and sighed.

"A good child — it's only her first time out in a secret realm, and she still remembered to bring her master a gift." Liu Menglan let out a mournful sound. "What a genuinely good child."

Gu Canglan said quietly: "This child has a fine character."

Luo Qingfeng: "What's the use in just praising her? The little one went out once and came back this seriously injured. Shouldn't we as her martial uncles say something?"

"Beat up Wushang Sect?" Liu Menglan offered. "I'm available!"

Nobody bothered with Liu Menglan the battle fanatic. Gu Canglan said: "I came across a seventh-grade spirit herb a few days ago by chance. When Junior Brother has time, head to the spirit market — I'll trade it to you. A gift when meeting Little Six for the first time."

The others chimed in: "Right, we should all give a first-meeting gift."

One by one, everyone began thinking of what treasures they had to offer Ye Wanwan.

Pei Xuan didn't refuse.

Well — the communication array was already open. He might as well get his disciple some benefits while he was at it.

At the close of things, Luo Qingfeng suddenly thought of his own disciple. "Where's Little Five right now? He should have reunited with his senior brothers and sisters by this point."

"He was in this secret realm together with them. The young one held his own well enough — knew to stick by his own people and make sure they weren't mistreated." Xunyin offered a brief assessment, clearly satisfied.

Luo Qingfeng: "That's fine then. I always knew that boy had a decent character. One look at his bone constitution and you could tell he was destined to be a Tianyi Sect disciple — it's just that he was rebellious, always trying to run off. Don't know what was going through his head. I chased him for five years while he ran for five years."

Luo Qingfeng looked pained. "If Senior Brother hadn't kept watch, I nearly didn't manage to catch him at all."

Yan Ju said coolly: "Senior Brother can rest easy. Once someone enters Tianyi Sect, there's no reason they should ever be able to leave."

Born a Tianyi Sect disciple.

Die a Tianyi Sect ghost.

You've already arrived.

Naturally, you stay.

Xunyin chuckled cheerfully. "Looking at these children, they all seem to have good character. This batch of seedlings — promising."

"Indeed, indeed."

Everyone was moved: Tianyi Sect finally has a next generation to carry things on.

Something to show their ancestors!

Lu Qingxuan said: "Seventh Junior Brother, I've found all three fourth-grade herbs you asked me to look for. I'll send them through the spirit market now so you don't have to wait half a month for me."

Pei Xuan: "Good."

Li Mingde mourned: "You lot — barely prosperous for five minutes and already throwing money around."

The spirit market charged transaction fees.

Lu Qingxuan said: "Sect Master Senior Brother, which of us is short on spirit stones? Seventh Junior Brother certainly isn't. Are you actually worried about him?"

Pei Xuan said flatly: "True. The entire sect owes me money."

Everyone: "......"

In closed cultivation. Do not disturb.

Ye Wanwan had no idea she had just accumulated a great many first-meeting gifts. At this moment she was cataloguing her own spoils — she had only brought out a portion of them before, and Fang He'an had already told her to put the rest away. So she'd never had the chance to do a full inventory of everything she'd collected from the secret realm.

She sorted all of the spirit herbs from the valley by category.

The total count of ordinary spirit herbs numbered in the tens of thousands.

First-grade spirit herbs and medicines came to over nineteen thousand.

Second grade numbered three to four thousand.

Third grade was scarce — only three to four hundred, some not yet fully mature, which she could continue cultivating in the spirit lake until they reached fourth grade.

Ye Wanwan made her selections carefully.

She divided all herbs below second grade into a thirty-seventy split — thirty percent for herself, seventy percent stored in a holding ring to be turned over to her sect.

From the mature third-grade herbs, she selected eight based on their attributes.

"This one is for Senior Sister Bai."

— Nourishing for the body.

"This one is for Senior Brother Fang."

— Nourishing for the spirit.

"This one is for Li Wanzhi."

— For healing injuries.

"And this one is for... Shen Nanzhou."

— For the eyes.

She had no idea what Shen Nanzhou might be lacking — in all likelihood, nothing at all. So Ye Wanwan simply chose the two most beautiful stalks she could find among the spirit-replenishing herbs.

"And there's also a share for the eldest senior brother I haven't yet met."

After setting aside gifts for her senior brothers and sisters, Ye Wanwan moved on to preparing something for Li Mingde, Yan Ju, and Xunyin as well.

Elder Huanmeng and Mengling watched the whole process, wondering: was this the same little terror who'd retaliated without mercy just moments ago?

This was... extraordinarily generous.

By the time Ye Wanwan finished organizing everything, three hours had passed. Night had fallen, yet the young woman was still perfectly alert. She took the remaining ordinary spirit herbs and put them up for sale on the spirit market.

The spirit market had specialized trading houses in addition to individual stalls that would buy herbs in bulk — though at a lower price than the trading houses down the mountain, the convenience made up for it.

And it also allowed her to conceal her identity.

With quantities this large, Ye Wanwan had no intention of selling them at the mountain base.

She had been planning to sell her entire thirty-percent share of ordinary herbs on the market, but Elder Huanmeng stopped her. "Don't you have the inheritance of a great pill-refining master in me? When you refine pills, you'll need large quantities of ordinary spirit herbs — if you sell all of these now, you'll just have to buy them back later."

"Why bother."

Ye Wanwan said evenly: "I understand. But I've thought about it — the herbs I'm selling are basic ones, and they won't be hard to buy back when needed. Right now, I need spirit stones more urgently."

Elder Huanmeng was puzzled. "What do you need them for?"

Ye Wanwan: "It's useful."

She sold all the basic herbs and obtained 1.2 million spirit stones. After sorting through the other sellable items, her final total came to 2.6 million.

Then the young woman brought out the spirit crystals Pei Xuan had given her.

Twelve spirit crystals.

Each spirit crystal was equivalent to one million spirit stones.

That came to twelve million in total.

Ye Wanwan's gaze dropped slightly. Before now she hadn't dared use them — she'd been afraid that after leaving in three years, she would have no way to repay this kindness. But now...

She could use them.

She deposited all the spirit crystals into the spirit market, returned to her bamboo house, and the residence upgrade screen materialized and blinked before her. Ye Wanwan selected her third type of dwelling.

A small cave residence at 14 million spirit stones.

"Fellow Daoist, are you certain you wish to use 14 million spirit stones to upgrade your cave residence?"

Ye Wanwan: "Confirmed."

chapters.title: An Independent World
chapters.content:
Ordinary thatched cottage: 10,000.

Refined bamboo house: 30,000 to 1 million.

High-grade manor: 3 million to 5 million.

Small cave residence: 14 million to 30 million.

Mid-grade cave residence: 50 million to 100 million.

High-grade cave residence: 1 billion.

Compound small cave residence: over 1 billion. This option appeared greyed out on the screen and had not yet been unlocked.

Ye Wanwan chose the lowest tier of the small cave residence range, at 14 million spirit stones.

Dwellings within the same tier varied in price, but the time flow rate remained the same — the only differences were the size of the space and the level of refinement, which accounted for the price gap.

Ye Wanwan didn't need anything spacious or lavish. What she needed was the time flow rate.

The time flow rate of a small cave residence was five to one.

She had estimated that the highest tier — the compound cave residence — could reach a flow rate of eight or even ten to one, but since that page remained locked and unavailable to her, she couldn't be certain.

Her assumption was that she didn't yet have the access level required for it.

But for now, five to one was sufficient.

The further along one went, the more spirit stones were burned.

The thatched cottage at the beginning was like a free starter gift in a game — priced low enough to lure you in. Once you experienced the benefits, the price leaped to an entirely different level.

Straight into the hundreds of thousands, the tens of millions.

But for Ye Wanwan, it was worth it.

Five days inside for every one day outside.

One outside month could be made to equal five cultivation months.

And the anti-indulgence restriction had also changed — from a matter of days to a full outside month. As long as she could carve out a month of external time, she could spend five months cultivating within.

Worthwhile.

Ye Wanwan chose "confirm" without hesitation.

The bamboo house changed its appearance entirely. The small cave residence took the form of a modest little courtyard — very simple and unassuming.

But what satisfied Ye Wanwan was that it had been more generous this time: there were two quiet cultivation chambers in the east and west wings, a refining room, a pill-refining room, and in the center a small courtyard with a tiny flowing-light barrier array overhead.

Tools and furnishings, naturally, were not included.

Only the space itself had been provided.

The rules were plain — if you wanted anything, spend the spirit stones to buy it.

In this place, as long as you spent enough spirit stones, it would provide you with whatever you needed.

But as the dwelling stood, Ye Wanwan was already quite pleased with it.

She brought Xingze, Mengling, and Elder Huanmeng inside with her. The moment Elder Huanmeng stepped into this space, his expression filled with shock — genuine astonishment.

"This is a spatial realm?"

"How can such a spatial realm exist — its rules are entirely unlike those of the outside world, defined by another entirely."

"Whose is this?"

Three questions, one after another.

Ye Wanwan: "I don't know."

Elder Huanmeng's shock was beyond measure. Even as only a memory construct, the inherited memories he carried offered no insight into this. He even felt — that behind this spirit market lay an enormous and mysterious design.

Because this was a void realm entirely independent of the Nine Provinces.

A world fully capable of evading the observation of any immortal — a world unto itself.

Elder Huanmeng wanted to explore it, but very quickly found he had no way to probe this spirit market at all. When he attempted to examine the inner workings of this world, a terrifying pressure descended upon him.

It felt like a warning — or like something was poised to erase him completely.

Elder Huanmeng felt fear.

The fear of death and of utter annihilation.

Only when Ye Wanwan spoke did that terrifying pressure vanish.

"Don't waste your effort. For now, the spirit market has only unlocked the home and trading systems. Everything else is unavailable."

Beyond the cave residence was a desert.

An endless, boundless desert — walk in any direction and you'd never see the edge, never come across a neighbor. That sort of thing didn't exist here. Within the territory of your cave residence, you were entirely alone.

And the token entry was locked to a soul signature.

No matter which token was used.

As long as the soul was verified, Ye Wanwan could enter.

The downside of using the disciple token, however, was that Tianyi Sect had a unique communication array and tracking formation, which made it very easy to be located and have her identity uncovered.

That was why she had asked Li Wanzhi to set up a few alternate accounts.

But no matter which one she used, entering the home would always take her to the same cave residence.

She couldn't upgrade a new one for every alternate account — the spirit stone cost was not something she was willing to endure.

Elder Huanmeng sat on the stone steps of the courtyard in what looked like a philosophical crisis. Xingze, for its part, rolled back and forth contentedly — this way, then that way.

Then it extended both its little arms and legs, waddled over to Ye Wanwan, and planted itself there with its hands on its hips. "Master, the time flow rate here is good, but the spiritual energy isn't nearly as strong as in Xingze Lake."

"It is."

Ye Wanwan answered just as plainly: "Which is why I'm going to borrow Xingze Lake to repair my golden cores."

Xingze asked: "How do you borrow it?"

Ye Wanwan: "You open the Ziyun Ring here and let me go inside — then isn't it already five times the flow rate?"

Xingze, Mengling, Elder Huanmeng: "...How clever."

Ye Wanwan: "...I think I'm beginning to understand why you failed your ascension."

Elder Huanmeng: "......"

That was a little too blunt.

Elder Huanmeng said with great dignity: "That wasn't me. I am merely a memory construct carrying inherited knowledge."

Ye Wanwan: Do you think I believe you?

Xingze opened the Ziyun Ring's entrance. To let Ye Wanwan enjoy the view of the new cave residence while ensuring the time flow rate would definitely apply, it opened it halfway — one half connected to the courtyard of the compound, the other half connected to the Ziyun Ring.

Even the core-condensing fruit tree appeared within the courtyard.

Its branches swayed freely, its spiritual energy commanding.

The entire courtyard became filled with rich spiritual energy.

Ye Wanwan hadn't expected it could work that way.

Xingze said proudly: "Master's ring is high-grade and a form-shifting tool in its own right — it can merge with me perfectly, so it can take on any shape."

To Xingze, this ring was like a vessel crafted specifically for it.

No matter which companion spirit held it, they would love this ring.

Xingze thought — it was a good thing it had recognized the ring early.

Ye Wanwan was also very pleased. She rewarded it with a Xuanling Pill. "For you."

Xingze caught the Xuanling Pill in both its tiny hands. It absorbed the spiritual essence within and couldn't help but light up, scurrying over at a run. "Master, master — where did you buy this pill? The spiritual essence and life force in this are incredible — are there more?"

Ye Wanwan had already settled down beneath the core-condensing fruit tree. Hearing the question, she replied: "I grew the Xuanling grass myself and pressed it into the pill myself."

Life force?! And spiritual essence?!

Mengling whooshed over to Xingze's side. "Let me taste it!"

"No."

Afraid Mengling would grab it, Xingze shoved the whole thing in its mouth, covered its face with both hands — and swallowed it down.

Mengling was furious. "You're a rock — can you even digest it? You're actually eating it? Can you even produce anything afterward?!"

"I can."

And with that, it squatted down, and with a small sound, produced a tiny bit of medicinal residue. It finished and looked back at Mengling with great satisfaction, as if showing off: see that?

Mengling: "......"

Ye Wanwan: "......"

"You two — get out of my sight. Now!"

chapters.title: It Seems the Lamp Is Nearly Burning Out
chapters.content:
A moment later.

Xingze and Mengling sat side by side on the stone steps, looking thoroughly aggrieved.

Against Xingze's black stone form, Mengling was wrapped in red talisman threads — like a five-spice dumpling tied up for the pot — struggling with great effort to poke arms and legs out through the strands, shooting venomous glances at Xingze.

Xingze had its head drooping, turned away, refusing to acknowledge it.

Elder Huanmeng was still contemplating the meaning of spiritual existence.

Ye Wanwan swept a look over these three spirits and inwardly let out a long sigh. She had really gone and collected herself three headaches.

The young woman settled her mind, shut out all distractions, formed five talisman seals, laid down a guardian formation array, and then began to circulate her cultivation technique — the Refining Spirit Formula — beneath the tree.

As the young woman circulated the technique, ten golden cores floated out from her body, moving along the meridian pathways she had mapped on the exterior of her form.

Seeing this, Elder Huanmeng and Mengling both turned to look simultaneously.

"Golden cores externalized."

Though it wasn't the first time they had witnessed it, each time they did, the young woman's talent never failed to astonish them.

A cultivator had one golden core. From that golden core they broke through to Nascent Soul, then step by step into Deity Transformation, Void Refinement, Body Fusion, Tribulation Crossing, Great Completion — and finally, ascension.

Survive the ascension, and one became a true immortal.

But the young woman's path was unlike any of theirs.

She had ten. And there would likely be more.

At this moment, the ten golden cores were moving along the pathways the young woman had laid out. Elder Huanmeng, with his vast experience, had long since discerned that the route Ye Wanwan had mapped was also drawn from the meridian pathways within her body — extended outward.

It was another meridian map.

As if beyond her body there existed another vast, sweeping network of meridians, and she was leading these golden cores to conquer those meridians, claiming them as her own.

This was also why Mengling would be dominated the moment it drew near to Ye Wanwan's space.

Because within this space, Ye Wanwan was the sole creator of its rules.

Or there was a more fitting word for it.

— Domain.

A Golden Core-stage cultivator who had awakened the domain power that normally only reveals itself at the Deity Transformation stage.

And used it with complete ease.

How could that not make her a genius?

Mengling muttered under its breath, but this time it had been thoroughly subdued. After all, the dreamscape space had been destroyed by Shen Nanzhou, and it had nowhere else to go. Following Ye Wanwan at least gave it a foothold. Follow Shen Nanzhou, and it might as well wait to die.

That young man was even more unhinged.

Elder Huanmeng murmured low: "Give her the time to grow — I don't even dare imagine how far she'll go."

Because even Elder Huanmeng couldn't tell what Ye Wanwan's next step would be.

He only felt that this young woman would bring the cultivation world something enormous — a great and staggering surprise.

Or perhaps a great and staggering fright.

Of the ten golden cores, five bore cracks.

Ye Wanwan drew those five toward her and set her sights first on the fire core. She brought out the fourth-grade fire Xuanjing crystal, which hovered in the air before her.

She circulated the remaining nine golden cores. Driven by the flow of spiritual power, the energy of the Xuanjing crystal was coaxed out bit by bit, and the fire core entwined with it.

Under the workings of the spiritual power, the core was mended using the pure concentrated energy of fire.

The process was tedious and monotonous.

It took Ye Wanwan a full month and a half before she succeeded, but with the experience from the first, the second — her water-attribute golden core — went considerably faster.

Only twenty days.

With two golden cores repaired, the five motes of condensed elemental energy within Ye Wanwan's body also showed signs of advancement.

Water, fire spirit roots: Qi Refinement, level thirteen.

Wood spirit root: Qi Refinement, level six.

Metal, earth: level five.

Ye Wanwan curled her fingers into a loose fist, thinking: "It's no wonder these are fourth-grade spirit herbs. The powerful spiritual essence not only repaired two golden cores fully — the energy that remained even pushed the third-stage elemental groups into a breakthrough. One step away from Foundation Building."

But looking at the remaining three elemental groups, she didn't rush.

In order to maintain the balance of the five elements, it was best to advance all five at once when the time came. So Ye Wanwan was in no hurry.

She calculated the time — sixty-five days inside the cave residence meant thirteen days had passed in the outside world. Nearly half a month. She should go out and have a look.

Ye Wanwan drew all her golden cores back within and stood. She found Mengling and Xingze — one a lamp wick, one a stone — each dozing on opposite ends of the stone steps, as if each had staked out their own little territory.

Elder Huanmeng had already retreated into the spirit pearl to sleep.

Ye Wanwan gathered them all up and looked at the dimmed remnant soul within the pearl. She said quietly: "You can't hold on much longer, can you."

That was why it had been in such a hurry to find someone to pass its inheritance to — because it couldn't wait.

The secret realm's collapse had taken it to the end of its rope as well.

Ye Wanwan ran a light fingertip over the spirit pearl. Perhaps she could find some spirit herbs for nourishing a soul.

Wusuan fruit would work — but Elder Huanmeng couldn't consume it directly, and merely absorbing the fruit's spiritual essence would be far too weak to have much effect.

A Soul Nourishment Pill would be better.

Ye Wanwan thought it over and decided to add pill-refining to her daily routine.

Setting aside one hour each day should be enough.

If it wasn't — then she'd add more.

Time, when squeezed, would always yield.

Ye Wanwan exited the spirit market. This time she browsed the stalls for a bit and noticed that no one had bought her Xuanling grass yet — she didn't mind and simply put up the two newest talismans she had drawn.

The moment they were posted, someone bought them immediately.

"Ding ding ding — congratulations, stall owner. Fellow Daoist 'Loaded' has purchased your Fire Warding Talisman. 14,000 spirit stones successfully credited."

Ye Wanwan: "......"

Him again?

Before Ye Wanwan could say a word, the wealthy young master struck first: "What's the matter with you, little stall owner — no new stock for so long? Giving up the business? Suddenly flush with spirit stones? Too good for money now?"

Ye Wanwan gathered herself. "I've been away on business recently."

The other party clicked their tongue a few times. "You cultivation people are always such a bother. Fine — what does this talisman do?"

"Fire Warding Talisman. Offensive."

"Loaded": "...Doesn't seem particularly useful. Ordinary offensive talismans are all over the spirit market. You're charging this much for something like that — aren't you ripping people off?"

Ye Wanwan: "Buy the other one too."

"Ding ding ding — congratulations, stall owner. Fellow Daoist 'Loaded' has purchased your Water Conducting Talisman. 14,000 spirit stones successfully credited."

Ye Wanwan: "......" This person really is loaded.

Says buy, buys.

"What's with one fire and one water?"

Ye Wanwan: "Have you ever tried fire and water striking each other?"

"Loaded": "...You mean, at the same time?"

Ye Wanwan: "Together. One plus one is more than three. This offensive talisman can land one strike on a Nascent Soul cultivator — but only one."

"Throw them and run. The water mist produced when the talisman's effect ends helps you escape. The window is twenty breaths."

"Loaded" was quiet for a very long time, before finally responding, voice slightly taut: "The water mist can block a Nascent Soul cultivator's soul-sense search?"

Ye Wanwan heard that and knew immediately the other person understood the crux of it — they had grasped the most important point at once. She curved her lips. "Yes. Which is why these talismans are sold as a pair. What they're selling isn't just the attack. It's also a way to save your life."

"Loaded"'s voice went low: "Are there more? I'll take ten sets!"

Ye Wanwan: "No. If you want more, place an order in advance."

"Ding ding ding — congratulations, stall owner. Fellow Daoist 'Just Browsing' has pre-ordered ten sets of your Fire Warding Talisman and Water Conducting Talisman. 280,000 spirit stones successfully credited."

Ye Wanwan: ?

"Loaded": ?

"Loaded" turned and spotted the figure beside him. He called out at full volume: "Oi! Friend — how many times has this been now?"

Every time he came here, this friend stubbornly showed up and bought alongside him.

And every time, with the air of someone doing something deeply suspicious.

"Just browsing." The other party said quietly. This was the first time Ye Wanwan had heard this client's voice. Compared to the wealthy young master's vivid, boisterous energy, this one sounded like...

An old person at the end of their days.

It was a very young-sounding voice — yet it seemed, somehow, that the lamp was nearly out of oil.

chapters.title: I'm the One Who's Fang He'an
chapters.content:
Ye Wanwan's heart clenched.

She had heard a voice like this before. When the man who had raised this body was dying, his voice had carried the same drawn-out, struggling quality — and even though Ye Wanwan had been very young at the time, she had known that his vital energy had been spent beyond recovery. And so in his final moments he had given her earnest instructions, telling her she must listen to her teachers and masters and remain obediently at Wushang Sect.

A pity she hadn't managed that.

The voice of "Just Browsing" before her now was younger.

Judging by the tone, perhaps twenty-three or twenty-four years old.

But it sounded as though they had been bedridden for a very long time.

Yet given how many talismans they were buying, they had to be a cultivator — so why were they so depleted...

"Loaded" was also taken aback. "Why do you sound so completely out of energy?"

"Just Browsing" said softly: "Stayed up to cultivate."

"...Young person, take care of your health. Overindulgence takes a toll, you know."

"...Hm?"

"Alright, alright — if you want to buy, buy. The little stall owner isn't going anywhere. Little stall owner, can I order another ten sets? And I'll take ten of those protection talismans too."

Ye Wanwan: "...A protection talisman only needs to be one."

"Not for me. I go through them fast."

"Loaded" waved a hand grandly and transferred six hundred thousand spirit stones to Ye Wanwan outright. After the platform's cut, four hundred and twenty thousand reached Ye Wanwan.

Ye Wanwan: "The protection talisman is ten thousand each."

He had paid six hundred thousand for thirty talismans — that came to twenty thousand per talisman.

"The extra is for you. Remember to deliver early."

Ye Wanwan thought for a moment. "Three days from now — I have things to attend to recently."

"Loaded": "...Don't spend all your time in closed cultivation. See the person beside you? That's what happens when you cultivate too long and go astray."

Ye Wanwan paid him no mind and turned to the other client. "Delivery in three days."

"Just Browsing": "Mm."

She pocketed the spirit stones and looked at the empty stall. Perhaps she could also put some pills up for sale.

The young woman left the spirit market and returned to the Ziling Cave Residence. At a single glance, she spotted three people crouching at the main entrance.

Bai Jian was gazing at the fruit in the courtyard, eyes soft with yearning, as if waiting for the right moment of ripeness.

Fang He'an had his arm around Li Wanzhi's shoulder, telling him: "I think we can push your training regimen a little harder."

Li Wanzhi: "...Senior Brother, you're the one hitting, and I'm the one getting hit. And if we push it harder, I'll still be the one getting hit."

Fang He'an: "Our Junior Uncle — which is to say, your master — has said that cultivation techniques are important but physical training can't fall behind. He told me I absolutely must supervise you properly."

"Last time you hit me so hard I couldn't get out of bed for two days."

"I went easy on you. Otherwise you could always try sparring with Senior Sister."

Li Wanzhi: "...Just say you want me dead."

Fang He'an: "It's settled then. Now that my master's back, there's plenty of medicine to patch you up with."

Li Wanzhi: "......"

Ye Wanwan listened to this ordinary exchange and stepped out of the cave residence. "Second Senior Sister, Third Senior Brother, Fourth Senior Brother."

All three turned around at once.

"Little Junior Sister!"

Bai Jian swept over to Ye Wanwan like a breath of wind, and seeing that she looked well, her eyes curved into a smile. She held out a round red apple.

"For you."

Ye Wanwan took it and noticed it was still warm from Bai Jian's hands — how long had she been cradling it? Something softened in her heart. "Senior Sister."

Bai Jian: "It's sweet."

Ye Wanwan: "Mm."

Ye Wanwan took a bite, smiling. "It's sweet."

Fang He'an said cheerfully: "Little Junior Sister looks like she's recovered well these past two weeks. Her aura is much more stable."

Ye Wanwan nodded. "Master gave me two fourth-grade spirit herbs recently. Two of my golden cores have already been repaired."

Fang He'an grinned with an air of mystery. "Then congratulations — your remaining three golden cores can be repaired too."

Ye Wanwan was taken aback.

Fang He'an planted his hands on his hips and laughed. "My master is back!"

Tianyi Sect's one and only pill-refining master had returned to the sect.

Qingcong Mountain.

Looking at the total devastation all around him, Lu Qingxuan pressed a hand to his chest in heartbreak. "Third Senior Brother, I understand you want a plot of land to grow spirit food. I have no objection. But did you really have to plow up all my spirit herbs?"

Xunyin looked completely unrepentant — trouser legs rolled up, straw hat on his head. "How am I supposed to grow spirit food without your spirit fields?"

"You have this enormous spirit field of mine, and you've killed every single thing you've planted in it — not one patch has survived." Lu Qingxuan collapsed to his knees and wailed at the withered plants all over the ground.

Xunyin was baffled. "How would I know? I followed the Shennong Scripture's method. Plant it, it dies. Every single time."

Lu Qingxuan stared at the Qingcong Mountain that had been lush and green when he left — now a barren wasteland. He lay facedown on the ground and couldn't collect himself for a long time.

"My fields......"

All withered.

"Wuwuwu......"

"Master, master!"

Four figures arrived on sword-light — two men and two women, upright and graceful.

Lu Qingxuan sprang upright in a full ninety-degree snap, brushed the dry grass off himself, and assumed the bearing of a transcendent sage. He gave a dignified nod to Li Wanzhi, who had surged forward first due to unsteady sword-riding.

"Mm. Little An, is it? You've grown quite a bit."

Li Wanzhi: "...Hm?"

Fang He'an: "......"

Xunyin: "......"

Fang He'an stepped in front of Li Wanzhi and looked Lu Qingxuan directly in the eye. His expression was blank. "Master. I'm the one who's Fang He'an."

Li Wanzhi adopted his most dignified manner and bowed respectfully. "Martial Uncle, I am Li Wanzhi, ranked fourth among the hundred and first generation of disciples."

Ye Wanwan followed with a bow. "Sixth Junior Disciple. Ye Wanwan."

Bai Jian saw everyone bowing and followed suit. "Second Junior Disciple. Bai Jian."

Xunyin shook his straw hat and beckoned them over. "Come, come, come — everyone get a good look at your Martial Uncle, or there'll be a day you go out and don't even know what he looks like."

Lu Qingxuan sent a quiet spiritual transmission: "...Stop rubbing it in."

Xunyin had already opened the communication array. "Fifth Brother just mistook his own disciple."

Everyone: "That's exactly what he'd do."

Lu Qingxuan cleared his throat and looked at Fang He'an, who was on the verge of tears with indignation. He twisted his hands and said with difficulty: "Well, you see — when I left, you were still very young."

Fang He'an started out pretending to wipe his eyes, but the more he said the more genuine it became.

"You just left and were gone for fifteen years......"

"You ran off and left me behind with nothing but a pile of books. If Senior Uncle hadn't looked after me, I wouldn't have known where to go or what to do......"

Lu Qingxuan felt genuine guilt. "Your master will stay longer this time."

"How long?"

"Just... I won't be leaving for ten years, at least."

He had to save what was left of Qingcong Mountain, at the very least.

Fang He'an pursed his lips, convinced Lu Qingxuan's reliability was zero — though he didn't care about that much right now. He pulled Lu Qingxuan forward. "Master, look at Little Junior Sister first. She took serious damage protecting us — someone smashed her golden cores."

Lu Qingxuan quickly said: "I know, I know."

As he spoke he gave Ye Wanwan a thorough, open look, the more he saw the more he liked, and he laughed as he asked: "Little Six, would you like to switch masters?"

Ye Wanwan was startled.

A cold wind swept across Qingcong Mountain, ice and snow rushing in, falling on the newly sprouted spirit seedlings. A detached voice sounded in midair.

"It seems Senior Brother is the one who wants to switch sects."

chapters.title: Warmth
chapters.content:
The temperature on Qingcong Mountain plummeted.

"My seedlings!"

Xunyin dived into the field in emergency rescue mode. "Old Seventh, pull back your ice and snow — these fragile little things can't take the cold. They'll be ruined."

Pei Xuan said evenly: "Third Senior Brother, your seedlings were going to die with or without the cold."

Xunyin: "...Could you say something encouraging for once?"

Ye Wanwan looked at the two senior figures currently at odds with each other — Lu Qingxuan and Pei Xuan — thought for a moment, and chose to walk toward Xunyin, who seemed considerably safer. "Martial Uncle, shall I have a look?"

Xunyin beamed at the sight of the young woman coming over. "You know about cultivation too? Come, come — these are seedlings your Martial Uncle has been tending for a whole year."

Ye Wanwan examined the roots and had a rough idea of the problem.

— Lack of water.

Or more precisely, the entire Qingcong Mountain was lacking water. There was almost no water element at all in the air. It would be strange if anything survived.

Ye Wanwan raised her hand and cast the Cloud-Summoning Rain Technique.

Then she cast the Pest-Warding Technique.

After a moment, the seedlings in the spirit field became lively and vibrant.

Xunyin: ...How had her short tending accomplished more than his entire year of effort? Was this what talent looked like?

He studied Ye Wanwan and murmured: "Would you still like to take on another master?"

Pei Xuan: "......"

Ye Wanwan took a small step back and bowed politely. "Martial Uncle, this isn't actually a major problem. Your aura is likely too powerful, which has affected the water element in the mountain's veins and spirit fields. If you simply suppress your aura and keep it within, it should resolve the issue."

Xunyin considered. "But I'm already keeping it quite well contained."

No one could even tell what cultivation stage he was at.

At least when he went down the mountain, people would assume he was just an honest old farmer.

Ye Wanwan pointed at something hanging at his waist. "You're concealing yourself very well, Martial Uncle. But your spirit tool is not."

Xunyin pulled the fan from his waist. "This thing?"

He raised his hand and fanned it. With a great swoosh, flames swept across half the mountainside. Fortunately Lu Qingxuan moved quickly — with a step and a sweep of his hand, a barrier went up just in time.

Otherwise half the mountain would have gone up in flames.

He was at his wit's end. "My Senior Brother! Why on earth are you carrying that thing around with you?!"

Xunyin muttered: "Isn't this the spoils of war I took from the Red Flame Devil Lord a few hundred years ago? I thought it looked nice, so I kept it on me. You know how hot this Qingcong Mountain of yours is — can't I wave a little breeze to cool down?"

Xunyin widened his eyes and immediately deflected.

Lu Qingxuan: "...Are you sure it cools things down?"

Xunyin tossed the fan away — straight to Ye Wanwan, who caught it by reflex. "Fine, fine. Never paid it much attention before. Who could have guessed the culprit was right there on my hip."

"Martial Uncle, this is......" Ye Wanwan held it out respectfully.

Xunyin waved his hand. "It's yours."

Ye Wanwan's hand tightened slightly around it. "This is a high-grade spirit tool."

Xunyin: "Too low-grade? Then come to Martial Uncle's cave residence some other day — I'll let you pick something out. I've, ah, gathered quite a few spoils of war."

"......"

Ye Wanwan looked toward Pei Xuan. Pei Xuan said: "Since Senior Brother is giving it to you, accept it."

Ye Wanwan bowed. "Thank you, Martial Uncle."

Xunyin grinned cheerfully.

Ye Wanwan thought to herself — perhaps she could make a copy of the Spirit Cultivation Technique Elder Yu Chun had given her and offer it to Martial Uncle. It wasn't a particularly high-level technique, but it ought to be useful.

Fang He'an and Bai Jian were both pleased for Ye Wanwan.

Li Wanzhi asked: "Can it be sold?"

Ye Wanwan smiled. "Of course — I'll sell you along with it, bundled together."

Li Wanzhi: "......" Junior Sister has gone bad!

At this point Pei Xuan was already speaking with Lu Qingxuan. Their exchange was simple and direct.

"Work?"

"Work."

As they spoke, Pei Xuan produced three spirit herbs.

Lu Qingxuan nodded. "I had thought putting them in the Clearspring Pool would help the blooms come faster."

There was a jade lotus.

And a Flame Blossom Essence that grew only deep within volcanic craters, as well as Earth Core Marrow that only formed in the depths of the earth.

Wood-attribute, metal-attribute, earth-attribute.

All present.

Lu Qingxuan beckoned to Ye Wanwan. "Come here, child."
