With Pei Xuan's quiet encouragement, Ye Wanwan walked over to Lu Qingxuan. She could feel his primordial spirit sweeping over her — but there was no sense of intrusive probing.

Instead, it felt like a warm spring breeze.

Like the care of an elder.

Lu Qingxuan's expression shifted to surprise. "Child, you actually absorbed both the fire Xuanjing crystal and the rain dew in just half a month? And — well, remarkable. The repair is extremely pure. You must have put in considerable effort."

Ye Wanwan answered honestly: "I used the spirit market's accelerated time flow. It actually took me over two months to complete — not just half a month."

Hearing Ye Wanwan mention using the spirit market's accelerated time flow, Pei Xuan, Xunyin, and Lu Qingxuan all paused slightly — but none of them showed much surprise.

Lu Qingxuan smiled. "Now that is a good method."

"Next, Martial Uncle is going to help you with treatment. There may be a small amount of pain — bear with it."

Ye Wanwan inclined her head. "Understood."

Seeing this, Xunyin raised his hand and a clean gust of wind carried Bai Jian, Fang He'an, and Li Wanzhi over to another part of the mountain. "Go play for a bit."

Then he raised his hand and laid down a barrier.

Holding it himself.

Pei Xuan took up his position on the other side.

Lu Qingxuan sat alone, face to face with Ye Wanwan.

Two great cultivators guarding the formation. One pill-refining master administering treatment.

Ye Wanwan found herself wondering what she had done to deserve this.

Lu Qingxuan said gently: "Your master told me — you're stubborn in your ways, and once you had the herbs, you'd definitely try to repair your golden cores on your own. But child, when elders are present, you don't have to push yourself so hard."

"Our purpose — it is to be the umbrella that shields you from wind and rain."

A vast wood-attribute spiritual power enveloped her like a warm pillar of light settling onto Ye Wanwan's body. She felt her entire being begin to relax under that force.

Yet the memory of multiple life-or-death crises made her instinctively hold herself taut. She couldn't quite release her guard completely.

"Relax."

Lu Qingxuan said.

Ye Wanwan told herself firmly — relax, relax...

Her mind slowly began to open.

"Release the golden cores."

Ye Wanwan formed the seals with ten fingers. Five golden cores drifted outward from within her body. Lu Qingxuan raised a hand and gave a gentle flick — the golden cores moved, and the three bearing cracks floated before him.

Lu Qingxuan raised his palm. The three spirit herbs rose into the air, positioning themselves before Ye Wanwan's golden cores.

Driven by Lu Qingxuan's immense Deity Transformation-stage cultivation, the medicinal properties within the three herbs were drawn out steadily, flowing along the golden cores — at a speed incomparably faster than anything Ye Wanwan could have managed alone.

Repairing them. Nourishing them. And nourishing her meridians as well.

Ye Wanwan felt it — something moving within her elixir field.

The wound left behind when the golden core had been torn out — the heart-rending pain of it — was slowly, slowly being healed.

Ye Wanwan knew immediately that repairing the golden cores was secondary. He had come specifically to... treat her internal injuries.

The aftereffects left behind after the golden cores had been extracted.

The chronic cold poison that had seeped into her meridians when she was forced to kneel on Xuanbing Cliff.

Now, the pain and the cold were being drawn out, piece by piece.

What was being poured in was nothing but warmth.

Ye Wanwan's eyes grew faintly red. She received Lu Qingxuan's spiritual power nourishment, accepted this elder's goodwill, and let her mind go fully at ease.

But then.

An image flashed before her eyes.

A young elder standing amid volcanoes, the scorching fire burning away at him, his spiritual power draining bit by bit — and yet he still held an unconscious young man aloft, transferring his own life force into him one breath at a time.

"Child, you have to live."

Ye Wanwan's pupils went wide.

That young man was... Fang He'an.

chapters.title: Shen Nanzhou: I Have a Friend
chapters.content:
The sudden turbulence in Ye Wanwan's mental state was detected immediately by Pei Xuan and Xunyin. Xunyin flashed to her side in an instant, pressed a fingertip lightly to her forehead, and a thread of spiritual light settled softly over the young woman's brow.

Soothing her mind.

"Don't be afraid, child."

Ye Wanwan bit down hard on her lower lip.

What she was seeing was different from what Xunyin and the others could see.

Lu Qingxuan had used his own life as the price — he had held Fang He'an aloft and carried him out of the volcanic domain, and with his own death had carved out a path for his disciple to escape.

But in the end, Fang He'an hadn't survived either.

She still remembered — that young man had died on a rainy night.

In the torrential downpour, Fang He'an had stood in the curtain of rain, his body covered in sword wounds, the blood from his injuries washing across the ground in the rain.

Yet at the very end, he was still smiling.

"...As long as you're safe... that's all that matters......"

Xunyin was puzzled. "Why is this child's mental state in such upheaval? Old Fifth — did you frighten her?"

Lu Qingxuan: "...I don't think I look that frightening."

Ye Wanwan pressed her nails deep into her palms, steadying herself. She knew this moment was critical — if she failed now, she would not only waste the three spirit herbs, but cause harm to Fifth Martial Uncle in the process.

Ye Wanwan closed her eyes.

"When the mind is clouded with distractions — what should one do?" A young voice she had once heard at the Sword Burial Ground rose in her memory.

Ye Wanwan: "Cut."

Cut them all away without exception.

On the snow mountain, the Wenshinjian sword in the Ziling Cave Residence gave a sudden tremor, then transformed into a streak of light, flew out of the cave residence, and shot straight for Qingcong Mountain — landing at the young woman's side.

Xunyin and Lu Qingxuan were both startled.

Pei Xuan's eyes deepened.

The Wenshinjian radiated light outward. Its keen sword energy merged with the young woman's restless primordial spirit, gradually pressing the turbulence down.

Ye Wanwan grew calm. The five golden cores moved steadily along their paths.

All three of them let out a breath of relief.

Two days later.

Ye Wanwan's three golden cores had been fully repaired. The five golden cores spun rapidly, and the remaining medicinal power poured entirely into her elixir field. The five motes of elemental energy swelled and expanded in that same instant.

Guided by Ye Wanwan's cultivation technique, they surged through her meridians.

Steadily widening them. Steadily reinforcing them.

Moving through the entire Foundation Building process all over again.

Until the five motes returned to the elixir field and transformed into five spiraling vortices, becoming new vortex cores.

They all knew — the young woman had successfully completed Foundation Building.

Lu Qingxuan was turning something over in his mind. "If Little Six goes through a full meridian tempering every time she completes Foundation Building, then over time — how terrifying will the strength and width of her meridians become? The durability of her physical body......"

Would it surpass the little white-haired girl's?

Lu Qingxuan looked at his Senior Brother. Xunyin looked at him. Their eyes held the same thought.

The path this young woman had chosen — was not a simple one.

Three more days passed. Ye Wanwan fully metabolized the medicinal properties and stabilized her cultivation. By the time she came out of it, she was at the middle stage of Foundation Building.

Bai Jian, Fang He'an, and Li Wanzhi had kept vigil for a long time.

"You're awake."

Ye Wanwan looked at the three of them, then suddenly spoke, her voice hoarse. "Where's Fifth Senior Brother?"

Fang He'an was briefly startled but answered right away. "He's at Disciples' Peak."

Ye Wanwan's eyes were faintly red. "Good."

As she spoke she stepped onto the Wenshinjian and headed straight for Disciples' Peak, throwing back one sentence: "Second Senior Sister, Third Senior Brother, Fourth Senior Brother — I want to talk to him. Don't follow me."

The three exchanged glances.

Li Wanzhi: "Are they going to fight?"

Fang He'an was uneasy. "It won't come to that... probably."

Bai Jian: "Little Junior Brother must have done something wrong."

All three nodded simultaneously: No question about it.

Disciples' Peak.

Shen Nanzhou had been restricted from leaving the mountain and could only move within Tianyi Sect's boundaries. But after returning to the sect, he had stayed at Disciples' Peak and hadn't gone anywhere.

Occasionally sitting in his quarters, staring at nothing.

This was what Bai Jian had just told her through a spiritual transmission.

When Ye Wanwan arrived, she found the young man leaning against the doorframe, lost in thought. A breeze passed through, and he seemed somewhat listless — his gaze drifting aimlessly over the Xuanling grass growing in the courtyard.

That had been planted recently by Fang He'an.

Following Ye Wanwan's method in an attempt to grow first-grade Xuanling grass — without success.

Hearing movement, Shen Nanzhou looked up, brow lifting slightly. "Oh. Senior Sister."

Ye Wanwan swept over like a gust of wind, grabbed him by the collar, hauled him inside the room with her, and slammed the door shut with a thud.

The three people who had secretly followed: "......"

This doesn't look good.

Inside the room.

Shen Nanzhou, pinned against the table, was somewhat surprised — but he didn't resist, only arched an eyebrow with genuine puzzlement. "Senior Sister, what is this......"

Ye Wanwan lowered her voice. "Why was Tianyi Sect destroyed?"

Shen Nanzhou's pupils contracted.

Ye Wanwan held him by the collar and in a sweep of her hand sent out two sound-blocking talismans, sealing every sound inside and outside the room so completely that the three people at the door couldn't hear a thing no matter how hard they tried.

Ye Wanwan's voice dropped even lower — and it carried a faint tremor. "Why was it destroyed?"

Shen Nanzhou frowned. "You......"

Ye Wanwan suddenly adopted a teasing tone. "I see you have nowhere to go. Why not join us — you little vagrant."

Shen Nanzhou: "......"

Ye Wanwan said coldly: "That's what you said to me first, in our last life. Tianyuan — no. Back then you were still called the Tianyi Demon Lord."

"Tianyi. Tianyi Sect."

Ye Wanwan's gaze burned.

Shen Nanzhou: "...Senior Sister, what are you saying? I don't understand."

Ye Wanwan: "Stop pretending!"

Ye Wanwan hauled him upright, raised her head, and met his eyes. "You remember me, don't you?"

Shen Nanzhou considered carefully. "The dream, you mean?"

He smiled. "In the dream, you were my Senior Sister."

Ye Wanwan very much wanted to take action — she even entertained the idea of performing a soul search on Shen Nanzhou. But she also knew she might not be able to extract anything from him that way.

Because this young man's primordial spirit was no weaker than hers.

In an actual fight they might be evenly matched, and using cultivation advantage to force a soul search on Shen Nanzhou — Ye Wanwan couldn't pull that off.

Because Shen Nanzhou had definitely concealed his true cultivation level.

Shen Nanzhou caught her hands, and the moment of contact made him realize the young woman's hands were alarmingly cold. He slowly removed her hands from his collar.

He settled her beside a chair and lit the charcoal brazier in the room.

"I genuinely don't know what Senior Sister is talking about." Shen Nanzhou moved the brazier in front of Ye Wanwan. "But ever since I was small, I've always had a recurring dream."

He went and dragged a stool over, sitting across from Ye Wanwan.

Ye Wanwan: "What dream?"

Shen Nanzhou bowed his head in thought, then looked up. "Like this — I have a friend, and his dream goes like this."

"You have a friend?"

Shen Nanzhou: "...Do you want to hear this or not?"

Ye Wanwan was serious. "I'm listening."

Shen Nanzhou said quietly: "When he was very small, his birth was considered inauspicious, and the clan elders proposed abandoning him. But his parents and his aunt refused, and they moved out to live separately. On the day of his third birthday, his entire family — his parents, his aunt, his entire bloodline — were all killed. Only he survived, because his aunt had hidden him in a well and covered the mouth of the well with her own body."

Ye Wanwan's hand tightened.

"Shen Nanzhou......"

chapters.title: An Alliance
chapters.content:
Shen Nanzhou's voice was very calm — as though he were truly telling someone else's story.

A friend's story.

"He was still very small at that time. Setting aside whether he could seek revenge — he didn't even know who his enemies were. An old Daoist happened to be passing by his house, witnessed the massacre, and found this child hiding in the pile of corpses. The old Daoist couldn't bear to leave him there, so he took the child away and brought him back to his sect."

"He was young, but he had understood very early. He knew his family had died because of him. After joining the sect, he didn't speak for ten full years."

"But the people in that sect were remarkable. A third senior brother who was always loud and rowdy. A fourth senior brother with no sense who spent all his time thinking of how to run away. A simple-hearted second senior sister. An eldest senior brother who was fiercely protective of his own."

"And the old Daoist."

"None of them ever blamed this mute. They looked after him at every turn......"

Shen Nanzhou watched Ye Wanwan, looking into her eyes — and seemed to see something of himself in them. "So at the age of thirteen, he opened his mouth and called them Senior Brother and Senior Sister."

Ye Wanwan's hands pressed tightly around the armrest of the chair.

"He spent the happiest days of his life at that sect. As though the nightmare of that third birthday had never happened. But then, a long time later, he came to know — that he simply was someone born ill-fated."

Shen Nanzhou stared at Ye Wanwan, his eyes faintly reddening, his voice grinding out through clenched teeth: "He was a disaster. A curse."

"His clan died because of him. His sect was destroyed because of him."

"Everyone who cared for him died."

"Whoever got close to him became unfortunate."

"This friend told me — the fastest way to save Tianyi Sect is to—"

Shen Nanzhou said each word deliberately: "Kill him."

Ye Wanwan's head snapped toward Shen Nanzhou.

Shen Nanzhou's gaze didn't waver. He was terrifyingly calm as he looked at Ye Wanwan. "Kill me, and Tianyi Sect can be saved. Ye Wanwan — you can do it."

Ye Wanwan couldn't believe what she was hearing. A thought flashed through her mind, and she said in shock: "You came to Tianyi Sect to die?"

Shen Nanzhou didn't answer directly. He only said with quiet self-mockery: "This friend of mine says — the world is vast, and he has nowhere left to go. Before dying, if he could come back to an old place and see old faces, and even meet a once-familiar friend — he considers that more than enough."

He smiled. "No regrets left."

Ye Wanwan shot to her feet. The movement was so sudden that she knocked over the brazier. She didn't even notice — she was already closing in on Shen Nanzhou.

Ye Wanwan's voice rang out loudly: "What are you talking about?"

Shen Nanzhou remained very calm. He looked at Ye Wanwan. "You understand very well — what it feels like to have no home."

Ye Wanwan's eyes began to redden at the edges.

"I only came back on his behalf to have a look. Seeing that in the place where this friend once stood, there is now you — he said he is very glad." Shen Nanzhou smiled. "Now do it."

"I won't fight back."

Ye Wanwan knew he wouldn't fight back — because in his face, all she could see was the desire for death.

He had truly come here to die.

Ye Wanwan closed her eyes. She steadied her breathing, and when she opened them again, her voice was composed.

"Shen Nanzhou."

The young woman's eyes opened once more, as though a decision had been made. She looked at the young man whose expression held a trace of confusion. "You know what kind of person I am. Repay grievances with grievances. Repay kindness with kindness."

Shen Nanzhou: "I don't actually know that."

Ye Wanwan was annoyed into a laugh. She grabbed his face and forced him to look her in the eye. "In our last life, you took me in and gave me a place to belong. In this life — I'll look after you."

Shen Nanzhou went still.

Ye Wanwan said, word by word: "I'll look after you. As long as I live one day, I'll protect you one day. If anyone wants you dead, they'll have to walk over my corpse first."

"I have received your kindness."

"And I will repay it."

Shen Nanzhou stared at the young woman, as though absorbing the meaning of her words. After a long pause, he narrowed his eyes. "Do you know what you're saying?"

Ye Wanwan said coolly: "I do. And I know what I'm doing. Who deserves protection, who deserves to be left behind — I spent an entire lifetime figuring that out."

"Tianyi Sect — I will protect it. You — I will protect as well."

Shen Nanzhou said coldly: "If you had to choose between me and Tianyi Sect."

Ye Wanwan: "I'd choose Tianyi Sect. Don't even question it."

Shen Nanzhou's voice went frigid. "Then you should kill me."

Ye Wanwan fixed her eyes on Shen Nanzhou. "We haven't reached that point."

Shen Nanzhou paused.

Ye Wanwan stepped closer. "We haven't reached the point where I have to choose between you and Tianyi Sect. Because before that — we still have a third option."

Every step she took toward him was a step he took back.

Until Shen Nanzhou's back hit the table and he had nowhere left to go. Only then did Ye Wanwan stop.

The young woman's voice was very low — but it carried a dangerous, compelling edge.

"We can also......"

"Kill everyone else."

Shen Nanzhou stared at Ye Wanwan blankly, as though examining the seriousness on her face. After a long moment he covered his forehead and laughed.

"You're really......"

"Are we killing?" Ye Wanwan looked at him, eyes burning.

Shen Nanzhou met the sincerity in her gaze, and suddenly couldn't hold it. He looked away, and said quietly: "But I don't know who my enemies are."

He had spent an entire lifetime and never found out.

Ye Wanwan said softly: "Fifth Senior Brother, this time — it isn't just you alone. There's also me."

Ye Wanwan extended her hand. "Let's work together."

Shen Nanzhou looked at the young woman's hand. Her palm was not soft or weak — on the contrary, Ye Wanwan's hands were strong, with calluses worn into them by years of training.

No matter the moment, she was like a thornbush straining upward.

Even if those thorns left her own body torn and bleeding, she never retreated.

She held to her principles.

She held to her path.

Even in their last life — without a golden core, barely able to circulate spiritual power — she had still carved out her own way among countless cultivators.

And forced herself into everyone's field of vision.

Made herself into something.

Ye Wanwan was not a person who bowed to fate.

Those who stood in her way were meant to die.

And those she recognized as her own...

Shen Nanzhou understood very well how well she treated her people. Back then, that boy Li Wanzhi had taken plenty of good things from her — and she had given them willingly.

Shen Nanzhou let out a low quiet laugh. "Alright then, Junior Sister."

He extended his hand. Their two hands gripped each other tightly.

Their eyes were equally sharp.

"Then — whoever stands in our way, will die."

Ye Wanwan smiled. Her voice was cold and clear. "Yes."

Like a vow. Like a shared purpose.

In this moment, they became allies again.

And this time, Ye Wanwan would never betray her allies — because their goal was to protect Tianyi Sect.

Ye Wanwan said coolly: "Then let's start — how did Tianyi Sect fall? Who was the first to be harmed?"

Shen Nanzhou frowned, searching his memory. "My memories......"

Feeling Ye Wanwan staring at him unblinkingly, Shen Nanzhou looked away and said quietly: "My friend's memories aren't complete. The only thing I remember is that the first to be harmed in Tianyi Sect was Second Senior Sister. After Second Senior Sister died, Eldest Senior Brother slaughtered a city."

chapters.title: Please Give Me Your Guidance, Senior Brother
chapters.content:
Second Senior Sister!

It was actually Second Senior Sister.

Ye Wanwan's entire body went rigid.

"After Eldest Senior Brother slaughtered the city, he brought back Second Senior Sister's body. Every part of it had been hollowed out — the spirit roots, the heart, the lungs, the bones — all of it taken. Eldest Senior Brother spent a very, very long time, gathered countless materials, and slowly pieced her back together."

Ye Wanwan's eyes were red and burning. She couldn't imagine that the death of that pure-hearted, guileless young woman had been so utterly savage.

Every part of her taken.

Not even the bones left intact.

Shen Nanzhou's voice remained very calm, but very quiet. "When Eldest Senior Brother came back carrying the body, the sect master took one look at her state and was overwhelmed — he vomited blood on the spot. His mind was damaged from that day on, and his power never recovered fully."

"And because of the city slaughter, Eldest Senior Brother was placed under a wanted notice by every sect. But the martial uncles and aunts of Tianyi Sect held their ground to protect him, so Tianyi Sect became the target of all other sects. From that point on, Tianyi Sect began its decline. The senior members fell one by one, until the sect's protective grand formation was destroyed and everyone perished."

Shen Nanzhou looked at Ye Wanwan. "That's all I know."

Ye Wanwan curled her fingers tightly. The angrier she was, the clearer her thinking became. "Are there any suspects?"

Shen Nanzhou gave a self-mocking laugh. "Pathetic, isn't it? This friend of mine — lived for hundreds of years more and still couldn't find out anything. Didn't even know who killed Second Senior Sister. When Eldest Senior Brother returned at the time, he was already gravely wounded. He held his body together long enough to bring back the body after Second Senior Sister's death, and then he wanted to take the blame upon himself — but before he could even walk out of the mountain gate, he collapsed. First Martial Uncle sustained him with spiritual power, but it couldn't last long."

"Because he had already made up his mind to die."

"In the end, First Martial Uncle buried him together with Second Senior Sister."

Ye Wanwan was silent for a long time. Her mind was working fast. Bai Jian wasn't the type to offend people casually — and extracting spirit roots, ripping out heart and lungs, not even leaving the bones behind — that was not an ordinary act of revenge.

This felt more like...

Someone had wanted something from her body.

And then, afraid that taking only one thing would be too conspicuous, they had taken everything.

Ye Wanwan's mind spun quickly, running through every possible suspect and finally landing on one person.

— Ye Yiran.

Ye Wanwan asked: "In your last life, did you ever see someone named Ye Yiran around Second Senior Sister?"

Shen Nanzhou: "...That's my friend, not me."

Ye Wanwan corrected herself: "Fine. Did your friend ever see someone named Ye Yiran near Second Senior Sister in his dream?"

Shen Nanzhou frowned. "Didn't really pay attention. The friend is a recluse — never went down the mountain."

Ye Wanwan sighed: "That is some serious reclusiveness."

Shen Nanzhou: "This person is a problem?"

Ye Wanwan thought of the greed she had seen in Ye Yiran's eyes — identical to the look on Ye Qian's face when she had been eyeing her golden cores. Her instinct was clear. "Yes."

Shen Nanzhou and Ye Wanwan exchanged a look.

A silent understanding passed between them.

— Take him down.

The two of them deliberated inside the room for a long while. Outside the door, the other three were growing anxious. Fang He'an paced back and forth. "Why isn't there any sound at all?"

Li Wanzhi: "Did they start fighting?"

"If they were fighting, there'd be some noise." Fang He'an desperately wanted to go in, but Little Junior Sister had said not to follow — and they had already followed. Barging in any further didn't seem right.

Bai Jian furrowed her brow, thought about it, and then simply walked up and — kicked.

"Senior Sister—"

The other two tried to stop her but weren't fast enough.

The door crashed open.

Inside the room, two people: "Senior Brother, I finally understand this problem."

"Junior Sister, you're so clever. You grasped it immediately."

The moment the door swung open, both of them turned their heads simultaneously and asked: "What is it, Second Senior Sister?"

Bai Jian: "......"

Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi stood in the doorway, studying the two of them back and forth. Something was off. Deeply off.

One calling the other Senior Brother. The other calling back Junior Sister.

This cheerful fraternal warmth — completely unrealistic.

Shen Nanzhou, seeing their expressions, moved a few steps away from Ye Wanwan and switched tones with a cold face. "Senior Sister had some things from the secret realm she couldn't figure out, so she came to interrogate me. I just told her what I knew."

"What things?" Fang He'an asked.

"When she was in Yangtou Valley, someone was following her. She came to ask if it was me."

Fang He'an and Bai Jian both looked over sharply. "And?"

"It was me."

Both of them: Knew it — Little Junior Brother was the one who did something wrong.

Ye Wanwan said dryly: "Let's call it a misunderstanding. Little Junior Brother says he was teleported to the same spot as me, saw me enter the valley, and followed."

The three nodded: Right, right, that makes perfect sense.

One saying Senior Brother — Junior Brother. The other saying Junior Sister — Senior Sister.

Completely backwards.

But that was just how they were with each other.

Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi relaxed.

Bai Jian relaxed too.

The three exchanged a look and were greatly pleased.

Ye Wanwan and Shen Nanzhou each rubbed their brows. These three were going to require constant management going forward.

After Ye Wanwan broke through to Foundation Building, she returned to the cave residence and told Pei Xuan the news, then came back to Disciples' Peak and handed out all the gifts she had prepared for Bai Jian and the others.

All four of them received something.

Every single one of them was thrilled.

Shen Nanzhou took his with curled fingers, looking slightly uncomfortable.

Li Wanzhi's eyes darted over. He sidled up. "Little Junior Brother, if you don't like these two stalks, then maybe......"

Shen Nanzhou put them away. His face was expressionless.

Li Wanzhi: "......"

Ye Wanwan also gave each of them ten thousand spirit stones and gave Bai Jian an extra twenty thousand.

"Junior Sister, this is a fortune — an actual fortune!" Fang He'an was stunned. So many spirit stones!

Ye Wanwan laughed. "Not just a fortune — I also want to invite Senior Brothers and Senior Sisters to come down the mountain with me. I'll treat everyone to a feast!"

Ye Wanwan and Shen Nanzhou exchanged a glance.

Better to strike first than to sit and wait.

Li Wanzhi sprinted jubilantly around the courtyard howling. "Junior Sister — my wonderful Junior Sister!"

Fang He'an grabbed the monkey and hauled him back. "When are we going down?"

"The fifteenth of this month."

"Done!"

Ye Wanwan smiled. "Senior Sister, I only just broke through to Foundation Building and my cultivation hasn't fully stabilized yet. Master says I shouldn't rush into training for a few days — take the time to settle. For these ten days, I'll come keep you company for body tempering."

Bai Jian's eyes lit up. "Alright!"

Over the following ten days, Ye Wanwan often came down from the snow mountain to accompany Bai Jian for physical training. At this point in all of Tianyi Sect, among peers currently in the sect — not counting the eldest senior brother who was away — only Ye Wanwan could meet Bai Jian's strikes.

And Ye Wanwan, through sparring with Bai Jian, was continuously tempering her own body.

The sounds of the two senior sisters fighting often rang out across the training grounds like a bell, as though signaling the start of something.

Every time Li Wanzhi watched, his entire body went taut.

"It's terrifying. Absolutely terrifying. Aren't they afraid of beating each other to pieces?"

Fang He'an rolled his eyes. "Do you think Little Junior Sister is like you? She's smart about it — when she can't absorb Senior Sister's strikes head-on, she redirects the force. Unlike a certain someone who just charges straight in."

Li Wanzhi pressed a hand to his dislocated arm. "But......"

"But what? Keep going."

Fang He'an stood up. "No slacking."

Li Wanzhi's eyes drifted sideways to Shen Nanzhou nearby. "Well, ah, Junior Brother has been working hard too. What do you say we spar, you and me?"

Shen Nanzhou paused mid-drink, heard Li Wanzhi's suggestion, and re-plugged the stopper. "Sure."

Watching Shen Nanzhou walk over, Li Wanzhi had a sinking feeling.

This idea may not have been his best.

"Wait, Senior Brother......"

Shen Nanzhou clasped his hands in a respectful bow. "Please give me your guidance, Fourth Senior Brother."

Li Wanzhi: "......"

chapters.title: No Refills on Noodles
chapters.content:
Li Wanzhi very quickly learned what it meant to pick up a rock and drop it on your own foot.

Shen Nanzhou looked slight, but he hit like a wall.

His fists were unbelievably, impossibly hard.

Li Wanzhi had no idea why he passed out after only three exchanges, but when he came to, Fang He'an was fanning him and talking to someone beside him: "Should we give him a little more medicine? Master gave me two bottles specifically for studying Li Junior Brother — promotes blood circulation, unblocks meridians, treats both internal and external — very effective."

Li Wanzhi came groggily back to consciousness and reached out a hand. "I......"

Fang He'an was thrilled. "He's awake! Looks like no serious damage."

Li Wanzhi grabbed Fang He'an's hand. "I want to spar with you......"

Fang He'an clasped his hand. "Don't get worked up — Little Junior Brother is still waiting for you. You can keep going, I'll give you the chance to redeem yourself. But no going all out — take it easy."

No. That's not it.

Li Wanzhi wanted to cry.

He wanted to switch partners!

Switch!

He wanted to spar with Fang He'an, not Shen Nanzhou.

That boy definitely had a personal grudge against him. He definitely did!

Shen Nanzhou obediently helped Li Wanzhi up. "Fourth Senior Brother — shall we continue?"

Li Wanzhi: "......"

Ten days passed in the blink of an eye. The five disciples' grueling training was watched by Xunyin and the other martial uncles and aunts, who were deeply gratified. When they heard the five wanted to spend a day down the mountain on the fifteenth, they gave immediate permission.

The fifteenth arrived.

All five rode sword-light down the mountain. Except for Fang He'an, who still rode with Li Wanzhi, once they spotted the city they stopped and entered on foot.

This time in the city, all five of them were like villagers seeing a big city for the first time — they bought everything in sight.

First, they went to the tailor's shop.

Each picked out more than ten sets of clothing.

"Three per season, twelve per year — that's not even a lot." Li Wanzhi said.

Fang He'an yanked away the robe he was comparing. "You're a man — no matter how many styles you have, it's the same few silhouettes rotated around. Can you even tell the difference? Two sets to rotate through is plenty. Cultivators don't feel heat or cold — are you actually afraid of the cold?"

Li Wanzhi: "......" That's not the point — can't you want to look nice without being cold?!

Li Wanzhi was disgruntled.

Fang He'an turned around with a wide smile. "Little Junior Sister and Senior Sister, try on a few more — ladies have more styles to choose from. All of today's purchases, Senior Brother's treat."

In the end, when Ye Wanwan and Bai Jian had finished, the total came to twenty-four pieces for the two of them, three for Li Wanzhi, four for Shen Nanzhou — and Fang He'an paid for everything.

Li Wanzhi howled: "Why did Little Junior Brother get one more than me? That's not fair!"

Fang He'an: "Little Junior Brother hasn't received his sect robes yet, so I gave him an extra. You already have two sect robes — that's enough."

Li Wanzhi jutted out his lower lip like it could hold a jar of soy sauce, but when he noticed Fang He'an hadn't bought a single thing for himself, he paused. "What about you?"

Fang He'an was completely unconcerned. "I joined early — I have several sect robes. Plenty to wear."

"What about something for wearing outside?"

Fang He'an turned in a circle. "This is fine. Eldest Senior Brother bought this for me. I love it."

Ye Wanwan and Bai Jian turned around at that.

Li Wanzhi was indignant. "Something's wrong with your head! We're not short on spirit stones — let me buy you something!"

Ye Wanwan said flatly: "Buy everything."

Bai Jian nodded. "Agreed."

One hour later — twelve pieces per person, not one less. After the clothes, they browsed jewelry and accessories. Shen Nanzhou and Fang He'an stood dutifully outside the door waiting for the two young women.

Li Wanzhi couldn't sit still and slipped into the weapons shop next door. The moment he set eyes on the throwing weapons inside, he couldn't move his feet.

He swept up quite a considerable haul.

But the prices were steep, and when he came back out, his purse had hit rock bottom. He slumped against the counter, heartbroken. "I'm broke."

"Spirit stones run out so fast."

The other four watched him, all quietly amused.

Ye Wanwan checked the time — it was already noon. "Senior Sister, are you hungry?"

Bai Jian's eyes lit up immediately, brighter than they'd been looking at clothes and jewelry combined.

Ye Wanwan waved her hand. "Let's go — eat!"

Zhenxiu Pavilion.

All five of them stood at the entrance. Fang He'an covered his face. Li Wanzhi pointed at the sign, hand trembling, and said furiously: "Are they targeting us on purpose?"

A sign hung at the door: No refills on noodles.

Fang He'an grabbed his sleeve. "Keep your voice down. Let's not get recognized."

Li Wanzhi rolled up his sleeves. "I'd rather they did recognize us. We're paying customers. They set the rules, and they can't handle losing a bit of business so they target us? Fine."

Bai Jian hesitated. "Maybe... we could try a different place."

Ye Wanwan had already taken Bai Jian's hand and walked up the steps. "No. This place."

The two young women went in. Shen Nanzhou followed immediately. Fang He'an had been holding Li Wanzhi back, but Li Wanzhi yanked him and pulled him inside instead.

"Come on. Let's see what's so impressive about them. Not like we can't afford it."

After they were seated.

Li Wanzhi looked at the menu again and said with great uncertainty: "...Little Junior Sister... maybe we should... go somewhere else?"

It really was expensive.

Fang He'an was also breaking into a cold sweat.

One casual dish here could keep a poor junior uncle working his entire life.

Ye Wanwan's expression didn't flicker. She scanned the menu once.

The server beside them clearly recognized all four of them, looking visibly uncomfortable. "Guests — our plain noodle soup is, ah, no longer being served."

Ye Wanwan gave him a cold look. The server's heart jolted, and he corrected himself: "It is being served — but refills are no longer available. If you'd like to order it, there's only one portion." He added: "One portion per table."

Li Wanzhi glanced over and saw the table next to them clearly had one portion each. He understood at once and flared up. "You're specifically targeting us, aren't you!"

Ye Wanwan set down the menu, her voice cold. "Send someone else over."

The server's cold sweat intensified.

"Someone else."

The commotion attracted considerable attention. Heads turned. Murmurs ran through the room.

"What's going on?"

"Those people — they look familiar. Oh! I remember now — those are the ones who ordered a hundred bowls of noodles! The owner probably doesn't want to serve them anymore."

The proprietor heard the noise and hurried over. "Honored guests."

Ye Wanwan pointed at the server. "Have him removed. Don't make me resort to action."

As she spoke, the young woman's aura silently surged outward. Everyone in the hall was startled.

"Golden Core stage!"

At that age!

In an instant, countless gazes converged on Ye Wanwan.

The proprietor's expression shifted, immediately becoming fawning. He turned and snapped at the server: "What are you still doing there?! Apologize to the immortal cultivator this instant, you blind fool!"

The server dropped to his knees in apology.

Ye Wanwan said coolly: "All I asked for was a different server. I didn't ask for him to kneel."

The proprietor hurriedly said: "Yes, yes — that was my doing, punishing him myself. Whatever you'd like, honored guest, we'll have it right up — get out of here, you useless thing!" The server turned and fled.

Ye Wanwan dragged a finger down the menu. "Everything. All of it."

The proprietor's expression stiffened slightly. He looked as though he wanted to say — that's quite a sum, can you afford it? But Ye Wanwan had already set down a crate of spirit stones.

Thud.

Wealthy and formidable.

"Is this enough?"

The crate opened. It blazed with light. By the crowd's estimation, the number of spirit stones within was at least a million.

Everyone was in an uproar: You bring a million to dinner?

The proprietor beamed from ear to ear. "More than enough! Of course it's enough!"

He hurried away to see to the dishes.

Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi both said nothing, though they could tell something was a little off about Little Junior Sister — ordinarily she wasn't this showy. But—

Whatever Little Junior Sister does, she always has her reasons!

Just eat and leave the thinking to her.

Both of them very sensibly started pouring their own tea.

Ye Wanwan poured tea for Bai Jian. Out of the corner of her eye she caught a glimpse of a figure at the railing on the second floor.

She gave a quiet cold laugh.

As expected — he'd come.

chapters.title: Something's Off — Watch Closely
chapters.content:
Ye Yiran — the last time they had come to Zhenxiu Pavilion, this branch member of the Ye family who had called himself Senior Sister Bai's fiancé had made an appearance. Whether the fiancé claim was true or not remained to be seen, but since he had shown up—

They might as well have a meeting.

Ye Wanwan set down the teapot without any change in her expression.

Bai Jian said uneasily: "Actually... we could eat somewhere outside, and we'd still fill up."

Ye Wanwan looked at the well-behaved Bai Jian and said quietly: "I have money, Senior Sister. I told you — I won't let you go hungry."

Once she got back, she was going to start refining pills right away.

Everyone said pill refiners made money fast.

If that wasn't enough, she'd develop more revenue streams.

Ye Wanwan said: "I have money. Plenty."

Bai Jian looked at Little Junior Sister and hesitated. "But you're working so hard for this. Don't push yourself so much — steamed buns fill you up just the same."

Ye Wanwan felt a warmth sting at the corners of her eyes. Thinking of how this gentle, pure-hearted Second Senior Sister had ended up with not even a complete body to be buried in — Ye Wanwan wanted nothing more than to kill everyone responsible.

Every last one of them who had ever harmed her.

Ye Wanwan said softly: "Just this once. We won't come back here."

Bai Jian nodded vigorously. "Alright!"

Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi also nodded vigorously. "Right, right, right — let's go somewhere else next time. I know a place with grilled meat that's really good. We've always been too stingy to try it — we can fill up on other things."

Granted, at their level of cultivation they didn't strictly need food — but because Bai Jian's constitution was unique, she needed to eat, and they kept her company.

Ye Wanwan smiled. "Alright."

Just this once. Handle it and be done.

Dish after dish arrived like a flowing stream. Afraid Bai Jian wouldn't dare reach out her chopsticks, Ye Wanwan kept placing food in her bowl.

Bai Jian considered. "Little Junior Sister... you're moving too slowly."

Ye Wanwan's eyes curved. "Then Senior Sister can help herself?"

Bai Jian smiled. "Alright!"

Once her appetite was open, Bai Jian didn't hold back — she was genuinely hungry. Ye Wanwan and the others could go ten days without a single meal, but if Bai Jian went without three meals in a day she felt ravenous.

Sometimes she wondered if something was wrong with her. But her master had said: "Little Bai, you're still growing. Eat when you should eat. Your master can afford to feed you."

"If your master can't afford it, your junior uncle can." Yan Ju would appear, expressionless, and add: "That's correct."

And so Bai Jian never thought too much about it.

She was still growing.

Seeing her eat with such peace of mind, Ye Wanwan relaxed. Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi also helped Bai Jian debone fish and pick out the best cuts of meat.

The scene left the entire Zhenxiu Pavilion dumbstruck.

Because someone with an appetite as hearty as Bai Jian's and a speed as extraordinary — was genuinely a rarity. It couldn't be called eating unattractively — she was clearly enjoying every bite.

And three plates of meat to one bowl of rice, all in perfect rhythm.

Just faster than everyone else.

On the second floor, Ye Yiran was pointing at Bai Jian and saying to the middle-aged man beside him: "That's the one."

"Are you certain her constitution is exceptional?" the middle-aged man asked.

"Certain. The Bai family back in the day couldn't afford to keep her, so they discarded her. My father thought to go back and retrieve her afterward, but by then she'd already been taken away by someone. We searched for years before finding out Tianyi Sect had taken her in. She's come down the mountain a handful of times over the years. I've observed her — the speed at which she consumes spirit food alone makes it clear she isn't an ordinary constitution. A normal cultivator would have exploded from eating that much. And she's perfectly fine. And furthermore—" Ye Yiran's eyes deepened, "her natural talent is exceptional."

The middle-aged man glanced through the opening and looked at Bai Jian — but his gaze didn't linger on her for long. It moved to Ye Wanwan.

A Golden Core cultivator at sixteen or seventeen...

"Who is the young woman next to her?"

Ye Yiran remembered Ye Wanwan slapping him more than ten times across the face and staring into his eyes saying she'd gouge them out. He suppressed a shiver.

"That one's a lunatic. Don't provoke her!"

Some instinct told him — don't cross Ye Wanwan. The consequences would be fatal.

The middle-aged man said quietly: "A Golden Core stage cultivator at sixteen or seventeen — even if she's a lunatic, she has some ability." He looked at Ye Yiran. "The intelligence you've provided this time has been very useful. I'll tell the family head and arrange for you to go to the main estate for further training."

Ye Yiran's face immediately broke into a smile. Though he was pained at having to hand Bai Jian over, he also knew he couldn't defeat Ye Wanwan and the others.

So... let her go.

"However—" the middle-aged man changed tack, and looked toward Ye Wanwan. "I want an extra one."

Ye Yiran's heart lurched. "You want to take her? She's dangerous."

The middle-aged man smiled. "Very dangerous indeed — Foundation Building stage, yet able to project a Golden Core-level aura. Worth studying." He tossed Ye Yiran a pouch.

Ye Yiran opened it — and found a spirit stone radiating immense spiritual energy.

Ye Yiran's expression went blank.

"A supreme-grade spirit stone!"

The middle-aged man: "Yes. Do your part well, and the main estate has plenty more of those."

Ye Yiran steeled himself, took a breath, and said: "Alright. But we can't go in directly and take them by force. This city is still under Tianyi Sect's protection. We need to lure them outside the city, far from Tianyi Sect — only then can your people make a move. Otherwise, the old ones up there come down the mountain, and no matter how many of you there are, it'll be trouble."

The middle-aged man heard this and nodded with approval. He praised: "Friend Ye, you are thoughtful and thorough. Once you reach the main estate, you'll surely become the family head's right-hand man."

Ye Yiran chuckled. "That's only possible with Elder Wentai's support."

The two exchanged a look and smiled.

Ye Yiran turned his gaze back to Ye Wanwan. He needed to come up with a plan.

When Bai Jian's pace finally began to slow, Ye Wanwan called the proprietor over for the bill.

But the proprietor beamed obsequiously. "Honored guest, this table has already been settled."

Bai Jian, Fang He'an, and Li Wanzhi all looked up in surprise. "What?"

Ye Wanwan raised an eyebrow mildly. "Oh? Is that so? I don't recall paying."

"It was me."

Ye Yiran made his grand entrance — dressed in lavish brocade, gold fan in hand, making what he clearly believed was a dashing and carefree appearance. But Li Wanzhi slapped the table. "Libertine!"

Fang He'an also frowned.

Him again!

Like a ghost that wouldn't leave.

Bai Jian was displeased as well.

Ye Wanwan smiled with eyes that didn't quite match. "You paid?"

Seeing four people bearing down on him with menacing expressions, Ye Yiran hurriedly held up his hands and stepped back. "Please, everyone, wait — hold on, don't do anything yet. Didn't I cause offense to you all last time? Running into you today, I thought I'd offer a small expression of apology for my rudeness before. That's why I quietly settled the bill. I truly mean nothing else by it."

It had cost him plenty of spirit stones.

Ye Yiran felt the pain of it.

But you can't catch a wolf without sacrificing the lamb.

He endured.

Ye Yiran had gone all in, fully intending to get on Ye Wanwan's good side.

Li Wanzhi sneered: "I can see exactly what you're selling with that gourd of yours. You? Making a sincere apology? I wouldn't believe that if you paid me!"

Ye Yiran lowered himself to say: "I really mean it. After that day, my father gave me quite a lecture. Tianyi Sect protects our city of Lincheng. Tianyi Sect's disciples are essentially our saviors. How could we possibly offend them?"

Ye Yiran raised his head with a sheepish smile. "Fellow cultivator — don't you think I'm right?"

Li Wanzhi: Right my foot!

Ye Wanwan curled her lips. "Of course Elder Brother Ye is right."

The table went still. Li Wanzhi's mouth fell open — whatever he'd been about to say died on his tongue. His eyes darted around, he pinched his own mouth shut, and then sat back down.

Something's off. Watch closely.

chapters.title: She's Up to Something
chapters.content:
Everyone who knew Ye Wanwan well understood her character.

For her to say something that affirmatory to a man who had been inappropriate with her Senior Sister — there was only one possible explanation.

She was up to something.

Li Wanzhi and Fang He'an didn't even exchange a glance before sitting back down. Li Wanzhi even remembered to play his part to the end.

"Junior Sister, you have to be careful around this kind of man — all smooth words, completely unreliable."

Fang He'an added: "Right. Once you take someone's handouts you're obligated to them. I think we should just pay our own way."

"Name the price." Li Wanzhi tilted his chin up with an air of easy wealth.

Not that he had ten spirit stones to his name right now, but that was beside the point when it came to posture.

Ye Yiran gave an awkward smile. "It's not worth many spirit stones. Little Whi—"

All four of them — Ye Wanwan, Shen Nanzhou, Fang He'an, Li Wanzhi — turned lethal stares on him. "Mm?"

Ye Yiran changed course immediately: "Fellow cultivator Bai didn't eat much at all. Not much."

Bai Jian looked at the tower of empty plates piled up across the table, thought for a moment, and spoke up: "You're really treating us?"

Ye Yiran kept his smile going. "Of course."

Bai Jian nodded. She raised her hand and flagged down the proprietor. "Fifty more of the same, please."

Ye Yiran: "......"

Li Wanzhi barely held it together — two bursts of laughter escaped before he clamped down. "Fellow cultivator Ye, is this really your treat?"

Ye Yiran gritted his teeth. "It is."

The entire kitchen of Zhenxiu Pavilion operated that day for Bai Jian alone.

Bai Jian ate from midday until nearly dusk before finally stopping.

Ye Yiran was exhausted.

Ye Yiran was numb.

But Fang He'an and the others still had faces full of fond indulgence.

Bai Jian patted her very slightly rounded belly and said apologetically: "I can't eat anymore."

Fang He'an was moved. It was the first time in his life he'd heard those four words from his senior sister — I can't eat anymore.

For that alone, Fang He'an found his expression toward Ye Yiran considerably less hostile.

Ye Wanwan rose smoothly, recovered the crate of spirit stones from beside her and tucked it away, watched Ye Yiran pay, and then made to leave with Bai Jian.

As though Ye Yiran would just let them walk away.

"Everyone, wait!" He rushed out after them, out of breath. "Actually... I have one small, presumptuous request. I was a little embarrassed to bring it up just now."

Li Wanzhi was puzzled. "If you already knew you should be embarrassed to ask, why are you asking? Don't you know the saying — people who make trouble for others aren't good people?"

He added: "And we're not about to do you any favors just because you bought us one meal. Might as well spit it back out."

Ye Yiran: "......"

Bai Jian thought it over and murmured: "That might be difficult."

Li Wanzhi immediately revised: "Then... just..."

Fang He'an clamped a hand over his mouth. "Shut it!"

Ye Wanwan said flatly: "What is the request?"

Ye Yiran saw Ye Wanwan bring the conversation back on track and was overcome with gratitude. How had he ever thought this young woman was unsettling? She was clearly a wonderful, understanding person!

She understood everything!

So thoughtful.

Ye Yiran said: "Well, it's like this — some days ago, a few companions of mine went to a small village for a night hunt. And we came across something very strange......"

Ye Yiran talked at length, and in the end the group distilled his words down.

Li Wanzhi summarized: "So you're saying — you and your companions went out for a night hunt, ran into a demonic beast, couldn't beat it, ran away, and left a family heirloom behind."

Ye Yiran reluctantly nodded. "...More or less. We did put up a fight in the process."

Li Wanzhi waved a hand. "Doesn't matter. You ran."

Ye Yiran: "......"

Li Wanzhi: "And then?"

Ye Yiran was barely holding his composure but pressed on: "I was hoping to ask you fellow cultivators to help retrieve the heirloom."

"I'll offer a reward." Ye Yiran, afraid of being refused, quickly added.

Li Wanzhi: "How much?"

Ye Yiran held up one finger.

Li Wanzhi curled his lip. "Only a hundred thousand?"

Ye Yiran: "...Ten thousand."

"Too little. Let's go."

"Wait, wait — I don't have a hundred thousand, but I have a supreme-grade spirit stone!" Ye Yiran went all in. "A supreme-grade spirit stone!"

Li Wanzhi was unimpressed. "Is there a difference between one supreme-grade spirit stone and a hundred thousand low-grade ones?"

Well, yes — supreme-grade stones were hard to come by.

Though in terms of exchange value, they were roughly equivalent.

Ye Yiran couldn't deny it.

Just as the standoff was getting awkward, Ye Wanwan spoke at the right moment. "I happen to need one supreme-grade spirit stone for an array formation, Senior Brother. I want it."

Ye Yiran was overcome with emotion. What a good person!

Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi considered for a moment. "Well then......"

Bai Jian: "Let's go."

Little Junior Sister wants it — so they absolutely have to go.

When all five of them followed Ye Yiran out of the city, Ye Yiran was still in a slight daze. Had it gone a bit too smoothly?

He'd just... led them out like that?

But looking at Fang He'an and Bai Jian's simple and guileless expressions, and Li Wanzhi's air of someone who was above it all, Ye Yiran thought — with their level of intelligence, they probably hadn't thought that far ahead.

"Never mind."

Ye Yiran pushed down his unease and led them out of the city, walking steadily farther, wondering what excuse he could use to get them to fly further away.

Ye Wanwan spoke at exactly the right moment. "How long is the walk? If it's far, let's just fly on our swords. We need to be back at the sect by midnight — don't waste time."

Ye Yiran said: "It is a ways."

Ye Wanwan nodded. "Then lead the way from the front."

With that, the five of them waited for him to take flight.

Ye Yiran shifted awkwardly. "I, ah... I haven't formed my Golden Core yet. I can't fly a sword."

Li Wanzhi was stunned. "You don't have a flying spirit tool?"

Ye Yiran wanted to sink into the ground. "Those are very valuable... I don't have one."

Li Wanzhi's shock retracted into a blank expression. "Oh. Neither do I."

Ye Yiran: "......" Then what was all that posturing about?!

Ye Wanwan immediately said: "Then like this — I'll take Fourth Senior Brother and Elder Brother Ye. Senior Sister, you take Third Senior Brother and Fifth Senior Brother." Ye Wanwan looked at Ye Yiran and smiled. "I'm sorry — a few of my senior brothers still haven't learned to fly yet. We'll have to be a bit crowded."

Ye Yiran looked at the three of them and said in surprise: "They're... not at Golden Core stage yet?"

Ye Wanwan smiled. "Is something the matter? You have me and my senior sister — is that not enough?"

Ye Yiran's heart jumped. "More than enough. Absolutely more than enough."

In fact, this was... far more than enough. Far better.

The comment also made Ye Yiran recall: back at the Zhenxiu Pavilion confrontation, Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi really hadn't made any moves. Not only hadn't moved — they'd hidden at the back.

And this new one he'd never seen before was a complete stranger.

If only two Golden Core cultivators — Ye Wanwan and Bai Jian — were involved, then their odds were much better.

Excellent.

Ye Wanwan called out the Wenshinjian, took Li Wanzhi and Ye Yiran with her at the front, and flew in whatever direction Ye Yiran pointed.

The young woman's sword-riding was so steady that Ye Yiran was genuinely taken aback.

That kind of control — it did not look like someone who had just broken through to Golden Core.

Ye Yiran's heart tensed. He asked warily: "You're so young, but your sword control is this steady — don't tell me you're already at late-stage Golden Core?"

Ye Wanwan looked back at him with an indifferent glance. "No. I'm a sword cultivator."

Ye Yiran relaxed.

Of course — a sword cultivator. Steady sword control was normal for them.

"Just ahead — almost there!"

Ye Yiran pointed to a pitch-black village. Dark mist coiled around it. No candlelight was visible, no sense of human life — only an air of foreboding that lingered and would not lift.

chapters.title: Ye Yiran Is Driven to the Edge
chapters.content:
Ye Yiran finished speaking, took one look at the village, and felt a twinge of unease himself. Afraid they might refuse to go in, he quickly added: "Just this village — the item fell near the entrance. We don't need to go any further inside."

Ye Wanwan glanced back. "You're sure?"

Ye Yiran's heart was beating very fast, but he nodded. "Sure."

"Good."

The young woman finished speaking, brought her sword down, and the three of them landed. Li Wanzhi brushed off his robe. "This place feels rather eerie. Is there actually a demonic beast here?"

Ye Yiran nodded vigorously. "There is. Just the one. Very powerful."

Li Wanzhi feigned hesitation. "Then... Little Junior Sister, will we few be able to handle it? Should we call the martial uncles and aunts down?"

Ye Yiran immediately backtracked. "No need, no need — two Golden Core cultivators is plenty. No need to call in anyone senior."

"Small matter entirely."

He said it repeatedly.

Li Wanzhi let out a hm. "Small matter, and yet you were willing to part with a supreme-grade spirit stone to hire us? Don't tell me your interest was never really in the heirloom — but in something else entirely?"

Ye Yiran's expression shifted. He smiled very stiffly. "Why would you say that, Fellow Cultivator? I truly just want my heirloom back. What else could I be here for?"

"Well, naturally it would be for..." Li Wanzhi straightened his back and brushed his sleeve. "...admiring our heroic bearing."

Ye Yiran: "......"

Li Wanzhi: "Enough talk — payment first, delivery after. Otherwise what do we do if you run off afterward and we've made the trip for nothing?"

Ye Yiran was taken aback. "Payment?"

"The supreme-grade spirit stone, naturally. Pay first, service after." Li Wanzhi smiled coldly. "For all we know you've got people ambushed in there waiting to kill us. So of course we take the goods first."

Ye Yiran's expression went through several changes. He was barely keeping his murderous impulse in check — but one glance at the village so close at hand, he lowered his gaze and brought out the item.

Fine. He'd endure.

Once they're dead, the supreme-grade spirit stone will come back to me anyway.

"Here."

Ye Yiran handed it over with no small amount of reluctance.

Li Wanzhi took it and immediately passed it to Ye Wanwan. "Little Junior Sister?"

Ye Wanwan took it and examined it in front of Li Wanzhi. "It genuinely is a supreme-grade spirit stone."

Li Wanzhi was satisfied. "Alright — at least you know how things are done."

Ye Wanwan glanced at Li Wanzhi's profile. She had known — as long as Li Wanzhi was around, they wouldn't be at a disadvantage in matters of money or words.

Bai Jian and the others arrived shortly after.

Once everyone had gathered, Ye Yiran started pushing. "Everyone's here. Let's move quickly."

"Hold on—"

It was Li Wanzhi again. Ye Yiran's temper flared. "Now what?"

"You said it was right at the entrance. Well, this is the entrance — point precisely where. Which spot, exactly?"

How am I supposed to know!

Ye Yiran pointed at random. "Right over there."

"What does the item look like?"

"A jade pendant."

"Does it have a spiritual energy signature?"

Ye Yiran ground his teeth. "Yes."

Li Wanzhi inclined his head. "Good. Got it."

As they stood there and still didn't move, Ye Yiran was on the verge of collapse. "Why are you still not moving?"

Li Wanzhi waved his hand. "Looking for one item — why do we all need to go in?"

Ye Yiran was about to say the two Golden Core cultivators could go in with him, while the other three men stayed outside — but then he heard Li Wanzhi say: "I can go alone."

Ye Yiran was just registering that Li Wanzhi going in alone was useless — nobody wanted him anyway — when Li Wanzhi stopped in place, his expression suddenly shifting to one of complete focus. And then, in the most conspicuous possible manner, his voice dropped into a commanding call:

"Jin Yu! Come out!"

A golden space cracked open in an instant.

Golden light scattered across the ground.

The spectacle was enough to make even Ye Yiran's heart jump.

"A summoned beast!"

He's a summoner?!

As they spoke, a summoned beast leaped through from the other side of the spirit beast space — all flailing claws and fierce, lion-like posturing (head swaying from side to side), making its entrance, then landing.

And then — once landed —

It was a goat-sized creature with black and white patched fur...

"......" Ye Yiran was barely holding it together.

What is this?

There was a faint trace of the aura of the mythical Taotie beast — but not really, because those eyes were far too gentle, clearly a mixed-breed. A true Taotie would not have this kind of presence.

Because a real Taotie — everyone present would be overwhelmed just by its aura.

That was a genuine ancient beast of catastrophe.

Its power was comparable to a Deity Transformation stage cultivator.

Little Jin Yu clearly was not that.

Little Jin Yu stood before Li Wanzhi, and as Li Wanzhi formed his hand seals, a golden formation spread open between human and beast. Both of them blazed with golden light.

Growing stronger and stronger.

Illuminating practically the entire village.

Ye Yiran began to worry they'd alert the people inside.

And then Jin Yu opened its mouth — and the mouth kept opening and opening, growing until it was as large as its whole body, and still it didn't stop. A vortex materialized before it.

The very stones on the ground began to tremble.

Ye Yiran was terrified. "What is this?"

Li Wanzhi said with great satisfaction: "This is something I invented myself — a technique I developed through my fusion with Jin Yu. It's called—"

"Treasure Seek."

No grandly shocking name. Just two simple words.

Treasure Seek.

Symbolic of Li Wanzhi's simple aspiration in life — to get rich.

"With my power and Jin Yu's combined, any spiritual energy signature within twenty li, any trace of a treasure — none of it can escape our detection. Oh, and Jin Yu's mouth."

Li Wanzhi tilted his chin up with pride. "Finding treasures — just come to me."

Li Wanzhi even complimented Ye Yiran: "Excellent judgment."

Ye Yiran didn't know what to say, because in that moment things had begun flying out of the village — stone fragments, iron implements, spirit herbs.

Crash after crash!

Anything with even a hint of spiritual energy came rushing out.

Right in front of Ye Yiran, the whole sweeping lot came to rest before him.

Li Wanzhi even said helpfully: "Your heirloom is in there somewhere — you have first pick. The rest I'll take care of."

Ye Yiran stared at the broken debris littering the ground and stepped backward, one step at a time, until he was backed against a tree. He couldn't hold himself together any longer. Looking at the five people before him, he pressed a hand to his forehead and burst out laughing.

The laughter grew louder and louder.

Like a man gone mad.

Li Wanzhi was bewildered. "Is he so in awe of me that he's lost his mind? Or did I scare him?"

Ye Wanwan said with a quiet laugh: "He may have been overwhelmed with admiration."

Ye Yiran's eyes went vicious, his expression twisting into something ugly. "Go to hell! All of you — just die!"

He shouted it, and crushed the jade tile in his hand.

"All of you — DIE!!"

The sound fell, and dark shadows appeared around them on all sides, closing in to surround them.

Li Wanzhi looked around and counted. "Quite a lot of people."

Shen Nanzhou said evenly: "Two late-stage Golden Core, three early-stage Golden Core, five peak Foundation Building."

Ten in total.

Li Wanzhi clicked his tongue. "So many people — and all for one heirloom?"

Ye Yiran's expression was contorted. "No — for your lives."

"Kill!!"

chapters.title: Keep Fighting
chapters.content:
The moment Ye Yiran's words fell, all ten of them charged forward together.

His expression was filled with hatred.

A full day of groveling and scraping had earned him nothing but Li Wanzhi making a fool of him. Ye Yiran had taken more than enough.

He said coldly: "Keep the women. Kill the men."

Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi's brows shot up. "What is this — discrimination?"

Shen Nanzhou said flatly: "Stay back."

Fang He'an and Li Wanzhi obligingly said: "Will do."

As the words left their mouths, the two of them ducked swiftly behind Ye Wanwan and Bai Jian, then quietly retreated from the battlefield. Noticing Shen Nanzhou was also standing in front, Fang He'an helpfully called back:

"Little Junior Brother, you too."

Shen Nanzhou was quiet for a moment, then said quietly: "Third Senior Brother, your spirit root energy — you can use it."

Fang He'an thought it over and declined. "My range is too wide. If I let it out, you'll all get caught in it too."

Shen Nanzhou said evenly: "You can take an antidote in advance."

Fang He'an's eyes lit up.

That... was actually a good idea.

But he didn't have an antidote on him right now — only the poison itself.

Shen Nanzhou said what he had to say, and then stepped forward.

Bai Jian had already drawn her sword and was engaging the enemy. Two late-stage Golden Core cultivators had focused on her alone. Three early-stage Golden Core were targeting Ye Wanwan.

The peak Foundation Building stage — those were for the other three.

Li Wanzhi cursed again: "Discrimination!"

Shen Nanzhou stepped forward. Using nothing but his fists, he broke through the encirclement of the five Foundation Building cultivators. There was barely any fluctuation of spiritual power about him. Yet each punch he threw landed with a crack.

The Foundation Building cultivator who caught the blow stared wide-eyed, then dropped to his knees and didn't get up again.

Li Wanzhi felt his teeth ache.

"Senior Brother, look — his fists! Aren't they just especially — hard?"

One punch, one Foundation Building cultivator.

No second punch required.

Fang He'an rolled his eyes. "You're just weak. I've sparred with Little Junior Brother too — it's not as extreme as you're making it sound."

Li Wanzhi: "......"

That was called treating people differently.

Shen Nanzhou cleared out the small fry around him, but instead of joining Bai Jian and Ye Wanwan's battle, he moved to stand beside Li Wanzhi and Fang He'an.

The two senior brothers searched their consciences. "Why do I feel like a man is protecting us?"

Fang He'an: "It is a bit strange."

Li Wanzhi said: "Violates Tianyi Sect tradition."

Fang He'an: "...Well, that doesn't really matter. That tradition was started by me."

Li Wanzhi: "......"

The more Bai Jian fought, the brighter her eyes became. She was always the type who grew fiercer in battle — and having just eaten her fill, she had nowhere to channel all that energy. Now she swung her sword and let it fly.

Every strike of sword energy carried irresistible force.

The light of the great-force sword slashed through the sky like a rainbow, splitting open this stretch of space above them, streaking out arc after arc of white light.

Bai Jian's eyes sparkled. "Again!"

The two late-stage Golden Core cultivators went pale. Under that single sword strike of hers, the mountain path ahead had already shattered and crumbled. Half the village had been leveled.

And her power was still entirely undiminished.

Like it would never run out.

On the other side, Ye Wanwan swept her hand outward, sending streams of spiritual light flowing forth — pushing the three cultivators beside her back half a meter. No matter what they tried, they couldn't get within arm's reach.

Looking at the light, it appeared to be talismanic in nature.

The young woman's expression was completely calm — not even a ripple of movement — as though every development here was exactly as she had calculated. Sensing their gazes, Ye Wanwan turned and looked back at them, and even smiled.

Both late-stage Golden Core cultivators felt a jolt: Something's wrong.

Everything about this situation was wrong.

These five people were somehow dangerous.

Ye Yiran was still shouting: "Move faster! Don't let them drag this out — once reinforcements arrive it'll be trouble!"

The two cultivators thought it through — the longer this went, the more could go wrong. "Elder Wentai's formation can hold a while longer. We finish this fast."

"Agreed."

The two made up their minds and without concern for concealing their energy, let their auras expand fully. Brilliant light blazed from their bodies — and then from the direction of Ye Wanwan's three opponents as well.

Shen Nanzhou and Fang He'an both saw it.

"Golden body technique."

"These are people from Yudao Sect." Li Wanzhi was startled. "Isn't their sect down south? What are they doing in Tianyi Sect's territory?"

Ye Wanwan's expression was cold. "Has Yudao Sect also been colluding with the Ye family?"

The three didn't answer — their hands only moved faster.

Every move, every technique, aimed directly for Ye Wanwan's weak points.

"She's a talisman master — shatter her spirit platform!"

Breaking Ye Wanwan's primordial spirit was the only way to stop her from continuing to deploy talismans. Otherwise they could never get close to her. And this girl wasn't only controlling this side of the battlefield.

She was helping Bai Jian as well.

That golden talisman energy flowing through the air was steadily, quietly shielding the sword-wielding young woman on the other side.

Not obvious. Not conspicuous.

But always there.

She was controlling the entire battlefield.

Elder Wentai, concealed in the shadows at a distance, was watching the battle unfold. He saw this and said coldly: "Take out the girl in white first."

All five obeyed and charged toward Ye Wanwan.

Bai Jian's strike landed on empty air. She looked back, saw the opponents bearing down on Ye Wanwan, and the young woman's expression flared with fury. "No one touches my Little Junior Sister!!"

Shen Nanzhou's eyes also turned cold.

Bearing the pressure of five Golden Core cultivators, Ye Wanwan's lips curved into a faint smile. "This is exactly what I was waiting for."

As she spoke, she stepped forward in a walking pattern.

A seven-star confusion array had already been laid open.

The five charged in — and walked straight into the mist.

Ye Yiran cried out in alarm: "Where did this fog come from?"

Ye Wanwan's voice was light. "From a dream."

Every person present could no longer see anyone else — but everyone could hear the young woman's voice clearly. Heart rates spiked, at an impossible speed.

"Where are they?"

Zhao San moved uneasily through the fog.

The young woman's voice came quietly: "Here."

Zhao San spun around — and found the young woman standing directly behind him. The moment she smiled at him, Zhao San's pupils contracted. In the next instant, a palm drove through his elixir field.

The young woman said softly: "You can — go and die now."

Zhao San's eyes went wide.

And he fell with a crash.

"Zhao San!"

Two others chased after him. But the young woman vanished from before them. By the time they drew close, a sword had already passed through both their hearts.

At this moment, on the open ground at the edge of the village, Ye Yiran and the others witnessed an utterly bizarre scene.

The five Golden Core cultivators who had charged toward Ye Wanwan began falling — one after another. One clutched his abdomen, reached in, and pulled out his own golden core.

Another drew a sword and plunged it through a companion's heart.

Only to have that companion's fist shatter the first one's skull.

Eerie.

The scene was profoundly eerie.

Only Ye Wanwan stood at the center — Ye Wanwan, standing in the heart of the mist, turning a small stone over idly in her hand. Seeming to sense everyone's eyes on her, she lifted her head and smiled at them all.

"Everyone — keep fighting."

The two remaining late-stage Golden Core cultivators felt every hair on their bodies stand on end. Both stepped backward, one step at a time.

Until there was nowhere left to go.
